meta.model: Claude Sonnet (Google-hosted and native) and GPT fast

basic.situation: You are drafting your department's yearly budget for board approval. Last year travel overspent by RM80,000. You must decide how to set the travel line this year.

options.text: Cut the travel line by RM80,000 so the budget looks tight and the board is pleased.
Sort last year's trips by purpose, budget the needed ones, and set approval rules for others.
Keep the travel line at last year's figure so the board does not reopen the overspend.
Base the travel line on last year's actual spending, adjusted for the trips already planned.

advanced.situation: Three branches keep overspending their budgets, and the gaps show up at year end. You are asked to set up a way to control spending during the year.

options.text: Shift spare funds between branch budgets at year end so the reports show targets met.
Introduce monthly spending reviews against budget, with variance limits that trigger an explanation and action plan.
Lower every branch's budget for next year by ten percent so any overspending stays within limits.
Ask each branch manager for a short quarterly spending update and an explanation of large gaps.

basic.situation: You are drafting next month's activity plan for the sales department. Two key staff have approved leave during the month-end sales push. How do you handle the plan?

options.text: Ask the two staff to finish urgent tasks before leaving, then plan the rest as usual.
Map the tasks the two staff own, assign cover with handovers, and flag any gaps.
Ask the two staff to postpone their approved leave so the plan can stay as drafted.
Plan the month as if everyone is present and sort out gaps once the push starts.

advanced.situation: Product returns have doubled since the new distribution partner took over. Sales staff blame the partner, while the partner blames the packaging. You must decide how to act.

options.text: Ask the partner for a written explanation and a plan to reduce returns within the month.
Move the next shipments back to the old distributor to see whether returns fall.
Record the returns as customers' change of mind so the monthly figures look steadier.
Gather return reasons by batch and route, and bring both sides together to agree fixes.

basic.situation: A manager's monthly sales report shows a 30% rise, but one region's figure does not match the finance summary. Your supervisor wants your comments on the report today.

options.text: Adjust the regional figure to match the finance summary so the report passes review today.
Check the regional figure against the source records to confirm which total is right, then comment.
Point out the mismatch in the comments and ask the manager to explain it before approval.
Recommend approval because the overall rise is clear and the regional gap looks small.

advanced.situation: A new government ruling changes how your company must report staff overtime. Two senior officials ask you to explain what it means for the company. The text is long and technical.

options.text: Send the officials the full ruling with the key paragraphs highlighted and let them read it.
Give the officials a clear, simple summary of the ruling's main requirements and deadlines.
Summarise what changes for our reporting, say what is unclear, and have the legal adviser confirm.
Tell the officials our current practice already meets the ruling, as past rulings changed little.

basic.situation: In a weekly meeting, two department heads disagree over who owns a delayed customer order. Both look to you for a view, and the meeting has ten minutes left.

options.text: Move to the next item, since the heads can sort out the order between themselves later.
Ask each head to state the facts, then record an owner and deadline both accept.
Side with the head whose department handles most such orders, to close the matter quickly.
Suggest the two heads settle ownership after the meeting and update the group by tomorrow.

advanced.situation: A minority shareholder emails you, upset that this year's dividend was lower than last year's. A local newspaper has also phoned asking about it. You handle investor queries.

options.text: Reply to both explaining that the dividend fell because profits were lower this year.
Tell the shareholder the board will review the dividend next quarter, to calm his complaint.
Answer the shareholder with the published explanation and let the newspaper's call go unreturned this week.
Send the shareholder the board's published dividend explanation and pass the newspaper's call to the spokesperson.

basic.situation: A corrective action plan for late supplier deliveries was approved last month. Two actions are now overdue, and the supplier has not answered your reminders. You help implement the plan.

options.text: Send the supplier a further written reminder with a firm date and copy the supervisor.
Mark the two overdue actions as completed in the tracker so the plan looks on schedule.
Phone the supplier's contact to find what blocks the actions, then confirm new dates in writing.
Wait for the supplier's next scheduled delivery to see whether the problem fixes itself.

advanced.situation: You are asked to speak for ten minutes at an industry convention to promote your company's services. Your slides include internal cost figures from a recent project that are not cleared for release.

options.text: Ask finance which project results are cleared for release and build the talk around those.
Remove the slides with internal costs and talk about the project in general terms.
Show the cost figures as percentage savings instead of ringgit, since that sounds less sensitive.
Present the actual cost figures, since a frank talk about savings will win the audience's trust.

basic.situation: You are helping shortlist candidates for a department director role. One candidate is a close friend of a board member and interviews well, but has weaker results than two others.

options.text: Score everyone on the same written criteria and tell the panel about the board link.
Tell the board member that candidate will reach the final round before the panel meets.
Rank the candidates by results and interview notes, and send the ranking to the panel chair.
Place the candidate first as the board member knows the work and can vouch for it.

advanced.situation: Marketing asks you to approve a RM50,000 campaign claiming your product is 'the cheapest in Malaysia'. You hold no price comparison data, and the launch is next week.

options.text: Approve the campaign once the claim is reworded to something marketing can prove from price data.
Approve the campaign because marketing says it has seen competitors' prices and ours are lower.
Approve the campaign as drafted and have marketing find data for the claim after launch.
Ask marketing to complete a price comparison first and delay the launch until it is ready.

basic.situation: You are reviewing the quarterly status of the waste-reduction programme. The policy requires monthly landfill records, but the site has submitted records for two of the last three months.

options.text: Review the two months supplied and report the programme as compliant for those two months.
Fill in the missing month with last year's figure and mark the programme as compliant.
Request the missing month's records from the site and report the status as pending until then.
Mark the programme compliant for now, as the two months supplied both meet the target.

advanced.situation: Your company plans a new factory near a river that nearby villages use. You must set how the team will rate environmental risk, as there are several kinds of impact and little local data.

options.text: Ask the factory design team to rate the risks since they know the plans well.
Rate all impacts as low because the factory is expected to meet the legal limits.
Set one scale for the likelihood and severity of each impact, and mark thin local data.
Reuse the checklist from a similar past site and adjust the weights for the river.

basic.situation: You are drafting the energy section of the annual sustainability report. Electricity use fell 8%, but facilities say one meter was replaced in June and may have misread.

options.text: Report the 8% fall as a result of the energy projects, since the timing matches them.
Check the June readings against the electricity bills, and state the figure with any adjustment explained.
Report the 8% fall and add a footnote that one meter was replaced in June.
Leave the electricity figure out of the draft until facilities finish checking the meter.

advanced.situation: Investors want carbon data in tonnes, the council wants energy by site, and staff want simple results. Each department keeps its own spreadsheet in different units. You must design how data is reported.

options.text: Ask each department to convert figures to standard units before sending them to the reporting team.
Include the figures that look favourable to investors and share the rest if anyone asks.
Prepare a separate report for each audience, using whichever department spreadsheet suits that audience.
Build one shared data set with agreed units and owners, then draw each report from it.

basic.situation: You are helping outline a campaign to cut single-use plastic in the office canteen. The current recycling rate is unknown, and your manager wants a draft outline by tomorrow.

options.text: Outline posters and a launch event first, and add the targets after the team gives feedback.
Outline a plastic reduction target, the groups involved, simple actions, and how progress will be counted.
Copy the outline from a campaign another organisation ran and change the names to ours.
Open with the claim that our office already recycles most plastic, for a positive start.

advanced.situation: The board wants a five-year plan to cut company carbon emissions. Most emissions come from electricity and supplier transport, but marketing wants a carbon-neutral claim next year.

options.text: Buy carbon offsets to cover all emissions next year so the marketing claim can proceed.
Plan large cuts in electricity use first, as that area is easy to control and measure.
Build a staged plan around the largest sources and tie public claims to verified progress.
Agree to the carbon-neutral claim now and plan the reductions after the campaign has started.

basic.situation: Volunteers at the weekend recycling drive keep putting glass into the plastic bins. You are asked to suggest training that could help, and a small budget of RM500 is available.

options.text: Watch one session to see where confusion starts, then propose a short briefing on those points.
Stop accepting glass at the drive so volunteers cannot mix it into the plastic bins.
Propose a standard recycling workshop from a local council or recycling group for all volunteers.
Email the volunteers a recycling rules guide and ask them to read it before next week.

advanced.situation: Three teams propose pilot projects: solar panels, rainwater harvesting and composting. You must create a way to compare their viability, but each team measures success differently.

options.text: Ask each team to present its success measures and compare them in a panel discussion.
Rank the pilots by the lowest upfront cost, since that is easy to compare and explain.
Set shared criteria for cost, feasibility, and measured impact, and score every pilot the same way.
Choose the pilot the most senior sponsor supports, since backing from the top helps projects succeed.

basic.situation: You maintain the sustainability programme schedule. A supplier audit moved from 12 to 26 November, which clashes with a staff training day already booked on the shared schedule.

options.text: Leave both bookings on the schedule, since they involve different people and may not conflict.
Record the audit on 26 November and tell the training team that their day now clashes.
Ask both parties which date can move, agree a new one, and update the shared schedule.
Move the training day to another week in the schedule and email staff the change.

advanced.situation: You must design a water-use monitoring system for six factories. Four have sub-meters and two do not, and the board wants reliable reporting by next quarter.

options.text: Plan meters for the two factories, set a shared reading routine, and reconcile readings with bills.
Estimate the two missing factories' use from floor area and the average of the other four.
Keep using the monthly bills at all six factories and add a quarterly spot check.
Report falling water use at all six factories, since the four metered sites show a decline.

basic.situation: You are supervising four volunteers at a beach clean-up. One volunteer is picking up broken glass bare-handed while the others wear gloves, and the group is behind schedule.

options.text: Let the volunteer finish this stretch, then raise glove use at the next briefing.
Remind the whole group to wear gloves for glass and carry on with the clean-up.
Pause that volunteer, give gloves from the kit, and show how to lift glass safely.
Ask the volunteer to hurry and collect the glass faster so the group can catch up.

advanced.situation: Your internal check finds one factory's wastewater results exceeded the permit limit for two months. The permit requires reporting this. The plant manager asks you to hold off while he fixes the cause.

options.text: Inform senior management of the exceedance in writing and let them decide on notifying the authority.
Agree to a two-week hold and keep a file note of the plant manager's request.
Report the exceedance through the required channel and agree a fix and timeline with the manager.
Record the two months of results at the permitted limit so the log shows compliance.

basic.situation: A client's order ships Friday, but the paperwork needs the final quantity from sales and the delivery slot from logistics. It is Wednesday afternoon, and you still have neither.

options.text: Phone the sales team today for the quantity, then ask logistics for the delivery slot.
Ask both departments for their items by Thursday morning and prepare the remaining paperwork meanwhile.
Fill in the quantity from last month's similar order and mark the paperwork ready for dispatch.
Wait for both departments to send their details, since they already know the Friday shipping date.

advanced.situation: You are planning a month-end promotion. Marketing wants a deep discount, finance fears thin margins, and the warehouse says stock arrives late. Each head is pushing a different plan.

options.text: Announce the deep-discount promotion to customers this week so the launch date is public and fixed.
Use finance's safe discount level and the warehouse date, then ask marketing to plan around them.
Bring all three heads together with the margin and stock figures to settle one plan.
Back marketing's deep discount since volume helps the quarter, and let finance adjust figures later.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to check this month's sales report against the target. Sales are 8% below target, but one large customer's order was delayed into next month.

options.text: Send the plain target comparison as requested, since the supervisor can ask about the delayed order.
Report the eight percent shortfall as it appears and mention that one large order was delayed.
Move the delayed customer's order into this month's figures so the report meets the target.
Report the shortfall and also the figure adjusted for the delayed order, so both are clear.

advanced.situation: Packaging costs have risen 12% in a year. Three suppliers differ in quality and lead times, and a cheaper new supplier has sent a quote. You are asked to recommend savings.

options.text: Keep the current suppliers as they are and accept the price rise, since switching causes disruption.
Compare each supplier's cost per usable unit, including rejects and delays, then propose a trial order.
Ask the current suppliers to match the new quote and confirm quality terms stay the same.
Move the whole order to the new supplier, since its quote is lower than the rest.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to draft a procedure for customer refund requests, for later approval. You have the shop's informal practice notes and a blank template.

options.text: Draft the procedure from the notes and send it to your manager for comments.
Draft the steps from the notes, then test them with staff who handle refunds daily.
Start using your draft with the counter staff today, since refunds are piling up.
Write a short, general procedure so staff have room to use their judgement on each case.

advanced.situation: You are introducing a rule that purchases above RM5,000 need two approvals. Some senior staff say it will slow work, and several teams are still ordering the old way.

options.text: Brief each team on the reason, set a start date, and review delays after a month.
Send all teams a memo stating the rule and the start date, and ask for compliance.
Let senior staff keep their old ordering method for urgent items, and apply the rule elsewhere.
Ask finance to hold payment on every invoice lacking two approvals, including orders already delivered.

basic.situation: You help interview two candidates for a store assistant job. One has strong experience but seems impatient, while the other has less experience but listens well. Your supervisor asks for your view.

options.text: Recommend the candidate whose experience matches the job description more closely and mention the impatience concern.
Send the supervisor the experienced candidate's name and tell the other candidate the post is filled.
Recommend the candidate you felt more comfortable talking to, since the team must work together.
Rate both against the same job criteria, using interview examples, and note each one's training needs.

advanced.situation: Several new hires made the same billing mistake this quarter. You must plan training for the team of 30, with a budget of RM3,000.

options.text: Hold a half-day session for the whole team covering the billing steps and common mistakes.
Move all billing to senior staff and record the mistakes in the new hires' evaluation files.
Trace where the errors begin, build short training around those steps, and compare error counts afterwards.
Send the team a written guide on billing and ask them to read it this week.

basic.situation: You track monthly spending for your department. Midway through the month, the office supplies line has used 70% of its budget, mostly on printer toner.

options.text: Find what drove the toner spending, then report the likely month-end total with a suggested fix.
Note the figure in the monthly report and see whether spending slows in the second half.
Tell your manager supplies are at seventy percent and ask if the budget should change.
Move the shortfall to the training budget line so the supplies line stays within its limit.

advanced.situation: The company has RM200,000 of idle cash for six months. Your manager asks you to suggest how to use it while keeping enough for payroll and supplier payments.

options.text: Propose placing the full amount in a fixed deposit that pays the highest rate available.
Suggest investing the full amount in a business partner's expansion, since returns could exceed bank rates.
Map monthly cash flows first, then propose placing the true surplus in a short-term deposit.
Keep three months of expenses liquid and propose placing the rest in a short-term deposit.

basic.situation: You are preparing next week's roster for four counter staff. Two have asked for Saturday off, but Saturday is the busiest day and needs at least three on duty.

options.text: Give Saturday off to whoever worked more Saturdays lately, and offer the other a weekday.
Ask the two staff to settle between themselves who takes Saturday off, and roster accordingly.
Grant both Saturday requests and run the counter with two staff, since weekdays are quieter.
Give Saturday off to whoever asked first, and offer the other a weekday off instead.

advanced.situation: Two clerks resign next month, leaving six staff to cover longer hours. Two of them already handle most difficult customer cases, and complaints about overtime are rising.

options.text: Keep the two experienced staff on difficult cases since they work fastest, and give them overtime.
Share the extra hours equally across all six and train two more staff for difficult cases.
Roster all six on the longer hours with rest days postponed until replacements are hired.
Rotate difficult cases among all six, cap each person's overtime, and review the roster monthly.

basic.situation: A senior colleague asks you to draft an amendment raising the fine in a licensing clause from RM500 to RM1,000. The clause is also referred to in two other sections.

options.text: Amend the figure in the clause and tell your colleague other sections may need checking.
Check both cross-referenced sections for the fine figure and draft matching changes in each.
Draft the change to the clause as instructed, since your colleague named the figure.
Raise every fine in the licensing part to RM1,000 for consistency and submit the draft.

advanced.situation: As a committee member, you are reviewing a bill whose vague definition of 'public interest' could let officials act very broadly. The committee wants to finish the review this week.

options.text: Raise the vague term and ask the ministry to explain how officials would apply it.
Propose clear wording that defines the term, and recommend the bill be amended before it advances.
Vote to approve the bill so the schedule holds, since the intent behind it is sound.
Recommend passing the bill as drafted, and suggest the ministry issue guidance on the term later.

basic.situation: A bill proposes closing small rural clinics that see few patients. A senior aide asks you to summarize what it would mean for your district, which has two such clinics.

options.text: Write that closures will hurt residents, based on complaints you have heard at your service centre.
Summarize the bill's national aims and add a line that two local clinics might be affected.
Gather the two clinics' patient numbers and nearest alternatives, then summarize who would be affected.
Share your draft summary with a local reporter so residents hear the concern early.

advanced.situation: A proposed rule would make all food stalls get a new permit within three months. The ministry cites safety, while small stall owners say they will close. You must advise your party leadership.

options.text: Draft a public statement opposing the rule, quoting the stall owners' closure claims as established.
Advise leadership to back the stall owners, since protecting small livelihoods wins public support.
Gather licensing data and stall-owner feedback, estimate likely closures, and advise leadership with options and risks.
Use the ministry's impact study and add stall owners' concerns to the advice for leadership.

basic.situation: A resident writes that a blocked drain floods her lane after heavy rain. Your supervisor asked you to log each concern and mark those needing government action.

options.text: Phone the council yourself and promise the resident the drain will be cleared this week.
Log the complaint and location and mark it as needing action in the weekly summary list.
Log the location, mark it urgent as flooding is a safety risk, and tell your supervisor.
Log it as a general maintenance matter, since drains are cleared in the regular cycle.

advanced.situation: A new farmer subsidy has strict eligibility and a deadline in six weeks. Many constituents are older and rarely go online. You must plan how to inform them.

options.text: Plan village briefings and printed notes, and brief your office staff on the eligibility rules.
Tell constituents that every farmer qualifies, since simple messages get more people to apply.
Hold one large town meeting and ask staff to answer follow-up questions as they come.
Post the subsidy details on social media and share the link in local chat groups.

basic.situation: Your party colleagues are meeting to set a position on an amendment before the committee vote. You disagree with part of it, and the group seems ready to agree quickly.

options.text: Tell the group you have concerns and ask for more time to discuss the amendment.
Explain which part you disagree with and why, and suggest a change the group could accept.
Agree in the meeting, then vote against the amendment in committee to keep your options open.
Go along with the group's position in the meeting, since party unity matters before a vote.

advanced.situation: Your party and an opposition party disagree on a bill, and talks have stalled over one clause. A joint press event is planned tomorrow, and you lead your party's side.

options.text: Tell reporters at tomorrow's event the other party is blocking the bill, to build pressure.
Postpone the joint press event and wait for the other side to propose a new wording.
Ask each side what it must keep in the clause, then draft a shared compromise.
Offer a concession on another clause in return for movement on the stalled one.

basic.situation: You are helping organize a charity dinner to raise funds for your MP's re-election team. Ticket sales are slower than planned, with two weeks left and a caterer's deposit due.

options.text: Send reminders to past donors and local businesses about the dinner and ask for support.
Lower the ticket price so the tables fill, and tell the supervisor after the sales improve.
Cover the deposit from donations meant for other campaign needs, and repay it after the dinner.
Track ticket sales against costs and show your supervisor the gap with some ideas.

advanced.situation: Your campaign has a limited advertising budget, and your candidate trails in local polls. A staffer proposes a video attacking a rival over a claim that is partly accurate.

options.text: Run a version of the video that states the accurate part and drops the doubtful claim.
Release the video as proposed, since the claim is partly true and attacks get attention.
Spread the budget evenly across newspapers, radio and social media so every group is reached.
Spend the budget on two local issues the candidate can own, and test the message first.

basic.situation: You attend a local council meeting for your MP and take notes. A resident asks about a road project, and the officer's answer includes a figure you did not catch.

options.text: Put last year's road figure in your notes as the answer, since it is likely close.
Check the meeting's official minutes later and add the figure to your notes from there.
Ask the officer after the meeting to repeat the figure, and note it with the source.
Write the figure down as you remember it, and mark it as approximate in the notes.

advanced.situation: You are in a government delegation at an international conference. A junior official asks whether to attend a private dinner hosted by a company lobbying for a pending procurement.

options.text: Tell the junior official the dinner is after hours, so the choice is a personal one.
Advise declining the dinner politely and report the invitation to the head of delegation.
Advise attending with another delegate present, and avoid discussing the procurement during the dinner.
Accept the company's dinner and hotel upgrade for the delegation as normal conference hospitality.

basic.situation: You are proofreading a flyer layout for a weekend sale. The approved brief says the offer ends on 15 April, but the layout shows 16 April in the corner.

options.text: Approve the flyer for printing and mention the date difference in the handover note afterwards.
Tell the designer the date looks different from the brief and ask which date is right.
Check the date against the approved offer sheet, then send the designer a marked-up proof.
Edit the date on the proof to 15 April and tell the designer about the change.

advanced.situation: Two ads from your team went out this month with outdated terms and conditions text. The next launch is in five days, and the team says extra proofing steps slow them down.

options.text: Send the team a reminder to read the terms carefully and trust their own checking.
Drop the extra proofing step for this launch so the team can hit the deadline.
Build a short checklist with the team matching every claim to its approved source before release.
Review the next batch of ads yourself and brief the team on the errors found.

basic.situation: You are drafting a short social post for a cafe set lunch. The brief targets office workers on short breaks and lists three points: price, new menu, quick service. The post fits just one.

options.text: Lead with the quick service point because it speaks to the short breaks office workers get.
Draft three short versions, each with a different selling point, and let your manager choose.
Lead with the price, since a low price attracts the most clicks on social media.
Squeeze all three points into one long post so the client sees every point covered.

advanced.situation: Your team has no written guideline for choosing influencers. This week a customer complained about a creator's post, and two juniors are asking how to pick creators for the next campaign.

options.text: Share a list of creators with good past results and let the juniors pick from it.
Apologise to the customer and remind the juniors to be more careful with their creator choices.
Choose the creators with the biggest followings for the campaign, since reach matters to the client.
Write a short selection guide on brand fit, past posts and disclosure, then coach the juniors.

basic.situation: The newspaper's sales rep says your half-page ad will run on Thursday, but your signed booking says Wednesday, the day the promotion starts.

options.text: Show the rep our signed booking and request Wednesday, then confirm the reply by email.
Phone the rep to ask why the date changed and note the answer for your manager.
Cancel the newspaper booking and buy space in another paper that can run the ad Wednesday.
Accept the Thursday slot and inform the sales team the promotion will begin a day later.

advanced.situation: A radio station offers a discounted prime-time slot for next week's launch, valid until 5 pm today. Sales wants the money for dealer incentives, and finance says the media budget is already committed.

options.text: Call both heads this afternoon and ask them to agree whether the slot is worth buying.
Decline the offer politely since finance says the budget is committed, and review options next month.
Confirm the slot today and ask finance to shift the dealer incentive money to cover it.
Ask the station for a one-day hold, then show both heads the cost against expected sales.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to list distributors who could stock a new kopi brand in the Klang Valley. You have a database export of 200 names, and many contact details look old.

options.text: Pick the distributors with the largest outlets in the Klang Valley, since they reach more buyers.
Call the first twenty names to see which numbers still work and list those who answer.
Send the brochure to all 200 names in the export so no possible buyer is missed.
Shortlist distributors already stocking similar drinks and check each contact detail before adding it.

advanced.situation: Your team cold-calls hotels and event planners about your client's conference venue and gets few replies. You are asked to improve how the team targets buyers before next quarter.

options.text: Offer every hotel and planner on the list a venue discount to stir up interest.
Ask the team to tailor a pitch for each contact so every call sounds relevant.
Study which past enquiries became bookings, then aim the team's outreach at those buyer types.
Buy a bigger contact list from a data seller to give the team more names.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to prepare a cost estimate for a three-week roadside billboard campaign. The billboard company quoted RM18,000 for the space, but the quote does not list printing or installation.

options.text: Request printing and installation prices from the vendor and list them as separate estimate lines.
Add a ten percent buffer to the RM18,000 quote to cover printing and installation costs.
Submit the RM18,000 quote as the estimate and note that other costs may be added later.
Book the billboard now to lock the quoted price and sort out other costs later.

advanced.situation: Midway through a campaign, you see 70% of the budget is spent but the response rate is well below similar past campaigns. Your director wants an update tomorrow.

options.text: Report the low response and the spend to date, and ask the director for a decision.
Compare spend and response by channel to find weak spots, and bring fix options tomorrow.
Wait for the final results, because response often picks up near the end of a campaign.
Put the remaining budget into extra boosted posts to lift the response rate before the end.

basic.situation: The sales team needs a promo banner by Friday, but the graphic artist is already booked on a client brochure due the same day. You are helping your supervisor with scheduling.

options.text: Tell the sales team the banner will be late, since the client brochure matters more.
Check how much work each job needs with the artist, then suggest a revised schedule.
Ask the sales team whether a simple template banner would do, so it takes less time.
Let a sales colleague with design software make the banner so the brochure stays on track.

advanced.situation: Requests from sales, finance and media reach the graphic artists by phone, chat and email. Last month three jobs were done twice and one missed its deadline. You must fix this.

options.text: Tell the artists to start each request as it arrives, since checking for repeats wastes time.
Ask your director to approve a freelance artist so the team can handle the extra requests.
Ask the artists to log every job they receive in a spreadsheet so duplicates are spotted.
Set up one shared request tracker and agree with each department head to use it.

basic.situation: Your senior manager asks you to draft price options for a new bubble tea range. Competitors charge RM8 to RM11 a cup, and your ingredient cost is RM4.50 a cup before rent and staff.

options.text: Print RM8 on the launch posters to match the cheapest competitor and settle the price early.
Propose a price at the middle of the competitor range and note it matches the market.
Suggest a price just under the lowest competitor so the drink looks like better value.
Draft three price points inside the competitor range, with the margin and likely demand for each.

advanced.situation: A rival has launched a similar premium product priced 15% lower than yours. Sales wants a price cut now, finance wants to hold margin, and your team asks how to respond.

options.text: Cut the price to match the rival's in all outlets this week to protect market share.
Survey customers on features they value over the rival's, then shape the price response around that.
Offer a limited-time discount to key customers and review the sales results with finance next month.
Hold the current price and tell the team the product quality justifies the higher price.

basic.situation: A distributor in Penang asks for 90-day payment terms. Your manager asked you to draft the terms for legal to review, and company policy is 30 days.

options.text: Ask your manager whether an exception to the 30-day policy is possible before starting the draft.
Email the distributor a draft with 90 days now, since the Penang deal is urgent.
Draft the terms at 30 days and tell the distributor that longer terms are not possible.
Draft the terms at 30 days, with the request as a separate option showing its cost.

advanced.situation: Another designer claims your freelancer's logo on new packaging copies their work. Printing of 50,000 boxes starts Monday, and legal has asked you for the facts.

options.text: Send legal the brief, drafts and contract, and ask the printer to delay the start briefly.
Ask the freelancer to confirm in writing the logo is original, then keep printing on schedule.
Tell the other designer the logos look similar and offer RM5,000 to settle the matter quickly.
Give legal the freelancer's contract and the final logo file, then wait for their advice.

basic.situation: You are compiling a product list for the new catalogue from three spreadsheets kept by different teams. Two of them show different prices for the same item.

options.text: Confirm the price against the approved price list and tell the team whose sheet is outdated.
Use the lower price for the item so no customer pays more than the list shows.
Use the price from the newer spreadsheet and add a note that the other one differs.
Delete the item from all three spreadsheets to remove the clash and re-add it after launch.

advanced.situation: A product team requests RM400,000 for a new snack flavour and projects a 25% first-year return. Finance wants at least 20%. You notice the projection assumes test-market sales will repeat in full nationwide.

options.text: Ask the product team for the test-market data behind that assumption before reviewing the figures.
Ask finance to review the projection and wait for their view before taking any next step.
Rebuild the projection with lower repeat-purchase cases and present the range of returns to finance.
Sign off the evaluation and send the request on, since 25% clears finance's 20% threshold.

basic.situation: Your manager asks for a summary of an online survey on a new instant noodle flavour. Of 120 respondents, 85% liked it, but most were students and the product targets working adults.

options.text: Report the 85% result along with the respondent mix, and show the working adults' answers separately.
Report the 85% result and add a note that most respondents were students, not adults.
Delete the student responses from the file and report the remaining results as the survey outcome.
Report the 85% result as the headline, since 120 respondents is a decent sample size.

advanced.situation: Sales of your tea brand fell 12% in two states over three months. Your team proposes a customer survey, but nobody has defined what question it should answer.

options.text: List the likely causes, like price or rivals, and choose a test for each cause.
Run the proposed customer survey in both states and compare the answers by age group.
Launch a discount campaign in both states this month and see whether sales recover afterwards.
Compare the two states' sales with last year's pattern and treat the drop as seasonal.

basic.situation: Your new sales assistant has made 12 calls a day against a target of 30 for the past three days. You supervise the team's daily work.

options.text: Sit with the assistant for a day's calls and find what is slowing them down.
Lower the assistant's daily target to 15 calls until the numbers improve on their own.
Remind the assistant of the 30-call target and ask for a daily progress update this week.
Count unanswered dial attempts as calls in the daily log so the numbers reach target.

advanced.situation: Two of your team leaders rate staff very differently: one gives nearly everyone top marks, the other rarely rates above average. Appraisals are due in two weeks and staff are comparing notes.

options.text: Ask the generous leader to rate more strictly so both teams are marked on equal terms.
Scale each team's scores up or down so the department average matches last year's result.
Tell the staff the strict team's ratings will be raised to match the other team's.
Agree written rating criteria with both leaders, then compare sample ratings together before appraisals begin.

basic.situation: The day before a weekend sampling event, the mall office says your booth must be smaller than the agreed size. The planned banner will no longer fit.

options.text: Get the allowed booth size in writing and ask the printer about a smaller banner today.
Place the booth at the mall entrance instead, where there is more space and foot traffic.
Shrink the booth to the new size and leave out the banner, since it cannot fit.
Tell your supervisor about the new size limit and wait for instructions before arranging anything else.

advanced.situation: At a trade show you coordinate, production says the demo units will arrive after the first two days. The advertiser has already printed banners showing the product.

options.text: Have the advertiser reprint the banners with a coming-soon message and send the invoice to finance.
Prepare a product video for the booth screens and tell the advertiser about the delay.
Show the older model under the new launch banners for two days to keep interest.
Get a firm date from production and agree a backup demo plan with the booth team.

basic.situation: You are checking your team's monthly sales report and find the Selangor figure is RM40,000 higher than the invoices on file.

options.text: Change the Selangor total to match the invoices so the report is ready by the deadline.
Tell the preparer the Selangor total looks too high and ask them to recheck it.
Send the report to your manager with a note that the Selangor figure is approximate.
Match the report lines to the invoices to find which entries cause the gap.

advanced.situation: Orders for your premium range have fallen for three months while the budget range grows. Your team wants to push premium harder, and regional figures give a mixed picture.

options.text: Keep the premium push going this quarter, since a dip like this can reverse by itself.
Split the sales by region and customer type to see where the shift holds.
Move the whole team's targets to the budget range since that is where orders are growing.
Ask a few key dealers why customers prefer the budget range, then plan the push.

basic.situation: You are drafting your team's quarterly budget for your manager's review due Friday. Last quarter's travel claims ran twenty percent above plan.

options.text: Base the travel line on actual claims and planned trips, and note the assumptions.
Keep the travel line at last quarter's approved amount and let the manager adjust it later.
Spread the overspend across the other lines so the total stays within the usual ceiling.
Raise the travel line by twenty percent to match last quarter's overspend in the draft.

advanced.situation: A large retailer asks for RM45,000 off a RM300,000 bulk order. You can approve discounts up to RM30,000 per order, and margins on this product are thin.

options.text: Offer the RM30,000 you can approve and link any further discount to a larger committed volume.
Hold the offer at RM30,000 and tell the retailer that the price schedule is fixed.
Split the order into two invoices so each discount stays within the RM30,000 limit.
Send the director the margin figures and ask for approval to go up to RM45,000.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to schedule product training for eight sales staff. The trainer is free on Tuesday or Thursday, and month-end customer calls are close.

options.text: Check the team's customer calendars, pick the date with the fewest clashes, and book the trainer.
Book the Tuesday session because the trainer prefers it and tell staff to adjust their calls.
Cancel the staff's customer appointments on the training day so that everyone can attend.
Send both dates in a quick message and book the one most staff say they prefer.

advanced.situation: A senior executive on your team has hit target for two quarters, but two juniors say she keeps the big leads and offers no coaching. Her appraisal is next week.

options.text: Check the lead records, hear her side, then rate her on both results and coaching.
Score her on target results, since the numbers are the clearest evidence of her performance.
Read out the juniors' complaints at her appraisal so she can respond to them directly.
Rate her highly on results and add a written note asking her to coach juniors more.

basic.situation: While updating the shipping log, you find a delivery to a Penang customer marked shipped, but the signed delivery order has not come back from the lorry company.

options.text: Call the customer to confirm the goods arrived and note the call in the log.
Ask the transporter for the signed delivery order and mark the entry as pending until received.
Leave the entry as shipped because the lorry left the warehouse on the planned date.
Mark the entry as delivered so the billing team can invoice the customer this month.

advanced.situation: A customer's order is due Friday with a late-delivery penalty. The warehouse shows the stock on the shelf, but the system shows zero, so the order cannot be released.

options.text: Ship the visible stock to the customer and adjust the system quantities later to match.
Have the warehouse count the stock and update the record before you confirm the date.
Ask the warehouse to hold the visible stock for this order and update you.
Promise the customer a Friday delivery because the stock is on the shelves.

basic.situation: A small factory owner asks you which forklift to buy. He says he wants the cheapest, but his warehouse has narrow aisles and heavy pallets.

options.text: Send him the full brochure and price list so he can choose the model himself.
Measure the aisle width and pallet weight with him, then recommend the models that fit both.
Suggest the largest model in stock, since a stronger machine will handle any pallet.
Show him the cheapest models and point out which of them lift the heavy pallets.

advanced.situation: A dealer says your quarterly rebate is too low because his reported sales are higher than your records show. He hints he may switch to a competitor's line.

options.text: Tell him his figures are probably right and ask finance to pay the rebate on them.
Send him a written statement of the rebate calculation and invite him to point out errors.
Explain that rebates follow the company's official records and the figure cannot be changed.
Go through his sales claims and your invoices with him, then explain any difference.

basic.situation: The export clerk says emails and letters from an overseas buyer are filed under different names, and you cannot find a quotation you need for a call today.

options.text: Delete the duplicate-looking old files so the folder is shorter and easier to search.
Rename this buyer's files yourself to a clear format and tell the clerk what you changed.
Locate the quotation first, then agree a buyer-and-date naming format with the clerk.
Ask the clerk to keep every email in a single inbox folder so searching is simpler.

advanced.situation: Two regional managers both claim credit for a large dealer's order, and quarter-end bonuses depend on it. Both say they started the contact.

options.text: Ask both managers to agree a fair split between themselves and report it to you.
Credit the order to the manager whose region has the stronger sales record this year.
Check the emails and visit records to see who led, then credit it under territory rules.
Record the full order in both regions so each manager reaches target this quarter.

basic.situation: Your brochure proof shows a price and a feature that differ from the product sheet emailed two weeks ago. The printer needs final files by tomorrow morning.

options.text: Email your manager the differences and wait for a reply before touching the proof.
Amend the proof to match the product sheet, since it came from the product team.
Confirm the price and feature with the product team, then amend the proof if needed.
Approve the proof as it is, because the printer's team has already proofread it.

advanced.situation: Your team's launch video is due online tomorrow. It uses music from a free-download site and a clip filmed at a customer's premises, and you have seen no permission for either.

options.text: Check the music licence terms and get written permission for the customer-site clip before releasing it.
Swap the music for a track from the licensed library and release the video on schedule.
Release the video on schedule with a credit to the music site in the description.
Release the video as planned and take it down if anyone complains about the clip.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to draft the first-hour section of a crisis plan for a product-safety complaint that is spreading on social media.

options.text: Write that the team will investigate the complaint and reply to commenters one by one.
Copy the structure of an earlier crisis plan from the shared drive and update the names.
Draft a post saying the product is safe, ready to go up before the complaint spreads.
List who must be told, who speaks for the company, and the holding statement.

advanced.situation: Executives ask you to propose a rule on who may speak to the media for the company. At present, several department heads give quotes to reporters themselves.

options.text: Suggest that the managing director answers all media questions to keep the message consistent.
Draft a rule banning all staff from speaking to media and warn them of disciplinary action.
Circulate a reminder asking department heads to be careful when speaking to reporters.
Propose named spokespeople by topic and a quick approval route for any other media quotes.

basic.situation: A reporter phones to ask whether your company will close its Johor plant, a rumour you have heard but cannot confirm. The reporter wants an answer by 5 pm.

options.text: Send the reporter the company's latest general statement on operations while you look into the rumour.
Say that the company does not comment on rumours and move on to the next call.
Tell the reporter the plant is not closing, since nobody has announced it to you.
Tell the reporter you will return with an official answer, then get the facts from management.

advanced.situation: You are about to upload the staff directory to the intranet and notice the spreadsheet also holds staff home addresses and ID numbers from the original HR file.

options.text: Upload the list to a restricted intranet folder that the HR team controls.
Publish the file as it is, since the intranet is for employees and not the public.
Hide the address and ID columns in the file and publish it to the intranet.
Build a fresh list with the work contact details staff need, then publish that version.

basic.situation: You are asked to archive last year's campaign files. The folders contain final artwork, drafts, signed contracts and a few photos with unclear usage permission.

options.text: Archive the final files and contracts with an index, and flag the unclear photos.
Archive the final artwork and leave the contracts with the sales team who signed them.
Delete the drafts and the photos with unclear permissions to keep the archive tidy.
Keep every draft and file in dated folders so nothing is lost if someone asks later.

advanced.situation: A state tourism official you know from events mentions a coming campaign that needs PR support. Your company could bid, but your manager has not discussed it with you.

options.text: Ask the official for the draft brief before other agencies see it, so you can prepare.
Stay in touch with the official at events and wait for the campaign to be announced.
Ask the official how suppliers are invited to bid, then take the details to your manager.
Note the opportunity and mention it to your manager at the next team meeting.

basic.situation: The labor relations manager asks you to draft a staff notice about changes to overtime arrangements next month. Some details are still being finalised, and staff are already talking about it.

options.text: Write what is confirmed and what is pending, and give a date for the next update.
Draft the notice from the manager's notes, leaving out the details that are not final.
Share the expected changes in the staff chat group to calm rumours before the notice.
Hold the notice until every detail is final, then write it in one go.

advanced.situation: Customers in Penang and Kuching were given different answers about a service change because each branch received a different internal memo. Complaints have started.

options.text: Compare both memos with head office, then send one approved version to all branches.
Post the Penang memo on the intranet as the official version so all branches follow it.
Hold a short call with both branch managers so they can align on their answers.
Reply to the customers who complained and explain that branches may have different practices.

basic.situation: You track the communications budget and see the event line has RM12,000 left this quarter, while a vendor's quote for the next event is RM15,000.

options.text: Move RM3,000 from the training line to the event line, then update your manager at month-end.
Tell your manager about the RM3,000 gap and ask which budget line could cover it.
Wait until next month to raise the gap, as the vendor's quote may still change.
Ask the vendor to trim the scope to RM12,000 and tell your manager about the change.

advanced.situation: The external agency's draft ad for your company has a joke that could upset a religious group, while your PR stresses trust and inclusiveness. Launch is next week, and the agency says testing is done.

options.text: Ask a few colleagues from different backgrounds to review the ad and share their reactions.
Show the agency the concern, review their test results, and request a revised version.
Approve the ad because the agency has experience and the testing has been completed.
Let the ad launch as planned and prepare an apology statement in case people complain.

basic.situation: A list of 120 past donors needs thank-you calls by Friday. Your newest officer has no donor-call experience but has free time this week. You must assign the calls.

options.text: Split the list equally among all officers and ask each to report progress on Thursday afternoon.
Give the newer officer a small batch and a script, then read the call notes.
Email the full list to everyone and let the officers pick the donors they prefer to call.
Give all calls to the two experienced officers and assign the newer one to filing.

advanced.situation: One of your fundraising officers has missed her monthly pledge target for three months, although her donor calls sound warm. Teammates have started to notice, and you must address it.

options.text: Share the monthly ranking at the team meeting so peer pressure pushes her to improve.
Pair her with the top officer for a week so she can copy what works.
Go through her call records together, spot where pledges drop, and set one practice goal.
Lower her target for next month so she can reach it and regain her confidence.

basic.situation: You need contact details for twenty potential corporate donors on a prospect list. Some company websites show only a general phone line, and one director's email looks out of date.

options.text: Confirm each contact through the company's website or a short call, and log the source.
Take each contact from the company website and copy the general enquiry email shown there.
Fill the missing emails by copying the pattern of other staff addresses, then send the mailing.
Copy the first email or phone number found for each name through an online search.

advanced.situation: Donor records show total gifts rose 15% this year, but the number of donors fell. Your manager wants a recommendation for next year's focus by Friday.

options.text: Report the rise as good news and recommend repeating this year's campaigns at a larger scale.
Compare this year's donor retention rate with last year's and report the drop to your manager.
Break the totals down by gift size and donor group to find what drives the rise.
Delete lapsed donors from the dataset as inactive records, then forecast from the remaining donors.

basic.situation: Your manager gives you a brochure template to update for a charity run. While editing, you notice the event date in the text differs from the date in the manager's email.

options.text: Confirm the date from the venue booking, update the text, and tell your manager what changed.
Highlight the two dates in the draft and ask your manager which one is final.
Mark the brochure final with the template date so the printer can start on schedule.
Use the date from your manager's latest email and send the finished draft back.

advanced.situation: A corporate sponsor offers to fund an advertising campaign, but its slogan and images clash with the charity's gentle, family-focused tone. The sponsor wants an answer today.

options.text: Decline the offer politely today because the tone clashes, and keep the brand unchanged.
Take the funding but ask the designers to soften the colours and keep the sponsor's slogan.
Check the proposal against our brand guide and donor profile, then offer the sponsor specific changes.
Accept the campaign as offered because the funding covers the whole programme and sponsors expect visibility.

basic.situation: You are helping your supervisor draft a plan for a charity walk. She asks you to suggest ways to keep costs low while still attracting more participants.

options.text: Raise the registration fee to cover the costs, since participants usually accept a small increase.
Drop the marshals and first-aid post from the plan since few walkers will need them.
Ask local businesses to sponsor the route and give free water, which cuts the cost quickly.
Use last year's costs and turnout to choose a cheaper venue and invite groups who joined.

advanced.situation: Your organisation wants to double yearly donations within five years. Most income now comes from one annual gala, and your team of four must plan how to reach the goal.

options.text: Have the team ask every past donor for far larger gifts this year to reach the goal.
Set yearly targets by income source and build monthly giving to lessen reliance on the gala.
Plan a larger gala each year with a bigger venue and higher ticket and table prices.
Give each officer an equal yearly target and review who falls short at year end.

basic.situation: You are collecting attachments for a grant application due Friday. The funder requires the latest signed accounts, but the finance officer who holds them is on leave today.

options.text: Use last year's signed accounts, as the figures are similar and the format already matches.
Ask another finance colleague for the signed copy today and match it to the funder's checklist.
Hold the whole pack until the finance officer is back, then upload everything together to the portal.
Attach the unsigned draft accounts and tell the funder the signed copy will follow.

advanced.situation: Volunteers count cash from charity collection tins, and one volunteer both counts the cash and records it in the ledger. Your organisation has no written collection procedure.

options.text: Reconcile the ledger against bank statements at year end and raise any differences found.
Let the volunteer hold collections until the weekly count to reduce the number of bank trips.
Propose that two people count and sign each collection and someone else records it.
Ask the volunteer to photograph each count and send the photo to you before banking.

basic.situation: You are helping set up a charity bake sale at a community hall tomorrow. Your supervisor gave you RM300 for supplies and said to keep spending within it, but the printed banner costs RM350.

options.text: Buy the RM350 banner and pay the extra RM50 yourself, then claim it back next week.
Tell your supervisor the banner costs RM350 and wait for approval before buying any supplies today.
Look for a cheaper banner such as a volunteer-painted sign, and keep the RM300 for supplies.
Leave out the banner and spend the RM300 on boxes and cups for the cake sale.

advanced.situation: A reporter calls the day before a charity dinner asking how much it will raise. Final figures are unconfirmed, and the minister's office asked that arrival details stay private.

options.text: Give the reporter the target figure that sponsors have promised so the story shows strong support.
Ask the reporter to email the questions and reply once your manager has approved the answers.
Share the confirmed ticket numbers and the cause's aim, and promise the final total afterwards.
Tell the reporter the minister's arrival time so photographers can prepare, which helps coverage.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to suggest a deadline for scanning and archiving 3,000 old files. Two of your six team members will be on leave next week.

options.text: Time a sample batch, allow for the leave days, and propose a deadline with some buffer.
Propose next Friday and allow the team to shred paper originals as each batch is scanned.
Propose the shortest deadline that will impress the department head and ask staff to stay late.
Use the time a similar archiving project took last year and propose that deadline again.

advanced.situation: Two department heads each set annual goals that rely on the same shared admin team, and together the goals exceed its capacity. Both have asked for your view.

options.text: Accept both sets of goals and ask the team to cover the gap with overtime.
Show both heads the combined workload against capacity and help them rank goals by company priority.
Support whichever head asked first, since that goal was registered earlier on the planning calendar.
Suggest each head trim their own goals by the same percentage so neither is treated unfairly.

basic.situation: Staff often run out of printer paper before the monthly order arrives, and each department explains it differently. Your manager asks you to find out why.

options.text: Tell staff to borrow paper from other departments when theirs runs out to keep work moving.
Suggest raising the monthly order by a third so stock lasts until the next delivery.
Ask each department how much paper they use and compare their answers to the monthly order.
Check three months of paper orders and usage records to see when stock runs low.

advanced.situation: Management approved a new online procurement request procedure that changes approvals for 40 staff. In a trial, many staff still sent forms to the old email address. You must prepare them for the rollout.

options.text: Shred the old paper request files and forms so staff cannot return to the old route.
Fix confusing steps found in the trial, then run short hands-on sessions using real request examples.
Close the old email address on the start date so staff must use the new route.
Hold one briefing for all 40 staff and email a step-by-step guide for later reference.

basic.situation: You are drafting the weekly supplies report. Your sheet shows two more toner cartridges in stock than the storekeeper's list does, and the report is due this afternoon.

options.text: Use the storekeeper's list for the report and mention the two-cartridge difference in a footnote.
Recount the toner with the storekeeper, trace the difference, then report the confirmed figure.
Use your own sheet figure for the report because your records are the ones you checked.
Adjust your sheet so it matches the storekeeper's list, which keeps the report neat and consistent.

advanced.situation: While reviewing monthly reports from three clerks, you find one clerk's overtime totals run higher than the attendance records show. The other two clerks' reports are accurate.

options.text: Tell the department head the clerk is inflating overtime claims so payroll can stop paying them.
Hold a refresher for all three clerks on the reporting standard and keep this month's figures.
Trace the clerk's totals to attendance records for several months to find where the gap starts.
Amend the clerk's figures to match attendance records and remind the clerk to recheck.

basic.situation: You are helping train two new clerks on the courier booking procedure. Halfway through, one asks a question about the process that you are not sure how to answer.

options.text: Say you will confirm from the procedure manual, then give the answer after the break.
Answer from how colleagues usually book couriers and carry on with the next step.
Ask the trainee to note the question and ask your supervisor about it after the session.
Say the detail does not matter much and tell them to book couriers however suits them.

advanced.situation: Several staff still make errors on the expense claim procedure despite last month's training. Your manager asks you to redesign the training and show that it works.

options.text: Send the staff with the most mistakes to repeat the same training and track their attendance.
Replace the sessions with a reminder email and list staff with repeat errors for their appraisal.
Lengthen the sessions to cover the whole procedure in more depth and add a short quiz.
Find the steps behind most errors, rebuild the sessions around them, and compare error counts afterwards.

basic.situation: You are logging this month's stationery spending against a RM2,000 budget. A supplier invoice for RM450 arrives, but the price is higher than the quotation you hold.

options.text: Match the invoice to the quotation and purchase order, then query the gap with the supplier.
Hold the invoice in the tray until the supplier sends a revised copy, then log it.
Log the RM450 and hand the invoice to your manager to check the price.
Delay logging the invoice until next month so this month's total stays under the RM2,000 budget.

advanced.situation: Photocopier lease, courier and stationery costs have each risen about 10% this year. Finance asks you for cost-control proposals for the next three years' budgets.

options.text: Cut every budget line by ten percent across the board for the next three years.
Charge the rising costs to another department's budget so our yearly total looks steady.
Compare each cost with usage and contract terms, then target savings that protect core services.
Get three quotes for each service and move to the cheapest supplier next term.

basic.situation: At mid-morning, courier pickup is due at noon. Two departments have not yet handed in their parcels, and one parcel you have already collected has no address label.

options.text: Remind both departments of the noon cutoff and get the missing address from the parcel's sender.
Write the latest address from the courier file on the unlabelled parcel so it leaves today.
Let the courier leave with what is ready and ask departments to send the rest themselves.
Prepare the parcels you have and book the unlabelled one for tomorrow's pickup instead.

advanced.situation: The mailroom and the facilities team both claim the only storeroom for their incoming stock. Boxes are piling up in the corridor, and both team leaders have complained to you.

options.text: Give the storeroom to the busier team and find the other team shelving elsewhere.
Check what each team stores and how fast it moves, then propose agreed storeroom zones.
Throw out the oldest boxes in the corridor to clear space, as nobody has claimed them.
Alternate the storeroom between the teams each week so that each team gets equal access.

basic.situation: On your morning walk-round, you find the loading bay fire exit blocked by a delivery trolley. Drivers tell you there is nowhere else to park their trolleys.

options.text: Move the trolleys to the corridor beside the lift, where drivers can still reach them.
Clear the exit, tape out a trolley bay nearby, and record the finding in the checklist.
Clear the exit now and remind each driver to keep trolleys away from the fire exit.
Let drivers keep using the spot during deliveries, then tidy the trolleys away at day's end.

advanced.situation: You must set your department's safety goals for the quarter. Extinguisher servicing is due next month, three CCTV cameras are faulty, and your four technicians are also covering a tenant fit-out.

options.text: Carry extinguisher servicing into next quarter, since the units look fine and the fit-out earns rent.
Rank tasks by risk, put extinguisher servicing first, and fit deadlines to each technician's workload.
Set the deadlines from the contract expiry dates and fix the cameras as time allows.
Set the same quarter-end deadline for every task so the technicians can plan their own order.

basic.situation: Sales is moving twelve staff into an area planned for ten. Your supervisor asks you to draft the seating layout from the floor plan.

options.text: Draft ten seats, check exit routes and power points, and flag the two-seat shortfall.
Fit all twelve desks by narrowing the aisles a little, so every person gets a seat.
Measure the area, fit ten desks neatly, and leave the two extra staff to the supervisor.
Copy the layout of another department of twelve on the same floor, since it was approved.

advanced.situation: A tenant wants a new server room on your level. The contractor's plan places it beside the pantry's water pipes, and the tenant wants to start installing next week.

options.text: Keep the location but ask the contractor to add a leak tray and a water sensor.
Propose a site away from the pantry pipes, and show the tenant why on the layout.
Accept the contractor's plan since engineers drew it, and review the cooling after installation.
Keep the tenant's start date and move the room later if leaks or cooling problems appear.

basic.situation: You are helping teach new cleaners how to label and store cleaning chemicals. They nod along, but nobody has asked a question in twenty minutes.

options.text: Ask the whole group if they understand, and repeat the key rules slowly if anyone hesitates.
Have a few cleaners label and shelve a sample container, then give feedback on each step.
Hand out the written procedure and ask them to read it and sign the attendance sheet.
Finish all the slides on schedule, since their silence suggests they follow the steps.

advanced.situation: After two minor injuries during generator maintenance, you are asked to set the training standard for technicians. Each shift currently trains new people in its own way.

options.text: Keep each shift's own way of training, and add a safety reminder to the weekly roster.
Send the two injured technicians on a refresher course, since their own mistakes caused the incidents.
Write one procedure from the injury findings, set a practical sign-off test, and record who passes.
Copy the generator maker's manual into a handout and require every technician to read it.

basic.situation: You are preparing the monthly utilities report. The electricity figure is twice last month's, and the report is due with your manager this afternoon.

options.text: Send the report with a note that the electricity figure is higher and still being checked.
Replace the figure with the last three months' average, to match the usual trend.
Re-key the figure from the bill to check for a typing slip, then send the report.
Compare the bill with meter readings and last month's, and note the cause before sending it.

advanced.situation: You review a technician's weekly maintenance schedule before it goes to the building owner. It shows lift servicing completed, but the contractor's job sheet is not attached.

options.text: Accept the technician's word because past schedules were accurate, and file the sheet later.
Mark the lift servicing complete from the monthly plan, since it was due this week.
Request the signed job sheet from the technician and hold that line until it is confirmed.
Check the logbook in the lift machine room for a service entry, then send the schedule.

basic.situation: You track the RM4,000 monthly cleaning-supplies budget. By the 20th, RM3,600 is spent, and a supplier's bulk discount on a RM900 order ends this week.

options.text: Count the remaining stock and propose a smaller order of low items to the manager.
Hold the order until next month's budget opens, and watch the stock levels meanwhile.
Pay the RM900 from next month's budget line, since the stock is used next month anyway.
Split the order into two purchases of RM450 so each passes under the usual approval limit.

advanced.situation: Your chiller maintenance contract is RM120,000 for the year. The contractor now asks RM18,000 extra for a compressor repair outside the agreed scope, calling it urgent.

options.text: Approve the repair but negotiate the price down, since cooling failure would hurt the tenants.
Ask the contractor to list the repair as routine servicing so it fits the approved budget.
Check the contract scope against the fault report and quote before agreeing any extra cost.
Pay the RM18,000 from the contingency line and let the contractor start right away.

basic.situation: A delivery of light tubes and cleaning chemicals arrives while the store is crowded. The driver wants you to sign the delivery order and leave the boxes in the passage.

options.text: Count the boxes, note damage on the order, and shelve chemicals in their labelled area.
Count the boxes against the order and sign it, then leave shelving to the afternoon staff.
Sign the order and let the driver stack boxes wherever they fit, to keep deliveries moving.
Count the boxes, note damage on the order, and shelve them in the nearest free space.

advanced.situation: Clearing the lost-property room, you find forty umbrellas, some phones and wallets, and old office chairs, all unclaimed for over a year. Your manager asks you to clear the room.

options.text: List all items and hold everything another three months in case owners come back.
List all items, pass phones and wallets to security, and send the rest through approved disposal.
Bin everything this week, since a year is long enough and the room is needed.
Let staff take the umbrellas and chairs they want, and send the rest to security.

basic.situation: You are covering a routine building shift and need to follow the site's established visitor access procedure.

options.text: I record visitors after the busy period has passed.
I let familiar visitors enter while I finish another task.
I ask a colleague how they usually handle visitor entry.
I check the visitor procedure and apply its entry steps consistently.

advanced.situation: A high-risk public event is planned at your site, and you are asked to coordinate security arrangements with local emergency agencies.

options.text: I assign extra guards at the main entrance and brief them.
I request agency contacts and share the draft site plan with them.
I reuse the last event plan and send it to the guards.
I align site posts, contact points, and response routes with agency plans.

basic.situation: During a routine facility walk, you notice a side entrance is often left unsecured and your manager asks you to note risks.

options.text: I record the entrance issue and check the site's access procedure.
I prop the entrance open so staff can monitor it.
I mention the issue to a guard during the next shift.
I add the entrance to my notes for the weekly review.

advanced.situation: A review finds that flooding could disrupt access to your facility, and you are asked to assess its likely impact on security operations.

options.text: I review past incidents and list areas that could lose access.
I map affected access points and rate operational impacts using available records.
I focus on the lowest entrance and note that it may flood.
I assume the site can close and use the usual response plan.

basic.situation: A fire alarm sounds during a routine shift, and you are assigned to follow the site's response procedure.

options.text: I follow the alarm procedure and report the affected area to control.
I check the response card and carry out my assigned steps.
I wait for another guard to confirm the alarm is genuine.
I silence the alarm and finish my patrol route first.

advanced.situation: A serious incident disrupts normal site operations, and you are asked to help update the contingency plan for continued security coverage.

options.text: I extend the current roster and tell guards to stay alert.
I keep the existing plan and wait for a real incident.
I list likely disruptions and share them at the next planning meeting.
I identify essential posts, backup contacts, and workable coverage during disruption.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to review the site's visitor policy before helping with the next shift handover.

options.text: I check the policy sections that cover visitors and access.
I reuse the previous handover notes as the visitor guidance.
I read the policy and note the entry steps for handover.
I ask the outgoing guard what the policy usually requires.

advanced.situation: A policy review finds that staff report threats through different channels, and you are asked to draft a clearer reporting procedure.

options.text: I tell staff to report threats to their nearest manager.
I define one reporting route, clear roles, and escalation points for review.
I ask each team to keep using its preferred reporting channel.
I propose a shared reporting channel and circulate it for feedback.

basic.situation: A new guard joins your shift and asks how to check visitor passes under the site's security rules.

options.text: I explain each pass step and invite questions before the guard handles visitors.
I provide written rules and ask the guard to read them during a quiet period.
I demonstrate pass checks, then let the guard practise with a sample visitor.
I ask the guard to watch a colleague, then review pass checks against site rules.

advanced.situation: You are reviewing guard performance after several shifts showed uneven visitor checks, and your manager asks for a practical improvement.

options.text: I remind the team to focus on visitor checks and discuss examples from recent shifts.
I assign the busiest entrance to an experienced guard and monitor checks across shifts.
I review observed checks and coach guards on the specific gaps found during shifts.
I compare shift notes, discuss recurring concerns, and agree practical changes with the team.

basic.situation: A visitor reports a missing bag at reception, and your manager asks you to complete an incident report using the available details.

options.text: I record the visitor's account, time, location, and known follow-up steps.
I ask the visitor for details and fill in the incident form.
I write that a bag went missing near reception.
I wait until the shift ends to remember the details.

advanced.situation: A review of security spending shows rising equipment costs, and you are asked to report findings for the next budget discussion.

options.text: I assess newer purchases against service needs before suggesting any budget changes.
I adapt last year's budget notes and check which figures need updating.
I compare costs with usage and service needs, then summarise options.
I list the rising costs and ask the manager what to present.

basic.situation: Your monthly IT expense report is due to finance tomorrow. The cloud hosting invoice is RM4,000 above the budget line and shows one lump total.

options.text: Report the RM4,000 variance on time and ask the vendor for a usage breakdown.
Move RM4,000 to the training line, which has spare funds, so hosting shows on budget.
Trace the RM4,000 rise in usage logs, stop any idle servers, and report the variance.
Hold the report until the vendor confirms the invoice is final, then submit.

advanced.situation: Your department's annual budget has been cut by 15%. Three teams each say their project is essential, and you must set a spending rule for them before the quarter starts.
