Ask about a task, hear an example, and share notes with the manager.

advanced.situation: New hires make inconsistent room checks, and experienced staff give different instructions. You are asked to improve team training and performance expectations.

options.text: Ask experienced staff to explain their own methods during the next shift briefing.
Tell new hires to follow whichever experienced colleague is available for their shift.
Define observable room-check standards, train staff with examples, and review performance against them.
Prepare a room-check demonstration and invite staff to practise the sequence together.

basic.situation: You notice a new ward clerk repeatedly leaves patient files on another desk during a busy shift.

options.text: Show the clerk where each file belongs and explain how to verify placement.
Move files aside, then ask the clerk to sort them using the unit guide.
Ask the clerk to follow the filing guide and pause for a quick check.
Review the filing steps with the clerk, then check several files together.

advanced.situation: Two department heads disagree over a nurse manager's performance review, and the review affects a pending transfer.

options.text: Discuss the disagreement with both heads and suggest a later review.
Compare the review with agreed unit criteria and ask each head for specific examples.
Use the latest complaints as the main basis for the review.
Accept the senior head's assessment to keep the transfer process moving.

basic.situation: A clinic's diagnostic queue grows while several inpatient beds appear unused on your daily ward report.

options.text: Check today's service and bed figures with unit teams, then report the mismatch.
Share the figures with your manager and ask whether capacity needs review.
Compare the queue and bed figures across recent daily reports before raising concern.
Coordinate with unit teams before directing patients toward beds shown as open.

advanced.situation: A proposed imaging service expansion could ease referrals, but facility data show uneven demand and rising operating costs.

options.text: Recommend expansion based on the referral backlog and projected demand.
Use last year's busiest month to justify adding imaging capacity.
Model demand, staffing, bed use, and costs across options before recommending expansion.
Share the utilization trends with planning colleagues for their assessment.

basic.situation: Your clinic is starting a health screening session, and you are assigned to coordinate staff and patient flow.

options.text: Use the approved session plan to coordinate staff roles and patient flow.
Set up the screening tables and let staff choose their stations based on demand.
Check the staff roster with the nurse leading the session before patients arrive.
Ask available staff to cover whichever station looks busiest during setup.

advanced.situation: Community partners want a rehabilitation program, but transport limits attendance and the clinic has few available staff.

options.text: Start with the clinic's usual schedule and invite partners to refer eligible community members.
Shape rollout around partner input, staff capacity, transport, and attendance measures.
Announce a full launch date to encourage early interest across the community.
Agree a small pilot with partners and review attendance before considering wider rollout.

basic.situation: Your monthly report shows fewer completed referrals than planned, and management asks for an update before its meeting.

options.text: Check referral records, note the shortfall, likely cause, and next steps.
Report the planned and completed totals from the dashboard, noting the dates covered.
Ask the referral team whether the lower total seems accurate.
Use last month's report to fill in missing referral figures.

advanced.situation: Board members request a service expansion update, while department heads report conflicting staffing and facility constraints.

options.text: Present the expansion target and ask department heads to resolve constraints after the board meeting.
Summarize department views and flag differences for discussion before the board decides.
Reconcile department inputs, outline constraints and options, then brief the board through agreed channels.
Use the largest staffing estimate to keep the proposed expansion plan moving.

basic.situation: A newly hired clinic assistant joins your unit, and you are helping with the first orientation session.

options.text: Use the approved orientation checklist and demonstrate the assistant's core duties.
Ask a colleague to explain the routine, then check key steps together.
Walk through the schedule, answer questions, and invite the assistant to practise core tasks.
Give the assistant the unit handbook and identify sections to review between tasks.

advanced.situation: A community education session on rehabilitation draws mixed literacy levels, and several participants have limited mobility.

options.text: Present the standard slides clearly and leave time for questions.
Adapt the materials and activities for access, literacy, and participant practice.
Print the slides in large type for everyone to follow.
Ask participants to repeat the key points before the session ends.

basic.situation: You are updating a unit roster and notice the proposed schedule exceeds available staff hours for the coming week.

options.text: Send the draft roster to your manager for a quick review before posting.
Match assignments to workload and staff hours, then flag uncovered shifts.
Keep the current roster and ask staff to swap shifts before confirming coverage.
Add overtime to the roster so every shift appears covered for now.

advanced.situation: A new patient-record system is proposed during budget planning, but staff workflows and service costs remain uncertain.

options.text: Ask department leads to estimate costs, identify workflow concerns, and report training needs.
Approve the purchase from the technology budget to secure availability.
Compare workflow, training, data needs, and costs before proposing phased implementation.
Include the vendor estimate in the budget and plan training later.

basic.situation: You are helping frame a small water-quality study, and the team needs a clear sequence of steps to examine its main question.

options.text: I would outline stages, checks, owners, and a review point for guidance.
I would map the sample steps against the question and note gaps.
I would reuse last month's sequence to save setup time.
I would list the question, sample steps, and a checkpoint for review.

advanced.situation: Early tests disagree, and the next sampling phase is costly. You need to guide the team toward a defensible research sequence.

options.text: I would keep the current sequence and report delays at the next review.
I would extend the current trial and review its results with the team.
I would stage the work, compare methods, and set decision gates across phases.

basic.situation: A routine equipment check is due, and a colleague asks which existing procedure to follow for the laboratory record.

options.text: I would ask a colleague which checks they usually record.
I would copy the previous entries and update the equipment date.
I would check the current procedure and record each required inspection.
I would use the last completed record as a guide for today's check.

advanced.situation: Your unit is considering a new instrument that changes how samples are handled. Staff need a workable standard before a pilot begins.

options.text: I would circulate the supplier guide and ask staff to flag questions.
I would adapt the supplier guide and brief staff before the pilot.
I would let each shift choose a method and compare their records later.
I would draft handling steps, pilot them, and capture staff feedback for revision.

basic.situation: You are drafting a proposal section for a small field study, and the project lead has shared the scope and expected deliverables.

options.text: I would reuse a past proposal section and replace the project name.
I would turn the scope into deliverables, dates, and a short rationale.
I would summarise the scope and list the main study activities.
I would draft the study rationale and ask the lead to fill gaps.

advanced.situation: A client questions whether your proposed sampling plan can answer their concern within the budget. You need to present the findings and clarify the scope.

options.text: I would show the evidence, explain trade-offs, and confirm scope before revising.
I would defend the current plan using the strongest result from testing.
I would present the findings and offer a lower-cost sampling alternative.

basic.situation: You are helping prepare a goal-setting meeting, and several planned field visits have expenses that are not yet entered in the budget tracker.

options.text: I would enter the known costs and share the updated tracker.
I would leave the missing visits out and focus on the planned goals.
I would reconcile receipts, flag missing entries, and bring totals to the meeting.
I would estimate the missing costs from the previous field visits.

advanced.situation: Management asks you to turn a broad research priority into annual goals while a major equipment request competes with ongoing project costs.

options.text: I would fund the equipment request first and adjust goals afterward.
I would list possible goals and ask project leads for cost estimates.
I would rank goals by expected impact, cost them, and show funding trade-offs.
I would draft measurable goals and compare them with the current budget.

basic.situation: You are helping shortlist applicants for a technician role, and the hiring panel has agreed on the essential laboratory skills.

options.text: I would shortlist applicants with relevant laboratory experience and qualifications.
I would pass along the first applications that meet the basic requirements.
I would favour applicants from laboratories similar to our own.
I would compare each application against the agreed skills and record evidence.

advanced.situation: Two experienced researchers are missing project milestones, and their work overlaps. You need to review performance and support the team's development.

options.text: I would review milestones, clarify ownership, and agree support with each researcher.
I would shift the delayed tasks to the researcher with more availability.
I would meet both researchers and discuss their recent project progress.
I would note the missed milestones for the next team review.

basic.situation: At a project meeting, a regulator asks what technical assistance the field team needs before the next sampling round.

options.text: I would take notes on the request and share them with the team.
I would ask the field lead to explain the team's current support needs.
I would note the request, clarify its scope, and record the agreed follow-up.
I would tell the regulator the team can manage with its current support.

advanced.situation: At a professional meeting, participants question how your team's findings could inform a regional project. You are presenting the results and coordinating technical discussion.

options.text: I would present the findings, explain their limits, and invite specific technical questions.
I would emphasise the strongest result to keep the discussion focused.
I would present the main results and describe the team's next research step.
I would share the headline result and offer to send the slides later.

basic.situation: You are helping draft a protocol section for a routine study visit, and the coordinator asks you to check how samples and visit data will be collected.

options.text: I would copy the collection steps from a similar study protocol.
I would list each collection step and check it against the visit schedule.
I would summarise the sample steps and ask the coordinator to review them.
I would paste the old sample instructions into the new draft.

advanced.situation: A proposed study adds home visits and several specimen types. You are reviewing the protocol for collection risks and gaps in data management.

options.text: I would accept the draft and track collection issues after enrolment begins.
I would compare the draft with a previous study using home visits.
I would review the new collection steps and note questions for the team.
I would map visits to specimens, data fields, and risks, then flag gaps for review.

basic.situation: You are preparing a simple recruitment flyer, and the study team has provided approved details about whom to contact and how to learn more.

options.text: I would use the approved study summary and add the clinic contact details.
I would draft clear study details and check the contact route with the team.
I would reuse the previous flyer and change the clinic name.
I would adapt an older flyer and update its study title and dates.

advanced.situation: Two clinics have limited appointment space, and a study visit requires both a procedure room and specific supplies. You are coordinating the schedule.

options.text: I would send participants the first available dates from both clinics.
I would ask each clinic for open slots and arrange visits around them.
I would match visit slots to room capacity, supplies, and each site's availability.
I would reserve the earliest openings and adjust the supply setup later.

basic.situation: A potential participant asks about a study visit while you help with screening and consent documentation under the coordinator's guidance.

options.text: I would answer from the study summary and complete the interview notes.
I would reassure them that the visit is routine and finish the form.
I would walk through the approved information and note their response.
I would explain the approved visit details and document their questions for review.

advanced.situation: A candidate's records leave one eligibility detail unclear, and the consent form has a correction. You are checking enrolment documentation before the visit.

options.text: I would pause enrolment, verify eligibility, and resolve the consent correction with the investigator.
I would file the form as complete and update it after the visit.
I would proceed with the visit and confirm the detail at the appointment.
I would flag the unclear detail and ask the investigator to review the form.

basic.situation: You are helping monitor routine study visits and notice one worksheet is missing a required date in the study file.

options.text: I would flag the worksheet and ask the coordinator how to complete it.
I would add a date based on the visit schedule to close the gap.
I would check the source record and document the missing date through the study process.
I would leave the worksheet in the file and mention it at the next review.

advanced.situation: During audit preparation, you find several visits used an outdated worksheet. The investigator asks you to help resolve the protocol documentation issue.

options.text: I would replace the worksheets in the file with the current version.
I would list the affected visits and share them with the investigator.
I would trace affected visits, preserve records, and raise a documented resolution plan.
I would remove outdated worksheets before the audit file is reviewed.

basic.situation: You are updating the study tracker after a participant withdraws, and the coordinator asks you to record the reason and contact attempts.

options.text: I would mark the participant inactive and close the tracker entry.
I would record the stated reason, dated contact attempts, and status in the tracker.
I would mark the participant withdrawn and summarise the last call.
I would update the withdrawal status and note the reason given.

advanced.situation: The final study dataset shows different dropout patterns across sites. You are interpreting results and preparing the report for the study team.

options.text: I would compare site patterns, review dropout records, and note report limits.
I would report the overall result and leave site differences for later.
I would combine sites and report the overall dropout rate first.
I would summarise site differences and discuss their impact with the study team.

basic.situation: A participant reports a new side effect during a follow-up call. You are recording the details and need to coordinate with the investigator about reporting.

options.text: I would note the side effect and alert the investigator for guidance.
I would add the symptom to the visit notes for the next review.
I would record details and contact the investigator through study channels.
I would reassure the participant and mention the symptom at the next visit.

advanced.situation: A sponsor requests a site update while one laboratory result is pending and a specimen shipment needs coordination. You are preparing the study team's response.

options.text: I would verify the result, confirm shipment details, and update the sponsor.
I would share the known status and tell the sponsor when to expect an update.
I would report that the site is on track and follow up later.
I would send the last site summary and arrange shipment with the laboratory.

basic.situation: You collect samples at three stream sites and must run the assigned chemical tests before the afternoon handover.

options.text: Rinse the kit between sites and repeat any reading that looks unusual.
Pool nearby bottles, run one test, and log the average for that site.

Keep bottles separate, follow the sampling sequence, and record times, locations, and readings.

advanced.situation: A contractor challenges your monitoring results after a discharge alert, and several field teams need one consistent sampling method.

options.text: Use the current method across teams and brief them on the discharge alert.
Share a simple checklist and ask each team to use its familiar sampling routine.
Adopt the contractor's method for the next round and compare the readings afterward.
Set shared sampling steps, train teams, and compare trial results before issuing the protocol.

basic.situation: A senior engineer asks you to run a simple runoff model for a small catchment before a routine drainage meeting.

options.text: Enter the catchment inputs, run the model, and save the output for review.

Reuse last month's inputs and send the new output to the meeting folder.
Adjust rainfall until the model resembles the previous report, then save the file.

advanced.situation: A proposed drainage upgrade shifts flood peaks toward a nearby village in your model, but the rainfall inputs are uncertain.

options.text: Test a range of rainfall inputs, compare peak flows, and map where risks shift.
Use the highest rainfall figure and recommend widening every modeled channel section.
Show the preferred run and note that rainfall inputs remain uncertain in the report.
Run a second rainfall case and share both outputs with the project team.

basic.situation: Your team needs the latest stream health records for a routine review, and several monitoring sheets have arrived from the field.

options.text: Scan the sheets into one folder and label it with the review month.
Copy the highest readings into the summary and set aside the field sheets.
File the sheets by collection date and note which sites each one covers.
Check each sheet for site and date, then log gaps before filing the records.

advanced.situation: A downstream community reports unusual water colour near a permitted discharge, and your team must investigate the concern and document findings.

options.text: Ask the operator for its latest results and include them in the case file.
Review permit records, compare upstream and downstream samples, and document the evidence trail.
Visit the downstream site, take a sample, and add notes to the file.
Close the case using the permit's listed discharge limits and file the complaint.

basic.situation: You are gathering information for a watershed health assessment, and a recent field visit noted bare soil beside a tributary.

options.text: Add the visit note to the general folder for the next assessment meeting.
Map the bare area, note nearby drainage, and flag it for erosion review.
Remove the note from the draft map until the site is revisited.
Mark the bare area on the map and add the field visit date.

advanced.situation: Two dry-season months have strained supply, while a proposed restoration area could also protect water quality and reduce runoff.

options.text: Compare supply needs, conservation gains, and water quality risks before ranking actions.
Commit the whole budget to the largest restoration area before the next dry season.
Prioritize restoration where land access is easiest and share the map with planners.
Map candidate areas and ask the planning team which sites seem practical.

basic.situation: You are compiling GIS data for a small stream project, and two GPS points appear to fall on the wrong bank.

options.text: Check the coordinate layer and field notes, then flag both points for verification.
Move both points to the nearest road and export the map for the team.
Keep both points and add a note that their locations need field review.
Use the older map coordinates and note the difference in the project folder.

advanced.situation: A detention facility design reduces modeled flooding, but its higher construction cost competes with several smaller watershed improvements.

options.text: Recommend the facility because its modeled flood reduction is the largest.
Compare lifecycle costs and expected benefits across the facility and smaller alternatives.
List construction costs and flood reductions for the main options in a table.
Use the smallest estimate for each alternative to keep the comparison manageable.

basic.situation: Your team is preparing a brochure about a river monitoring programme, and nearby residents ask what the sampling visits involve.

options.text: Describe the visit schedule and list the contact point for resident questions.
Promise residents that the programme will improve the river within a month.
Reuse last year's brochure and add this season's meeting date.
Explain the sampling purpose, visit routine, and how residents can share observations.

advanced.situation: A village and a nearby facility both seek dry-season supply, and your team is developing a community water programme.

options.text: Map demand, discuss shared constraints with both parties, and record agreed next steps.
Draft a supply schedule around the facility's request and circulate it to residents.
Offer the village the full allocation before the facility's review meeting.
Collect each party's preferred schedule and summarize the differences for your team.

basic.situation: A late van brings sacks of incoming mail just as your section starts preparing outgoing items for the evening dispatch.

options.text: Put all late sacks aside and finish outgoing items before the dispatch cutoff.
Ask one nearby section to take the late sacks while you finish outgoing mail.
Sort the late sacks by route and fit them into the current processing sequence.
Check dispatch priorities, assign available staff, and track both mail streams to cutoff.

advanced.situation: Two nearby postal facilities report backlogs after a vehicle disruption, while your facility still has outgoing mail to process.

options.text: Send spare staff to the busier facility and keep your outgoing work moving.
Move all available staff to the largest backlog and postpone local dispatch work.
Compare backlogs and dispatch needs, then coordinate staff support across both facilities.
Ask each facility for its backlog total and relay the figures to your manager.

basic.situation: You are drafting next week's counter roster, and two staff members have requested the same Friday leave day.

options.text: Check expected counter demand, draft cover for Friday, and send the roster for review.
Give both staff the day off and ask colleagues to manage the counter together.
Draft the roster around usual demand and flag the overlapping requests for review.
Approve the earlier request and leave the counter short for that shift.

advanced.situation: A payroll review finds several clock-ins missing after shift swaps, and the next roster must still cover a busy month-end period.

options.text: Compare attendance records with approved swaps, resolve discrepancies, and update the roster.
Mark uncertain entries for follow-up and keep the month-end coverage plan unchanged.
Use the published roster for payroll and list the missing clock-ins separately.
Reconstruct each shift from staff notes and submit the payroll totals today.

basic.situation: You are helping interview applicants for a counter role, and one candidate has strong customer examples but little postal experience.

options.text: Choose the applicant with the longest postal work history for the shortlist.
Write down the candidate's examples and send your notes to the hiring lead.
Score the candidate against the role criteria and note relevant examples from the interview.
Recommend the candidate because customer examples sound more useful than postal experience.

advanced.situation: Several supervisors use different measures when evaluating counter staff, and the annual review cycle begins next month.

options.text: Collect the existing measures and circulate them as examples for supervisors.
Use the highest current measure for every role and publish it as the standard.
Set role-based measures, explain evidence expectations, and guide supervisors through sample reviews.
Ask supervisors to submit their preferred measures before the review cycle starts.

basic.situation: Your manager asks for a weekly activity summary, and one delivery count differs between the shift log and the draft report.

options.text: Check the shift log with the relevant clerk, then update the count and report.
Use the larger count and submit the summary before the weekly deadline.
Use the draft count and mention that it differs from the shift log.
Include both counts in a note and submit the summary on schedule.

advanced.situation: Monthly summaries from several postal sections use different labels for delayed items, making the manager's service comparison difficult.

options.text: Replace each section's labels with the largest delay category before comparing totals.
Define shared labels, give sections examples, and check a sample of submitted summaries.
Publish each section's figures as supplied and explain the label differences in a note.
Combine similar labels in the final report and retain each section's original sheet.

basic.situation: A staff representative disputes a weekend shift change, and your manager asks you to attend the discussion and take notes.

options.text: Tell staff the change will stand and record their concerns for the manager.
Note the representative's concerns and ask the manager how to respond afterward.
Listen to both sides, record proposals, and check disputed details with the manager.
Suggest moving the change back one week so staff can adjust their plans.

advanced.situation: Talks over repeated weekend coverage have stalled, and both sides bring different records of staff availability to the meeting.

options.text: Compare both records, clarify shared facts, and explore coverage options with each side.
Summarize both lists and send them to the manager before further talks.
Set the weekend roster from the management list and document objections afterward.
Use management's availability list as the basis and ask staff to respond later.

basic.situation: A customer says a tracked parcel has not arrived, and the counter queue is growing while you check the complaint details.

options.text: Offer a replacement service and record the customer's tracking number afterward.
Take the tracking number and tell the customer the delivery team can review it.
Ask the customer to return tomorrow when the queue is shorter.
Check the tracking status, explain the next step, and record the complaint details.

advanced.situation: Several customers report parcels delayed on the same route, and one customer is upset because a time-sensitive item is involved.

options.text: Check affected tracking records, explain available updates, and flag the common route pattern.
Tell customers the route is under review and promise delivery by tomorrow.
Record each complaint and send the route details to the operations team.
Apologize for the delay and ask each customer to submit a separate enquiry.

basic.situation: You are updating the rental register after several unit viewings and one signed tenancy agreement.

options.text: Ask the agent to send a weekly summary before changing the register.
Record each confirmed rental, date, and deposit against the unit file.
Copy last month's availability list and add today's new enquiries.
Update the viewing and rental log after checking the signed tenancy papers.

advanced.situation: An owner asks you to negotiate a management contract with disputed fees, response times, and reporting duties.

options.text: Compare the proposed fee, service levels, and exit terms against owner priorities.
Accept the vendor's template, then clarify any disputed clauses at renewal.
Ask the board chair to settle every clause before drafting changes.
Negotiate measurable response times and reporting duties, recording agreed exceptions clearly.

basic.situation: During your routine grounds inspection, you notice a loose rail beside a busy stairway.

options.text: Photograph the rail, log its location, and flag it for maintenance review.
Mention the rail at next week's routine handover after checking it again.
Enter the rail in the maintenance book and notify the facilities lead.
Tell the cleaner about the rail and ask them to watch the area.

advanced.situation: Three contractors submit bids for a repair, but their scopes, access assumptions, and prices differ.

options.text: Choose the lowest quote and ask the contractor to confirm the schedule.
Score bids against the same scope, timelines, safety steps, and itemized costs.
Check exclusions and site access assumptions before recommending a balanced bid.
Send the three totals to owners and ask which contractor they prefer.

basic.situation: A resident reports late-night noise from a nearby unit and asks you to address it.

options.text: Call the neighbor and ask what happened before updating the complaint log.
Listen to the resident, check the house rules, and log the noise complaint.
Check the time and unit details, then arrange a calm follow-up.
Tell the resident to contact security next time and close the entry.

advanced.situation: Two owners dispute responsibility for recurring water seepage, and the committee asks for a recommendation.

options.text: Recommend a practical settlement based on past cases and shared costs.
Review the documented concerns and relevant house rules before the committee discussion.
Draft a neutral issue summary and list questions needing legal advice.
Tell each owner the committee will decide after hearing both accounts.

basic.situation: Your building's routine fire inspection is approaching, and you need to confirm the agency visit details.

options.text: Email the building contact and file the reply with the safety records.
Ask the security desk whether an agency notice arrived during the morning shift.
Call the fire department to confirm the scheduled inspection window for your block.
Wait for the next visit and mention any missed notice then.

advanced.situation: You are preparing a rental advertisement with an eligibility statement that may exclude some interested applicants.

options.text: Ask legal counsel to identify any wording that could create unequal access.
Review the rental advertisement draft against the approved eligibility and property details.
Publish the current draft and collect feedback from prospective tenants.
Compare the wording with recent ads and flag unclear eligibility claims.

basic.situation: Several residents have paid monthly assessments, and you are updating the collection records.

options.text: Update the collection sheet from bank entries and flag unclear payments.
Send a polite reminder to residents whose monthly fee remains unpaid.
Match incoming assessment payments to unit accounts and note overdue balances.
Estimate the shortfall from last month's collection rate for the report.

advanced.situation: Repair costs have risen, and owners need a revised property budget with clear explanations for major changes.

options.text: Compare actual spending with approved categories and explain key variances to owners.
Carry forward last year's budget and adjust each line by inflation.
Ask the treasurer to choose a target total before preparing options.
Separate recurring costs from one-off repairs before revising the annual property forecast.

basic.situation: You are helping arrange routine maintenance visits across several occupied units next week.

options.text: Group the routine tasks by building and share a draft weekly schedule.
Check the maintenance calendar and confirm the plumber's access time with residents.
Book the first open slot and notify the affected units by message.
Ask the technician which day suits them, then update the noticeboard.

advanced.situation: A major repair project is behind schedule, and residents need an accurate update on access and expected work.

options.text: Ask the site lead for a new completion date before updating owners.
Compare reported progress with the agreed scope and raise schedule risks early.
Keep the original completion notice while the contractor changes the sequence.
Track project milestones, access needs, and resident notices in one operations update.

basic.situation: Your agency is starting a local service, and you are asked to introduce it to a nearby residents' group.

options.text: Forward last year's invitation to the old community contact list.
Share the program leaflet and ask which community meeting welcomes visitors.
Ask your supervisor for the approved contact and meeting details first.
Send a brief email explaining the service and invite a reply.

advanced.situation: Several agencies report gaps in referrals, and you are helping coordinate shared service standards.

options.text: Map each agency's referral role and agree shared response targets at a joint meeting.
Write a joint referral guide with named contacts and a review date.
Reuse the old referral list and share it at the next meeting.
Ask the agencies to send updates when a service gap appears.

basic.situation: A volunteer attended training, and you are updating the agency's training records.

options.text: Use last month's attendance totals to fill the blank record.
Update a volunteer's training record after checking the attendance sheet.
Copy the session date into the shared training log before filing attendance.
Ask the trainer to confirm a missing signature before marking completion.

advanced.situation: Program teams submit budget figures in different formats, making the board's financial report hard to compare.

options.text: Define standard budget fields and monthly checks so teams report costs consistently.
Compare spending categories across programs and flag gaps for finance review.
Keep each team's spreadsheet and combine totals before the board report.
Replace the current form with a simple template and ask teams to use it.

basic.situation: A client asks for help finding support, and you need to make an appropriate referral.

options.text: Give the client the agency directory and explain how to request an appointment.
Ask about immediate needs, confirm consent, and match an eligible referral.
Send the client to the nearest provider based on their first request.
Check consent and eligibility before connecting the client with a service.

advanced.situation: A client has raised repeated complaints about service access and wants a clear resolution plan.

options.text: Offer a meeting with the case worker and record the client's requested outcome.
Ask the client to restate the issue, then route it to the appropriate service.
Review complaint history, identify risks, and agree a follow-up plan with the client.
Use the response script and send the client clear appeal steps.

basic.situation: Your team is gathering information about unmet needs from visitors to a local service.

options.text: Collect short survey responses at the food pantry about unmet service needs.
Ask each visitor the same needs question and record responses by service.
Ask visitors which service they used and enter answers in the tally sheet.
Use the number of forms returned to estimate which service is most needed.

advanced.situation: Staff training feedback is mixed, and managers want evidence before deciding whether to change the next session.

options.text: Compare attendance and quiz results against the training objectives before reporting.
Repeat last quarter's training format and update the slides with new examples.
Ask participants whether the session was useful and share their comments.
Set learning goals, collect pre and post feedback, and adjust the next staff training.

basic.situation: An applicant's eligibility question falls near a gap in the current intake checklist.

options.text: Check the current eligibility checklist, then explain the matching application steps.
Use the approved form and note any question the applicant raises.
Change the eligibility steps to match what applicants say is easiest.
Ask a colleague to confirm the procedure when a case detail is unclear.

advanced.situation: The board has set new service objectives, and staff report inconsistent intake handoffs between programs.

options.text: Ask the director to decide each intake question before drafting guidance.
Change the eligibility steps to match what applicants say is easiest.
Compare the proposed intake steps with board objectives and map clear staff responsibilities.
Reuse the current workflow and add a checklist for missing documents.

basic.situation: A volunteer role is vacant, and you are helping review applications under the coordinator's guidance.

options.text: Forward all applications to the coordinator and ask which candidates to contact.
Offer the role to the first available applicant so the vacant shift can be covered.
Review volunteer applications and flag candidates who meet the posted role needs.
Invite a suitable applicant to an interview after checking the shared calendar.

advanced.situation: Staff ask how a program requirement applies to two unusual cases, and current written guidance is unclear.

options.text: Tell staff to follow the existing checklist until a formal answer arrives.
Reconcile agency guidance with policy text and explain the implications across affected programs.
Apply the same interpretation to every case to keep staff aligned.
Write a short FAQ showing the relevant rule and examples for common cases.

basic.situation: You are drafting shelter procedures for a community hall ahead of monsoon season. Your lead asks for a usable first draft by Friday.

options.text: Copy a nearby district's plan and send it as your site's procedure.
Reuse last year's evacuation checklist and update the location names before sharing it.
Draft shelter steps from the existing template, then ask your lead to review them.
Map each hazard to an action, contact, and handoff in the draft procedure.

advanced.situation: A recent exercise exposed confusion about who alerts the clinic during a flood. You are asked to propose a procedure update before the next exercise.

options.text: Revise the alert sequence to name the trigger, caller, recipient, and backup contact.
Keep the current sequence and brief staff to use better judgment next time.
Ask the exercise lead to write a revised sequence for the plan.
Add a reminder to contact the clinic during the next flood response.

basic.situation: You are checking a local emergency centre's radios before a scheduled drill. One unit will not hold a charge, and the equipment log is on your clipboard.

options.text: Swap in a nearby unit and note the change after the inspection.
Mark the radio operational because it worked during the last exercise.
Mark the radio as faulty and continue checking the remaining equipment.
Record the failed charge, test the spare, and tell your lead before the drill.

advanced.situation: After a flash flood, road closures affect two districts and a clinic reports damage. You are compiling assessments for the multi-agency response briefing.

options.text: Compare agency reports by location, flag conflicts, and circulate a shared damage summary.
Ask the clinic and district teams to confirm their figures before circulation.
Forward each agency's damage figures to the response group as they arrive.
Use the clinic's first estimate as the total damage figure for both districts.

basic.situation: You are helping prepare a community notice about the nearest flood shelter. The address has changed, and your supervisor asks you to distribute the updated information.

options.text: Keep distributing the old notice until printed copies run out.
Check the new address against the shelter contact, then distribute the notice.
Tell residents the shelter location will be confirmed at the next briefing.
Replace the old address and share the notice through the usual channels.

advanced.situation: A residents' group asks you to explain how its long-term flood plan should connect with district arrangements. You have twenty minutes and varied familiarity in the room.

options.text: Present a standard evacuation leaflet as the group's long-term planning guide.
Walk through the district plan and invite questions at the end.
Hand out the district plan and ask residents to read it later.
Use a simple map to show shared contacts, warning links, and plan handoffs.

basic.situation: You are updating resource materials for the district flood plan. The contact list has two different clinic numbers, and the annual review is due tomorrow.

options.text: Keep both numbers in the list and add a note about the mismatch.
Check the clinic number with its liaison and update the shared contact list.
Use the number on the latest clinic email and flag it for review.
Choose the number printed most often in the old plan materials.

advanced.situation: A grant-funded siren project is behind schedule after a supplier delay. The next progress report is due soon, and community representatives expect an update.

options.text: Show the project as on track because the grant funds remain available.
Send the original timeline with a short note that installation is pending.
Report the delay, revised milestones, spending to date, and its effect on coverage.
Ask the supplier for a revised date before preparing the grant update.

basic.situation: You attend an emergency management workshop where a speaker describes new guidance for shelter planning. Your team maintains the local response plan.

options.text: Write down the shelter guidance and file the notes with workshop materials.
Keep using the current plan because no formal notice was issued at the workshop.
Ask an attendee to summarize the shelter guidance after the workshop.
Record the guidance, note its source, and share it with your plan lead.

advanced.situation: During an annual plan review, you find a local shelter procedure that conflicts with a newly circulated municipal instruction. You are asked to check compliance.

options.text: Compare the instruction with the procedure, document the conflict, and draft a focused revision.
Flag the conflict for the plan lead and summarize the affected section for review.
Replace the shelter procedure with the municipal instruction's wording, then record the update.
Keep the procedure unchanged because staff already know the established shelter routine.

basic.situation: A storm warning prompts the district to open a public shelter. You are assigned to help prepare the entrance and check the opening supplies.

options.text: Arrange the supplies, check entrance access, and tell the shelter lead when ready.
Use last season's opening list and leave the new checklist for later.
Open the entrance while another worker checks the supplies nearby.
Follow the opening checklist, confirm access arrangements, and report any missing supplies.

advanced.situation: An evacuation order covers a care home and nearby homes. You are coordinating shelter arrivals, including residents who need mobility assistance, across two receiving sites.

options.text: Ask both shelter leads to confirm available spaces before routing the arriving groups.
Route care home residents to the larger site and update both shelter teams.
Keep arrivals together at the first site while pending transport requests settle.
Match arrivals to capacity and mobility support, then share assignments with both teams.

basic.situation: A family asks to book a cremation next week, but your schedule shows a tentative service at the same time. You are handling bookings with guidance.

options.text: Check the tentative booking, confirm the family's preferred window, and update the schedule.
Offer the family the next open time and note their first choice.
Hold the requested time while you check with the scheduling lead.
Book the requested time and move the tentative service to another day.

advanced.situation: Monthly sales reports show fewer families choosing a recently added memorial service. You are asked to set a financial goal for the next quarter.

options.text: Set a quarterly revenue target using recent booking figures as a reference.
Review several months of bookings before setting a measurable quarterly target.
Set a modest uptake goal, then track enquiries, bookings, and family feedback monthly.
Keep the current target while promoting the service more often during arrangements.

basic.situation: A family arranging a burial is unsure what to include in the obituary notice. You are meeting them to discuss service details.

options.text: Ask what they want remembered, then help shape wording they can approve.
Suggest a short notice focused on the service date and location.
Choose a familiar template and submit the notice for publication.
Share a sample notice and invite them to adapt its wording.

advanced.situation: Two services overlap, and an attendant calls in sick. You are directing the team while an embalmer finishes preparation for the earlier service.

options.text: Ask the available attendant to cover the earlier service first.
Reassign coverage around service timing, confirm essential duties, and brief affected staff.
Keep the original assignments and ask each team to manage the gap.
Move the embalmer to help with attendance once preparation is complete.

basic.situation: You are completing a family's service record and notice that the product inventory entry does not match the signed selection sheet.

options.text: Keep the entry pending, document the mismatch, and schedule follow-up with the arranging colleague.
Ask the arranging colleague to confirm the family's selected item before making record changes.
Compare the signed selection against inventory, update the entry, and document the verified change.
Change inventory only after checking the signed selection sheet against the delivered item records.

advanced.situation: A client asks to prearrange services and wants a price fixed for several years. You can discuss contract terms but cannot approve exceptions to the home's policy.

options.text: Discuss a lower deposit and ask the manager whether it can be approved.
Promise the requested fixed price and prepare the paperwork for signing.
Offer the standard terms and invite the client to take them home.
Explain the available terms, clarify the client's priorities, and document the agreed choices.

basic.situation: You are interviewing an applicant for a funeral attendant role. The hiring panel has agreed on the duties and selection criteria.

options.text: Ask each applicant the same role-based questions and record evidence against criteria.
Discuss the duties and ask the applicant to describe relevant experience with examples.
Offer the role to the applicant who can start earliest.
Focus on the applicant's availability and whether the team feels comfortable.

advanced.situation: A contracted transport provider has arrived late twice this month, though families praised the drivers. You are reviewing vendor performance before renewal discussions.

options.text: Renew the provider because families value the drivers' respectful manner.
Compare arrival records, family feedback, and agreed service terms before recommending changes.
End the arrangement now and begin calling other providers for cover.
Ask the provider to explain the late arrivals before recording a review.

basic.situation: You are reviewing monthly sales reports with guidance. Merchandise sales are steady, but overtime costs rose during the same period.

options.text: Compare this month's overtime with the previous month's figure.
Flag the overtime increase and ask the manager what to review next.
Cut scheduled shifts next month to bring overtime costs down.
Compare overtime with service volume and staffing patterns before suggesting a change.

advanced.situation: Staff feedback and service reviews show repeated uncertainty about explaining cremation options. You are identifying development needs for the team.

options.text: Ask staff to nominate training topics, then compare them with feedback.
Group feedback by skill gap and plan practice for affected staff.
Wait for further complaints before identifying a team training need.
Arrange a team refresher session covering cremation options and common family questions.

basic.situation: A client calls after a service to dispute an invoice and asks whether payment can be split. You are handling post-service enquiries.

options.text: Tell the client the invoice is final and close the enquiry.
Offer a payment arrangement based on the balance shown in the account.
Review the invoice with the client, clarify disputed items, and discuss payment choices.
Explain the payment schedule, offer to forward the concern, and outline available next steps.

advanced.situation: Staff have asked why the home is changing its appointment handoff process. You are asked to explain the new procedure at the weekly team meeting.

options.text: Tell staff to follow the new handoff because management approved the procedure.
Read the updated procedure aloud, distribute copies, and answer staff questions after the meeting.
Describe the change briefly, then ask staff to review the procedure later.
Explain the goal, outline the handoff, and invite staff to test a case.

basic.situation: A new member asks how to adjust a resistance machine before trying it. You have a few minutes before the next class starts.

options.text: Point out the controls and let the member choose a comfortable setting.
Suggest the same setting you used last time and move to class.
Demonstrate the seat and weight controls, then watch one careful repetition.
Explain the seat adjustment and ask whether the controls feel clear.

advanced.situation: Attendance has fallen in your weekly classes, and participants have different mobility levels. You are asked to refresh the next month's class plan.

options.text: Offer a low impact class alongside the usual strength and cardio sessions.
Add a popular circuit class and keep the remaining sessions unchanged.
Repeat the current schedule and promote it more widely this month.
Build varied sessions with adaptable movements, then check attendance and feedback.

basic.situation: You are helping organize a weekend community walk. The route is agreed, but volunteers are unsure where to report on the morning.

options.text: Send volunteers the meeting point and ask them to arrive early.
Share the route, meeting point, and assigned posts with each volunteer.
Brief the group on the meeting point and divide posts together.
Let volunteers choose their posts when they arrive at the park.

advanced.situation: Your organization wants a quarterly wellness program for staff at several sites, but available rooms and work shifts differ across locations.

options.text: Offer the same weekly talk at every site to simplify coordination.
Plan varied sessions around site capacity, shifts, and participant feedback.
Coordinate a monthly class and talk, then gather site attendance figures.
Use one shared class timetable and ask each site to adapt locally.

basic.situation: A contracted instructor arrives to lead a stretching session, but the class size is larger than the booking estimate.

options.text: Ask the instructor to split the group and start the session.
Let the instructor begin with everyone and review the class afterward.
Confirm the instructor can manage the group, then agree on a safe format.
Review the booking and ask the instructor how they will manage numbers.

advanced.situation: Two instructors give new staff different advice about greeting participants. You are leading a short staff learning session before the next class.

options.text: Read the service notes aloud and continue with the class schedule.
Ask each instructor to share one greeting tip with the team.
Use a short role play to align greetings and discuss participant feedback.
Review the service notes and invite questions about greeting participants.

basic.situation: Your wellness class has used fewer supplies this month, but attendance also dropped. You are asked to report whether the cost saving is working.

options.text: Compare the supply bill with last month and report the lower total.
Summarize the lower bill and mention the class attendance decline.
Report that the lower supply use shows the saving is successful.
Compare supply costs per attendee and note the attendance change.

advanced.situation: A six month wellness program has ended. Attendance rose, but participant feedback is mixed and the final report is due to management.

options.text: Summarize attendance and feedback, then suggest a smaller follow up survey.
Compare attendance, feedback, and goals before recommending program changes.
Use attendance totals to recommend running the same program again.
Highlight the attendance increase and leave mixed comments out of the report.

basic.situation: A treadmill belt slips during your morning check. A maintenance technician can visit later today, and members are starting to arrive.

options.text: Place a service note nearby and direct members to another treadmill.
Mark the treadmill out of use and arrange the technician visit.
Tell the front desk about the belt and request a repair check.
Ask members to try the treadmill gently until the technician arrives.

advanced.situation: You oversee a busy fitness room where cleaning logs are incomplete and several machines show wear. A safety inspection is scheduled for tomorrow.

options.text: Fill gaps in the logs from memory and prepare the room as usual.
Check the room, document faults, and assign cleaning and repair follow up.
Review the logs and ask staff to report any machine problems.
Ask staff to finish the cleaning logs before closing the room.

basic.situation: A member asks whether your wellness program offers beginner friendly lunchtime sessions. The current timetable lists several classes but no descriptions.

options.text: Explain the listed class formats and direct them to the coordinator for details.
Describe the lunchtime options and offer to check their experience level.
Tell them the busiest class is probably suitable for beginners.
Point to the timetable and suggest they try a lunchtime class.

advanced.situation: Several members request an evening beginner class, but your current timetable is full. You are asked to recommend whether to add the service.

options.text: Check recent attendance and ask members which evening they prefer.
Add the evening class next month and announce it to members.
Review attendance, member requests, and room capacity before recommending a trial.
Recommend replacing a low attendance class with the evening option.

basic.situation: A new spa receptionist starts during a busy afternoon. You have a short handover to explain their service duties and basic guest policies.

options.text: Explain their greeting, booking, and guest privacy duties during handover.
Show the receptionist the service guide and let them read it later.
Ask them to copy the previous shift's greeting and booking routine.
Walk through the booking screen and answer their first questions.

advanced.situation: Product sales vary widely across shifts, and new therapists receive different coaching. You are asked to prepare a team training plan and shared expectations.

options.text: Schedule a product briefing and agree on one service goal.
Send the product list to staff and expect sales to improve.
Plan product practice, guest service coaching, and shared performance measures.
Set a weekly sales target and ask senior therapists to coach others.

basic.situation: At closing, the cash total differs from the payment terminal summary by a small amount. You are preparing the day's cash record and deposit.

options.text: Check the receipts against both totals and ask a colleague to recount.
Record the cash total and note the terminal difference for review.
Recount cash, compare receipts, and record the unresolved difference clearly.
Adjust the cash entry to match the terminal summary and prepare deposit.

advanced.situation: The spa's monthly revenue target is falling behind, while supply costs are rising. You are asked to help prepare budget goals for the next quarter.

options.text: Compare last quarter's figures and propose a modest target increase.
Cut supply orders across services to protect the quarterly budget.
Raise the revenue target and ask each shift to sell more products.
Review service revenue and supply trends before setting realistic quarterly goals.

basic.situation: During a routine check, a treatment bed's height control responds slowly. The next appointment is due in ten minutes.

options.text: Mark the bed for checking and arrange another room for the appointment.
Check the control once more and tell the therapist what you found.
Ask the therapist to work around the slow control for this appointment.
Tell the therapist to use the bed at its current height.

advanced.situation: You notice that a treatment room's cleaning record is missing entries, and a new therapist's credential file is incomplete before a busy weekend.

options.text: Ask the therapist to complete the file and remind staff about cleaning logs.
Inspect the room and ask the therapist to bring credentials next shift.
Review credential evidence and room records, then flag gaps for follow up.
Assume the therapist has the required credentials and keep the schedule.

basic.situation: A guest asks whether a treatment package is available next week, and you notice their contact details are outdated in the client database.

options.text: Confirm the package and keep the old contact details for now.
Explain the package options and invite the guest to call back.
Check the booking calendar and ask the guest to confirm contact details.
Check availability, explain the package, and update confirmed contact details.

advanced.situation: A member complains that a prepaid treatment was unavailable twice. They are considering cancelling, and you can review their booking history.

options.text: Apologize and help them choose a less busy appointment time.
Tell them the schedule is busy and suggest they try another week.
Offer a small product discount and ask them to book again.
Review the booking history, acknowledge the pattern, and offer available remedies.

basic.situation: The spa plans to introduce a short weekday foot treatment. Your manager asks you to help plan the service details for a small trial.

options.text: Choose a trial day and ask therapists to suggest service steps.
Offer the treatment during quiet hours and collect guest comments.
Set the trial hours, service steps, and guest feedback method together.
Add the treatment to every shift and promote it at reception.

advanced.situation: Retail sales are below the spa's target, and a new promotion is being considered. Therapists say guests often ask for advice but feel rushed.

options.text: Pair product guidance with realistic goals and review guest response and sales.
Coach therapists to explain products and track weekly retail sales.
Set a daily retail target and remind therapists during shift briefings.
Offer a discount on popular products and count sales each week.

basic.situation: Two guests request the same treatment room at 3 pm, and the oil used for one service is running low before the weekend.

options.text: Move one guest to another room and order the usual oil quantity.
Check room availability, adjust one booking, and verify oil stock before ordering.
Offer another appointment time and ask stores to check the oil supply.
Keep both appointments in the room and borrow oil from another service.

advanced.situation: A maintenance repair will close one treatment room for a day, and a delayed supply delivery may affect several booked services.

options.text: Reschedule some guests and check with the supplier about delivery timing.
Map room capacity and stock needs, then adjust affected bookings and orders.
Move appointments to open rooms and use remaining supplies carefully.
Keep the schedule unchanged and ask therapists to share available supplies.

basic.situation: A team asks you to update an SOP after its document template changes, but the old procedure has unclear steps.

options.text: Compare the current workflow with the draft, then note unclear steps for review.
Map each approved step to the draft and flag gaps before controlled review.
Send the inherited procedure as final so teams can keep working.
Copy the old procedure and update its date before circulating the draft.

advanced.situation: A new product launch spans several markets, and teams disagree about which submissions must be ready before the planned release.

options.text: List the known filing dates and discuss gaps at the next project meeting.
Build a market-by-market submission plan with owners, dependencies, and launch decision points.
Ask each country contact to send its usual submission checklist by Friday.
Use the previous product's launch calendar and adjust dates for this team.

basic.situation: A submission packet is due tomorrow, and you are asked to check its forms for basic accuracy against the source records.

options.text: Review the cover page and rely on the preparer's completion checklist for details.
Reuse the last packet's figures wherever the new forms have matching labels.
Check names, dates, and figures against the source records, then mark each discrepancy.
Scan the forms for obvious errors and send any concerns to the lead.

advanced.situation: Marketing wants to release a user manual today, but one claim appears stronger than the evidence in the approved product information.

options.text: Ask marketing to soften the claim and review the revised manual later.
Compare the manual with an older approved version and flag major changes.
Release the manual with a note that the claim is still being checked.
Trace each claim to approved product information and mark unsupported wording for revision.

basic.situation: An internal audit begins next week, and your manager asks you to assemble records showing how a product change was documented.

options.text: Use the prior audit folder as a guide, then update its cover sheet.
Collect requested records and label them with the audit topic.
Send the latest change summary and ask the auditor which files remain outstanding.
Gather change records by date and link each decision to its supporting evidence.

advanced.situation: A serious product complaint may require a recall, and the audit team is asking whether complaint records support the current response plan.

options.text: Share the summary figures and explain that detailed records are still being assembled.
Reconcile complaint records with the response plan and document unresolved evidence gaps.
Ask the complaint team for its latest count before briefing the audit team.
Use the last complaint summary because the new figures are not yet final.

basic.situation: A colleague asks whether a proposed packaging change could be affected by emerging environmental rules you have been tracking.

options.text: Tell the team the packaging is covered because no new rule is in force.
Forward the headline and ask the colleague to assess the packaging change.
Check the source update, note its status, and summarize possible packaging impacts for review.
Add the update to your trend log and summarize its likely relevance.

advanced.situation: A packaging redesign supports a sustainability target, but the proposed material has an unresolved environmental compliance question.

options.text: Approve the preferred material because it improves the packaging footprint.
Record the concern and ask the project team to compare alternative materials.
Assess material concerns against the target and document trade-offs for the decision team.
Ask sustainability staff to confirm the target before the regulatory review continues.

basic.situation: A product complaint has been reviewed, and you must format the supporting records before the lead decides whether an agency submission is needed.

options.text: Arrange the records by complaint timeline and label evidence so the lead can assess them.
Reuse last month's complaint packet and replace its first page with this case.
Put the records in the requested template and check that each file opens.
Attach the complaint summary and send the remaining records as one bundle.

advanced.situation: A proposed environmental requirement may affect packaging across several product teams, and you are meeting an agency contact to understand its likely impact.

options.text: Tell teams to pause packaging changes until the agency finalizes its position.
Ask the contact whether the proposal is likely to affect your packaging plans.
Ask focused questions about scope and timing, then share a sourced impact summary across teams.
Request the agency's published materials and circulate them with a short note.

basic.situation: An agency asks for clarification about a product label, and you are assigned to draft a response using approved product information.

options.text: Reply from memory that the label reflects the product's current features.
Forward the agency email to the product team and request suggested wording.
Draft a short reply using the label text and send it for lead review.
Answer each question from approved information and flag any point needing lead review.

advanced.situation: An international agency raises a policy concern affecting a major product decision, and you are asked to prepare the organization's position for senior representatives.

options.text: Summarize the concern from earlier discussions and ask the team to confirm details.
Brief representatives on the agency concern, approved evidence, and pending decisions.
Tell representatives the organization supports the product plan and can explain later.
Send the agency's policy note and the product team's latest response to representatives.

basic.situation: A staff member reports that a supplier approval may have skipped a required review, and you are asked to identify whether follow-up is needed.

options.text: Close the report as a misunderstanding because the supplier was approved.
Note the report in the intake log and wait for another similar concern.
Check the approval record against the stated review steps and log the specific gap.
Ask the approver to explain the missing review before recording a concern.

advanced.situation: An internal review finds evidence that several managers altered approval records, and you must help direct the investigation and consider external reporting.

options.text: Preserve relevant records, define the investigation scope, and assess reporting duties with authorized counsel.
Secure the approval log and report the suspected conduct to the agency today.
Review the records separately and prepare a factual summary for the compliance lead.
Interview the managers together and compare their explanations with the approval log.

basic.situation: Your team has recurring delays in logging gifts, and a senior colleague asks you to draft a clearer step for the compliance procedure.

options.text: Add a reminder to log gifts promptly and share the draft for review.
Draft a simple logging step with an owner, timing, and route for questions.
Reuse the gift wording from another team's procedure and change the department name.
Remove the logging step so staff can avoid the repeated delay.

advanced.situation: A new industry practice affects several business units, and leaders want one organization-wide compliance procedure that teams can apply consistently.

options.text: Send one standard procedure to every unit using the current central template.
Ask each unit to update its procedure and send you a copy.
Compare current unit practices and draft common requirements for leadership review.
Set a shared control, assign accountable owners, and define how units report exceptions.

basic.situation: You receive a new employee complaint and need to update the compliance activity log while the investigation is still open.

options.text: Close the log entry using the reporter's initial description as the finding.
Wait for the investigation outcome, then enter the complaint with its resolution.
Record the date, issue category, status, and next review point in the log.
Add the complaint summary and mark the case as pending investigation.

advanced.situation: A regulator's reporting deadline is approaching, but investigation findings differ across teams and the supporting records are still being reconciled.

options.text: Check findings against records, log open points, and prepare a draft for review.
Flag the deadline and conflicting figures to the reporting lead, requesting direction.
Gather team findings and ask the reporting lead to resolve conflicting figures before drafting.
Submit the most complete narrative before the deadline, despite unresolved figures.

basic.situation: You are helping deliver an induction session, and several new staff ask how to raise a compliance concern confidentially.

options.text: Show the reporting slide and invite staff to read the policy afterward.
Tell staff to raise concerns with their manager during the next team meeting.
Describe the usual reporting route and offer to share the policy link.
Explain the reporting channels, confidentiality limits, and where staff can ask follow-up questions.

advanced.situation: Managers are unsure how to handle reports about a senior colleague, and you must advise them while training staff on the reporting process.

options.text: Walk through the standard route and send managers the reporting procedure afterward.
Advise staff to resolve the concern directly with the senior colleague first.
Explain alternate reporting routes, protect confidentiality, and coach managers on prompt escalation.
Ask managers to review the policy and bring questions to a later session.

basic.situation: An external auditor requests samples showing that staff followed the gift approval procedure during the last quarter.

options.text: Gather the requested approvals and arrange them by month for the auditor.
Select traceable samples, match approvals to the procedure, and note any missing evidence.
Send the policy and a recent approval example while locating the other records.
Use the cleanest approvals as the sample set and archive the rest.

advanced.situation: A periodic review finds that one business unit uses an old approval form, and staff received different instructions about the current procedure.

options.text: Record the finding and schedule a follow-up review after the next reporting cycle.
Ask the unit to replace its form and remind staff to check the shared folder.
Remove the old form from the folder and close the review finding.
Trace the form's use, update the controlled procedure, and confirm staff receive one current instruction.

basic.situation: An employee contacts you privately, unsure whether a manager's request conflicts with the gifts policy and how to raise the concern.

options.text: Clarify the concern privately, explain reporting routes, and record agreed follow-up securely.
Suggest the employee reread the gifts policy and contact you with questions.
Ask the employee to raise the concern with the manager at their next meeting.
Forward the employee's message to the manager so they can explain the request.

advanced.situation: A difficult compliance case may involve legal exposure and staff misconduct, and you must coordinate advice and consistent disciplinary handling.

options.text: Ask HR to recommend an outcome and send counsel the decision for comment.
Consult counsel on legal exposure and coordinate proposed actions with HR's process.
Tell the manager to apply the usual discipline and inform counsel afterward.
Share verified facts with counsel and HR, then agree on a consistent response plan.

basic.situation: During a busy evening shift, you notice two guards leave the same aisle uncovered during their rounds.

options.text: Pair a newer guard with an experienced colleague for the next round.
Mark missed rounds complete so the handover stays on schedule.
Ask the team to follow the usual rota and finish today's patrols.
Reassign rounds around busy hours and brief guards on priority aisles.

advanced.situation: Several stores report similar refund patterns, and early evidence suggests a group may be targeting the chain.

options.text: Ask each store to send its recent refund reports by day's end.
Have each manager review refunds and send any unusual cases to you.
Share the suspected group's names with all store teams to watch.
Compare verified incidents and assign discreet checks across the affected stores.

basic.situation: An exception report shows a till shortage, but the cash log and closing notes do not match.

options.text: Adjust the report to match the closing total and send it onward.
Check the deposit slip and ask the supervisor about the mismatch.
Trace the entries against the till log and note the unresolved difference.
Ask the cashier to explain the shortage before checking the paperwork.

advanced.situation: A heated dispute near the entrance is drawing a crowd, and staff report threats as customers continue arriving.

options.text: Tell nearby staff to keep the entrance clear while you call the manager.
Send a message that names one disputant as the threat to staff.
Use the site response plan to move people away and alert trained responders.
Ask the crowd to stay calm while you learn what started the dispute.

basic.situation: A deposit bag total differs from the cash audit sheet during your routine store check.

options.text: Check the sheet against the deposit slip before asking about the gap.
Use the bag total as the audit figure and finish the check.
Ask the cashier to recount the bag while you review the sheet.
Reconcile the count with till records and record the difference for review.

advanced.situation: A store's stock records look sound, but an inspection finds blocked exits and inconsistent security tag checks.

options.text: Review the safety checklist and sample a few tag records before reporting.
Map each finding to the relevant procedure and document the store's control gaps.
Close the audit using the stock figures and mention the exits separately.
Tell the manager to clear the exits and repeat tag checks today.

basic.situation: You observe a shopper conceal an item, then pause near the exit as staff prepare to approach.

options.text: Ask the shopper about the item and note their response for the file.
Tell the shopper you saw theft and ask them to return the item.
Follow store procedure, ask neutral questions, and record what you observed.
Ask a nearby colleague to confirm what happened before speaking to them.

advanced.situation: A confidential report alleges an employee bypassed stock controls, and the manager asks you for an update before interviews begin.

options.text: Collect the stock logs first and arrange interviews with relevant staff.
Separate verified records from allegations and plan confidential, impartial interviews.
Tell the manager the employee likely diverted stock based on the report.
Ask the employee's team for informal views before scheduling interviews.

basic.situation: Your shift ends after a shoplifting incident, and the next team needs a clear account of the response.

options.text: Log times, actions, evidence locations, and the handover contact in the case file.
Summarize the response and attach the available incident notes for the next team.
Write that staff handled the incident and leave details for the manager.
Record the incident time and names of staff who attended in the handover log.

advanced.situation: A bank flags a pattern of fake refund receipts across stores, and an officer requests records for an external fraud inquiry.

options.text: Confirm the request through established contacts and coordinate a factual records handover.
Ask your manager which records can be shared with the officer.
Send the records to the officer's listed email and update your manager.
Call the known liaison and arrange a records review with the officer.

basic.situation: A small store asks how staff should document suspected internal theft during a busy shift.

options.text: Recommend a simple incident log that separates observations, times, and follow-up actions.
Suggest recording the time, item, and staff who were present.
Ask the manager to keep notes and contact loss prevention later.
Suggest that staff write down the employee's name and suspected item.

advanced.situation: A manager asks whether a new store procedure meets several safety and inventory requirements across different locations.

options.text: Ask the manager to compare the procedure with the current store checklist.
Review the checklist and note any steps that appear to be missing.
Tell the manager the procedure is compliant because it matches the usual checklist.
Map each procedure to its applicable requirements and flag gaps for qualified review.

basic.situation: A turbine repair estimate is due today, and you have the work order and recent parts prices. You need to estimate the cost with guidance.

options.text: I would use the work order and recent parts prices to draft the estimate.
I would reuse last year's repair figure to finish the estimate quickly.
I would separate parts and labour, note assumptions, then ask my lead to review.
I would price the listed parts and add a standard labour allowance.

advanced.situation: Two wind farms need major work, but the budget cannot cover both this quarter. A contractor offers a discount if you sign a long maintenance contract today.

options.text: I would rank the work by lost generation and compare contract terms.
I would compare safety, downtime, and lifecycle costs before setting priorities.
I would accept the discount and reserve funds for both sites later.
I would fund the site with the larger immediate repair estimate.

basic.situation: You are completing the daily operations form after a turbine stopped for an hour. The operator has shared the time and a brief fault note.

options.text: I would copy yesterday's downtime entry and adjust the time.
I would record the time, fault note, and source in the daily form.
