advanced.situation: A body is found with no identification, and no missing person report matches. You lead the effort to establish the person's identity.

options.text: Ask the person who found the body who it might be and record their view.
Take fingerprints and dental details, search databases, and ask police about a public appeal.
Name the person in the file after a resemblance to a recent missing person photo.
Take fingerprints and search the fingerprint database, then wait for a match to appear.

basic.situation: A senior coroner asks you to complete a standard death certificate form for a natural death. The doctor's notes list heart failure as the cause.

options.text: Copy the cause from the notes, check names and dates, and pass the form for review.
Copy the cause from the doctor's notes and complete the other fields from the file.
Fill in the form from memory of the case since you reviewed the file yesterday.
Enter old age as the cause of death because it is less upsetting for the family.

advanced.situation: You must certify a death that follows a judicial order and finalise the case file. A required court form has not arrived, but officials want the file closed today.

options.text: Ask the court clerk to confirm the order by phone, then certify the death today.
Certify the death now and add the court form to the file when it arrives.
Wait for the court form, record the delay, and tell officials why the file stays open.
Fill in the court form details from an earlier similar case and close the file.

basic.situation: You help trace the next of kin for a man who died alone. His ID lists an address, and a neighbour mentions a sister living abroad.

options.text: Note the neighbour's comment in the file and wait for someone to ask about the man.
Record the sister's details, log each attempt to reach her, and update your supervisor.
Record the sister's details and ask the neighbour to tell her about the death.
Post a message about the death on social media to find the family quickly.

advanced.situation: A family is angry about delays after a sudden death and wants their father's watch and phone released today. The case is not yet closed.

options.text: Explain that the case is still open and promise to call them when items are ready.
Release both items to the loudest family member to end the confrontation at the counter.
Release the watch today to the family but keep the phone until the case is closed.
Explain what you can share, check who is authorised, and arrange release when the case allows.

basic.situation: You inventory a deceased man's wallet and jewellery at the scene. You may later be asked to testify about what you recorded.

options.text: List each item and the cash count, photograph them, and have a witness sign.
List the valuable items and bag the remaining belongings together to save time at the scene.
Hand the wallet to a relative at the scene and list it later from memory.
List each item with a description and keep the list in your notebook for the file.

advanced.situation: You must present forensic findings at an inquest next week. A police officer asks you to simplify your conclusion on the cause of death.

options.text: Agree to the officer's simpler wording so the inquest goes smoothly for the family.
Give the officer a short summary of your findings and keep your full report for court.
Prepare a plain-language account that keeps your conclusion as supported, and review it with counsel.
Change the wording of your report to match the officer's view before the inquest.

basic.situation: A supervisor asks you to check a new face mask's product label against the labelling checklist before 50,000 labels are printed.

options.text: Check every item against the checklist, flag anything missing, and send findings to your supervisor.
Approve the label for printing now and fix any problems on the next print run.
Check the main claims and warnings on the label and tell the supervisor it looks fine.
Compare the label with last year's mask label and assume it meets the same rules.

advanced.situation: You lead an internal audit of batch records for a vaccine product. Several records have signature gaps, and one has a mismatched temperature entry.

options.text: List all gaps in the audit report and ask the department to fix them by next week.
Note the signature gaps as minor and focus the report on the temperature entry.
Add the missing signatures from supervisors who were on duty and close the audit.
Rank each gap by risk, trace the temperature entry to source data, and report actions needed.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to gather documents for a product registration submission. The checklist lists eight documents, and you can find seven.

options.text: Compile the seven documents, flag the missing one, and ask its owner for it by Friday.
Use a similar document from an earlier submission in place of the missing one for now.
Compile the seven documents and tell your supervisor that one is still to come.
Write the missing document yourself from the product description and add it to the pack.

advanced.situation: A regulatory agency asks for additional data on a device's battery safety within 10 days. The test team says some results will take 15 days.

options.text: Ask the test team to shorten the tests and send all results on day 10.
Send the available data on day 10 and send the rest when it is ready.
Send estimated results for the unfinished tests on day 10 and label them as final results.
Send the available data, explain the test timeline, and request a short extension in writing.

basic.situation: You update the company's regulatory database after a product approval arrives. The approval letter shows a new expiry date and a changed approved name.

options.text: Enter the expiry date now and update the name when someone asks about it.
Enter the new expiry date and name, attach the letter, and check the entry against it.
Enter the new expiry date and attach the letter to the record for reference.
Overwrite the old record with the new details and delete the old approval letter.

advanced.situation: An inspector visits your plant next week for a product approval renewal. The technical file has outdated sections, and the team is stretched.

options.text: Update the sections the inspector is most likely to ask about and note the others.
Present the old technical file and say that nothing has changed since the last approval.
Tell the inspector the file is being updated and invite them to come later.
Update the outdated sections of the technical file, assign owners for gaps, and brief staff.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to draft a short email to the agency about a submission made six weeks ago. She will approve it before it is sent.

options.text: Draft an email asking when the product will be approved and send it for approval.
Draft a polite email with the submission number and date and a clear question on status.
Send the email to the agency directly to save your manager's time this afternoon.
Draft an email saying the delay is hurting sales and asking the agency to hurry.

advanced.situation: Complaints about a faulty seal are rising. You must recommend how to adjudicate them and track quality metrics, while production wants them classed as isolated.

options.text: Analyse complaints by batch, recommend risk-based adjudication, and set a metric to track seal failures.
Agree with production that the complaints are isolated and review them again next quarter.
Close the complaints as user error to keep the quality metrics within the target.
Recommend adjudicating each complaint separately and track the total number of complaints each month.

basic.situation: A new regulation was announced on medical device labelling. Your team lead asks you to read and summarise the update for the team.

options.text: Forward the full update to the team and ask them to read it for themselves.
Read the full update, list changes and dates that affect our products, and share it.
Read the agency's news summary and email its key points to the whole team today.
Summarise the update from a trade newsletter and present it as the official text.

advanced.situation: A regulation change means your company's complaint handling SOP is outdated. You write the new SOP and train staff.

options.text: Compare the regulation with the SOP, draft revised steps, get reviews, and train all staff.
Keep using the old SOP until an auditor raises the change as an issue.
Add a note to the SOP saying the regulation changed and staff should read it.
Revise the SOP's main steps for the change and email the new version to staff.

basic.situation: A colleague asks what labelling is needed to export a skin cream. You have the labelling requirements checklist for the target country.

options.text: Send her the checklist and ask her to contact you with any questions later on.
Tell her labelling is checked after shipment arrives, so it can be added at that stage.
Tell her the labels used in the home market will be accepted for export.
Go through the checklist with her and offer to check the draft label.

advanced.situation: A major product launch is planned for next quarter, but a new regulation could require extra clinical data. Management wants advice on the launch date.

options.text: Advise delaying the launch until the regulation is fully clear, to avoid any regulatory risk.
Assess how the regulation applies, estimate the data timeline, and present launch options with risks.
Advise keeping the launch date and adding the data later if the agency asks.
Advise that the regulation does not apply to this product based on a colleague's view.

basic.situation: A client is importing 500 boxes of ceramic tiles. You are asked to gather the customs invoice and certificate of origin for the shipment.

options.text: Request both documents from the client and file them as soon as they arrive.
Use the invoice from the client's last shipment of tiles and request the certificate.
Request both documents, check names and values against the packing list, and file them.
Prepare both documents yourself from the packing list so the shipment is not delayed.

advanced.situation: You hold a power of attorney to sign customs documents for a client. Duty charges on a shipment look too high, and the client wants an appeal prepared.

options.text: Pay the charges as billed now and ask the client later whether it wants to appeal.
Prepare an appeal explaining that the charges look too high and sign it for the client.
Review classification and value, prepare the appeal with supporting papers, and sign within your authority.
Sign a new declaration lowering the goods' value so the duty comes down, then appeal.

basic.situation: A client asks you to quote the duty on imported cotton fabric. You have the tariff schedule open, and the fabric has a clear description.

options.text: Quote a lower duty rate than the schedule says so the client accepts the service.
Quote the rate from the schedule line for woven fabrics and mention it may vary.
Quote the duty rate you used for similar fabric last month for another client.
Find the fabric's code in the schedule, read its duty rate, and quote both.

advanced.situation: A client exports parts after importing materials. You are asked to apply for a duty drawback, but the records of materials used are incomplete.

options.text: Apply for the drawback using the figures the client gives and note that records are incomplete.
Apply for a smaller drawback amount that the existing partial records seem to support.
Fill in the missing material quantities with estimates and submit the application as complete.
Rebuild the material records from invoices and production logs, then apply with supporting papers.

basic.situation: A small importer asks you to help obtain a bond for its first shipment. Your supervisor gave you a list of approved bond providers.

options.text: Suggest the importer buys a bond from a friend's insurance agency at a lower price.
Request a quote from the first approved provider on the list and tell the importer.
Get the shipment value and details, request quotes from two approved providers, and compare them.
Tell the importer to ship first and arrange the bond after the goods arrive.

advanced.situation: A client ships electronics worth 2 million ringgit by air. You arrange the bond, insurance and duty payment, and payment is due tomorrow.

options.text: Confirm the bond, insure the cargo at a standard amount, and pay the duty tomorrow morning.
Skip cargo insurance since air freight is fast and pay the duty and bond on time.
Pay the duty from another client's deposit and repay that account when funds arrive.
Confirm the bond, insure the cargo at full value, and schedule the duty payment early.

basic.situation: A client asks where a container of furniture is. You have the shipping line's tracking tool and the container number.

options.text: Check the tracking tool and tell the client the container is on its way.
Enter the container number, note the location and expected arrival, and tell the client.
Give the client the arrival date from the original booking sheet and promise delivery.
Tell the client the container left last week, so it should arrive within a few days.

advanced.situation: A client's sea-and-rail shipment is delayed at the port, and its factory needs the goods in three days. You can contract freight forwarders for destination services.

options.text: Sign a two-year contract for the client with the first forwarder who offers a same-day truck.
Hire the fastest forwarder you know for trucking and inform the client of the cost afterwards.
Wait for the rail operator to reschedule and keep telling the client it is coming.
Get quotes from two forwarders for trucking from the port, and update the client on options.

basic.situation: You are asked to stay current on import rules for your team. This week, a colleague mentions that rules for electrical goods changed.

options.text: Tell the team the change does not apply to shipments already booked, from your memory.
Ask the colleague to explain the change and tell the team what they said.
Read a news article about the change and tell the team it is confirmed.
Look up the official notice, read the changes, and share a short summary with the team.

advanced.situation: A quarantine officer holds a shipment of fresh fruit over a paperwork query. You confer with officials to clear goods, and the fruit will spoil within two days.

options.text: Ask the client to call the agency's head office to complain about the delay.
Send the officer the full file of documents and wait for a reply by evening.
Offer the officer a small payment to speed up the release of the fruit.
Ask the officer what is missing, supply the documents quickly, and request priority handling.

basic.situation: A new importer asks how to lower the duties on his first shipment. You know a few legal steps from your training.

options.text: Tell him to check the tariff schedule for lower-rate codes that fit his goods.
Explain that accurate classification and valuation matter, and offer to check which schemes apply.
Tell him to split the shipment into several smaller ones to stay under duty limits.
Tell him to ask the supplier for a lower invoice value, which cuts the duty.

advanced.situation: A client wants to import goods from a country with a quota and an insurance requirement. The tariff system is complex, and the client wants a quick yes or no.

options.text: Check quota status, tariff treatment and insurance rules, then give a written answer with conditions.
Tell the client yes, since similar imports from that country went through last year.
Tell the client yes and handle any quota or insurance problems when the goods arrive.
Check the quota status and tell the client it is possible if quota remains.

basic.situation: You are given the blueprint for a small shophouse renovation and asked to prepare a basic estimate of materials and labour hours, with guidance.

options.text: Measure the main quantities from the blueprint and price them using the rate sheet.
Use the cost per square metre from a similar shophouse job and scale it up.
Add a percentage to the last renovation quote and present it as a new estimate.
Measure quantities from the blueprint, apply the rate sheet, and have a senior review.

advanced.situation: Your team repeatedly overruns costs on tile-laying work. You study the work to develop standard hour data and decide whether to make or buy components.

options.text: Use the supplier's published labour hours as the standard for all your tile jobs.
Set the standard at the fastest crew's quickest day and apply it to every job.
Time several jobs, set standard hours per square metre, and compare making against buying components.
Take the average hours from last year's invoices and use them as the standard.

basic.situation: A manager asks you for a simple cost estimate to plan the budget for a warehouse extension. You have the floor area and a rate list.

options.text: Use the budget from the last warehouse and tell the manager it is similar in size.
Multiply the area by the matching rate, add a contingency, and give the manager the workings.
Give the manager a lower figure than you calculated so the project gets approved.
Multiply the area by the matching rate and give the manager the total figure.

advanced.situation: You run tendering for a building project. Three subcontractors bid, and the lowest bid is 25 percent below the others, with unclear inclusions.

options.text: Ask the lowest bidder to clarify scope, compare all bids line by line, then negotiate.
Recommend the middle bid, since it is neither too high nor suspiciously low for the work.
Recommend the lowest bid because it saves the most money for the project budget this year.
Tell the other bidders the lowest price and ask them to beat it by Friday.

basic.situation: You collect historical cost data on past road repair jobs to help estimate a future one. You have invoices from five projects.

options.text: Record each job's cost per kilometre with year and conditions, and note price changes.
Pick the three cheapest jobs for the data so that the estimate looks competitive.
Use the most recent invoice as the cost data, since it reflects current prices.
Record each job's total cost and take the average for the future estimate.

advanced.situation: You set up a cost monitoring system for a long project. Site teams report in different formats, and managers want weekly reports.

options.text: Define one reporting format and email it to the site teams to start next week.
Define one reporting format, train site teams, set weekly dates, and check the first reports.
Collect each team's reports as they are and combine them by hand each week.
Report cost figures to managers from the site teams' verbal updates each Friday afternoon.

basic.situation: You visit a site for an estimate and record access, drainage and utilities. The site is a hillside plot with a narrow road.

options.text: Take a few photos from the road and use the map for the other details.
Photograph the road and slope, note drainage and utilities, and record the measurements.
Note the road width and slope and record where the utilities connect to the plot.
Skip the site visit and fill in the site details from an online map.

advanced.situation: A project is halfway through, and actual costs are 12 percent above the bid. You track costs and assess cost effectiveness for management.

options.text: Wait for the next monthly report before telling management, in case costs settle down.
Report the 12 percent overrun to management and ask the site teams to cut costs.
Move some site costs to the next project's account so this one looks on budget.
Compare actual and bid costs by item, find the causes, and forecast the final cost.

basic.situation: Your lead asks you to update the supplier directory with new contact details. A supplier emails new bank details along with its new phone number.

options.text: Update the phone number and bank details and tell your lead about the email.
Update the phone number and bank details and approve the next payment to the new account.
Update the phone number and forward the new bank details to the finance team to process.
Update the phone number, then confirm the bank details by calling a number already on file.

advanced.situation: You prepare cost and expenditure statements for a three-year project. Late invoices keep arriving for completed months, and the totals change.

options.text: Add late invoices to the month they arrive and explain this in a footnote.
Change the invoice dates to the month of the work so earlier totals stay the same.
Hold each statement until all invoices for that month have arrived from every supplier.
Accrue for work not yet invoiced, reconcile late invoices monthly, and note restatements clearly.

basic.situation: A client asks why your estimate for kitchen cabinets is higher than another quote. You have your estimate worksheet in front of you.

options.text: Explain that your estimate uses good materials and a skilled team, so it costs more.
Offer to match the other quote and adjust the numbers to fit it this week.
Walk the client through your worksheet and ask what the other quote includes.
Tell the client the other quote must be missing items, as ours covers everything.

advanced.situation: The architect proposes a design change that adds an expensive facade, but the owner wants the original budget kept. You adjust the cost estimate.

options.text: Price the facade and send the new total to the owner for a decision.
Leave the facade out of the estimate so the owner's budget still looks met.
Keep the original total by lowering the contingency to absorb the facade cost for now.
Price the facade, show the effect on budget, and propose cheaper alternatives to both parties.

basic.situation: You screen 30 applications for a clerk job that needs a diploma and one year of experience. Five applicants lack the diploma but have three years of experience.

options.text: Shortlist applicants who meet both requirements and put the five aside for later review.
Shortlist applicants who meet both requirements and send the manager the five others to decide.
Shortlist the five with experience first, since experience matters more in the job.
Add the diploma to the five applicants' records so they qualify for the shortlist.

advanced.situation: You design the hiring process for a senior finance role and guide managers on the final decision. Two finalists are close, and one is the manager's former colleague.

options.text: Score both against agreed criteria, record reasons, recommend one, and flag the manager's relationship.
Add a second interview round for the finalist the manager does not know well.
Score both finalists against the agreed criteria and leave the final decision to the manager.
Let the manager choose his former colleague and record the decision as a panel choice.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to find candidates for a data entry role using job boards and databases. A supervisor guides you.

options.text: Post the vacancy on your personal social media account and wait for people to apply.
Contact candidates from the databases and promise them the job before the manager agrees.
Search job boards for data entry and send the manager every profile you find.
Search job boards using the role's key skills, shortlist suitable profiles, and send them on.

advanced.situation: Management asks for advice on a retention programme. Several skilled engineers resigned this quarter, and the budget is limited.

options.text: Recommend withholding the final pay of resigning engineers to persuade them to stay on.
Recommend a pay increase for all engineers and ask finance to find the budget.
Recommend hiring replacements faster and offering larger signing bonuses to all the new engineers.
Analyse exit reasons and pay data, propose targeted retention steps, and track results.

basic.situation: A new employee asks how many days of annual leave she gets in her first year. You have the leave policy and a script.

options.text: Tell her she can take as many days as she likes in her first year.
Read her the leave entitlement from the policy and ask her to check the details herself.
Read her the entitlement from the policy, explain how it is counted, and share the link.
Tell her the usual number of leave days in most companies and say hers is similar.

advanced.situation: Managers want to introduce a hybrid work policy, but handbook rules on working hours and overtime might conflict. You advise on implementation and compliance.

options.text: Draft the hybrid policy as managers describe it and note that handbook rules may differ.
Publish the hybrid policy and update the handbook later if staff raise conflicts.
Compare the draft policy with handbook rules and contracts, list conflicts, and propose revisions.
Tell staff the new hybrid policy overrides their contracts on working hours and overtime pay.

basic.situation: An employee resigns, and you run the exit interview and complete the termination paperwork with guidance. He says his supervisor regularly shouted at staff.

options.text: Thank him and leave the supervisor comment out of the notes since he is leaving.
Record his comments, finish the paperwork, and pass the supervisor concern to your HR lead.
Tell the supervisor which employee complained, so he can respond before the notes are filed.
Record his comments and finish the paperwork, then file the interview notes in his record.

advanced.situation: A staff member alleges harassment by a senior manager, and the manager denies it. Witnesses are reluctant. You must resolve the issue and follow equal opportunity rules.

options.text: Tell the complainant the matter is closed since no witness is willing to speak up.
Open a formal investigation, protect the complainant, interview witnesses privately, and report to senior HR.
Interview the manager and the complainant and decide based on how convincing each one is.
Ask the two to meet and settle things between themselves with a short apology.

basic.situation: You update a promoted employee's record in the HR system. The promotion letter shows a new title and salary starting next month.

options.text: Enter the new title and salary with the effective date, and attach the signed letter.
Enter a higher salary than the letter shows after the employee says it was agreed verbally.
Enter the new title now and enter the salary when payroll asks for it.
Enter the new title and salary now and attach the letter to the record.

advanced.situation: Leadership asks why staff turnover rose this year. You have exit data, absence records and survey results, and must prepare a report.

options.text: Analyse turnover by department and tenure, link it to exit reasons, and recommend actions with caveats.
Leave out departments with the highest turnover so the report shows a clear trend.
Report that turnover rose because of the job market, which is outside the company's control.
Report the turnover rate by department and list the reasons given in exit interviews.

basic.situation: You schedule an orientation for 12 new employees and prepare basic materials. The trainer is free on Thursday morning.

options.text: Book Thursday morning, confirm the room and equipment, and send the agenda to everyone.
Book the orientation for Friday and ask the trainer to adjust his plans on the day.
Book Thursday morning and tell the new staff the details on their first day.
Book Thursday morning and send the agenda to the new staff and the trainer.

advanced.situation: You train managers on documenting performance issues. They write vague notes like bad attitude, which have weakened past disciplinary cases.

options.text: Give managers a template with fields for dates and facts and ask them to use it.
Teach managers to record dates, facts and impact, and practise on anonymised real examples.
Tell managers HR will rewrite their notes into proper wording before any disciplinary hearing.
Tell managers to write longer notes so that important details are not missed later.

basic.situation: A supervisor asks you to help screen applicants for fruit-picking work. Ten people came, and the job requires lifting 20 kg.

options.text: Check each applicant's ID and age, ask about experience and lifting ability, and note results.
Accept every applicant who says he is over 18 and start him on the same day.
Pick the applicants who look strongest and tell the others to leave their contact details.
Ask each applicant about experience and lifting ability and note who seems most suitable for picking.

advanced.situation: You design the recruitment plan for 200 seasonal harvest workers. Demand peaks in six weeks, and previous agents charged workers high recruitment fees.

options.text: Use licensed agents for most workers and let local contacts bring in the rest.
Recruit workers from the border by cash agreement and arrange their papers after arrival.
Plan recruitment through licensed channels, cover fees yourself, screen in batches, and train team leaders.
Hire through the previous agents again since they deliver workers on time every season.

basic.situation: You assist a foreman in assigning daily tasks to 15 workers harvesting vegetables. Two workers are new, and one has a sore back.

options.text: Assign tasks by the usual list and ask workers to tell you if there is a problem.
Pair the new workers with experienced ones and give the sore-back worker lighter tasks.
Give the sore-back worker the heaviest lifting task so the other workers finish early.
Give the new workers simple tasks and let the sore-back worker choose his own.

advanced.situation: Two foremen disagree about enforcing the rule that workers stop at noon during extreme heat. Productivity is behind, and the owner is pressing.

options.text: Tell the foremen to work through the noon heat for a week to catch up.
Allow shorter breaks when workers agree, so the crews can catch up on output.
Enforce the noon break for all crews, explain why to both foremen, and adjust the schedule.
Let the foreman who follows the rule continue and speak to the other later.

basic.situation: You help set up drinking water stations for a crew of 30 workers in an oil palm field. Your supervisor gave you six water containers.

options.text: Place containers in shaded spots near work areas, fill them with clean water, and tell workers.
Place the containers at the field entrance and fill them with clean water each morning.
Fill the containers from the irrigation canal, since it is closer to the field.
Fill the containers with tap water from the farm office and leave them in the sun.

advanced.situation: You audit welfare facilities at three farm camps. One camp has broken toilets, a drinking water tap with chemicals stored nearby, and no handwashing area.

options.text: Ask the camp manager to improve the facilities and check again at the next audit.
Fix the drinking water and move the chemicals, then plan the toilets and handwashing next month.
Rank the hazards, fix water and toilets first, schedule other upgrades, and re-inspect with a checklist.
Rate the camp as acceptable in the audit because workers have not complained about conditions.

basic.situation: You hand out hoes and sickles to 20 workers at the start of the shift under supervision. Some tools have loose handles.

options.text: Give the loose tools to the newest workers since they will use them least.
Hand out the tools and tell workers to report any that feel loose during work.
Check each tool, set aside the loose ones, and record who receives each tool today.
Tighten the loose handles with tape as you hand the tools out to workers.

advanced.situation: You manage tool supply for 150 workers across several fields. Tools often go missing or break, and the cost is rising. You also train staff on maintenance.

options.text: Charge workers for lost tools through wage deductions to discourage further losses in the fields.
Buy cheaper tools in bulk and replace them when they break, and stop tracking usage.
Set up a sign-out register, schedule regular repairs, and train staff to inspect tools.
Count the tools each week and replace any that are missing or broken at once.

basic.situation: You help load 25 workers onto a farm truck to go to the field. The truck's seats hold 20, and the field is 10 minutes away.

options.text: Load 20 workers and ask the other five to wait for a ride from another driver.
Load all 25 and ask the driver to drive slowly, since the trip is short.
Let five workers stand on the open back of the truck to fit everyone in.
Load 20 workers, send the other five on a second trip, and tell your supervisor.

advanced.situation: You plan transport routes for six trucks carrying workers to scattered plots. Some roads flood in heavy rain, and one truck's brakes were reported weak.

options.text: Plan routes to avoid flood-prone roads and have the weak-brake truck serviced next week.
Keep all six trucks on their usual routes and tell drivers to be careful.
Take the weak-brake truck out of service, avoid flood-prone roads, and set a rain backup plan.
Assign the weak-brake truck the shortest route on dry roads and keep the plan.

basic.situation: You help calculate daily wages for 12 workers with a manager. The manager gives you the hours sheet and the daily rate.

options.text: Round every worker's pay down to the nearest ringgit to keep the figures simple.
Multiply each worker's hours by the rate, add listed overtime, and have the manager check.
Use last week's totals for workers whose hours look the same and calculate the rest.
Multiply each worker's hours by the rate and give the totals to the manager.

advanced.situation: A group of workers says they were underpaid last month. Records are incomplete, and the owner says the claims are exaggerated. You audit payroll compliance.

options.text: Pay half of the claimed amounts now and settle the balance if records are found.
Ask each worker how many hours he worked and pay according to his statement.
Back the owner and tell the workers there is no record, so no payment is due.
Rebuild hours from attendance logs and reports, calculate what is owed, and pay it with records.

basic.situation: A senior specialist asks you to draft a first contract proposal on shift allowances for collective bargaining. Last year's agreement is in the file.

options.text: Draft allowance clauses from last year's agreement, update the figures given, and mark open points.
Write the clauses from your memory of the company's usual position on shift allowances.
Draft higher allowances than the senior suggested to give the union a good start.
Copy last year's allowance clauses and update the dates for the senior to review this week.

advanced.situation: You set the standard for contract language, and a junior asks how to word an amendment on working hours. The draft wording could be read two ways.

options.text: Show the junior how to define terms, remove ambiguity, and test the wording on likely disputes.
Tell the junior to keep the wording flexible so the company can choose its reading later.
Tell the junior to keep the original wording since both sides have seen it.
Rewrite the clause yourself in plain language and ask the junior to use it.

basic.situation: The union proposes a 10 percent wage increase, and your supervisor asks you to identify simple alternatives the company could offer.

options.text: List alternatives such as a smaller raise with a bonus or extra leave, with rough costs.
Suggest the company rejects the proposal and waits for the union to lower its demand.
Suggest promising the union 10 percent now and quietly cutting other benefits after signing.
List alternatives such as a smaller raise or a one-time bonus and send them.

advanced.situation: You advise on bargaining strategy for a negotiation with three unions and a government observer. Each union wants a different priority.

options.text: Offer the same package to all three unions and refuse to discuss separate priorities.
Negotiate with the largest union first and try to apply that outcome to the others.
Promise each union its own priority in private talks and sort out conflicts later.
Map each union's priorities, find trades between them, set goals and limits, and brief the team.

basic.situation: You help schedule a grievance hearing for an employee dismissed for lateness. The union rep and the manager give different available dates.

options.text: Pick the manager's date and send the union rep a notice of the hearing.
Find common dates, confirm the room, and send both parties a written notice with the agenda.
Set the hearing for the earliest date either side offers and inform them the day before.
Schedule the hearing on the manager's date and tell the union rep on the morning.

advanced.situation: A bitter dispute over retrenchment has stalled and both sides distrust each other. You select a mediator and lead the process.

options.text: Appoint a mediator who is friendly with the company's managers to move things quickly.
Let the company choose the mediator, since it is paying for the whole process.
Pick an experienced mediator you have used before and invite both sides to the first meeting.
Shortlist neutral mediators, get both sides to agree on one, and set the process in writing.

basic.situation: An employee asks what the collective agreement says about overtime pay on public holidays. You have a checklist and the agreement open.

options.text: Tell him the holiday rate is probably the same as the normal overtime rate.
Tell him the agreement does not cover holiday work, so no extra pay is due.
Find the overtime clause, read the holiday rate to him, and give him the clause number.
Tell him the holiday rate from the checklist and say the agreement has the details.

advanced.situation: A clause says overtime is paid where work exceeds normal hours, but the union and management disagree whether this includes travel time. You advise leadership.

options.text: Advise leadership that the clause clearly excludes travel time and refuse to discuss it.
Advise leadership to follow the reading the company has used so far, until challenged.
Review the clause history and past practice, set out both readings, and recommend clarification.
Advise leadership to adopt the union's reading to avoid conflict this bargaining round.

basic.situation: You check pay data against the contract's wage scale for 40 workers. Two workers are paid below their grade's rate.

options.text: Note both cases with grade and rate, calculate the shortfall, and report them to your supervisor.
Tell the payroll team to fix the two workers' pay next month and record it done.
Note the two cases and tell your supervisor the pay looks low for their grades.
Mark all 40 as compliant since the large majority are paid the right rate.

advanced.situation: Several supervisors give written warnings that look harsh and inconsistent. You audit company practice for systemic risk and review one dismissal for approval.

options.text: Review the warnings one by one and approve those that follow the written policy.
Approve the dismissal and ask the supervisor to add missing warning records to the file.
Approve all the warnings to support the supervisors and raise the pattern next quarter.
Compare warnings with policy and past cases, find the pattern, and recommend training and review.

basic.situation: You gather basic documents and witness statements for a simple complaint about unpaid allowances, with help from a senior specialist.

options.text: Write the witnesses' statements yourself from what you expect they would say if asked.
Collect the pay slips and a written statement from the employee who complained.
Ask the witnesses to sign statements prepared in advance that support the company's position.
Collect pay slips, the contract and attendance records, and take dated statements from witnesses.

advanced.situation: You prepare for a high-stakes disciplinary hearing of a senior engineer accused of falsifying safety checks. You prepare evidence and witnesses and assess the hearing's risk.

options.text: Collect the check records and prepare witnesses with a written summary of what happened.
Tell witnesses what to say so the accounts match and the hearing runs quickly.
Prepare the evidence against the engineer and leave risk assessment for after the hearing.
Verify the check records, prepare witnesses on process, and assess the legal risks of each outcome.

basic.situation: You allocate 200 cartons of cleaning supplies between two warehouses. Warehouse A normally needs twice as many as B, but B just reported a surge in orders.

options.text: Send the usual two-thirds to A and one-third to B, and adjust next month.
Check both warehouses' current orders and split the cartons in proportion to the orders.
Send all 200 cartons to B, since it reported the surge, and tell A afterwards.
Check both warehouses' orders and stock, split the cartons by need, and hold a small reserve.

advanced.situation: You redesign how goods move from a port to five stores. Costs are high because trucks run half empty, and the stores want daily deliveries.

options.text: Analyse volumes per store, consolidate loads onto fixed routes, and pilot the change with stores.
Keep daily deliveries and ask the haulier to lower its rate for half-empty trucks.
Cut deliveries to the two smallest stores and tell them to collect goods themselves.
Move to deliveries every second day for all five stores to fill the trucks.

basic.situation: A contact at a retail customer calls to say a delivery was late. Your supervisor asks you to maintain the relationship and learn what they need.

options.text: Apologise and explain the cause of the delay, then pass their comments to your supervisor.
Apologise, ask what the delay affected, note their needs, and promise to update them by tomorrow.
Blame the driver by name and say he has been dismissed for the late delivery.
Tell them delays happen in this business and offer a discount on the next delivery.

advanced.situation: You review logistics performance with a key customer against the service agreement. On-time delivery was 91 percent against a 95 percent target, and the customer is upset.

options.text: Show the customer last year's better figure in place of the current quarter's actual results.
Present the 91 percent figure and promise to reach the 95 percent target next quarter.
Present the data, break down late-delivery causes, agree improvement steps, and set a follow-up date.
Point out that the 91 percent is close to the target and compare with industry results.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to report on the progress of a warehouse relocation project. Two of five phases are done, and one is delayed.

options.text: Report that two of five phases are done and one is behind schedule this week.
Report all five phases as on schedule until the delayed one has caught up.
Report the two finished phases, the delayed one and its cause, and the new dates.
Report that the project is mostly on track since one phase is slightly behind.

advanced.situation: Management is choosing between buying and leasing forklifts for a warehouse. You must perform a lifecycle cost analysis and assess the impact of a layout change.

options.text: Recommend leasing because it needs no large payment now and keeps the budget flexible.
Compare the purchase price with total lease payments over five years and recommend the cheaper.
Model purchase, lease, maintenance and resale costs over the full life, including the layout impact.
Recommend buying because the supplier's sales representative says purchased forklifts cost less overall.

basic.situation: You direct a small team of three logisticians and schedule this week's work. One member is on leave on Wednesday, when a large shipment arrives.

options.text: Reassign the absent member's tasks, set shipment priorities, and confirm the plan with the team.
Cancel the member's approved leave and ask him to work Wednesday for the large shipment.
Ask the two other members to cover Wednesday's tasks and treat the shipment as a priority.
Schedule the shipment handling on Wednesday and tell the team to manage with whoever is in.

advanced.situation: A subcontractor delivering to your warehouse keeps missing delivery windows. You review its proposals, set performance specifications, and act as liaison.

options.text: Add extra buffer time to the delivery windows in the schedule so the misses disappear.
Warn the subcontractor in writing that further missed windows will be reviewed at renewal.
Replace the subcontractor with a new one this week and tell them by email.
Meet the subcontractor, set measurable delivery windows in the specification, and track results weekly.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to explain a proposed new pick-and-pack process in a short written proposal for the warehouse team.

options.text: Copy a proposal from another company's process and change the names to ours.
Describe the benefits the manager hopes for as proven results from other warehouses already.
Describe the current problem, the proposed steps, the expected benefits, and what staff must do.
List the proposed steps in order and attach the manager's earlier slides for more detail.

advanced.situation: You develop a proposal for a customer's new distribution centre, with documentation for the cost estimates. The customer wants a fixed price by Friday, but some data is incomplete.

options.text: Give a fixed price with a large safety margin to cover the incomplete data.
Give a fixed price using the lowest estimates and fix the data gaps after signing.
Document assumptions, mark incomplete data, and offer a price range with conditions for fixing it.
Give a fixed price based on current data and note that incomplete items may change it.

basic.situation: You plan a logistics support activity, a monthly maintenance schedule for five forklifts. You have the manufacturer's manual and the service history.

options.text: Skip the manual's service steps that look unnecessary and shorten each forklift's service time.
Check the manual's intervals, review each service history, and set dates with spare cover.
Check the manual's intervals and set the same service date for all five forklifts.
Service the forklifts when they break down, since that saves on routine costs each month.

advanced.situation: You manage the logistics for a product nearing the end of its life. Spare parts are costly to store, and some customers still need support for two years.

options.text: Keep all spare parts in storage for two years and review the stock at the end.
Tell customers support ends next month and scrap the parts to avoid more storage costs.
Scrap the remaining parts now to stop storage costs and offer customers replacements later.
Forecast remaining demand, make one final parts order, and plan a phased sale of surplus.

basic.situation: You analyse warehouse inventory data for a supervisor. Last quarter, the inventory turns for one product dropped from 8 to 5.

options.text: Check data source and period, compare with stock and sales, and report the drop with causes.
Report the drop from 8 to 5 and suggest the warehouse team look into it.
Tell your supervisor the drop is seasonal, since sales often slow in that quarter.
Replace the low figure with the average of earlier quarters before sending the report.

advanced.situation: You design a supply chain for a new product line to limit cost and environmental impact. The cheapest route uses long-haul trucking, and rail costs 6 percent more.

options.text: Recommend trucking and describe the route as low-carbon in the customer proposal document.
Recommend trucking because it is cheapest, and add carbon offsets later if the customer requires.
Recommend the rail option because it cuts emissions, and note the extra 6 percent cost.
Model cost and emissions for each route, include delivery risks, and recommend the balanced option.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to identify cost-reduction opportunities in a packing process. You observe a shift and see packers walking long distances for materials.

options.text: Suggest moving materials closer to the packers and share the idea with your supervisor.
Tell the packers to use whatever materials are nearest, even if the size differs.
Suggest hiring more packers to make up for the time they spend walking each shift.
Record walking distances, suggest moving materials closer, and estimate the time this would save.

advanced.situation: You build a model to predict how a 20 percent fuel price rise would affect your fleet's annual costs. Management also wants carbon tax scenarios.

options.text: Apply last year's cost increase rate to this year's costs and present one figure.
Pick assumptions that show small cost increases so management approves the new fleet plan.
Build fuel and carbon tax scenarios, test sensitivity, and present ranges with stated assumptions.
Model the 20 percent fuel rise and add a single carbon tax estimate on top.

basic.situation: You are asked to develop specifications for a small warehouse's shelving layout. The supervisor gives you the floor plan and product list.

options.text: Group products by size and pick frequency, then draft aisle and shelf specifications from the plan.
Copy the shelving layout from another warehouse and adjust it to fit the walls.
Fill the floor plan with as many shelves as fit and specify narrow aisles.
Group products by size and draft the shelf specification from the floor plan provided.

advanced.situation: You write procedures to cut carbon output from moving materials between plants. Managers want a quick drop, but the fleet is old and contracts run two more years.

options.text: Write procedures requiring a switch to new trucks now and renegotiate the contracts later.
Start with route consolidation and driver training, plan fleet renewals at contract ends, and track emissions.
Write procedures that report carbon output for the cleanest routes and leave out older trucks.
Write procedures for route consolidation and driver training for all plants and review yearly.

basic.situation: You develop a cost forecast for next quarter's transport spending. Your supervisor gives you three months of invoices and a fuel price outlook.

options.text: Average the three months of invoices and add a percentage for expected fuel prices.
Use last quarter's total as next quarter's forecast and note that fuel may differ.
Set the forecast at the supervisor's budget figure and adjust the invoices to match it.
Group invoices by route, project volumes, apply the fuel outlook, and show your assumptions.

advanced.situation: You prepare a logistics strategy for a planned production facility and develop KPIs for business units. The facility will serve three regions with different delivery needs.

options.text: Propose one central distribution site for all regions and set KPIs on time and cost.
Map needs per region, propose a network design, and set KPIs linked to service and cost.
Set KPIs the business units can easily meet and describe the strategy as proven.
Copy the strategy of the existing facility and apply its KPIs to the new one.

basic.situation: You prepare basic documentation for a logistics reporting system. The system exports weekly data, and your supervisor wants a one-page guide for users.

options.text: Describe each report, its data source, update frequency, and who to contact with questions.
Copy the vendor's manual pages into the guide and put your own name on it.
Write the guide from your memory of how the system worked last year.
List the reports the system exports each week and explain how to open them.

advanced.situation: You direct logistics analysts and validate documentation on a new management information system. Two analysts disagree on how to define on-time delivery in the documents.

options.text: Pick the definition used by most customers and ask both analysts to use it.
Check customer contracts, define on-time delivery once in the documents, and explain why to both.
Let each analyst keep their own definition and note both of them in the documents.
Choose the definition that shows the better delivery rate and apply it to all reports.

basic.situation: A customer asks you to propose a simple logistics solution for moving 500 boxes monthly between two cities. A senior colleague is helping you.

options.text: Propose road transport because it is the most common option and give a price.
Propose the solution the company used for a similar customer and quote the same price.
Compare road and rail costs and times, propose the better fit, and have it reviewed.
Propose air freight at a price lower than our cost to win the customer's business.

advanced.situation: A manufacturer asks you to recommend logistics technology for its production. Vendors promise big savings from tracking tools, and the manufacturer's data is scattered across systems.

options.text: Recommend buying the tool this month and tell the manufacturer the savings are guaranteed.
Recommend the vendor tool with the largest promised savings and quote the vendor's figures.
Recommend the vendor tool with the most features and suggest cleaning the data afterwards.
Assess data readiness, define requirements, trial two vendor tools, and recommend a phased rollout.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to compute last month's on-time delivery rate. There were 400 deliveries, and the log marks 36 as late.

options.text: Report 100 percent on time because the 36 late ones were all minor delays.
Report 90 percent, rounding down to be safe, since 36 is close to 40 late deliveries.
Divide the 364 on-time deliveries by 400 and report 91 percent to your supervisor.
Divide the 364 on-time deliveries by 400, give 91 percent, and note how late is defined.

advanced.situation: You develop predictive models to forecast demand. A new product launch has no sales history, and the planning team wants one number by Monday.

options.text: Use the sales of the closest earlier product as the single number and say so.
Use the launch target from the marketing plan as the forecast and call it modelled.
Use similar past launches, build a range forecast with assumptions, and update it weekly.
Ask the sales team for a number they are comfortable with and use it.

basic.situation: You contact carriers for rates and schedules for a weekly shipment from Penang to Johor, under supervision. Your supervisor gave you three carrier contacts.

options.text: Ask the carrier your team used last time and send your supervisor its quote.
Send all three carriers the same shipment details, compare their replies, and share a table.
Tell the carriers a lower rate was offered by others to pressure them into a discount.
Ask two carriers for rates and schedules and send your supervisor the cheaper one.

advanced.situation: You manage relationships with global carriers and optimise multi-modal schedules. An ocean carrier announces a two-week delay on a key route, and air freight is expensive.

options.text: Identify affected orders, rank by urgency, move urgent ones to air or rail, and inform customers.
Move all affected orders to air freight so that no customer experiences a delay.
Keep the ocean booking and tell customers the delay is the carrier's responsibility alone.
Cancel the carrier's contract this week and book spot rates for every route it serves.

basic.situation: You enter 60 delivery records into the logistics database from paper slips, following written instructions. Some slips have smudged quantities.

options.text: Enter the smudged quantities as the numbers look most likely to you at a glance.
Enter the clear slips and leave the smudged ones in a pile for later.
Enter the clear slips, flag the smudged ones, and ask the sender to confirm quantities.
Enter the average quantity from earlier slips for each smudged record to finish today.

advanced.situation: You design a logistics reporting database for the organisation. Three departments track shipments separately with different codes, and their reports conflict.

options.text: Pick the largest department's codes and overwrite the other departments' records to match them.
Keep three separate databases and create a monthly report that combines them by hand.
Build one database and ask each department to convert its own codes by quarter end.
Agree common codes with the departments, build one database with access rules, and migrate data carefully.

basic.situation: You monitor industry trends and standards for your team. This week, a newsletter claims a new packaging standard will apply to all exports from January.

options.text: Find the official notice, confirm the date and scope, and share the verified details.
Update the team's export checklist now to include the new packaging standard from January.
Check a second news source for the claim and share it as confirmed if both agree.
Share the newsletter item with the team and say it still needs to be checked.

advanced.situation: You develop a demand forecasting model and revise the SOP for monthly inventory ordering. The old SOP uses a flat reorder point that causes stock-outs in peak months.

options.text: Raise the flat reorder point for all months and update the SOP to match.
Remove the reorder point from the SOP and let planners order whatever they want.
Build a seasonal forecast, set monthly reorder points, update the SOP, and trial it.
Keep the SOP and ask planners to order extra stock before the peak months themselves.

basic.situation: You recommend simple improvements to a distribution process under supervision. Trucks wait 90 minutes at the loading dock because paperwork is checked after loading.

options.text: Suggest checking paperwork before loading to shorten the wait for trucks at the dock.
Suggest adding a second loading dock so trucks can be handled at the same time.
Suggest skipping the paperwork check for regular drivers to save time at the dock.
Time the waits, show paperwork checks cause them, and suggest checking before loading.

advanced.situation: Pricing in a customer's contract does not cover rising fuel and handling costs. You confer with the logistics management team on service levels and costs.

options.text: Reduce the service levels in the contract to cut costs and keep the price unchanged.
Absorb the cost gap in the logistics budget by moving it to other customers' invoices.
Raise the contract price by the average cost increase and inform the customer in writing.
Show the cost gap by component, propose a price adjustment clause, and test service level options.

basic.situation: A customer asks where its parcel is. You track product flow using the tracking tool, and the parcel shows no scan for two days.

options.text: Tell the customer the parcel is moving normally since parcels often skip scans in transit.
Tell the customer the tool shows no scan for two days and you are investigating.
Tell the customer the parcel was delivered yesterday to ease their worry about it.
Check the last scan location, ask the carrier for status, and update the customer with findings.

advanced.situation: You use a web-based system to monitor global container flows. The system shows 120 containers at a hub, but the hub's own records show 105.

options.text: Report the lower figure of 105 as the stock and note the system may be stale.
Delete the 15 extra containers from the system records so the two figures agree.
Ask the hub to recount the containers and update your record to match the count.
Compare container IDs on both lists, trace the 15 unmatched ones, and update the records.

basic.situation: Your senior manager asks you to draft a schedule for a website launch project. You have the task list, and the launch date is six weeks away.

options.text: List tasks with durations and owners and fit them evenly into the six weeks available.
Mark all tasks as starting today and finishing on time, and tell owners afterwards.
List tasks with durations and owners, order them by dependency, and add some buffer time.
Copy the schedule from the last website project and change the dates to this launch.

advanced.situation: A client requests a major scope change midway through a project. It would delay delivery by three weeks, and the team says it is doable. You approve plan changes.

options.text: Tell the client the change fits the original deadline and settle the schedule later.
Accept the change and ask the team to catch up on the delay by working weekends.
Assess the impact on time and cost, get written client approval, and update the plan.
Accept the change, extend the deadline by three weeks, and inform the client by email.

basic.situation: You log project costs and compare them with the budget, with help. This month, travel costs reached 90 percent of the yearly budget with six months left.

options.text: Move some travel costs to the training budget line to keep travel under control.
Log the costs and wait to see whether travel spending slows down by next month.
Log the costs, flag that travel is 90 percent used, and ask your lead.
Log the costs and mention in your report that travel is running high this year.

advanced.situation: You set budget standards for a programme and prepare cost reports. Two project managers report spending on different bases, so the totals do not reconcile.

options.text: Adjust one manager's figures so the totals match and send the report to finance.
Pick the basis used by the larger project and ask the other manager to switch.
Define one cost basis, reconcile past reports with both managers, and issue a standard template.
Report both bases side by side and note that the totals do not match yet.

basic.situation: You draft a status update and attend the meeting with a supervisor present. The project is on schedule but 5 percent over budget.

options.text: Send the supervisor the budget and schedule figures and let her decide what to say.
State the project is on schedule and within budget, since the overrun is small.
State the schedule is on track, the budget is 5 percent over, and why.
State the project is on track overall and leave the budget details for the supervisor.

advanced.situation: A client threatens to reject a deliverable because it lacks a feature that was never in the signed requirements. You lead the negotiation and set communication standards.

options.text: Edit the requirements document to include the feature and show it to the client.
Add the feature quickly at the project's own cost to keep the client happy.
Show the client the signed requirements and explain that the feature cannot be added now.
Show the signed requirements, acknowledge the need, offer a priced change request, and document the talk.

basic.situation: You assign simple tasks to four team members for a product demo and check in as directed. One member seems overloaded.

options.text: Ask the overloaded member which task could go to someone else and pass it on.
Review everyone's workloads, move a task from the overloaded member, and tell your lead.
Keep the assignments and ask the overloaded member to work late until the demo.
Give the overloaded member two more tasks, since the demo is close and he is capable.

advanced.situation: A senior team member keeps missing deadlines, and a supplier has not delivered a key part. You give performance feedback and negotiate for materials. The project deadline is firm.

options.text: Tell the team member off in the team meeting and wait for the supplier to call.
Give the team member written feedback and ask the supplier to hurry the delivery.
Talk privately with the member, agree a plan, and negotiate a firm date with the supplier.
Take over the member's tasks yourself and buy the part from another supplier at any price.

basic.situation: You track simple milestones and join project meetings with a lead. Milestone three was due Friday, and the team says it is 90 percent complete.

options.text: Change the milestone's due date to a later date so that it is not late.
Mark the milestone as complete since most of the work is finished and move on.
Ask what the remaining 10 percent involves, get a finish date, and update the tracker.
Mark the milestone as nearly complete in the tracker and note the team's estimate.

advanced.situation: You define milestone criteria for a complex software and hardware project and facilitate the team. Deliverables are tracked inconsistently, and some count as done when started.

options.text: Count deliverables as done once work has started to keep the progress charts looking healthy.
Define measurable done criteria per deliverable, agree them with the team, and show how to update.
Define done criteria for each milestone and email them to the whole team today.
Ask each member to explain in meetings what done means for their own tasks.

basic.situation: You help review vendor lists and schedule vendor interviews for a printing contract, with guidance. Three vendors bid, and one is the manager's relative.

options.text: Drop the other two vendors from the schedule since the manager prefers his relative.
Tell your lead about the relative, schedule all three interviews, and let the lead decide.
Schedule all three interviews and say nothing since the manager knows his own family.
Schedule all three interviews and mention the relationship to the manager at the start.

advanced.situation: You set vendor selection criteria for a project. A vendor offers you a personal gift if it is selected, and the decision deadline is Friday.

options.text: Accept the gift and rank the vendor higher in the scoring as a thank you.
Return the gift later and keep the vendor in the process on its merits.
Decline the gift, report the offer, and score all vendors against the agreed criteria.
Decline the gift and score all vendors against the agreed criteria as originally planned.

basic.situation: Your lead asks you to learn why claims approvals are slow in one unit. The unit head can give you one afternoon.

options.text: Use step times from a similar unit's earlier study to fill in the findings table.
Copy the process chart from the staff manual and mark it as current practice.
Watch two approvals from start to finish and confirm each step with the staff.
Ask the unit head to explain each approval step and write the process down.

advanced.situation: You must plan data collection for an audit across finance, procurement and logistics. Each department keeps records in a different format, and none has spare staff.

options.text: Reuse last year's figures for any department that is slow to respond.
Visit each department, observe its process and note findings in that team's own format.
Request raw exports from each department and combine them yourself after all have arrived.
Agree one common template with each department and pilot it in one team first.

basic.situation: Your data shows returns take four days to process at the north branch and two days at the south branch. Your supervisor asks what it suggests.

options.text: Tell your supervisor the north branch staff are slower and should be warned.
Check whether both branches count days the same way, then compare workloads and steps.
Propose adding two staff to the north branch to bring its return time down.
Report that the north branch is slower and suggest copying the south branch's routine.

advanced.situation: Order approval delays cost about two days per order. Sales wants the approval limits removed, while finance wants every order checked. You have the waiting-time data for last quarter.

options.text: Back sales and remove the limits for the top ten customers until a review.
Map where orders wait and propose tiered limits with extra checks for large orders.
Suggest a second approver on shifts when delays are longest and review after a month.
Back finance and suggest hiring one more approver to clear the queue faster.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to outline the scope of a study on how the stores team handles stock requests. The study must finish within three weeks.

options.text: Copy the scope from a past study of the payroll team and change the names.
Cover the whole supply chain from supplier to store so no problem is left out.
List the stock request problems staff mention and use that list as the scope.
Draft a scope naming the request types covered, the data needed and weekly milestones.

advanced.situation: You are planning a study of production and costing across two plants. Plant A holds a full year of data, but Plant B holds just three months.

options.text: Ask Plant B to build a full year of data before the study begins.
Compare the plants over their shared three months and test seasonality using Plant A's year.
Scale up Plant B's three months to a full year and compare it with Plant A.
Use the shared three months for both plants and note the limit in the report.

basic.situation: A new clerk asks where signed supplier contracts go. Your department's records guideline says contracts are filed in the locked cabinet and logged in the register.

options.text: Tell the clerk to follow the guideline and file the contract in the locked cabinet.
Walk the clerk through the guideline, then file and log the contract together.
File the contract in the cabinet now and add the register entry at week's end.
Keep the contract on the clerk's desk where the team can read it easily.

advanced.situation: You are rolling out a records program across five offices. Managers say the new retention and access rules slow their staff, and some ask you to waive the first audit.

options.text: Explain why the rules exist to the managers and keep the audit as planned.
Meet the managers to find the slow steps, simplify them, and keep the audit schedule.
Waive the audit for offices with good past records and tell head office afterwards.
Delay the audit by one month so the offices can adjust to the new rules.

basic.situation: A user tells you the monthly leave form is confusing because two boxes ask for dates. Your supervisor asks you to review the form and report back.

options.text: Watch three users fill in the form and note where they hesitate.
Tell the user to read the instructions on page two before filling in dates.
Delete one date box from the master form and replace the live copy today.
Compare the form with the leave policy and mark any boxes that repeat information.

advanced.situation: Finance proposes a new expense claim form with six extra fields. Branch staff say it will double their claim time. You have the authority to approve form changes.

options.text: Trial the form with branch staff, cut unused fields, then approve a shorter version.
Approve the form and require every past claim to be resubmitted on it.
Approve the form and ask branches to send feedback after the first month.
Reject the form and ask finance to keep using the current claim form.

basic.situation: A new expense-claim form goes live on Monday. You are asked to write a one-page guide for staff and support the short training session.

options.text: Present the new form in training and tell staff to ask questions afterwards.
Write the steps in order with an example form and test it on a colleague.
Update the old guide's title to the new form and send it to staff.
Copy the form's printed instructions into a one-page guide and hand it out.

advanced.situation: A new scheduling system goes live for 300 staff next month. Pilot users say supervisors keep using the old spreadsheet, and you lead the training.

options.text: Meet supervisors to learn why they keep the spreadsheet, then train them on those gaps.
Delete the old spreadsheet from the shared drive before supervisors have switched over.
Run extra training for all 300 staff on the full system before the launch date.
Ask the project sponsor to order supervisors to stop using the spreadsheet by launch.

basic.situation: You inspect a hotel ballroom booked for a 200-guest seminar. The client's checklist requires a working projector, a wheelchair ramp and clear aisle space.

options.text: Compare the room against the hotel's brochure and record that it matches the checklist.
Go through the client checklist item by item in the room and photograph each result.
Copy the ticks from last month's inspection of the same ballroom to save time.
Confirm the projector works and ask the hotel to confirm the other items by email.

advanced.situation: Your conference ended with complaints about long registration queues and a catering shortage. The client wants a review, and your team will run next year's event too.

options.text: Send the client the attendee survey scores and promise to fix the queue problem.
Hold a team debrief and list the lessons learned in a short report.
Combine survey results, staff notes and vendor logs, then set targets for next year.
Blame the caterer in the report and drop that vendor from future events.

basic.situation: A caterer's invoice for the staff dinner shows 120 meals, but your attendance sheet shows 105 guests. Your supervisor asks you to review it before payment.

options.text: Query the extra 15 meals with the caterer and pay the amount for 105 meals.
Pay the invoice as billed, since a few extra meals are normal, and note the gap.
Ask the caterer for its meal records and hold payment until the gap is explained.
Change the attendance sheet to 120 guests so that the figures match the invoice.

advanced.situation: A client gives you a fixed budget of RM60,000 for a two-day product launch. Their wish list adds up to about RM80,000, and the date cannot move.

options.text: Ask the client to increase the budget to RM80,000 to cover the full list.
Propose a shorter one-day format that keeps the main sessions within RM60,000.
Rank the wish list with the client and cut lower priorities to fit the budget.
Plan the full wish list and bill the extra RM20,000 after the event.

basic.situation: You keep the event file for a training day. A supplier hands you a handwritten receipt for RM450 of printing, with no company name or date on it.

options.text: Record the RM450 in the budget sheet and keep the receipt to file later.
File the handwritten receipt and add a note saying who gave it to you.
Ask the supplier for a proper receipt with company name and date before filing it.
Fill in the missing name and date yourself from the quotation so the file is complete.

advanced.situation: You must choose an audio-visual company for a 500-person conference. Company A is cheapest, Company B knows the venue, and Company C has the strongest references.

options.text: Choose Company A since the saving can go towards other event needs.
Choose Company B since it knows the venue and the setup should go smoothly.
Score all three against the client's requirements and contact each one's recent references.
Sign Company C this week on the strength of its website to secure the date.

basic.situation: A speaker's workshop at tomorrow's seminar needs a projector and two microphones. The hotel's equipment list shows one projector and one microphone free that day.

options.text: Confirm the projector in writing and arrange a rental for the second microphone.
Book the free equipment and tell the speaker to bring a second microphone.
Borrow a microphone from the hall next door while that event is on break.
Ask the speaker whether one microphone is enough and then confirm the projector.

advanced.situation: A convention for 1,500 delegates uses four hotels. Shuttle times, meals and sessions clash for delegates with mobility needs, and three vendors each sent different schedules.

options.text: Cancel the earliest session so the clashes disappear and tell delegates on arrival.
Assign extra staff to guide delegates with mobility needs between the hotels.
Merge the schedules into one master timeline and check each mobility need against it.
Ask each vendor to confirm its schedule in writing and flag any clashes to you.

basic.situation: A school wants a fun sports day but gives no other details. You have a first meeting with the school's coordinator tomorrow.

options.text: Ask the coordinator to email a full written brief before you meet.
Plan a general sports day with standard activities and send the quotation tonight.
Bring a sample sports-day plan from last year and ask the coordinator to react.
Prepare questions on numbers, budget, activities and safety to ask at the meeting.

advanced.situation: A hotel offers a conference venue deal with a large cancellation fee after 30 days. Your client cannot confirm attendance until two weeks before the event.

options.text: Sign the deal as offered and plan to cover any cancellation fee from other lines.
Accept the terms and ask the client to confirm attendance within 30 days.
Ask the hotel to hold extra rooms free of charge until the client confirms.
Negotiate a sliding cancellation fee tied to confirmed attendance and a later final-number date.

basic.situation: You help hire 10 volunteers to staff registration at a charity run. Applicants are students and retirees, the run is on Sunday and the briefing is on Saturday.

options.text: Brief them on tasks and safety, then pair each new volunteer with an experienced one.
Assign tasks on Sunday morning as volunteers arrive and explain the cash box then.
Send all volunteers the instruction sheet and ask them to read it before Saturday.
Let any volunteer who arrives early handle the cash box to speed up registration.

advanced.situation: You direct a three-day forum with five new team members. Registration emails are piling up, promotional material is late to the printer and the finance log is incomplete.

options.text: List the three jobs by deadline, assign owners, and set a short daily check-in.
Close the inbox to attendee queries until the printing and finance log are finished.
Handle the printer and finance tasks yourself and leave emails to the newest staff.
Ask the whole team to work late until all three jobs are completed.

basic.situation: You design a poster for a charity walk next month. The organiser gave you the date, venue and registration link, and the poster needs approval by Friday.

options.text: Add a large photo and a catchy slogan and leave smaller details for the website.
Check every detail against the organiser's brief and send a draft for review on Thursday.
Print the poster now using last year's registration link to meet the deadline.
Use last year's poster layout and update the date and venue for this year.

advanced.situation: A junior colleague's press release for your gala says the charity has helped 10,000 families. Your records show 6,200 families helped this year and 10,000 across all years.

options.text: Change the claim to 6,200 families helped this year and send it out.
Keep the claim, since all-time totals are normal in charity releases, and add a footnote.
Send the release as written, since the gala is tomorrow and journalists are waiting.
Revise the release to give both figures with their time periods and check them with finance.

basic.situation: A donor gave RM500 to the school-building fund last week. Your supervisor asks you to write a thank-you letter for today's mail.

options.text: Send a short email saying thanks because letters take longer to prepare.
Name the donor and the gift, say what it will fund, and ask for review.
Add a request for a larger gift next year and post it today.
Use the standard thank-you template and fill in the donor's name before posting.
