advanced.situation: A company director asks whether donating RM20,000 through her business can be deducted from tax. Your charity's tax-exempt letter is on file, but you are not a tax adviser.

options.text: Send her the exemption letter and a donation receipt template to review herself.
Explain what the receipt and exemption letter cover and suggest she confirm with her adviser.
Offer to backdate the receipt to last year so she can claim in the earlier year.
Tell her the full RM20,000 is deductible since the charity holds a tax-exempt letter.

basic.situation: You help track the budget of a school appeal. The monthly expense report shows printing costs of RM1,200 against a budget of RM800.

options.text: Remove the extra printing invoices from the report until next month's budget starts.
Check what caused the extra printing cost and report the variance to your supervisor.
Mark the line over budget in red and send the report to your supervisor.
Wait to see if next month's printing costs are lower before raising the overspend.

advanced.situation: Your annual appeal raised 20 percent less than last year. Donor numbers are stable, but average gifts dropped, and the board wants a new plan within a month.

options.text: Email all donors again with a stronger appeal before the month ends.
Tell the board the drop comes from the economy and cut next year's target.
Segment donors by gift size, test higher suggested amounts with one group, and report results.
Add a second appeal letter for lapsed donors and present the plan to the board.

basic.situation: You assist with a silent auction for a hospice. Your supervisor gives you a list of 30 donated items to arrange on display tables.

options.text: Group items by type, prepare bid sheets with start prices, and check the layout.
Remove the donor names from the items and bid sheets so the display looks simpler.
Display the most valuable items first and leave the smaller ones in boxes.
Set starting prices from online listings and print the bid sheets for approval.

advanced.situation: A bank offers RM50,000 sponsorship for your charity dinner but wants its logo on the main stage and a speaking slot for its CEO. The dinner programme is already full.

options.text: Accept the logo request and decline the speaking slot to protect the programme.
Propose logo placement and a short CEO welcome, then adjust the programme with the committee.
Accept both requests now and tell the committee to remove two other speakers.
Ask the bank to raise the sponsorship before agreeing to any speaking slot.

basic.situation: While updating the donor database you find two entries for Mr Lim Wei Han with the same phone number but different addresses. Your supervisor is away until Monday.

options.text: Flag both entries, check gift records, and ask your supervisor to confirm the merge.
Update the address from the more recent entry and keep both records.
Delete the older entry so that the database has one record for him.
Leave both entries as they are until your supervisor returns on Monday.

advanced.situation: You must submit a grant application with donor and programme data. The funder's rules say all figures must come from audited accounts, but the latest audit is two years old.

options.text: Use the audited figures, label their year, and add current figures in a separate note.
Update the audited figures yourself to this year's levels so that they look current.
Present current internal figures as the main data and attach the older audit.
Ask the funder if unaudited current figures are allowed, and use the audited ones meanwhile.

basic.situation: You help recruit volunteers for a charity fun run. You posted the call on social media, and only 12 of the 40 needed have signed up so far.

options.text: Contact past volunteers and local student groups with the date, tasks and sign-up link.
Lower the volunteer target to 12 and tell your supervisor the event will be smaller.
Repost the call on social media with a reminder of the closing date.
Add friends' names to the volunteer list so the target looks met.

advanced.situation: An online auction closes tonight, and your manager, who is travelling, has said the closing time must stay. Two volunteers report payment errors and bidders ask about delivery.

options.text: Message your manager and wait for instructions before taking any action.
Handle the platform provider yourself and leave bidder questions until the auction closes.
Extend the closing time by a day to give volunteers time to fix errors.
Have one volunteer report errors to the platform provider and another answer bidders.

basic.situation: You interview a clerk to write a job description. She describes duties her supervisor has not mentioned and says some tasks are missing from the current description.

options.text: Keep the supervisor's list of duties because it is the official record for the role.
Copy the duties from a similar job advert online and drop her extra tasks.
Add all her duties to the job description and send the draft to her supervisor.
Record her duties, then verify them with her supervisor and a peer.

advanced.situation: A company merges two teams and needs a new role defined. Managers disagree on what the role does, and you must design the job analysis tools and run a focus group.

options.text: Draft a task checklist and questionnaire, then hold a focus group with staff.
Run a focus group with the managers who disagree and record their final views.
Write the role description yourself from the senior manager's view to end the dispute.
Use the questionnaire from the last job analysis and update the job title for this role.

basic.situation: You calculate pay for a new clerk grade. The salary guideline sets starting pay at RM2,400 plus RM150 per year of relevant experience. A candidate has four years.

options.text: Calculate RM2,400 plus four years at RM150 each, giving RM3,000, and record the working.
Offer RM2,400 starting pay and say experience may raise it later in the year.
Ask the candidate to send her payslips first and then decide the pay.
Apply the pay of the last similar hire in the department, whatever the guideline says.

advanced.situation: A union asks for a 6 percent pay rise. You must run a cost analysis for management, using payroll data that covers three grades with different headcounts and overtime patterns.

options.text: Apply 6 percent to total basic pay for all grades and add a note about overtime.
Show management the lowest cost estimate to help it settle the talks quickly.
Model cost grade by grade with overtime and benefits across a range of cases.
Copy last year's cost model for a 5 percent rise and adjust the final figure.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to help draft a one-page policy for overtime meal allowances. She gives you last year's draft and the finance limits.

options.text: Revise the draft to match the finance limits, add examples and send it for review.
Raise the limits in the draft a little to match what staff expect to receive.
Fill in the finance limits in last year's draft, tidy the wording and send it back.
Write a new policy from templates you found online and send it to your manager.

advanced.situation: Your company wants an equal opportunity programme to raise women's representation in senior roles. Managers worry about fairness, and you must design how success will be measured.

options.text: Set a target for women in senior roles and report progress each year.
Define baseline numbers and selection criteria, set yearly targets, and review results.
Add bonus points to women candidates' promotion scores to improve the numbers quickly.
Run a survey of staff views on fairness and design the programme from the results.

basic.situation: Your legal team's note says overtime payments must be reported each month. The company's policy says they are reported once a year, and you are checking the policy.

options.text: Flag the mismatch to your manager and draft a policy change to monthly reporting.
Keep the yearly report and note that the legal team's note may be outdated.
Add a monthly reminder to the payroll calendar and leave the policy text as it is.
Ask a colleague in payroll how the yearly report has been handled in past years.

advanced.situation: An employee complains that she is graded lower than a colleague doing the same work. Her manager says the grading was fair, and you advise on the complaint alone.

options.text: Compare both job descriptions and grading records, then explain your finding to both.
Move her to the same grade as the colleague to settle the complaint.
Ask the manager for the reasons behind the grading and pass them to her.
Tell her the grading follows the company structure and she can apply for promotion.

basic.situation: Your manager is preparing for a negotiation with the staff union and asks you to prepare the documents. The union has sent its list of ten demands.

options.text: Collect last year's agreement and the pay data and leave the analysis to your manager.
Summarise each demand with its cost and link it to current policy and past agreements.
Copy the demands into a table and add the current policy beside each one.
Remove the demands that look unrealistic from the table before your manager sees it.

advanced.situation: Negotiations with a union have stalled over shift allowances. Management says it cannot pay more, and union representatives say members will refuse overtime on Friday.

options.text: Bring both sides together and ask each to restate its position in writing.
Ask management for a small allowance rise to calm the union before Friday.
Warn union representatives that members who refuse overtime on Friday will face disciplinary action.
Meet each side privately to find priorities, then propose a trade-off like phased increases.

basic.situation: You update the staff handbook after a policy change that adds two paid leave days. Your supervisor gave you the new leave table to put in section 4.

options.text: Remove the old leave table and leave section 4 blank until staff ask about it.
Update the leave table in section 4 and check other sections that mention leave days.
Add a note at the front of the handbook announcing the two days.
Replace the leave table in section 4 with the new one and save the file.

advanced.situation: You design a half-day workshop for 40 supervisors on the new performance-pay scheme. Their experience varies and the scheme starts next month.

options.text: Give supervisors a short summary and tell them to use their own judgement on payouts.
Present the scheme rules slide by slide and leave time at the end for questions.
Check what supervisors already know, build scenario exercises, and pilot the workshop.
Send the scheme document to all supervisors and invite them to a drop-in session.

basic.situation: You must schedule a two-day safety class for 25 staff. Room 2 is free both days, but its projector is booked out on day two. The trainer is free both days.

options.text: Book the room with a projector both days, or borrow one for Room 2.
Book Room 2 for both days and ask the trainer to use handouts on day two.
Take the projector from the booked event, since your class is more important.
Move the class to next month, when the room and projector will both be free.

advanced.situation: You must run an orientation for 200 new hires across three sites in one week. Sites have different shifts, and head office wants a common core message.

options.text: Let each site design its own orientation and send head office a summary afterwards.
Email a recorded presentation to every site and ask managers to share it.
Build a common core module and adapt delivery times and examples to each site.
Run the full orientation at head office and ask sites to send staff in groups.

basic.situation: An instructor sends you a 20-page handout for a customer service course. The training policy says handouts must be in plain language and no more than ten pages.

options.text: Shorten the font and margins so the handout fits ten pages, then print it.
Mark the long, complex parts against the policy and return it with comments.
Approve the handout as it is because the content is accurate and print it.
Ask the instructor to cut the handout to ten pages and resend it.

advanced.situation: A sales course shows no gain in test scores after two months. Trainers say the content is fine, while learners say sessions are too long and passive.

options.text: Add a longer quiz at the end of each session to raise scores.
Shorten every session by half but keep the same slides and trainers.
Review feedback and test results, then trial shorter, practice-based sessions with one group.
Change the test questions to easier ones so that the scores show improvement.

basic.situation: You must find out what training new call-centre agents need. The manager says agents struggle with billing questions, and you have a week.

options.text: Interview the manager and two team leaders about the billing problems they see.
Copy the training needs list from another company's call centre report.
Use the manager's view and plan a billing course for all agents.
Survey agents, review billing call notes and confirm findings with the manager.

advanced.situation: Your company must train 300 staff on a new safety procedure within six weeks. Staff are on six sites, and travel costs have risen.

options.text: Choose in-person sessions at head office since practical training works better there.
Choose virtual sessions for all six sites because they cost less than travel.
Email the procedure to all 300 staff and record them as trained once opened.
Compare cost and results of in-person, virtual and mixed delivery for each site.

basic.situation: You deliver a one-hour session on workplace email to 15 staff. Halfway through, you notice several people are looking at their phones.

options.text: Ask a few staff direct questions about the content to bring them back.
Tell the people on their phones to leave and return next week.
Pause and set a short group exercise where pairs rewrite a poor email together.
Speed up and finish the slides early so the session ends before time.

advanced.situation: You design a leadership programme for staff who may become supervisors. The budget is small, and the managers want results within a year.

options.text: Combine mentoring, stretch tasks and short workshops, and track readiness for each participant.
Promise staff supervisor posts after the programme to keep them motivated.
Copy a large company's programme and ask managers to find extra funds for it.
Run a series of monthly workshops on leadership topics for selected staff.

basic.situation: After each training session you must record attendance and feedback scores. A manager asks you to leave out the low scores from last week's session in the summary.

options.text: Remove the low scores from the summary as the manager asked this morning.
Record all scores as collected and add a note on possible causes.
Tell the manager you will average the scores and not list individual ones.
Send the manager the full table and let her decide how to present it.

advanced.situation: A new instructor's feedback scores are 30 percent lower than his peers, and learners say he reads from slides. He is booked to teach a key course next week.

options.text: Post the scores of all instructors on the staff board to encourage improvement.
Replace him next week and ask him to attend a class first.
Observe one session, share specific feedback, and refer him to a facilitation class.
Send him a skills class link and keep him on the schedule as planned.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to keep up with developments in workplace learning. You have an hour each week and a stack of journals.

options.text: Forward the journals to the team and ask them to tell you what matters.
Pick two journals, note useful ideas each week, and share one with the team monthly.
Read one journal your manager likes and keep the rest on the shelf.
Read the summaries of every journal and mark articles to read later.

advanced.situation: A client asks you to guarantee that its sales staff will raise sales by 20 percent after your training. Your fee is RM30,000 and the client has not given baseline sales data.

options.text: Promise the 20 percent increase in the contract to win the work.
Refuse to promise anything and offer a standard course at the standard fee.
Agree learning goals, collect baseline data and link part of the fee to results.
Offer to track sales for three months and report the changes found.

basic.situation: You collect age and income data from a store's loyalty-card records for a market report. Some records show ages of 0, and others are blank.

options.text: Keep all records in the age analysis and mention the zero ages in the report.
Flag the invalid ages, leave them out of the age analysis, and note how many.
Delete every customer record with a blank or zero value and continue the analysis.
Replace the zero and blank ages with a typical age so the charts look complete.

advanced.situation: Monthly sales rose 15 percent in the last quarter, and your manager asks you to forecast next year's sales. You have three years of monthly data.

options.text: Check for seasonality, then forecast with ranges and note what could change the trend.
Extend the last quarter's 15 percent growth through all months of next year.
Use the target sales figure set by the sales team as the forecast.
Fit a trend line to the three years of monthly data and report the forecast.

basic.situation: You gather competitor prices for a report. A rival's website lists a product at RM89, but a shopper's photo of its shelf label in store shows RM99.

options.text: Use the lower price in the table so that your client's price looks competitive.
Use the website price since it is public and easy to cite.
Use the average of the two prices in the comparison table.
Record both prices with sources and dates and check one against the store.

advanced.situation: Your team follows industry news from many sources, and each analyst records trends differently. A client wants a quarterly view of competitors and market position.

options.text: Ask each analyst to submit trend notes in their own format by the quarter end.
Write the quarterly view from the competitors' own press releases and promotional posts.
Buy one industry report and use it as the base for the quarterly view.
Set a common template and source list, assign owners and review trend notes each quarter.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to hand out a paper questionnaire to shoppers at the mall entrance. You notice that question 5 can be read two ways.

options.text: Hand out the questionnaire and note which shoppers asked about question 5.
Hand out the questionnaire and explain question 5 to shoppers who seem unsure.
Tell your supervisor about question 5 and suggest a clearer wording before handing out.
Rewrite question 5 yourself on the printed copies in pen and continue.

advanced.situation: You design a survey of 2,000 customers on advertising needs across three regions. Response rates are expected to be low in one region, and interviewers are new.

options.text: Increase the sample in the low-response region and train interviewers on the script.
Fill the low-response region's quota with answers collected from the other two regions.
Plan samples by region, pilot the survey and train interviewers on a script.
Send the survey online to all three regions in place of interviews.

basic.situation: You enter satisfaction scores from 120 customer surveys into a sheet. Some scores are written as 'ok' instead of a number.

options.text: Treat each 'ok' as 3 out of 5 and total all 120 scores.
List the unclear entries and ask the supervisor how to treat them before totalling.
Convert each 'ok' to 5 out of 5 since customers who say ok are satisfied.
Leave the unclear scores out of the total and mention how many there were.

advanced.situation: A campaign raised website visits by 40 percent, but sales did not change. The agency says the campaign succeeded, and your team must evaluate it for the client.

options.text: Report the 40 percent visit gain as success and mention the flat sales.
Survey visitors to learn why they did not buy and add this to the report.
Accept the agency's evaluation and forward it to the client under your name.
Track visits through to purchases, compare against past campaigns and report effects on sales.

basic.situation: You format a table of survey results for a report. It has eight columns, many decimals and no title. The report goes to the manager at noon.

options.text: Paste the table in as exported and tell the manager it is the raw result.
Add a title and clear labels and leave the numbers exactly as exported.
Delete the columns that look confusing so the table fits on one page.
Round to one decimal, add a title and labels, and group the less important columns.

advanced.situation: You must present complex survey findings to executives. The results show three segments with different needs, and the executives have ten minutes.

options.text: Summarise the segments in a long paragraph of text and read it aloud.
Use one chart per segment with a plain headline, and give detail in an appendix.
Show the full results table and talk through each number in turn.
Present the segment that matches the existing plan and leave the others out.

basic.situation: At a staff meeting, managers discuss a price rise for your company's bottled drinks. Your supervisor asks you to take notes on what is decided.

options.text: Leave notes until the end and write the decisions from memory afterwards.
Note decisions, owners and dates, then send a summary to your supervisor afterwards.
Note the new prices from the slides and leave the discussion out.
Write down everything said in order and give your supervisor the full notes.

advanced.situation: You lead a conference on a promotional proposal for a new product. Sales and finance disagree on discounts, and your survey interviewers have data on price sensitivity.

options.text: Let sales and finance debate and report their final positions to the executives.
Ask sales and finance to give their cases and then take a vote.
Present the price data, set out both views and agree next steps.
Back the sales view and drop the price data that disagrees with it.

basic.situation: You set up an email promotion for a sale starting Friday. The list has 5,000 subscribers, and 200 of them unsubscribed last week.

options.text: Add the unsubscribed contacts back to the list so the sale reaches more people.
Remove the unsubscribed addresses, send a test email to staff, and check the links.
Delay the email until Monday so the list can be cleaned up properly first.
Schedule the email for Friday morning using last month's template and subject line.

advanced.situation: You lead a launch campaign using social posts, paid search and affiliates with a RM30,000 budget. Early data shows affiliates drive most sales, while paid search drives most traffic.

options.text: Keep the planned split across the channels until the campaign ends next month.
Track sales by channel, then shift budget in steps and keep testing the others.
Move most of the paid search budget to affiliates since they bring sales.
Credit the affiliate sales to paid search in the report to look efficient.

basic.situation: You help set up analytics tracking on a new landing page. The developer asks you to confirm which button clicks should count as conversions.

options.text: Tell the developer to track every button click on the page and sort them later.
Tell the developer to count each page view as a conversion for now.
Ask the campaign owner which actions matter, then list those buttons for the developer.
Pick the main sign-up button and tell the developer that is the conversion.

advanced.situation: You run an A/B test on a checkout page. After three days the new version shows 8 percent higher conversion, but only 200 visitors have seen it.

options.text: Share the 8 percent gain with managers as a likely win and wait for more data.
Keep the test running to reach the planned sample size, then check the result.
Roll out the new version to half the traffic and watch the results weekly.
Stop the test now and switch all visitors to the new checkout version today.

basic.situation: Your report needs page views, visits and click-through rate for last month. The analytics tool shows page views twice as high as visits.

options.text: Report the page view numbers and add the visits if your manager asks.
Pull the figures, note that views include repeat views per visit, and report both clearly.
Use the page view figure as the visit count because it is larger.
Divide the page views by two so that they match the visit count.

advanced.situation: A client sells running shoes and wants to rank for new search terms. Keyword tools show high volume for 'cheap shoes', but your interview notes suggest buyers want quality.

options.text: Choose 'cheap shoes' because its volume is highest and file the interview notes.
Choose terms that competitors already rank for, since they must be working.
Combine keyword data with customer interviews and sales data to rank terms by buyer intent.
Target the high-volume keyword first and add quality-related terms in the next phase.

basic.situation: Design staff send you a banner for your email campaign, but the logo colours differ from the brand guide. The campaign goes out in two hours.

options.text: Delay the campaign by a day so design can redo the banner properly.
Send the banner as it is and tell design to fix it for next time.
Change the logo colours yourself in a free editor and send the banner.
Ask design for a quick colour fix using the brand guide and check the file.

advanced.situation: You must present search performance to executives. Organic traffic is up 12 percent, but revenue from search is flat, and the executives expect a growth story.

options.text: Lead with the traffic gain and mention the flat revenue at the end.
Show traffic and revenue together, explain the gap, and propose changes to attract buyers.
Add direct and paid sales to the search revenue figure to show growth.
Present the traffic growth and say revenue should follow in the next quarter.

basic.situation: Your team wants a tool for scheduling social posts. Your manager asks you to list three options with price and features.

options.text: Subscribe to one paid plan with your own card to trial the tool.
Compare three tools on price, features and reviews, and note which fit your team.
Pick the cheapest tool you find and add two others from a quick search.
List three well-known tools with their monthly prices copied from their websites.

advanced.situation: A new platform with video shopping features is getting attention. The CEO asks whether the company should use it for search marketing, and you have a small trial budget.

options.text: Commit the full trial budget to the platform and tell the CEO it works.
Review case studies from other brands and recommend based on what they report.
Wait until a few competitors adopt it and then follow their approach closely.
Run a small trial with clear targets, compare results to current channels, then recommend.

basic.situation: You help keep the online product catalogue accurate. A promotion ends tonight, but the catalogue still shows the sale price tomorrow.

options.text: Email the operations team about the promotion end date and wait for a reply.
Edit the sale price in the catalogue yourself tomorrow morning when you see it.
Leave the sale price showing and honour it for any orders that arrive.
Ask the catalogue owner to schedule the price change and check it after midnight.

advanced.situation: Your legal team confirms new rules require accurate product claims in online listings. Your catalogue has 3,000 products across four channels, and inventory and merchandising teams update different fields.

options.text: Ask each team to review its own fields once and confirm in writing.
Set a claims checklist, name field owners in each team and audit samples monthly.
Delete every product claim from all four channels today and tell the teams later.
Ask an outside agency to rewrite all 3,000 listings within the month.

basic.situation: You are asked to review an existing disaster recovery plan for a branch office. The plan was last updated three years ago and lists a supplier that has closed.

options.text: Replace the closed supplier with a similar one from the web and update the date.
Tell your lead the plan needs a full rewrite and stop the review.
Mark the closed supplier, check other contacts and report the findings to your lead.
Sign off the plan as reviewed since most of its content still looks fine.

advanced.situation: You are asked to develop a recovery plan for a company data centre that hosts payroll and customer systems. The finance director wants it within two weeks.

options.text: Write a plan for payroll first and treat the customer systems as covered by it.
List the equipment in the data centre and ask the vendor to write the plan.
Adapt a recovery plan template from another company's data centre and add your site's details.
Map critical systems and dependencies, set recovery targets with owners, and schedule a test.

basic.situation: You help set up a call tree so staff can be reached during a disaster. Three staff members' phone numbers in the list have changed.

options.text: Add the numbers staff mention in conversation, then check them at the next test.
Ask the department heads to update their own team numbers when they can.
Remove those three staff from the call tree until they send new numbers.
Confirm the new numbers with each person and update the call tree.

advanced.situation: Your company has plans for each department, but during a test, finance and operations used different recovery priorities and blocked each other. You oversee the integration.

options.text: Ask both heads to adjust their plans to fit each other and test again.
Write a short memo asking both departments to cooperate more in the next test.
Gather both heads, agree one ranked priority list for critical processes, and retest the plans.
Let each department keep its plan and decide on the day who has priority.

basic.situation: You read a new regulation that says critical staff records must be backed up and stored in two locations. Your company keeps one backup copy on site.

options.text: Note the requirement, compare it with current storage and report the gap to your manager.
Add the regulation to the plan's reference list and update it next year.
Ask the IT team whether the single backup is enough under the regulation.
Tell your manager that the existing on-site backup already meets the requirement.

advanced.situation: A new supplier will provide your company's sole payment system. You must set recovery time targets, but the supplier says its system can be down for 24 hours.

options.text: Accept the 24-hour limit and prepare manual payment procedures for any outage.
Analyse the payment system's impact on sales, set shorter targets, and negotiate backup arrangements.
Ask the finance team how much a 24-hour outage would cost before agreeing.
Set a four-hour target in the plan and note that the supplier will meet it.

basic.situation: You help prepare next year's continuity budget. Your manager gives you last year's figures and says the backup site rent will rise 10 percent.

options.text: Copy last year's budget and tell your manager the rent line may change.
Raise every line in the budget by 10 percent to leave a buffer.
Cut the training line by the rent increase so the total stays the same.
Update the rent line by 10 percent and ask your manager about other known changes.

advanced.situation: Your intelligence feed shows several alerts about phishing emails targeting finance staff in your sector. Two days later your own finance team reports one odd email.

options.text: Ask finance to forward the odd email and wait for a clearer pattern.
Send a general reminder to all staff about phishing and wait for further reports.
Compare the alerts with the report, brief the security team and warn finance staff.
Tell finance the email is harmless because it appears to be a one-off.

basic.situation: Your company offers a one-day course on new disaster recovery methods. It is during a busy week, and your manager says attendance is your choice.

options.text: Attend the course and share three key points with your team afterwards.
Register for the course and cancel on the day if the work gets busy.
Read the course outline online and plan to attend a later course.
Ask a colleague to attend the course and send you their notes afterwards.

advanced.situation: You design a service to reduce the risk of data loss using cloud backup. The vendor offers low-cost storage, but data would be held in another country.

options.text: Choose a local provider that costs more and keeps all data in the country.
Use the vendor for backups of general files and keep customer data on site.
Check data rules and contracts for foreign storage, then pilot with non-sensitive data.
Use the vendor for all data now and check the data rules afterwards.

basic.situation: You help keep the network diagram up to date. The IT team tells you a server was moved to a new room last week, but the diagram still shows the old room.

options.text: Update the diagram with the new room, confirm with IT, and note the date.
Redraw the server in the room that seems most likely from what you heard.
Add a comment to the diagram that the server may have moved.
Ask IT to send you a full new diagram when they find the time.

advanced.situation: You must write a report on last quarter's continuity test results for the board. The test met only two of five recovery targets, and the sponsor prefers positive wording.

options.text: Report all five results, explain causes and fixes, and set a deadline for each.
Lead with the two targets met and list the other three in an appendix.
Count partial recovery as met for all five targets so the result looks stronger.
Describe the test as a good learning exercise and list the targets briefly.

basic.situation: You review a draft recycling policy for an office. It says bins are emptied weekly, but the cleaning contract says twice a month.

options.text: Tell the cleaners to empty bins weekly from now to match the policy.
Leave the policy as written and add a note that the schedule may vary.
Flag the mismatch, check the contract with facilities, and mark the policy for update.
Change the policy to twice a month and send it back to the author.

advanced.situation: You are developing a company strategy to cut energy use by 20 percent in three years. Operations wants low-cost changes, while the finance team wants projects with fast payback.

options.text: Set the 20 percent target in the strategy and decide the measures later.
Choose the low-cost measures first and review the costly options again after a year.
Adopt the finance team's payback rule for all measures and report it to management.
Rank measures by saving, cost and payback with both teams, then agree a phased plan.

basic.situation: You are making a brochure for staff about a new food waste bin scheme. Your manager gives you the rules and a photo of the bins.

options.text: Write short plain steps, add the photo, and ask a colleague to read it.
Use the photo and a slogan and let staff ask about the rules.
Paste the full rules into the brochure beside the photo of the bins.
Describe the bin colours from memory since the photo is hard to read.

advanced.situation: A manager proposes replacing 400 office lights with LEDs at RM60,000. Staff worry about glare, and savings estimates vary between suppliers.

options.text: Approve the supplier with the highest savings estimate and monitor staff comments.
Trial samples in one area, compare supplier savings, and present cost and staff views.
Present the highest savings estimate as the expected result to win approval.
Ask suppliers to guarantee savings in writing before you assess anything else.

basic.situation: You help identify what a new composting programme needs. The pilot site has bins but lacks signs, a collection schedule and a staff contact.

options.text: Tell your lead the pilot needs more resources and ask what to do.
Order signs for the bins and ask your lead about the rest.
Remove the bins from the pilot site since it is not ready to run.
List the missing items, estimate costs and name who can supply each.

advanced.situation: Waste audit photos show contractors mixing recyclables with general waste at a site. The contract and recycling policy both require separation.

options.text: Tell site staff to separate the waste themselves before the contractor arrives.
Check the photos against the contract, raise the breach, and agree a fix date.
Delete the photos and treat the issue as closed once the contractor promises to improve.
Email the contractor a reminder of the separation rules and ask for confirmation.

basic.situation: You collect monthly electricity readings for three buildings. Building B's reading looks much lower than usual, and you suspect the meter was misread.

options.text: Recheck the meter, compare against past months, and record any note before reporting.
Use last month's figure for Building B until someone can review the reading.
Round Building B's reading up to match the other two buildings' pattern.
Report the reading as recorded and flag it for your supervisor to review.

advanced.situation: Your company wants to measure progress on supply chain sustainability, but no suitable indicator exists. Suppliers have varied data and limited resources to report.

options.text: Adopt an indicator used by another large company and ask all suppliers to report.
Pilot a simple indicator with a few suppliers, check data quality, then refine.
Set a target for suppliers and count those who say they comply.
Create an indicator from the data your company already holds on purchases.

basic.situation: Your lead asks for information on green building practices for a new office. You find a brochure from a materials supplier claiming its product saves 40 percent energy.

options.text: Note the claim as a supplier statement and look for independent sources to compare.
Use the 40 percent figure as a fact in your summary since it is specific.
Include the claim in your notes with the supplier's name as its source.
Ask the supplier to send test results and wait before including it.

advanced.situation: You prepare a presentation to show senior staff whether a two-year waste reduction scheme worked. Waste fell 10 percent, but production also fell 12 percent over the same period.

options.text: Present the waste fall as the result of the scheme and attach the data.
Leave production out of the presentation to keep the message clear and simple.
Show the 10 percent fall and add a footnote that production also fell.
Show waste per unit produced alongside totals and explain how production changed.

basic.situation: You help draft the budget section of a rebate application for solar panels. The form needs supplier quotes, and one quote is missing a signature.

options.text: Use the unsigned quote's price for estimating and ask a colleague what to do.
Sign the quote in the supplier's name so the application is complete.
Ask the supplier for a signed quote and fill the other budget lines meanwhile.
Submit with the unsigned quote and mention in the cover note it will follow.

advanced.situation: A city council office asks your team to help with a complex waste-to-energy issue involving regulations, community concerns and costs. You support the project lead.

options.text: Collect all public documents on the issue and send them to the lead.
Prepare a sourced briefing on rules, cost options and community views for the lead.
Tell the council office the project is feasible based on early cost numbers.
Send the lead a summary of one recent news report about the issue.

basic.situation: You list a handmade batik scarf in your online store. The scarf's colour looks darker in your photo than in real life.

options.text: Use the supplier's brighter stock photo of the scarf in place of yours.
Keep the photo and write in the product description that colours may vary slightly.
Brighten the photo heavily in an editor so the scarf looks more vivid.
Retake the photo in daylight and describe the colour as it looks in person.

advanced.situation: You must price a new set of earphones that costs RM25 to buy. Three competitors sell similar sets at RM49, RM55 and RM39, and shipping adds RM6.

options.text: Price at RM39 to match the lowest competitor and attract more orders each month.
Price at RM29 to undercut every competitor and win the top search spot.
Double your purchase cost to RM50 and see whether customers buy the set.
Work out total cost with shipping, then price within the competitor range with a margin.

basic.situation: You are asked to research whether a small online store should sell phone cases. Your supervisor wants three facts about demand and competition by Friday.

options.text: Check search interest, marketplace listings and competitor prices, and summarise three facts.
Search marketplaces for similar phone cases and count the top sellers listed.
Ask friends whether they would buy phone cases and report their answers.
Report that phone cases are in demand because so many stores stock them.

advanced.situation: Your online store sells garden tools and sales fall each winter. The owner asks you to revise the business plan, with a stock budget of RM40,000 for the year.

options.text: Order RM60,000 of garden tools now on credit to sell during the spring peak.
Cut the stock budget for winter months and leave the rest unchanged.
Add a winter product line and plan stock and marketing around cash flow.
Raise prices on garden tools in winter to protect yearly income and margins.

basic.situation: You draft a post for an online hobby forum about your store's new fishing line. Forum rules say members may not post direct sales links in the first week.

options.text: Share a helpful tip about the line and mention your store in your profile.
Wait until the week ends before posting a message with the sales link.
Post the direct sales link now because the forum has many active readers.
Post a short review of the line and ask members to message you.

advanced.situation: A search shopping specialist offers to feature your product ads on high-traffic pages, but the fee takes half your monthly marketing budget. Your product data feed has errors.

options.text: Accept the offer and fix the data feed during the first month.
Fix the data feed first, then agree a smaller trial and review sales.
Move the whole marketing budget into the offer to make the trial effective.
Negotiate a lower fee and accept the ads with the feed as it is.

basic.situation: A customer messages asking when her order will arrive. Your shipping page says delivery takes three to five days, and her order was sent four days ago.

options.text: Send her the shipping page link and ask her to check it.
Reply that delivery takes three to five days and ask her to wait another day.
Check the tracking, share the latest status, and give her a date to expect it.
Tell her that the parcel is out for delivery today so she stays calm.

advanced.situation: A customer says a RM300 item arrived damaged and wants a refund plus compensation. Your policy covers damage reported with photos within 48 hours; she wrote after 60 hours with no photos.

options.text: Pay the full refund plus compensation straight away to avoid a bad review.
Offer a half refund to settle the complaint quickly and avoid a bad review.
Ask for photos, check your packing record, and explain what you can offer.
Explain the 48-hour rule politely and decline both the refund and compensation.

basic.situation: An order for three items arrives. Your stock shows two items on the shelf and the third item on back order from your supplier.

options.text: Ship the two items and leave the third item to the customer to chase.
Hold the whole order until all three items arrive and then ship together.
Pack the two items, confirm the supplier's date and tell the customer the plan.
Substitute a different item for the third product and ship all three today.

advanced.situation: Your store gets 200 orders a day and payment, stock and shipping labels are handled by hand. Errors are rising, and your budget is limited.

options.text: Set payments to be marked as complete automatically before the bank confirms them.
Hire two part-time workers to check each order before it is shipped.
Buy an expensive software suite that handles every step and set it up quickly.
Map the manual steps, automate the highest-error one first, and measure the results.

basic.situation: You prepare a quote for a customer buying three items at RM40 each. Tax is 8 percent on the goods, and shipping is RM12 with no tax.

options.text: Add 8 percent tax to the goods and the shipping together for a total of RM142.56.
Quote RM132 for goods and shipping and add the tax when the order ships.
Quote RM120 and tell the customer shipping and tax are covered by the store.
Total the goods at RM120, add 8 percent tax of RM9.60, and add RM12 shipping.

advanced.situation: Your store's revenue rose 20 percent this year, but profit fell. Your spreadsheet shows shipping costs and returns increased sharply, and the owner asks why.

options.text: Tell the owner that costs rose with revenue, which is normal for growth.
Break down profit by product, shipping and returns, and show which items lose money.
Remove returns from the spreadsheet so that the profit trend looks stable.
Compare this year's expense categories with last year's and highlight the biggest rises in cost.

basic.situation: A shop-lot office reports three missing laptops in two months. Your senior specialist asks you to find what physical threats could explain this.

options.text: Check entry points, key control and CCTV coverage, and note where the gaps are.
Interview the office manager about who holds keys and access cards to the office.
Conclude that a staff member is taking the laptops, since outsiders enter rarely.
Advise the office to buy cable locks for every laptop and review in a month.

advanced.situation: A factory storing high-value parts has received a threat note. You lead the risk analysis and must recommend countermeasures to the owner within three days.

options.text: Rate likelihood and impact for each threat, then recommend layered measures with costs.
Install more cameras around the stockroom and report the cost to the owner.
Add guards at all entrances and review the situation again next week.
Advise the owner to hide the threat note from staff to avoid panic.

basic.situation: You review CCTV system drawings for a small clinic. The drawings show a camera at the pharmacy door but no label for cable routes.

options.text: Add the cable routes yourself based on similar drawings you have seen.
List the missing cable route labels and return the drawings to the lead designer.
Mark the drawings as complete since the camera positions are all shown.
Approve the drawings and ask the installer to label the routes on site.

advanced.situation: You prepare for a pre-bid meeting for a hospital security system. Bidders ask what the minimum criteria are, but the client has not given a clear scope.

options.text: Draft criteria from the hospital's risk areas, confirm with the client and share them.
Give bidders verbal criteria from memory and decide the details after the bids close.
Tell bidders to propose their own criteria and compare the proposals after the meeting.
Reuse the criteria from your last project at an office building as a guide.

basic.situation: You are drafting a simple procedure for the lobby alarm response. Your manager gave you last year's version and the new alarm panel manual.

options.text: Add a note to last year's procedure saying the alarm panel has changed.
Rewrite the procedure from the manual and send the new version to the guards.
Update the steps to match the new panel and send the draft for review.
Keep last year's steps in place because the guards already know them well.

advanced.situation: Your client's staff share access cards at the main gate during busy hours, and security logs show unknown entries. You must update the access card policy.

options.text: Install a second gate guard during busy hours and leave the policy unchanged.
Review logs, interview gate staff, then set card rules with checks and clear consequences.
Issue extra cards to every department so that nobody needs to borrow one.
Add a rule that cards must not be shared and remind staff by email.

basic.situation: During a visit, your supervisor asks you to check the fire alarm panel at a warehouse. The panel shows a fault light, and the manager says it has been on all week.

options.text: Photograph the panel with the fault light and add it to the monthly report.
Test a smoke detector to see if the alarm still sounds and note it.
Record the fault, report it to your supervisor and tell the manager to arrange repair.
Reset the panel to clear the fault light and carry on with the visit.

advanced.situation: You lead a security audit of a data warehouse that must meet fire and intruder standards. The previous audit found minor issues, and the client wants a quick sign-off.

options.text: Check that the minor issues from the last audit were closed and sign off.
Review the client's own records of compliance and sign off if they look complete.
Audit against each standard on site, test the systems, and report findings with deadlines.
Sign off now to meet the client's schedule and do the audit visit next month.

basic.situation: You review digital recordings from a stockroom to find who might be taking items. At 9:40 pm someone enters, but the face is not visible.

options.text: Note the time and clothing, compare with the access log and report to your lead.
Tell your lead who the person likely is based on their build.
Post the clip in the staff chat so colleagues can name the person.
Check the other cameras for the same person entering the building earlier.

advanced.situation: You are on call when a data room alarm triggers at 2 am. The guard reports a door forced open, and the client's IT manager is not answering the phone.

options.text: Ask the guard to stand at the door, record the scene, and keep a log.
Wait until morning for the IT manager to answer before taking any action.
Reset the alarm remotely and log the event as a false alarm until morning.
Have the guard secure the area, call the police, and keep trying the IT manager.

basic.situation: You assist a senior trainer teaching new guards to use handheld metal detectors. Two guards struggle to hold the detector at the right angle.

options.text: Tell the two guards to watch the others and copy what they do.
Demonstrate the right angle slowly, watch each guard try, and give brief feedback.
Mark both guards as trained so the class can finish on time.
Hand the two guards the manual and ask them to practise later.

advanced.situation: A contractor installing your client's alarm system uses a cheaper cable than specified. The site manager says it works, and the deadline is tomorrow.

options.text: Compare the cable with the specification and require a replacement or written client approval.
Test the whole system and accept the cheaper cable if everything passes the test.
Accept the cable and tell the contractor to leave it out of the report.
Report the difference to your client and let them decide after the deadline.

basic.situation: You are counting petty cash at a clinic. The cash on hand is RM85 less than the ledger shows, and the custodian is on leave until Monday.

options.text: Recount, check recent vouchers for the gap, and tell your supervisor the difference.
Ask the receptionist to cover the RM85 so the count can be closed.
Record the RM85 shortage as found and ask your supervisor what to do.
Adjust the ledger down by RM85 so that the records match the cash.

advanced.situation: Your firm's small client still uses paper ledgers and spreadsheets. You are asked to design and document a new recordkeeping system with current accounting software.

options.text: Keep the paper ledgers and spreadsheets and add a backup copy each month.
Switch the client to the new software on year-end day and delete old records.
Install popular accounting software and move last year's spreadsheet data into it.
Map current transactions, set the account structure, choose fitting software and write procedures.

basic.situation: You inspect the accounts payable book for a retailer. Three supplier invoices dated in March are recorded in February.

options.text: Mention the dates in your working papers but leave the invoices as recorded.
Ask the retailer why the invoices are in February and note its answer.
Change the invoice dates in the book to March so the records are consistent.
List the three invoices, note the date error, and report it to your supervisor.

advanced.situation: While evaluating a client's payment system, you find one clerk can both create vendors and approve payments. The client says staff numbers are too small to change that.

options.text: Recommend a control such as owner review of vendor changes and monthly payment reports.
Note the weakness in your report and accept the client's view on staffing.
Remove the weakness from your report because the client says it cannot change.
Recommend hiring one more person to split the duties between two clerks.

basic.situation: You reconcile a bank statement with the company cash book. The statement shows a RM350 cheque cleared that is not in the cash book.

options.text: Ask the finance manager whether a cheque for RM350 was issued last month.
Remove the RM350 from the bank statement figures to match the cash book.
Trace the cheque in payment records, confirm the payee and record it.
Record RM350 as a miscellaneous expense so that the reconciliation balances today.

advanced.situation: Your payroll audit finds ten employees paid every month who do not appear in the attendance system. The payroll clerk says they are field staff.

options.text: Ask the HR manager to confirm the ten employees' positions and start dates in writing.
Accept the field staff explanation and note the ten names in your working papers.
Warn the clerk you suspect fraud and ask for evidence of work next week.
Verify the ten employees through contracts and supervisors, and examine pay account details.

basic.situation: You are preparing an adjusting entry at month-end for rent paid in advance. The company paid RM6,000 for six months in January and recorded all as expense.

options.text: Ask the bookkeeper whether the rent should be split across the six months.
Leave the full RM6,000 as expense since the cash has already left the bank.
Record RM1,000 as rent expense and move the remaining RM5,000 to prepaid rent.
Record RM1,000 as rent expense and ask your supervisor about the remaining RM5,000.

advanced.situation: A client plans to open a second branch. You are asked to project revenue and expenses for two years using three years of costs and sales trends.

options.text: Use the client's own sales target and add typical costs from industry averages.
Double the first branch's revenue and costs for each projected year and report it.
Project revenue growth for both branches and leave new costs for later review.
Project items from trends, add the new branch costs and show high and low ranges.

basic.situation: Your manager asks for a brief summary of this month's finances for a department meeting. You have the income statement and the bank balances.

options.text: Send the full income statement and bank balances with a short covering note.
Present the bank balances in the meeting and leave the income statement out.
Report the income figure and leave out the expenses to keep it short.
Summarise income, expenses and cash in a few lines and keep details ready.

advanced.situation: You supervise an audit of a small manufacturing client with limited time. Last year's audit found weak inventory controls, and the client has since changed its warehouse system.

options.text: Repeat last year's audit programme in full and add a note about the new system.
Focus the scope on inventory and the new system and assign staff by risk.
Accept the client's inventory report and cut the audit to the year-end balances.
Reduce the audit to a review of the main accounts to save time.

basic.situation: You set up accounts for a new bakery and assign its first entries. A purchase of an oven for RM8,000 needs to go into the right account.

options.text: Record the oven as equipment under fixed assets since it will be used for years.
Record the oven under general expenses and review it again at the year-end close.
Ask the owner or accountant which account suits an oven and record it there.
Record the oven as inventory for sale since the bakery buys and sells goods.

advanced.situation: You are reviewing whether a company's stated goal of reducing waste is reflected in its managers' decisions. Purchasing keeps buying in bulk to get discounts, creating surplus.

options.text: Report the surplus to the finance director as a conflict with the goal.
Compare purchasing records and budgets with the goal, then interview managers about priorities.
Conclude in your report that purchasing managers are working against the goal on purpose.
Review the company's policy documents and conclude the goal is stated clearly enough.

basic.situation: You inspect a customer's antique wall clock for an insurance valuation. There is a small crack on the case that the customer did not mention.

options.text: Ask the customer how the crack happened and record her explanation in notes.
Photograph and measure the crack, record it in your notes, and tell the customer.
Record the crack in your notes and mention it when you write the report.
Leave the crack out of your notes since it is small and minor.

advanced.situation: A seller offers a rare watch with a certificate of authenticity. The serial number on the watch differs from the certificate by one digit.

options.text: Edit the certificate digit by hand to match the watch and value it.
Value the watch as authentic and note the digit difference in the report.
Check the serial against maker records, examine the watch, and hold the valuation.
Ask the seller why the serial differs and accept his explanation for the report.

basic.situation: A business owner wants her restaurant equipment valued because she plans to close next month and sell everything quickly. You must choose the type of valuation.

options.text: Choose liquidation value since the sale is quick, and state this in your notes.
Ask the owner which type of value she would like to see in the report.
Choose fair market value and mention that a rushed sale could lower prices.
Choose replacement value since it gives the highest figure for the owner.

advanced.situation: An insurer asks you to value a unique printing press for a claim. No similar machine has sold in years, and the owner says it is priceless to her.

options.text: Compare replacement cost with condition and income potential, explain your method, and state limits.
Use the sale price of a modern press from the same maker as the value.
Use the original purchase price adjusted for inflation and note it is an estimate.
Use the owner's figure because she knows the press better than anyone.

basic.situation: You value a used laptop using three recent sales prices: RM1,800, RM2,000 and RM2,200. The laptop is similar to all three, but its battery is weak.

options.text: Use the lowest price of RM1,800 since the battery is weak and old.
Average the three prices to RM2,000 and adjust downward for the weak battery.
Use RM2,000 as the value and mention the battery in the notes.
Use the highest price of RM2,200 since the owner expects a good price.

advanced.situation: You valued a warehouse's machinery six months ago. The owner now reports a fire that damaged half the machines and asks you to update the value.

options.text: Inspect the machines, record damage by item, and revise the values.
Ask the owner to send photos and a list and update from those.
Reduce the previous total by half and send the updated report today.
Keep the original value in the report until the insurer completes its claim.

basic.situation: You must find recent sales of similar used forklifts for a valuation. The database lists a forklift sold at RM5,000, which is less than half the usual price.

options.text: Include the RM5,000 sale with the others and note it is low.
Raise the RM5,000 price in your notes to match the other sales.
Leave the RM5,000 sale out of the list and use the other sales.
Check the listing details, mark the sale as unusual, and look for similar sales.

advanced.situation: Your firm tracks comparable sales of used machines in a database that three appraisers update. You notice duplicate entries and inconsistent condition ratings.

options.text: Ask each appraiser to review their own entries when they have time.
Agree standard rating definitions, clean the duplicates, and set a check for new entries.
Remove the duplicate entries you can see and tell the other appraisers.
Delete every entry with an inconsistent rating so the database looks consistent.

basic.situation: You write a description of a diamond ring for an appraisal report. Your notes list the stone's weight and cut, but not the metal.

options.text: Describe the ring as gold since most rings are made of gold.
Describe the stone and add a note that the metal is not yet confirmed.
Check the ring again for the metal mark, note it, and finish the description.
Copy the metal type from a similar ring in your previous report.

advanced.situation: A junior appraiser's report on antique furniture has no explanation of method and uses vague wording. It goes to the client tomorrow, and you must set the standard.

options.text: Add a line saying the method follows industry practice and send it out.
Send it to the client as it is and give feedback to the junior later.
Return it with specific comments, share a report template, and review the revised version.
Rewrite the report yourself overnight so it reaches the client on time.

basic.situation: You are asked to give evidence in court about the value of a used tractor. You valued it six months ago, and your notes are in a file at the office.

options.text: Review your notes and report, check the figures, and note the method you used.
Rely on your memory of the valuation, as you did the work yourself.
Read your final report once and bring it with you to court.
Ask the client what figure helps the case and use it in your evidence.

advanced.situation: You are testifying about a valuation when the opposing lawyer says another appraiser valued the same item at double your figure and asks you to agree it was too low.

options.text: Agree that the figure might be low to avoid a long argument.
Explain your method and data calmly, and say why the two valuations may differ.
Say that you stand by your figure and cannot comment on the other appraiser.
Say the other appraiser is not qualified, though you have not seen the work.

basic.situation: You inspect a terrace house with your supervisor for a valuation. The owner says the roof was replaced last year, but you see damp patches on the ceiling.

options.text: Record the roof as replaced because the owner says so and mention the damp.
Photograph the damp patches and ask your supervisor how to record the roof.
Ask the owner for roof invoices and wait to record anything until they arrive.
Leave the damp patches out of your notes because they may be old stains.

advanced.situation: A developer has added a new floor and a garage to an old shophouse. You must determine how much the improvements add to its value.

options.text: Use the developer's expected sales price for the upgraded shophouse as the value.
Add a standard percentage to the earlier value for the floor and garage.
Inspect the works, check approvals, and compare costs with similar upgraded shophouses.
Add the developer's stated building cost for the floor and garage to the earlier value.

basic.situation: You search public records for sales of houses in a taman for a valuation. Two records show the same house sold twice in a month at different prices.

options.text: Use the higher price of the two since it shows the market strength.
Use the average of the two sale prices in your comparison list.
Check both records, note the dates and prices, and ask your supervisor which to use.
Use the later sale in your list because it is the most recent.

advanced.situation: Assessed values in one district were raised 12 percent, but sales prices rose 4 percent and construction costs 6 percent. Owners are objecting, and you must check the assessments.

options.text: Compare assessments with sales and cost trends by property type and flag outliers.
Tell the objecting owners that the assessments follow district policy and will stand.
Re-check a sample of assessments against recent sales and report the differences.
Lower all assessments by 8 percent in the system to reduce objections.

basic.situation: You are checking zoning bylaws for a house a client wants valued. The bylaw says the lot is residential, but a neighbour runs a small shop there.

options.text: Ask the neighbour whether the shop has a licence and record what he says.
Value the house as residential and mention the neighbour's shop in your notes.
Value the house as if the lot allowed shops, since the neighbour has one.
Check the zoning map and bylaws, and ask your mentor about the neighbour's shop.

advanced.situation: The legal description for a lot in the county records shows 0.5 acre, but the owner's survey plan says 0.45 acre. The valuation date is in three days.

options.text: Compare both documents, check the title record, ask the surveyor and hold the valuation.
Use the average of the two areas and note it in the report.
Use the county records and note the survey plan difference in the report.
Use the larger area of 0.5 acre because it gives the higher value.

basic.situation: You estimate the replacement cost of a 1,500 square foot house using a building valuation manual. The manual gives a cost per square foot for standard finish, but the house has a better finish.

options.text: Use the standard finish cost per square foot and mention the better finish in notes.
Use the manual's cost for the highest finish level for the whole house.
Use the manual's cost per square foot, then adjust for the better finish.
Use the cost from a recent house you valued with a similar size.

advanced.situation: You compute the final value of an office building using depreciation, rental income and similar sales. The three methods give RM4.2 million, RM4.8 million and RM5.5 million.

options.text: Use the highest figure of RM5.5 million to avoid undervaluing the building.
Check each method's data quality, weigh them by reliability, and explain the final figure.
Use the middle figure of RM4.8 million and mention the full range in notes.
Use the income method result because the building is let to tenants.

basic.situation: You photograph a house interior for a valuation. The owner asks you not to photograph the bedroom, which contains personal items.

options.text: Photograph the bedroom when the owner steps out and share the images with the client.
Photograph the other rooms and leave the bedroom out of the report entirely.
Respect the request, photograph the other rooms, and note the bedroom was not photographed.
Photograph the bedroom quickly and delete any photo of personal items later.

advanced.situation: You prepare land diagrams and photos for an appraisal of a sloping lot with a drainage channel. The client questions your lower value for the lot.

options.text: Add photos of the channel to the report and explain the lower value in writing.
Offer the client a quick site walk and explain the value there.
Leave the drainage channel off the diagram so the lot looks more attractive.
Draw the slope and channel to scale, annotate them, and link photos to the diagram.

basic.situation: You draft a simple value report for a flat with your supervisor's review. You have the comparable sales, photos and measurements.

options.text: Give the value in one line and keep the working in your file.
Reuse a similar flat's report from last month and change the address.
State the value, list the comparable sales and explain how you reached it.
State the value and attach the comparable sales and photos for review.

advanced.situation: You testify about a property valuation in a land dispute. The opposing lawyer says your comparable sales were chosen to support a high figure.

options.text: Offer to recalculate the value with the comparables the lawyer prefers and report back.
Say that you cannot remember how you chose the comparables and refer to the file.
Explain how you selected the comparables, show your criteria and data, and answer calmly.
Say that your method follows appraisal standards and ask the court to review your report.

basic.situation: You review a department's monthly budget report. Travel spending is at 95 percent of the annual limit, and it is only month five.

options.text: Move travel costs into the training line so the report looks on track.
Wait for next month's report to see if the pattern continues or eases.
Flag travel as running over pace and send the report to your supervisor.
Check the travel entries for the cause and tell the department head the trend.

advanced.situation: You review five years of operating budgets for a hospital. Staff costs rise 9 percent a year while patient numbers rise 2 percent, and management wants a long-term view.

options.text: Project staff costs at 9 percent a year and recommend a larger budget.
Assume staff costs will grow at 2 percent in the projection to match patients.
Recommend a freeze on hiring until patient numbers catch up with costs.
Break down staff costs by role, project the trend and show funding needs.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to compare two printer leases over 24 months. Option A is RM400 a month plus a RM600 setup fee. Option B is RM450 a month with no setup fee.

options.text: Choose the option the printer salesperson recommends and note that in the file.
Pick Option B because it has no setup fee and costs little more monthly.
Pick Option A because its monthly cost is lower and report it.
Calculate the total cost of each over 24 months and compare the figures.

advanced.situation: A department needs RM2 million for new equipment. It can lease, take a bank loan or use savings that earn interest. You must design a framework to compare these financing methods.

options.text: Choose the financing method the equipment supplier offers to speed up the purchase.
Compare total cost, risk and flexibility over the same period and rate.
Compare the monthly payments for the lease and loan and choose the lower.
Use the savings since that avoids paying interest to outside lenders at all.

basic.situation: You check a unit's budget estimate against a checklist. The estimate has all the required lines except a signature from the unit head.

options.text: Return the estimate to the unit head for signature and note the missing item.
Sign the estimate in the name of the unit head to keep the schedule.
Accept the estimate and add a note that the signature may not be needed.
Mark the estimate as nearly complete and chase the signature later this week.

advanced.situation: The finance office asks you to set standards for budget accuracy and train staff. Several programme budgets do not match the totals for their broader programmes or the emergency fund line.

options.text: Set a standard that totals can differ by 5 percent and leave notes optional.
Review the budgets yourself each month and fix any mismatches you find.
Send staff a memo with the rules and ask them to follow it.
Define reconciliation checks, a sign-off checklist, and run a hands-on session using real errors.

basic.situation: You summarise a unit's budget request of RM90,000 for new software. The unit's supporting quotes total RM75,000, and your supervisor asks for a recommendation.

options.text: Recommend approving RM90,000 and tell the unit it can use leftover funds elsewhere.
Recommend funding RM75,000 and ask the unit to explain the remaining RM15,000.
Recommend approving RM90,000 and ask the unit to send the final quotes later.
Recommend rejecting the request until the unit sends new quotes totalling RM90,000.

advanced.situation: You direct a team preparing a special budget report on capital projects for the board. Two analysts use different assumptions on inflation, and the report is due Friday.

options.text: Ask both analysts to prepare their versions and show both in the report.
Choose the lower inflation assumption since it keeps the project costs smaller.
Agree one inflation assumption with both analysts and record it in the report.
Remove the inflation adjustment so that the two versions no longer conflict.

basic.situation: A new budget directive says all travel claims over RM1,000 need prior approval. A colleague asks whether a RM900 flight plus a RM200 hotel on the same trip counts.

options.text: Read the wording, check whether it covers the whole trip, and ask your senior.
Tell her that the total of RM1,100 is over the limit and needs approval.
Tell her to submit two separate claims so neither goes above the limit.
Tell her each item is under RM1,000 so no approval is needed.

advanced.situation: You are asked to establish a new policy requiring cost estimates for every purchase over RM5,000. Departments say it will slow urgent purchases.

options.text: Set a higher limit of RM20,000 to reduce workload and review it next year.
Draft the policy with a fast-track route for urgent buys and brief the departments.
Apply the policy to every purchase with no exceptions, since exceptions weaken rules.
Let each department decide for itself which purchases need a cost estimate.

basic.situation: A manager says her programme was cut from 20 to 15 participants and asks whether her budget needs adjusting. She sends you the old and new plans.

options.text: Tell her to keep the budget as it is in case numbers grow back.
Compare the plans, work out the cost changes and propose the adjustment.
Move the extra budget to another programme at once and tell her later.
Tell her to reduce the whole budget by a quarter to match participants.

advanced.situation: A new supervisor asks you to mentor her on fiscal allocation. She has a fixed budget but demands from five teams that add up to twice the amount.

options.text: Suggest she divides the budget equally among the five teams to keep peace.
Advise her to approve all five requests now and request extra funds later.
Tell her to fund the teams that submitted their requests first this year.
Show her how to rank demands against objectives and allocate by priority, with rationale.

basic.situation: A small bakery applies for a RM100,000 loan. Its financial statements show profit, but its credit report lists two late payments last year.

options.text: Review the statements, ask about the late payments, and note the risk.
Note the profit as strong and mention the late payments in your summary.
Leave the late payments out of the file because the amounts were small.
Ask the bakery to provide a guarantor before you complete any analysis.

advanced.situation: You guide a junior analyst on a RM5 million loan request from a manufacturer. The company's debt is high, but a large contract with a government agency is signed.

options.text: Ask the junior to compare the debt level with the industry average.
Tell the junior to rely on the signed contract as the main safeguard.
Tell the junior to recommend approval because the agency is a reliable payer.
Ask the junior to test cash flow if contract payments are delayed.

basic.situation: You prepare data for a loan to a retail shop. Sales grew 12 percent last year, and your supervisor asks you to list the key points on income growth.

options.text: Record the 12 percent sales growth and compare it with the shop's costs.
Record the 12 percent sales growth and note that the shop is expanding fast.
Record the growth as 20 percent to reflect how busy the shop was in December.
Record sales growth for the last three years and note what drove the increase.

advanced.situation: A client wants a loan to expand a restaurant chain. You must predict profitability over three years and advise on the loan portfolio, but the chain's management changed this year.

options.text: Use the chain's past three years of growth to forecast the next three.
Use the owner's forecast as submitted because he knows the business well.
Model outlet profit with ranges and test the new management's effect.
Use the average growth rate for restaurants in the region as the forecast.

basic.situation: You compare a furniture maker's liquidity with similar firms in the same region for a loan review. A trade association publishes average ratios by industry and size.

options.text: Use the national average ratios for all manufacturers from the trade association's page.
Use the ratios of one large well-known furniture maker as the comparison.
Look up the ratios for similar firms in the region and record the source.
Use the ratios from last year's file on this same maker as the benchmark.

advanced.situation: You must define benchmarks for loan reviews across five industries and train two new analysts. Some industries have very few comparable firms.

options.text: Use one common benchmark for all industries and train the analysts on it.
Define benchmarks for the industries with the most data and add others later.
Set benchmarks from wider groups where firms are few and train with examples.
Tell the analysts to set benchmarks from their own experience of each industry.

basic.situation: You enter a customer's balance sheet into the ratio software. The current ratio comes out at 12.0, far above the usual range of 1 to 3.

options.text: Report the 12.0 ratio and note that it looks unusually high to your supervisor.
Assume the software is faulty and calculate the ratio again by hand.
Cap the ratio at 3.0 in the file so that it looks normal.
Recheck the figures you entered against the statement and fix any entry mistake.

advanced.situation: A client's team asks for ratio templates that include lease-adjusted debt. After you customise the template, it shows an error message when loading some files.

options.text: Check which files fail, trace the formula cause, and test fixes on a copy.
Send the template to the team with a note that errors may appear.
Ask the software vendor to fix the template and wait for the update.
Remove the lease adjustment from all formulas so the template loads every time.

basic.situation: Your supervisor gives you a template for credit summaries. You are preparing a summary for a customer whose figures look fine but whose latest bank statements are missing.

options.text: Fill in the template and leave the bank statements out of the summary.
Fill in the template with what you have and mark the missing bank statements clearly.
Wait to write the summary until the bank statements have all been received.
