Write in the summary that bank statements were reviewed and found satisfactory.

advanced.situation: You review a junior's complex credit report for a RM3 million loan. The risk rating is 'medium', but the text lists several serious concerns about the company's cash flow.

options.text: Change the rating to 'high' yourself and sign the report for the committee.
Delete the paragraph on cash flow concerns so the report matches the rating.
Keep the rating, add a line noting the concerns, and pass the report on.
Return the report, point out the mismatch and ask for a supported rating.

basic.situation: A customer applies for a RM20,000 personal loan. The application is missing proof of income and the loan committee meets on Thursday.

options.text: Submit the application with the credit analysis and note that income proof will follow.
Use the customer's verbal statement about her income and submit by Thursday.
Ask the customer for proof of income now and explain the Thursday deadline.
Estimate her income from her job title and submit it to the committee.

advanced.situation: A customer complains that her loan payment was recorded late and charged a penalty. Her transfer receipt is dated on time, but bank records show it arriving a day after the due date.

options.text: Remove the penalty from her account yourself to settle the matter today.
Explain the due date policy again and tell her that the penalty stands.
Trace the transfer with the payments team and explain the finding to her.
Ask her to send the bank transfer details and promise a reply next week.

basic.situation: You are asked to price a bond using the standard formula. Your supervisor gives you the coupon rate, years to maturity and the market yield.

options.text: Use the bond's face value as the price since it will be repaid.
Apply the formula with the given inputs and check the result against a similar bond.
Use the price of a similar bond from the market as your answer.
Apply the formula with the given inputs and send the price to your supervisor.

advanced.situation: Your team prices a new share offering for a mid-size company. Peers trade at different multiples, and the issuer wants the highest price possible.

options.text: Compare peers on growth and risk, set a price range and explain your reasons.
Price at twice the average peer multiple because the issuer expects high demand.
Price at the average peer multiple and mention a possible premium to the issuer.
Price at the top peer multiple to satisfy the issuer's request for a high price.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to use the company's standard model to see how a RM10 million equipment purchase would change the debt-to-equity ratio. A loan funds the purchase.

options.text: Reduce equity by RM10 million in the model since the cash is spent.
Estimate the new ratio from the previous year's figures and send it over.
Enter the loan and equipment in the model and report the new ratio.
Ask your supervisor to run the model for you since the amount is large.

advanced.situation: A client asks you to build a model for a new capital structure with convertible bonds, which your team has not modelled before. The client meeting is in a week.

options.text: Present a simple chart of the structure and say the full model will follow.
Adapt your existing debt model by treating the convertible bonds as ordinary debt.
Ask the client to share any model that its own team already uses.
Study how convertibles work, build the model in stages and have it reviewed.

basic.situation: You track economic news for your team each morning from three provided sources. Two sources report different inflation figures for last month.

options.text: Report the average of the two figures and mention both sources to the team.
Note both figures with their sources, check the official release, and tell your team.
Report the figure from the source that your team uses most often.
Report the higher figure since it makes a more interesting story for the team.

advanced.situation: You synthesise industry news to predict shifts in the packaging sector. Reports show falling plastic prices, new recycling rules and a competitor merger, and your boss wants a call.

options.text: Weigh each development's impact and timing and state your view with caveats.
List all three developments and tell your boss the picture is unclear.
Base the call on the news from the one source you read most.
Pick the competitor merger as the main factor and base the call on that.

basic.situation: A client asks whether to invest RM50,000 now or wait for lower prices. Your senior asks you to prepare basic points on investment timing.

options.text: Write that prices will probably fall soon, so the client should wait.
Prepare points on goals, time horizon and past results of waiting versus investing.
Write that the client should invest everything now since prices may rise.
Write that markets cannot be timed and suggest investing the amount in parts.

advanced.situation: A junior analyst advises a client on raising capital and suggests issuing shares at once. The client's debt is low, and market conditions are uncertain. You mentor the junior.

options.text: Ask the junior to sit in on a few of your client meetings first.
Tell the junior to add a risk warning about the uncertain market to the advice.
Review options with the junior, compare cost and timing, and revise the advice.
Send the advice to the client and tell the junior to improve next time.

basic.situation: Your senior gives you a financial analysis of a property fund and asks you to help draft a simple investment plan for a client.

options.text: Link the fund's key figures to the client's goals and draft the plan.
Draft the plan using a recent news article about the fund, since it is current.
Copy the analysis summary into the plan and send it to your senior.
Draft the plan from the fund's yearly returns and a standard plan template.

advanced.situation: You help design an investment fund of green companies. Several candidate companies advertise green goals, but their reported emissions have risen for three years.

options.text: Include the companies in the fund and add a note that emissions are rising.
Rely on the companies' own sustainability reports and market the fund as green.
Set clear green criteria based on reported data, screen the companies, and review yearly.
Choose the companies with the strongest green advertising claims for the fund.

basic.situation: You format a slide deck for a client meeting tomorrow. The slides have three different fonts, and one chart has axis labels too small to read.

options.text: Remove the chart from the deck because its labels are hard to read.
Use one font, enlarge the chart labels and check the slides in slideshow view.
Apply one font to all the slides and send the deck to your senior.
Enlarge the chart labels and leave the fonts for the next version.

advanced.situation: You oversee the materials for a RM80 million transaction closing next week. The legal team notes a missing consent from a minority shareholder, and the client wants to proceed on schedule.

options.text: Raise the missing consent with legal and the client and set a deadline.
Proceed with the other documents and ask legal to handle the consent later.
Prepare the closing documents as if the shareholder consent had already been given.
Tell the client the consent is needed and wait for its instructions on timing.

basic.situation: You interview a new client about her income, expenses and insurance. She says she has no debts, but then mentions an instalment for her car.

options.text: Record the car instalment as a debt in her file and move on.
Leave the car instalment out of her expense list since she called it no debt.
Ask about the car instalment, record the amount, and check for other commitments.
Note that she has no debts, as she said first, and continue the interview.

advanced.situation: Your firm wants a faster intake process for clients with property, shares and business interests. Advisers now spend an hour each on data entry before the first meeting.

options.text: Cut the intake form down to income and expenses and gather the rest later.
Ask clients to bring all their statements and enter the data in the meeting.
Let clients fill in the form online and accept the figures as entered.
Design a form by asset type, test it with two clients and refine it.

basic.situation: A client has three debts: a credit card at 18 percent interest, a car loan at 5 percent and a personal loan at 9 percent. She can pay an extra RM500 monthly.

options.text: Direct the extra RM500 to the 18 percent card while paying minimums on the others.
Take a new loan to clear the credit card and keep the RM500 for spending.
Split the extra RM500 equally across all three debts and review in six months.
Direct the extra RM500 to the smallest debt balance first for quick wins.

advanced.situation: A high-net-worth client wants advice on a niche private equity fund. Your model library covers listed shares and bonds, and the fund's terms involve lock-ins and capital calls.

options.text: Share the fund's marketing returns with the client with a note on lock-ins.
Adapt the listed shares model with a longer holding period and extra caution.
Build a cash-flow model of calls, lock-in and exits, and test liquidity with ranges.
Tell the client the fund is similar to a bond fund and has low risk.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to review a market report on interest rates and note any trends affecting client portfolios. The report says rates may fall next year.

options.text: Summarise the trend, list affected client holdings and ask your senior to review.
Summarise the trend in a few lines and send it to your senior.
Email the key clients that rates will fall so that they can prepare.
Tell your senior rates will fall and clients should change their portfolios.

advanced.situation: You mentor junior advisors. A junior wants to rebalance every client portfolio after one week of market falls and asks for your view on interpreting the shift.

options.text: Explain the longer trend and rebalance where a client's plan requires it.
Tell the junior to wait a month before changing any client portfolio at all.
Tell the junior to rebalance the most active clients' portfolios first as a test.
Tell the junior to rebalance all portfolios now to avoid client complaints later.

basic.situation: A new client asks what your role as a financial advisor includes and whether you will manage her money. Your firm's service guide lists planning, advice and referrals.

options.text: Walk her through the guide, say what services you provide, and answer questions.
Tell her you can promise good returns on any investments you suggest.
Tell her you will handle all her money matters from now on.
Give her the service guide and tell her to call you with questions.

advanced.situation: You prepare a standard report template for your team and train staff to interpret complex statements. Clients often misread the fee section of investment performance reports.

options.text: Ask staff to explain the fee section verbally to each client in meetings.
Add a plain fee summary box and a worked example, and train the staff.
Add a long footnote under the fee section explaining all the terms used.
Move the fee section to the last page so that clients see returns first.

basic.situation: A young client with RM20,000 savings asks about insurance and investments. Your senior says to suggest basic options after checking her goals.

options.text: Suggest a high-risk fund with a bonus so her RM20,000 grows fast.
Ask about her goals and dependants, then suggest basic cover and a simple fund.
Suggest the fund your firm promotes this quarter since it is easy to arrange.
Suggest a low-cost index fund and explain how it works to her.

advanced.situation: A client couple in their sixties have a house, a family business, a will and two children. They ask you to design a strategy for retirement income and passing on assets.

options.text: Advise them to put all savings into the family business to ease succession.
Map assets and goals, coordinate with their lawyer and accountant, and propose phased options.
Propose retirement income from the business and a will update with their lawyer.
Suggest they transfer the house to the children now to simplify things.

basic.situation: A client calls to ask why her plan includes a bond fund when she wanted growth. You have her plan and notes open.

options.text: Tell her to sell the bond fund today and buy growth shares instead.
Read her the plan notes aloud and ask if she wants a full review.
Explain the bond fund's role in lowering risk and offer to adjust the plan.
Tell her the plan was set by the firm and cannot change.

advanced.situation: You oversee implementing a complex portfolio plan for a client with an overseas property and a family trust. Her lawyer and accountant disagree about how to hold the property.

options.text: Follow the accountant's view since tax costs matter most and tell the lawyer.
Ask the client to choose between their views and implement her choice.
Arrange a joint meeting, put their positions in writing, and hold implementation until they agree.
Buy the property through the trust now to save time and sort out issues later.

basic.situation: You review a life insurance application. The applicant's form says she does not smoke, but her medical report notes a past lung condition treated last year.

options.text: Refer the case to a senior underwriter with the medical report attached.
Request the full medical details and note the mismatch in the file.
Approve the policy and change the form to show the lung condition yourself.
Approve the policy at standard rates and ask her to update her form.

advanced.situation: A factory insurance application covers RM50 million of property in a flood-prone area. The applicant also holds two other policies on the same property.

options.text: Check the other policies, test flood loss scenarios, and assess whether total cover is excessive.
Approve cover at the requested amount because the flood loading raises the premium.
Approve cover and tell the applicant that the other policies do not matter here.
Price the policy with a flood loading and note the other two policies in the file.

basic.situation: A motor insurance applicant has two past claims. Your guideline says to add a 20 percent loading for two claims in three years and to attach a driving course endorsement.

options.text: Apply the 20 percent loading and ask your supervisor whether the endorsement applies.
Apply the 20 percent loading and attach the endorsement as the guideline says.
Apply a 5 percent loading to keep the quote attractive and drop the endorsement.
Ask the applicant for more driving history before you apply any loading.

advanced.situation: You set standards for applying ratings to a new class of cover for fishing boats. Early claims show a few large losses, and sales wants low ratings to win customers.

options.text: Set ratings by boat size, area and loss history and review after more claims.
Copy the ratings used for cargo ships and adjust them by boat length.
Set low ratings now to win customers and raise them if losses grow.
Set a high rating for all boats until the claims data is clearer.

basic.situation: A cargo policy for RM8 million exceeds your authority, which stops at RM5 million. Your guideline says to refer such policies for reinsurance review.

options.text: Ask the client to split the cargo into two policies below your RM5 million limit.
Approve RM5 million of the cover yourself and tell the client the rest follows.
Mark the policy for reinsurance review and send it to your supervisor.
Hold the policy until your supervisor is back and then raise it with them.

advanced.situation: You guide new underwriters on when to authorise reinsurance for large industrial risks. One asks if a RM30 million plant needs it when the insurer holds large reserves.

options.text: Tell them to authorise reinsurance for every plant valued above RM20 million.
Explain that exposure and risk quality decide it, and check each case against the guideline.
Tell them the reserves are large enough, so reinsurance is rarely needed there.
Tell them to avoid reinsurance on big risks since it reduces the premium kept.

basic.situation: An applicant for fire cover runs a fireworks store in a wooden building with no sprinklers. Your guideline lists such risks as excessive.

options.text: Decline the application under the guideline and tell the applicant the reason.
Refer the application to a senior underwriter with a note that it looks excessive.
Approve cover at standard rates because the applicant has a clean claims history.
Offer cover with a higher premium and a large deductible on every claim.

advanced.situation: You train new underwriters and must set criteria for declining excessive risks in the travel insurance line. Claims from certain adventure sports have risen sharply.

options.text: List the adventure sports to decline and train staff to follow the list.
Define decline triggers by activity and loss history and train with real cases.
Tell trainees to accept all applicants and raise premiums next year if needed.
Tell trainees to decline anyone who mentions adventure sports on the form.

basic.situation: To find insurance in force on a warehouse, you check the company's records. The system shows two active policies, but a third policy appears in an old paper file.

options.text: Total the two active policies and discard the paper file as outdated.
Total the two active policies and mention the paper file in the notes.
Confirm the third policy's status with the policy team and total the cover.
Total all three policies including the paper file and report the figure.

advanced.situation: You audit the record-keeping process for a large portfolio and find that exposure data for coastal properties is entered by hand in two systems. Totals differ by 4 percent.

options.text: Reconcile the two sets of totals once now and report the 4 percent difference.
Trace the differences to their source, use one system as master and add checks.
Use the lower total in all reports to be consistent with the systems.
Ask staff to be more careful when entering the coastal property exposure data.

basic.situation: You must write to a field agent to ask for the survey report for a client's building, then quote the premium. Your template has blanks for the request and rate.

options.text: Fill in the template, ask for the survey report and give a deadline.
Fill in the template and send the rate quote before the survey report arrives.
Send the agent a short message asking to call you about the report.
Quote the premium to the client directly and send the agent the quote later.

advanced.situation: You develop underwriting guidelines for field agents on cyber cover for small businesses. Agents often explain exclusions in different ways, causing disputes with clients.

options.text: Send agents the full policy wording and a note to explain exclusions clearly.
Tell agents to leave exclusions out of sales talks to prevent client confusion.
Hold a one-time call with agents to discuss exclusions and take questions.
Write plain guidelines with exclusion examples and a standard script for explaining them.

basic.situation: You gather data for a credit risk review of a firm's suppliers. One supplier's financial data comes from a free website, while the firm's own records show different numbers.

options.text: Use the website data since it is public and easy for others to cite.
Compare both, note the differences, and ask the firm which source is verified.
Average the two sets of figures and record that as the supplier's data.
Use the firm's own records and note the website differences in the file.

advanced.situation: Your risk system takes in trade data from four desks. One desk records currency codes in different formats, and some risk figures look off as a result.

options.text: Ask the desk to change its currency format and fix past records by hand.
Delete the trades from that desk so that the system shows no errors.
Add a note to the risk reports saying currency data may be inconsistent.
Set a standard format, add input checks, and reconcile past records that were affected.

basic.situation: You run a statistical analysis to estimate the loss risk of a loan portfolio using your firm's software. The output shows a 95 percent confidence level and a loss figure of RM2 million.

options.text: Report the RM2 million loss figure along with the software settings you used.
Check the inputs, then report the loss figure with its confidence level.
Report RM2 million as the maximum possible loss from the whole portfolio.
Round the loss down to RM1 million so the portfolio looks safer.

advanced.situation: Your bank uses a model to rate corporate borrowers. Over the last year, defaults have been twice as high as the model predicted, and the risk head asks for a monitoring process.

options.text: Adjust last year's reported default numbers down to match the model's predictions.
Retrain the model once with last year's default data and test it again.
Add a warning label to the model reports and continue to use them.
Design regular back-testing against actual defaults with set triggers for model review.

basic.situation: You look at price, yield and stability data for a bond fund for your manager. The yield has risen over three months while the price has fallen.

options.text: Report that the yield is up and the fund looks more attractive now.
Tell your manager the data must be a mistake because the trends disagree.
Explain that yield and price move oppositely and check the rate trend.
Report that the fund is performing poorly because its price has fallen.

advanced.situation: You design scenario analyses for a trading book. Management wants a scenario of an extreme market crash, but the available data covers mild downturns.

options.text: Scale up the worst mild downturn in the data by a factor of three.
Tell management a crash scenario cannot be built from the data available.
Build a scenario from historical crashes and expert views and state data limits.
Assume a crash would lose 5 percent and mark the scenario as extreme.

basic.situation: You assess a company investment for key risks. The firm has a large customer who gives 60 percent of its sales, and a founder who also owns the factory.

options.text: List customer dependence as the main risk and mention the founder in a footnote.
List customer dependence and founder control as key risks and note any mitigating contracts.
List the company's profit margin as the main strength and note both risks.
Remove the large customer from the risk list since the contract is signed.

advanced.situation: A client plans to adopt solar panels and a building management system for a large office. The vendor claims a payback of three years, but the technology is new to your firm.

options.text: Test the vendor's payback claim with independent data and assess key risks.
Accept the three-year payback figure and note the risk of new technology.
Present the vendor's payback claim to the client as your own estimate.
Ask the vendor for references from similar projects and review the results.

basic.situation: You draw a chart for a risk report showing three portfolios' exposure. The chart's axis starts at 80 instead of 0, which makes small differences look large.

options.text: Keep the chart as it is because it makes the differences easy to see.
Reset the axis to start at zero, label the units and check the labels.
Change the chart type to a pie chart to avoid the axis issue.
Keep the axis as it is and add a note that it starts at 80.

advanced.situation: You review risk disclosures in a draft offer document for a fund. The draft describes the currency risk in one sentence, and the fund holds mostly foreign assets.

options.text: Replace the sentence with a statement that currency risk is low for this fund.
Move the currency sentence to the start of the document to make it prominent.
Draft a clear currency risk disclosure with an example and send it to compliance.
Expand the sentence to two lines and keep the rest of the draft.

basic.situation: A client calls asking about the risk of loss on her portfolio. Your report says the one-day loss at the 95 percent level is RM40,000.

options.text: Read her the figure from the report and offer to send the report.
Explain she should expect losses above RM40,000 on about one day in twenty.
Tell her the risk is low and she can stop worrying about it.
Tell her the maximum she could lose in one day is RM40,000.

advanced.situation: A corporate client with large foreign currency sales asks how to reduce risk. Currency swings have cut profit twice this year, and treasury has limited experience with hedging.

options.text: Review exposures, compare hedging options and costs, and recommend a simple policy.
Recommend invoicing every customer in ringgit so the currency risk disappears for us.
Recommend hedging all future foreign currency sales with forward contracts every quarter.
Recommend taking currency positions on rate moves to recover the losses already made.

basic.situation: A regulator issues a revised rule on how banks report large cash deposits. Your supervisor asks you to read it and explain what it requires of the banks you examine.

options.text: Read the rule, list the new requirements, and check unclear points with your supervisor.
Read the regulator's summary note and list its main points for your supervisor.
Assume the revised rule matches the old one and tell your supervisor it is unchanged.
Ask a colleague who already read it what the rule requires of banks.

advanced.situation: Proposed rules would require banks to hold more capital against loans to property developers. You must lead the analysis of their impact on three banks you examine.

options.text: Read the proposal closely and write a note on likely effects on property lending.
Wait until the final rule is published and then ask the banks for their views.
Tell the banks the proposed rule will be softened before it takes effect.
Estimate each bank's shortfall using its loan book and brief the team on findings.

basic.situation: You review a bank's loan documents against its balance sheet. The balance sheet lists RM12 million of loans, but the documents you reviewed total RM11.4 million.

options.text: Report the RM600,000 gap to your supervisor and move on to the next task.
Assume the missing loans are in other files and close the review today.
Note the RM600,000 gap, check for missing loans and ask the bank to explain.
Adjust your total to RM12 million so that the review matches the balance sheet.

advanced.situation: A bank's cash reserve and collateral records are inconsistent across two branches. You must resolve the issue and set standards for verification accuracy.

options.text: Accept the head office figures as final and update your working papers today.
Count cash and inspect collateral at both branches, then trace the discrepancy.
Average the two branches' figures in your report and describe them as verified.
Ask both branch managers to recount cash and collateral and submit signed figures.

basic.situation: You help gather documents for a compliance check on a credit union. Your supervisor lists board meeting minutes for the last two years, but one set of minutes is missing.

options.text: Tell your supervisor which minutes are missing and request them in writing.
Collect the remaining minutes and mention the gap at the end of the day.
Prepare the file as complete and mark the missing minutes as received already.
Leave the file open and tell the credit union to send the minutes when ready.

advanced.situation: You design the audit strategy for a group of small lenders. Internal audit reports repeatedly note weak loan approval controls, and the lenders share the same software.

options.text: Rely on the internal audit reports and reduce the planned testing this year.
Audit the largest lender in depth and apply its findings to the others.
Audit every lender equally using last year's programme, sample sizes and timetable.
Test the shared software controls, sample approvals across lenders, and prioritise by risk.

basic.situation: You help organise files for a bank merger application. Some files are labelled by date and others by subject, and your supervisor reviews them tomorrow.

options.text: Sort the files by date and give your supervisor an index of what exists.
Remove files that look duplicated to make the set shorter for tomorrow.
Sort all files under one scheme, list them in an index, and flag missing items.
Leave the files as they are and tell your supervisor how they are labelled.

advanced.situation: A bank's application to merge with a smaller lender is incomplete because the data systems plan is missing. The bank says it will send the plan after approval.

options.text: Write the missing data plan section yourself from the bank's website details.
Recommend approval on the condition that the data plan is sent after approval.
Hold the review until the plan arrives and mark it as a required item.
Review the rest of the application and ask for the plan within a month.

basic.situation: You draft a short exam report for a small cooperative bank. Your supervisor marked your first draft with a comment that your findings lack supporting figures.

options.text: Insert estimated figures where you do not have the data and resubmit.
Add the figures from your working papers to each finding and resubmit.
Cut the findings that lack figures from the report and resubmit a shorter draft.
Add a sentence saying figures are in the working papers and resubmit.

advanced.situation: You lead a meeting with a bank's directors and senior management to discuss serious weaknesses found in loan monitoring. The chairman challenges your findings as exaggerated.

options.text: Tell the chairman the findings are final and close the meeting early.
Suggest postponing the meeting until the chairman has read the full report.
Present the evidence for each finding, hear the chairman's points and note agreed actions.
Walk through the key findings and offer the working papers for later review.

basic.situation: You are following your firm's procedure to give a short compliance training to three new bank employees. The procedure lists a presentation, a quiz and a sign-in sheet.

options.text: Give the employees the slides and ask them to read them on their own.
Deliver the presentation and send the quiz by email to be done later.
Sign the sheet for all three employees and let them leave early today.
Run the presentation and quiz, and keep the signed sheet as the procedure says.

advanced.situation: A new regulation tightens loan loss reporting. One senior examiner wants to apply it to existing cases this quarter, while another wants to wait until next year. You set the guidelines.

options.text: Let each examiner follow the approach they prefer for their own cases.
Wait until next year as the second examiner suggests and review the policy then.
Apply the regulation to all existing cases this quarter to stay on the safe side.
Read the regulation's start date and transitional rules, then issue guidelines that follow them.

basic.situation: A new client brings her payslip, a list of debts and her bank statement. The statement shows regular payments to a gym and a streaming service.

options.text: Estimate her monthly spending from her friends' typical budgets and record that.
Record the income and debts from the list and ask about the spending later.
Use the payslip and debt list and treat the subscriptions as minor items.
List income, debts and monthly expenses from all three documents and note any gaps.

advanced.situation: A client on a debt plan has lost her job and had a new baby. Her payments are now unaffordable, and the plan allows a review when circumstances change.

options.text: Tell her to keep paying the old amount and tell you if she misses any.
Tell her to stop all payments to creditors until she finds a new job.
Ask her to send the new details and promise to review the plan next month.
Gather her new income and costs, rework the budget, and propose a revised plan.

basic.situation: A client earns RM3,200 a month after tax. Her essential costs are RM2,100 and her debt payments now total RM900. Your supervisor asks you to work out the money available for debt.

options.text: Subtract her debt payments of RM900 from her income and report RM2,300.
Add her essential costs to her income and report RM5,300 as available.
Subtract essential costs of RM2,100 from RM3,200 to get RM1,100 available for debts.
Use her income of RM3,200 as the amount available for debt payments.

advanced.situation: A family facing eviction asks for help getting permanent housing. They have two incomes, small savings and a poor rental record, and rent programmes have waiting lists.

options.text: Apply to the programme with the shortest waiting list and wait for the outcome.
Advise them to find private housing quickly and pay any deposit upfront from savings.
Check each programme's rules, apply to several, and plan temporary housing meanwhile.
Advise them to leave their savings off the application forms to qualify faster.

basic.situation: A client asks what types of personal loan she can get and what the requirements are. You have a leaflet from your agency listing loan types and eligibility.

options.text: Tell her she should apply for any loan available to get cash quickly.
Tell her she qualifies for every loan type in the leaflet already.
Give her the leaflet and tell her to call you with questions.
Go through the leaflet with her and explain each loan type and requirement.

advanced.situation: You are asked to teach a seminar on budgeting to 40 young adults with different incomes. Some are students and some are in debt, and you have 90 minutes.

options.text: Use the first hour to promote your agency's paid services to attendees.
Teach one simple budgeting method with group exercises and a take-home template.
Hand out a budgeting guide and let attendees ask questions at the end.
Present a detailed lecture with slides covering every budgeting topic in the time.

basic.situation: A client emails asking whether she should close her old credit card account. She does not say whether it has a balance.

options.text: Reply that closing old accounts can hurt her credit score and ask her to call.
Reply that closing the card will clear any debt she has on it.
Ask whether the card has a balance and how old it is, then explain the effects.
Reply that she should close it right away to avoid temptation to spend.

advanced.situation: A client has missed three mortgage payments and received a notice from the lender. She asks you what her options are to avoid foreclosure.

options.text: Review her finances, explain restructuring options and help her contact the lender.
Tell her to sell the house now before the lender takes action against her.
Tell her to contact the lender and ask for more time to pay.
Tell her to put the notice away until the lender calls her.

basic.situation: After a counselling session, you must update the client's records with notes, her new address and an agreed payment of RM300 monthly.

options.text: Enter the notes, new address and RM300 payment, then check against her form.
Enter RM300 as the payment and copy the address from her old file.
Enter the notes and payment and tell her to send the address later.
Enter the new address and RM300 payment and write the notes tomorrow morning.

advanced.situation: You prepare a contract for a debt management plan for a client who owes RM40,000 across five creditors. She asks you to promise the plan will stop all collection calls.

options.text: Write the contract and tell her you cannot promise anything about calls.
Write the contract with a promise that all collection calls will stop.
Write the contract and add a line that collection calls will usually stop.
Write the contract with the plan terms and note which creditors may still call.

basic.situation: A client's car may be repossessed next month after two missed payments. She asks what you can look into to help her keep it.

options.text: Tell her to hide the car in a friend's garage to prevent repossession.
Research her lender's hardship options and rules on repossession and report back to her.
Tell her to sell the car quickly and use the money for the debts.
Call the lender once to ask what it can offer her at this stage.

advanced.situation: During sessions, a client with debts also reveals she is being threatened by a loan shark and has nowhere safe to stay. Your service covers debt counselling.

options.text: Tell her this is outside your service and suggest she come back later.
Refer her to social services and a safe shelter and continue her debt plan.
Offer to meet the loan shark yourself to negotiate on her behalf.
Give her a list of community organisations and ask her to contact them.

basic.situation: A walk-in customer asks about a RM30,000 personal loan and what documents she needs. Your branch checklist lists salary slips, ID and bank statements.

options.text: Give her the checklist and tell her to come back with all the documents.
Give her the checklist, explain each document, and book a time to submit them.
Tell her the loan will surely be approved so she can start planning.
Tell her that salary slips and ID are enough to start the application.

advanced.situation: Many loan applications at your branch come back incomplete. You are asked to improve the intake workflow, and a junior is stuck with a self-employed applicant.

options.text: Allow applicants to submit missing documents after approval to speed up the intake.
Add an intake checklist and a second check, and coach the junior on proofs.
Give the junior the salaried checklist and let her adapt it to the case.
Tell all staff to be more careful when they receive loan application documents.

basic.situation: You can approve personal loans up to RM50,000. A customer with a good credit record applies for RM65,000.

options.text: Offer the customer RM50,000 within your approval limit and explain the reason.
Approve the full RM65,000 yourself since the customer's credit record is good.
Hold the application until your manager has time to look at it.
Refer the RM65,000 application to your manager with your analysis and recommendation.

advanced.situation: You must set approval standards for small business loans and mentor a junior. A bakery with strong sales but weak records applies for a RM80,000 loan.

options.text: Tell the junior to decline the loan because the records are weak.
Set cash flow evidence standards, test the bakery against them and coach the junior.
Tell the junior to approve if sales are strong and records can be fixed later.
Tell the junior to approve the loan since bakeries seldom fail in this area.

basic.situation: A young couple want to buy a home in five years. A senior officer asks you to help identify their basic financial goals before suggesting any loan.

options.text: Give them a leaflet on home loans and ask them to decide later.
Ask about their income, savings, home budget and timeline, and write down the goals.
Tell them to apply for the biggest home loan the bank will offer.
Ask about the home budget and suggest a home loan to match it.

advanced.situation: A wealthy client with several properties wants a financial strategy for buying a hotel. You must develop it and train a peer on planning methods.

options.text: Analyse his assets and goals, propose financing options and explain the method.
Offer a standard property loan package and train your peer on that product.
Tell the client to speak to an outside investment adviser about the hotel.
Approve a bridging loan against all his properties to speed up the purchase.

basic.situation: A customer asks about the difference between a fixed-rate and a floating-rate home loan. You have a guide that explains both.

options.text: Explain both types using the guide with examples, and ask which suits her plans.
Tell her the fixed-rate loan is cheaper and she should choose it.
Tell her that floating rates cannot rise much, so she should choose that.
Read the guide's definitions aloud and ask whether she has questions about them.

advanced.situation: A customer is angry that his loan application was declined without a clear reason. He says he will complain to the bank's head office, and your manager is away.

options.text: Tell him you will reverse the decision if he drops his complaint to head office.
Listen, check the file for the reasons and explain them with reapplication options.
Apologise and promise that your manager will call him back within a few days.
Tell him the decision is final and he can write to head office.

basic.situation: You update a customer's credit file with her latest payslip. The payslip shows a salary of RM4,500, but the file lists RM4,000.

options.text: Ask the customer to confirm the new salary before you change anything in the file.
Update the salary to RM4,500, attach the payslip and note the date.
Delete the old payslip from the file and attach the new one.
Attach the payslip to the file and leave the salary field as RM4,000.

advanced.situation: You audit the credit file system at your branch for compliance. Some files lack signed consent forms, and staff say they store consents in personal folders.

options.text: List the missing consents, bring them into the files and train staff on filing.
Report the gaps to the branch manager and wait for further instructions.
Ask all staff to move their personal consent folders into the system this month.
Mark all files as compliant since the consents exist somewhere in the branch.

basic.situation: You are given a list of local business owners from a chamber of commerce. Your manager asks you to find potential loan prospects from the list.

options.text: Add the list to the bank's mailing system and send a loan offer to all.
Check each business's size, years open and need, and shortlist the likely prospects.
Pick the ten largest businesses on the list as your likely prospects.
Call every business on the list and ask if they want a loan.

advanced.situation: You develop a referral network to reach prospects in a new town where the branch has no clients. The team asks for a market expansion plan.

options.text: Offer cash referral fees to any person who brings in a borrower this month.
Map local professionals who meet SMEs, agree referral terms, and track results by source.
Open a booth at the mall for a month and wait for enquiries.
Visit the town's main market and hand out loan leaflets to shop owners.

basic.situation: You check a filed tax form and find that the taxpayer's ID number on page one differs by one digit from the number on page three.

options.text: Change the ID on page three to match page one and process the form.
Check both numbers against the taxpayer record and flag the form to your supervisor.
Use the number on page one and note the mismatch in the case file.
Return the form to the taxpayer and ask her to check all the numbers.

advanced.situation: You review a batch of returns to decide which need a full audit. Several self-employed taxpayers claim large vehicle deductions that look high for their income.

options.text: Compare claims with income and industry norms, rank by risk and select returns.
Request receipts from all the self-employed taxpayers before deciding on any audit.
Pick the taxpayers with the highest incomes for full audit regardless of their claims.
Select all returns with vehicle claims above a set amount for full audit.

basic.situation: A taxpayer's return shows income from an employer that does not match the employer's report. You are asked to contact her about the difference.

options.text: Change her income to the employer's figure and inform her of the change later.
Tell her she owes extra tax and must pay the amount this week.
Mail her a letter listing both figures and asking her to reply within thirty days.
Call her, explain the mismatch and ask for her payslips by a set date.

advanced.situation: A business owner disputes a large assessment and says your office misunderstood the rules on deductions. He wants to meet you and has brought an adviser who speaks quickly.

options.text: Repeat that the assessment follows the rules and end the meeting politely.
Ask him to put his arguments in writing and promise a reply by letter.
Offer to reduce the assessment by 20 percent if he withdraws the dispute.
Listen to his points, cite the rule involved and set a review date.

basic.situation: A taxpayer has not paid by the due date. Your instructions say to send a first notice with a 14-day deadline and record the date sent.

options.text: Send the notice with the 14-day deadline and note the date at month end.
Send the notice with the 14-day deadline and record the date sent.
Send the notice and add a handwritten reminder asking the taxpayer to call.
Send the notice with a 30-day deadline to give the taxpayer more time.

advanced.situation: A company owes RM250,000 in unpaid tax and says it cannot pay in full. You are to develop a collection strategy for this complex case and oversee legal steps if needed.

options.text: Review its cash flow and assets, offer a payment plan and prepare enforcement steps.
Issue a seizure notice for all company assets at the first deadline missed.
Agree to accept 50 percent of the amount to close the case this week.
Offer a payment plan based on what the company says it can pay.

basic.situation: A taxpayer claims she cannot pay her tax debt. You are asked to research court records for liens and mortgages on her property.

options.text: Check her employer details and assume she can pay from her monthly salary.
Search court records for liens and mortgages and record the results in her file.
Accept her claim and close the file since she says she has nothing.
Ask her to send copies of any liens or mortgages that she has.

advanced.situation: A delinquent restaurant owner claims inability to pay RM90,000 but drives an expensive car and owns a second property. You lead the asset investigation.

options.text: Offer a compromise based on the amount he says he can pay.
Verify ownership records and income, assess ability to pay, then choose enforcement.
Post notices about the debt at his restaurant to pressure him to pay.
Seize the car at once since it is the most visible of his assets.

basic.situation: You help prepare documents for a tax evasion case. Your senior asks you to search a company's records and copy relevant invoices.

options.text: Copy all invoices from the past ten years to avoid missing something.
Search as instructed, copy relevant invoices and log what you took and when.
Copy the invoices you think look suspicious and leave the log for later.
Take the company's original files home to study them over the weekend.

advanced.situation: You direct the service of a garnishment notice on a taxpayer's employer. The employer says the taxpayer has left, and a colleague suggests serving the notice on the taxpayer's neighbour.

options.text: Serve the notice on the old employer anyway and record its response.
Serve the notice on the neighbour as your colleague suggested to save time.
Return the notice to the file until the taxpayer contacts the tax office.
Confirm his employment status, find the new employer and serve the notice there.

basic.situation: You enter tax return information into the computer. One return shows income as RM48,000 on the form but RM84,000 on the attached statement.

options.text: Pause the entry, flag the difference, and check with your supervisor which figure applies.
Enter the higher figure of RM84,000 to be safe on behalf of the revenue.
Enter RM48,000 from the form and add a note about the statement figure.
Enter the average of the two figures so the entry looks reasonable.

advanced.situation: You maintain case records and establish standards for a team handling 300 cases. Contacts, phone numbers and actions are logged inconsistently, and an appeal hearing is soon.

options.text: Rewrite the logs for the appeal cases from memory of the contacts.
Tell officers to keep the logs in whatever format they find easiest to use.
Set a standard case log format, train the team and audit a sample.
Ask each officer to update their own logs before the appeal hearing starts.

basic.situation: You complete a simple individual tax return using the form instructions and tax table. The table shows RM1,250 for her taxable income, but your first calculation gives RM1,520.

options.text: Enter the average of the two amounts since both of them look possible.
Enter RM1,250 and change her income figure so that it fits the table.
Recheck your arithmetic and the income figure against the form instructions and table.
Enter RM1,250 from the table and keep your calculation sheet for review.

advanced.situation: A small business owner brings records for a sole proprietorship with rental income, freelance income and a part-time salary. She needs a complete return within a week.

options.text: Prepare the return from her salary slip and estimate the other two incomes.
Prepare the return for the business and salary and add rent if time allows.
Leave the freelance income off the return since it is hard to verify.
Sort the records by income source, prepare the return and review it with her.

basic.situation: A client asks which deductions she can claim. She has paid for a medical checkup and a book, and she has the receipts for both.

options.text: Claim the medical checkup since health expenses are usually allowed under the rules.
Claim both items in full plus another receipt she says she can find later.
Claim the medical checkup and the book based on what you did last year.
Check the tax guide for each item, note the limits and file the receipts.

advanced.situation: A high-income client has rental income, share dividends and a foreign pension. He asks you to apply every credit and deduction possible to reduce his tax.

options.text: Claim his family holidays as business travel costs, as he suggested to you.
Review each income source and apply the credits and reliefs the law allows.
Ask him to find a tax planner and prepare a basic return meanwhile.
Apply last year's deductions again and add any new ones he mentions to you.

basic.situation: You ask a client basic questions to collect income and expense details. She says she has no other income, but mentions she sold some jewellery last year.

options.text: Ask the sale price and cost, then check with a senior if it matters.
Note the sale in her file and ask her to bring receipts next time.
Tell her that jewellery sales do not need to be reported on any return.
Leave the sale out of the return since it was a one-off event.

advanced.situation: You interview a client who runs a home bakery and also drives for a ride service. She keeps no records, but you must uncover all taxable income and deductible expenses.

options.text: Record the bakery income and leave out the ride service earnings from the return.
Use the bank deposits as her income and add a standard deduction amount.
Reconstruct income from bank statements and app reports, and list her costs with receipts.
Ask her to estimate her yearly income and costs and record her answers.

basic.situation: You check a colleague's completed return with a checklist. The totals add up, but the checklist says to confirm that each figure matches the source document.

options.text: Compare the three largest figures with the source documents and sign off.
Recheck the totals once more and sign the checklist as fully completed.
Sign off the checklist at once since the totals add up properly.
Compare each figure with its source document and note any difference found.

advanced.situation: You verify complex records for a small business return. The bank statement shows two deposits of RM15,000 that are not in the sales invoices.

options.text: Ask the client what the deposits were, request supporting records and adjust the return.
Leave the deposits out of the return and tell the client the books are fine.
Treat the deposits as loans and leave them out of the sales income.
Include the deposits as sales income since they appear in the bank account.

basic.situation: A client has a question about her foreign pension. You look it up in the tax handbook and find a rule, but it was published eight years ago.

options.text: Tell the client that the rule from the handbook applies as printed.
Tell the client her pension is not taxable since you cannot find newer rules.
Use the handbook rule and tell the client that it may have changed.
Check the latest bulletin for changes to the rule and confirm with a senior.

advanced.situation: A client sold a plot of land and received part of the payment in shares. The return is atypical, and the handbook has no matching example.

options.text: Check bulletins for similar cases, ask a senior and document the answer.
Report the cash part as income and leave the shares for a later year.
File the return with the land sale left out, since it is unusual.
Treat the shares as cash at their market value and add a note.

basic.situation: A client asks whether she needs to keep her receipts after filing. Your reference guide states the retention period for tax records.

options.text: Tell her the retention period is six months, from your memory of the rule.
Read her the retention period from the guide and show her which records to keep.
Tell her to keep her receipts for a few years to be safe.
Tell her she can throw them away now that the return is filed.

advanced.situation: A client with a complex return asks for future tax planning, and you must set your fee. Your standard rate is RM100 per hour, and her return took about nine hours.

options.text: Charge for twenty hours so the fee covers future planning calls she may make.
Charge RM900 for nine hours at your rate and give a short planning outline.
Charge the flat fee for simple returns and add a short planning note.
Charge a lower fee because the client is new and may refer others.

basic.situation: Your senior analyst asks you to refresh the yield curve inputs in a bond pricing model after this morning's market data download.

options.text: Update the inputs, save a dated version, and tell your senior the model is ready.
Overwrite the shared model and its backup with the new inputs to keep one clean version.
Paste the new market data over the old inputs and email your senior the file.
Update a copy, compare the outputs with yesterday's run, and show your senior.

advanced.situation: Your team's derivative pricing model and a vendor library give slightly different prices on deep out-of-the-money options. Nobody has written down which one is trusted.

options.text: Compare both on a sample of strikes and report the differences to your team lead.
Keep your own model since it has run for years, and ask the vendor to explain.
Build an independent check model, compare both across strikes, and agree a tolerance with the desk.
Switch the desk to the vendor's prices today because they come from a recognised source.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to work out the present value of a client's simple loan repayment schedule.

options.text: Reuse the present value from a similar loan last month and send it to the client.
Use the sum of all payments as the value, since the interest rate is small.
Discount each payment at the agreed rate and send the total to your senior.
Discount each payment at the agreed rate, then check the total against a spreadsheet function.

advanced.situation: You are building a volatility estimator for the team's shared model library. Backtests show the estimates jump badly after market shocks.

options.text: Test other estimators on the shock periods, document the choice, and add tests first.
Cap the daily change in estimates at a fixed limit and release the update.
Exclude the shock dates from the backtest data, since they are unusual events.
Switch to a smoothed estimator that reduces the jumps, then release it to the library.

basic.situation: You are testing a new risk reporting tool against its written specification. One report shows a column that the specification does not list.

options.text: Log the extra column and ask the developer whether the specification should list it.
Treat the column as a helpful addition and mark the report as passing.
Delete the column from the report template so the output matches the specification.
Note the extra column in your test log and carry on with the other checks.

advanced.situation: Your desk wants a new tool to attribute portfolio returns to sector choices. Two teams propose methods that give different answers on the same data.

options.text: Pick the method used by the larger team and build the tool around it.
Run both methods on past portfolios, explain the gaps to both teams, and recommend one.
Choose the method that gives higher returns for the desk and build the tool around it.
Run both methods on one past quarter and build around the one matching reported returns.

basic.situation: Your senior's regression of a stock against the market index gives a beta of 1.4, but the standard error is large.

options.text: Round the beta up to 1.5 for the summary since the error is large anyway.
Report the beta with its large uncertainty and ask your senior about the data window.
Report the beta of 1.4 and mention that the standard error is large.
Leave the standard error out of the table to keep the summary short.

advanced.situation: You must specify a model to predict loan defaults for a new customer segment with two years of data. The risk team wants it next month.

options.text: Copy the model used for the older segment and apply it to the new customers.
Build a complex model that fits the two years closely and present it as ready.
Propose a simple model and warn the risk team that two years is short.
Propose a simple model, state its data limits, and suggest gathering more history.

basic.situation: A trader tells you the daily profit and loss report is slow to open and hard to read on the desk screens.

options.text: Ask which figures the trader checks first, then draft a simpler layout to try.
Remove columns from the live report that traders rarely mention to make it open faster.
Tell the trader you will ask the technology team to speed up the report.
Send the trader a shorter report you already use for another desk.

advanced.situation: In a meeting, two analysts disagree with a trader about whether a hedging model works when markets move sharply. Other quants wait for you to speak.

options.text: Back the trader's view since the desk carries the profit and loss risk each day.
Change the model's hedge ratios yourself to match the trader's view and update the desk.
Suggest the group reviews the hedging model after the next sharp market move.
Ask for the days the model failed, test those days, and share the results.

basic.situation: You must write a one-page summary of a backtest of a trading signal for the research team. The signal made money in six of ten years.

options.text: Highlight the six profitable years and leave the four losing years out to save space.
State the six of ten result, show the losing years, and ask for feedback.
Summarise the signal as profitable overall and attach the full results table.
Describe the profitable years and mention briefly that four other years lost money.

advanced.situation: A senior trader urgently asks for a valuation of an unusual bond. Your data shows two vendor prices that differ by two percent.

options.text: Give the trader the vendor price your team normally uses and move on.
Give the trader the average of both vendor prices and say it is approximate.
Give both prices and the gap, explain what differs, and offer a model check.
Give the trader the higher price so the position looks safer on the books.

basic.situation: A branch sends you a report of three small, unusual withdrawals from an elderly customer's account. You must decide whether it needs a full investigation.

options.text: Call the customer to ask whether the withdrawals were theirs, then close it if so.
Close the report because the amounts are small compared with your usual cases.
Check the account history for a pattern and recommend whether to open a case.
Freeze the customer's account today and tell the branch to keep the reason private.

advanced.situation: You lead a small team on a suspected procurement kickback. A police officer asks for your case files today, before your team has finished its checks.

options.text: Hand over everything the team holds today, including unfinished notes, to show full cooperation.
Send the officer a summary of the findings so far and offer the files later.
Tell the officer to wait until the company's own report is finished and approved.
Agree a handover with the officer and legal counsel, starting with the finished files.

basic.situation: Monthly billing from one vendor has risen every month for a year, while the number of orders stayed flat. Your supervisor asked you to review the trend.

options.text: Phone the vendor's account manager to ask about the invoices and request revised ones.
Wait for next month's invoice to see whether the pattern continues before reporting.
Match invoices to orders and delivery records, then list the gaps for your supervisor.
Flag the vendor to your supervisor as a concern based on the rising billing trend.

advanced.situation: You are asked to rank which of a retailer's branches carry the highest fraud risk. Cash handling, refunds and stock records differ widely between branches.

options.text: Rank branches by the size of their cash takings, since cash is easiest to steal.
Rank the branches by the number of past incident reports filed against each.
Score each branch on refund, cash and stock indicators, then explain the ranking to management.
Pick the branch managers you least trust and mark their branches as high risk.

basic.situation: Your team lead asks you to keep up with new money laundering methods. A colleague forwards a social media post about a new trick.

options.text: Check the post against official advisories, then share what is confirmed with the team.
Tell a bank client about the trick as fact so they can alter their controls.
Add the trick to the team's watch list since the post has many shares.
Read the post carefully and share it with the team as a possible new trick.

advanced.situation: You are asked to design a rule that flags payment splitting used to avoid approval limits. A very strict rule will flood the team with false alerts.

options.text: Set the rule to flag just the largest split payments to keep alerts few.
Set the rule at a strict level and loosen it later if alerts become too many.
Test the rule on past payments, tune thresholds, and agree a review routine with the team.
Set the rule to block flagged payments automatically so no split payment slips through.

basic.situation: You spent the morning reviewing invoices for a case. Your supervisor wants your notes by evening, and the case file shows no record of your work.

options.text: Write dated notes of each document you reviewed and what you found, and file them.
Write a short summary of the main findings and file it by evening.
Keep your notes in your notebook and tell the supervisor the findings by phone.
Rewrite the case file's earlier entries so the timeline looks neat and consistent.

advanced.situation: Your unit keeps fraud cases in scattered spreadsheets. You are asked to set up one shared database for cases and patterns, holding names and account details.

options.text: Create one master spreadsheet with all cases and let everyone in the unit edit it.
Design fields and access rules with your supervisor, then migrate the old cases in stages.
Build the database with all fields open to every staff member for quick searching.
Upload the case data to a free online tool so the team can search from home.

basic.situation: You must take a witness statement from a bank teller about a disputed transaction. The teller seems nervous and keeps adding opinions.

options.text: Suggest wording that fits the other evidence and have the teller sign the statement.
Ask open questions, record what the teller saw, and read the statement back for confirmation.
Write up the statement from memory after the interview and ask the teller to sign.
Record the teller's account in their own words, including opinions, and have them sign.

advanced.situation: A suspect in an internal fraud case agrees to an interview but brings a lawyer, who objects to many of your questions. You must still prepare the report.

options.text: Keep to the questions you prepared and record the answers given in the report.
End the interview when the objections start and report that the suspect refused to cooperate.
Press the suspect to answer by hinting that refusing will lead to a police report.
Stay calm, keep to factual questions, and record objections, answers and refusals accurately.

basic.situation: Your case goes to court next month. A prosecutor asks you to organise the invoices and bank statements you collected as evidence.

options.text: Label each document, log where and when you got it, and keep the originals secure.
Hand the prosecutor the summary you wrote, and keep the documents in the case folder.
Replace faded pages with clean reprints so the documents are easier to read in court.
Sort the documents by date and hand the prosecutor a copy of each.

advanced.situation: A manager admits to taking company funds and offers to repay in instalments. Your company wants the money back and the matter closed quickly.

options.text: Record the admission, involve legal counsel, and put repayment terms in a signed agreement.
Agree to the instalments and ask the manager to confirm the amounts by email.
Accept a smaller lump sum now so the company recovers cash and closes the case.
Promise the manager that no report will be made if the full amount is repaid.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to draw a flow chart of how a leave request moves from employee to manager to HR in the staff portal.

options.text: Draw the steps your senior described and mark the chart as approved by HR.
Copy the flow chart from another department's process, since leave requests are similar.
Ask staff who handle requests to walk you through each step, then draw it.
Draw the steps from the portal's menu screens and send the chart to your senior.

advanced.situation: Your team has no written test procedure for system changes, and two recent releases broke payroll reports. You are asked to fix the process.

options.text: Ask developers to test more before each release and review payroll reports after launch.
Write a checklist from the two failures and ask developers to follow it from now on.
Roll back both releases and delete their change records to start the process fresh.
Draft test steps and quality standards with the team, then trial them on one release.

basic.situation: A manager asks you to add a new department field to the staff directory screen. The field also appears on printed reports.

options.text: Add the field in the live system after hours and watch for complaints next day.
Find every screen and report that uses the table, add the field in test first.
Add the field to the directory screen and check that it saves properly.
Rename an unused field in the live database to department and keep the old data.

advanced.situation: The warehouse team's stock and cost reports are produced by hand from three systems. Management wants one integrated view to speed up monthly closing.

options.text: Build a script that merges the three exports and give users the combined report.
Pick the largest of the three systems and ask other teams to move into it.
Map the data flows with warehouse and finance users, then propose a staged integrated design.
Replace all three systems with one new package this quarter to settle the matter.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to list what a ready-made leave management package can do, for a small company of 40 staff.

options.text: Copy the feature list from the vendor's brochure into a table for your manager.
Sign up for the free trial using the company's staff list to test it.
List the features reviewers praise on comparison websites and send them to your manager.
Test the vendor's demo and list the features that match the company's needs.

advanced.situation: Your company must pick a new customer system. Sales wants a cheap package, IT wants a flexible one, and finance wants the lowest running cost over five years.

options.text: Recommend the flexible package because IT will support it for many years.
Compare options against agreed requirements and five-year costs, then recommend one with the trade-offs.
Recommend the cheapest package since low cost helps every department in the first year.
Recommend the package from the vendor that offered you a course place and demo trip.

basic.situation: You are told to connect the attendance machine's export file to the payroll system using the vendor's setup guide.

options.text: Follow the guide on the live payroll and check one employee's pay afterwards.
Follow the guide on a test copy and compare results with last month's payroll.
Follow the guide and skip the steps that look optional to finish faster.
Edit the payroll database directly to accept the file's format since the guide is long.

advanced.situation: After a software update, the orders system and the billing system stop sharing data. Customers are not being invoiced, and each team blames the other.

options.text: Trace a sample order through both systems, find where it stops, and brief both teams.
Ask both vendors for their error logs and wait for them to find the cause.
Restart both systems and re-send the day's unbilled orders manually to the billing team.
Disable the checks in billing that reject the new data format and reprocess orders.

basic.situation: Your senior gives you a checklist to confirm every morning that the overnight batch jobs finished on the server.

options.text: Mark all jobs complete if the server is running, and restart any that look stuck.
Check the server's summary screen and tell your senior if anything shows red.
Work through the checklist, record each result, and report any failed job to your senior.
Check the jobs that failed last week, since those are most likely to fail again.

advanced.situation: A vendor's long technical report on database performance recommends a major configuration change. Management asks you to define what the team should monitor next quarter.

options.text: Apply the vendor's configuration change to production and drop the older monitoring measures.
Monitor the figures the report highlights and review them at the end of the quarter.
Monitor everything the system can measure and send all alerts to management.
Pick measures linked to business goals, set thresholds with the team, and review them quarterly.

basic.situation: A staff member says the accounting software closes whenever they print a report. Other staff use the same report without problems.

options.text: Ask them to restart the computer and try again, then log the call.
Reinstall the accounting software on their computer and delete their local report settings.
Ask what happened before it closed and try the print on their computer.
Send them the printing instructions that other staff use for this report.

advanced.situation: Management wants staff to adopt a new approval workflow, but many staff see it as extra work. You must align it with management goals and train staff.

options.text: Tell staff the old approval method will be locked and let them find help themselves.
Send staff a user guide and ask managers to remind them to follow it.
Show management where the workflow helps, then train staff using their own approval tasks.
Run a training session on every step of the new workflow for all staff.

basic.situation: You help test a new nursing handover screen in the hospital system. A nurse says the medication list takes too many taps to reach.

options.text: Move the screen to the live system so more nurses can try it and comment.
Report the nurse's comment to the senior specialist and move on to the next test.
Change the screen layout in the test version yourself so the list shows first.
Count the taps, note the nurse's comment, and report it to the senior specialist.

advanced.situation: Ward nurses and pharmacists want different layouts for a new medication alert in your hospital system. Too many alerts could cause nurses to overlook important ones.

options.text: Set every alert to pop up at maximum urgency so no nurse can overlook one.
Observe both groups at work, pilot a design with fewer alerts, and measure results before rollout.
Choose the pharmacists' layout because they hold the main responsibility for medication safety.
Combine both layouts into one design and ask each group to approve it.

basic.situation: A ward sister asks you to record the number of patient falls on her ward each week for a month.

options.text: Enter last month's figures again for the new weeks to fill the table quickly.
Collect each week's incident reports, count each fall once, and confirm totals with her.
Ask the nurses to tell you each week how many falls they remember.
Count the falls from the incident reports and enter the totals each week.

advanced.situation: Wait-time data shows that discharge delays are longest on weekends in several wards. The hospital director wants a plan to improve nursing services.

options.text: Break down delays by ward, task and shift, test explanations with nurses, then propose targeted changes.
Present the average wait times by ward and let the director decide on changes.
Report the weekend pattern and suggest adding more nurses to every weekend shift.
Blame the weekend staff in your report because the delays appear on their shifts.

basic.situation: A nurse asks you to email her a screenshot of a patient's record so she can show a colleague at another hospital.

options.text: Black out the patient's name and send the screenshot through your hospital email.
Ask her to confirm the colleague's identity by phone, then send the screenshot.
Explain the policy and offer the approved secure referral route for sharing the record.
Send the screenshot to her personal messaging account since it is faster for her.

advanced.situation: A regional health body sends you a confidential draft standard on sharing patient records between private and public hospitals and asks for views. You see gaps in consent and access logging.

options.text: Reply that your hospital will follow whatever standard is finally approved by the body.
Tell the body the draft is sound on the whole and list one small improvement.
Share the draft with your hospital's vendor to ask how they would meet its requirements.
Submit written comments on consent and logging gaps with examples and a suggested stronger wording.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to stay updated on nursing informatics. A conference invitation arrives, and the speaker list includes a vendor selling your hospital's system.

options.text: Read the conference summary online afterwards and tell your manager it covered updates.
Check the programme for relevant sessions, attend them, and share short notes with your manager.
Register the hospital's name for a sponsor package after the vendor's representative offers one.
Attend the vendor's talk and share their slides and pricing with your manager.

advanced.situation: You plan a small study on whether a bedside tablet cuts nurses' charting time. The ward has agreed, but patient data would be collected.

options.text: Copy last year's charting times from another hospital's report and present them as your results.
Time nurses' charting before and after the tablets and report the average difference.
Define the question and measures, get ethics approval, and protect the data before starting.
Start the study on one ward and apply for ethics approval if results look good.

basic.situation: A nurse cannot connect her ward laptop to the new wireless printer for patient labels. She is in a hurry.

options.text: Connect the printer for her yourself and tell her it is ready.
Give her your login to the hospital network so she can print from your account.
Send her the printer's user manual and ask her to follow it later.
Check the printer settings with her on screen and show her each step to connect.

advanced.situation: The hospital is rolling out electronic charting to 300 nurses on three shifts. Past training sessions had low turnout and many nurses made mistakes afterwards.

options.text: Run extra classroom sessions and send nurses a written manual on the charting system.
Switch on charting for all wards and train nurses as they raise problems.
Train ward leaders in detail and ask them to pass the knowledge on to staff.
Plan short shift-based sessions with practice cases and a manual, and check skills afterwards.

basic.situation: A nursing student asks you what a hospital information system does and why nurses must record data in it.

options.text: Let the student practice entering data using a real patient's record on the system.
Describe the system's main modules and show the student where nurses enter data.
Give the student the system's technical manual and tell them to read it.
Explain in plain words how entries support patient safety and care, using a ward example.

advanced.situation: Engineers say a requested change to the discharge workflow needs a major redesign. Nurses say it is a small tweak. You must translate between the two groups.

options.text: Ask the engineers to explain their estimate to the nurses in a meeting.
Tell the nurses the engineers say it is complex and ask them to be patient.
Model the workflow with both groups, clarify what each means, and document agreed requirements.
Tell the engineers to build the change quickly as the nurses described it.

basic.situation: HR emails you that a staff member who resigned today should lose access to the finance folder by end of day.

options.text: Disable the person's whole account as well, to be safe, and tell HR.
Delete the person's whole user folder along with the access to keep things tidy.
Check the HR approval, remove the folder access, and record the change in the log.
Remove the folder access today and reply to HR that it is done.

advanced.situation: Your company plans to send customer records from a branch to head office daily over the internet. The current link is not encrypted.

options.text: Send the records through a free public file-sharing site with a long random link.
Set up an encrypted tunnel limited to both sites and test before the first transfer.
Encrypt the files before sending and share the key by phone with head office.
Open the firewall port for the transfer and rely on head office to protect the files.

basic.situation: Your checklist says to review the weekly report of who opened the payroll files. One name you do not recognise opened them at night.

options.text: Block the person's account and delete their recent activity records from the report.
Check the staff list for that name and note the result in your weekly log.
Message the person directly to ask why they opened the payroll files at night.
