Check the access requests for that name and report the entry to your senior.

advanced.situation: A manager has twice shared their password with an assistant to speed up approvals. You must discuss the rule breach and stop it recurring.

options.text: Explain the risk and remind the manager that sharing passwords breaks company policy.
Report the manager straight to the board and cut their access until further notice.
Reset the manager's password and send a warning email copying the manager's superior.
Explain the risk, set up proper delegated access for the assistant, and agree a follow-up.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to run the standard weekly test that checks whether the file server's backup restores properly.

options.text: Restore a sample file to a test folder, check it opens, and record the result.
Ask the backup vendor to confirm by email that restores are working.
Check that last night's backup job shows as completed and record the status.
Restore a sample file over the original on the live server to confirm it works.

advanced.situation: Before a new payment app goes live, you must assess its security. The launch date is fixed and the developers say the code is already reviewed.

options.text: Run an automatic vulnerability scan and attach its report to the launch approval form.
Approve the launch to keep the date and schedule the security tests afterwards.
Test the app for known weaknesses, rate each risk, and tell management what must be fixed.
Review the developers' code review notes and approve if no serious issue appears.

basic.situation: A security bulletin you follow reports a new virus spreading through email attachments. Your antivirus signature updates run weekly.

options.text: Delete all emails with attachments from staff mailboxes to remove any chance of infection.
Check the vendor for a new signature update and ask your senior to approve it now.
Send a warning to staff about unknown attachments and wait for the weekly update.
Wait for the weekly signature update since the vendor will have added the virus.

advanced.situation: You are developing an emergency data processing plan for a hospital's patient records system, which must stay available. The budget allows one standby arrangement.

options.text: Rank the risks, choose the fastest-recovery standby option, and test it with staff.
Choose the cheapest standby option and document the recovery steps for the team.
Keep a weekly backup in the same building and write that down as the plan.
Store patient record copies on staff laptops as standby so records stay available.

basic.situation: You finish the quarterly test of the office firewall rules and find two rules that no longer match the network. Your senior wants a record.

options.text: Update the firewall rules to match, then record that no problems were found.
Note in the log that the firewall was tested and two rules need changes.
Record the date, tests run, the two outdated rules, and their fix status.
Save the test tool's output file in the shared folder and tell your senior.

advanced.situation: Your company has security rules spread across emails and old slides. An auditor visit is coming, and you are asked to organise the policies and emergency procedures.

options.text: Collect all the files into one folder with an index for the auditor.
Write new policies from an online template and keep them for the auditor.
Consolidate them into one template with owners and review dates, and test emergency steps.
Backdate the new policy documents so they appear to have existed for several years.

basic.situation: You are asked to give a short talk to new staff on spotting phishing emails.

options.text: Show real examples from your company's blocked mail and let staff practice reporting them.
Present the standard phishing slides from the awareness pack and take questions.
Send new staff a link to a phishing article and ask them to read it.
Send a fake phishing email to staff next week and name those who click.

advanced.situation: A vendor is installing a new access control system at head office. Your internal teams and the vendor disagree on who sets up user roles and when.

options.text: Agree a written plan with both sides naming owners, dates and role approval steps.
Set up the user roles yourself, since you know the company's structure well.
Give the vendor administrator access to start early and sort out roles later.
Let the vendor set up all roles using a copy of the staff list.

basic.situation: Your lab's image-recognition program runs too slowly on the lab's older server. Your guide asks you to suggest options.

options.text: Reduce the image quality in the live system so it runs faster for everyone.
List hardware and software options, with rough costs and effort, for your guide to review.
Suggest buying a faster server because slow programs usually need stronger hardware.
Suggest rewriting the program in a faster language, since that has worked in other labs.

advanced.situation: A hospital partner asks your lab to predict which patients will miss appointments. The data is messy and the partner expects a working model in a month.

options.text: Define the problem with the partner, test a simple baseline, and state the data limits.
Ask the partner to clean the data first and agree to start after that.
Promise the partner a working model next month and fill gaps in the data with estimates.
Build the most accurate model you can from the data and report its score.

basic.situation: A senior engineer asks you to draft the user login component of a prototype robot control app. A standard login library is available.

options.text: Use the standard library, follow the senior's design notes, and ask for review before merging.
Write your own login code so you understand how every part works.
Store the passwords in a plain text file for now to keep the prototype simple.
Use the standard library and add a few tests of your own before sending it.

advanced.situation: Your group wants to apply computer vision to a new use: detecting cracks in bridge photos. Early results look promising on a small sample.

options.text: Train the model on the small sample for longer to improve its scores.
Offer the model to bridge inspectors now as a tool that replaces manual checks.
Publish the promising results quickly so others know the group is working on bridges.
Test on more varied photos, compare with inspectors' findings, and report limits before any wider use.

basic.situation: Your team lead asks you to explain the lab's policy on sharing datasets with outside researchers to a new intern.

options.text: Tell the intern from memory that outside sharing is fine if the dataset is old.
Read out the policy with the intern, point to approval steps, and answer questions.
Give the intern the policy document and ask them to read it before sharing anything.
Let the intern send a dataset to a friend at another university to practise.

advanced.situation: You are asked to set performance standards for evaluating new machine learning models in the lab, then review one group's latest model against them.

options.text: Use the standards from a well-known benchmark and score the model against them.
Agree measures and thresholds with group leaders, then evaluate the model and report results.
Set the standards to match the model's present results so it passes.
Judge the model by the accuracy score its authors reported in their paper.

basic.situation: In a weekly meeting, a vendor's engineer reports that a sensor driver keeps crashing your lab's test rig. You are asked to help resolve it.

options.text: Ask for the error logs, share the rig settings, and agree a test plan.
Install a driver from an unofficial website that other users say works on rigs.
Ask the vendor for a newer driver version and install it on the rig.
Tell the vendor the crashes are their problem and wait for a fix.

advanced.situation: You lead the software side of a robotics project with mechanical engineers and designers. They disagree about whether the arm should be slower for safety or faster for demos.

options.text: Bring the groups together, test both speeds, and agree a safety limit before any demo.
Choose the faster speed for the demo because a strong demo helps secure funding.
Set the arm to full speed in code and leave a note for demo staff.
Ask the mechanical engineers to decide, since they know the arm's limits.

basic.situation: You attend a meeting where a user from the biology department describes what they need from a new data tool. You are asked to take notes.

options.text: Write down the features the user mentions and add others you think they will want.
Write a clean summary of the main needs and send it to your supervisor.
Record the needs in the user's words and send the notes back to confirm.
Record the meeting on your phone to capture every detail for later.

advanced.situation: A company wants a language-understanding system for its call centre, but staff, managers and the vendor each describe different goals. You must define the requirements.

options.text: Choose the vendor's goals since they will build it, and tell the others later.
Write requirements from the managers' goals and share them with the vendor.
Interview each group, list conflicting needs, and get stakeholders to rank them in writing.
Combine every goal mentioned into one long requirements list and send it for approval.

basic.situation: Your project lead gives you a list of five small tasks for the week and asks you to put them in order.

options.text: Order them by your interest and do the more interesting ones first.
Drop two tasks from the list that look tedious and report the rest as done.
Order them by estimated time, shortest first, and show the lead your list.
Ask the lead which tasks are most urgent, check dependencies, then order them.

advanced.situation: Your team has three urgent deadlines in the same week and two members are on leave. You must schedule work to meet priorities.

options.text: Ask team members to work extra hours until all three deadlines are met.
Rank deadlines by impact, reassign tasks, and tell stakeholders about any deadline likely to slip.
Promise all three deadlines to the stakeholders and reduce testing time to meet them.
Split the work evenly across all three deadlines and see which ones finish.

basic.situation: A new accounts clerk needs access to the shared finance folder. Your senior gives you a form listing the folders she may open.

options.text: Give her access to the whole finance share so she has no problems later.
Set permissions for exactly the folders on the form, then check them with the clerk.
Copy the permissions from another clerk in the same team to save setup time.
Make her a member of the administrators group so she can open everything she needs.

advanced.situation: Firewall logs show repeated failed login attempts from one overseas address on your company's remote access service over three nights.

options.text: Watch the logs for a few more nights to see if the attempts stop.
Reset every staff member's password tonight and email the new ones in plain text.
Block the address and note it in the log for the next review.
Block the address, check whether any attempt succeeded, and report the pattern to management.

basic.situation: You are asked to run a network cable from a wall port to a new desk in the finance office.

options.text: Use a long spare cable from the store room and tape it to the floor.
Choose the right cable length, label both ends, and test the connection at the desk.
Run the cable along the floor to the desk and test that it connects.
Unplug a colleague's cable from the wall port and use it for the new desk.

advanced.situation: A branch office is getting new wireless access points and a fibre uplink. The old switches must keep working during the change, and staff work through the day.

options.text: Schedule an after-hours cutover, test new gear beside the old, and keep a rollback.
Install the access points first during working hours and switch the uplink later.
Replace the old switches at the start of the day to finish early.
Install the new equipment during lunch when fewer staff are online, then test everything afterwards.

basic.situation: A user reports they cannot reach any websites, but their colleague on the same floor can. Your senior asked you to help.

options.text: Restart the user's computer and the desk switch, then check whether websites load.
Swap the user's computer for a spare one from the store room.
Copy the colleague's network settings, including the address, onto the user's computer.
Ask what changed, check the cable and settings, and test with another port.

advanced.situation: Video calls drop several times a day in one department. Cables, switches and the Wi-Fi all seem fine at first check.

options.text: Reset the main router and switch settings to factory default during working hours.
Capture traffic during a drop, compare devices, and trace the pattern to its cause.
Ask the video call provider to check their service for problems in that area.
Replace the department's switch since it is the shared point for all devices.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to check how much disk space is left on the file server and report it.

options.text: Check each volume's free space in the server tool and report the figures.
Report the free space shown from last month's check since it changes slowly.
Check the main drive's free space and report that one figure to your senior.
Delete old files from the server until it shows plenty of free space.

advanced.situation: WAN performance data shows the link to the branch is full every afternoon. Management wants to avoid paying for a bigger link if possible.

options.text: Block video and social websites at the branch router for all branch staff.
Ask branch staff to avoid large downloads in the afternoon and watch the graph.
Analyse which applications use the link, shape traffic, and show management the data first.
Recommend upgrading the link to the next size since it is full every afternoon.

basic.situation: After fixing a user's printer connection, your senior reminds you to document the support activity in the team's system.

options.text: Copy an older entry for a similar printer problem and change the user name.
Write a short note saying the printer was fixed and who it was for.
Tell your senior verbally what you fixed and plan to write it up later.
Record the user, the problem, the steps taken, and the result in the system.

advanced.situation: A major switch replacement at head office changed many connections. You are asked to document the changes so future staff can support the network.

options.text: Update diagrams and configurations, show old and new setups, and ask a colleague to check.
Delete the old network diagrams so staff do not use outdated ones.
Save the switch's configuration file in the shared folder with a short explanatory note.
Update the main network diagram and add the new switch's address and its location.

basic.situation: A caller says their laptop shows no internet. You are on the help desk phone.

options.text: Tell them to restart the laptop and call back if it still fails.
Ask simple questions, guide them through checking the Wi-Fi, and log the call.
Ask the caller to bring the laptop to the IT room during their break.
Ask them to read out their login password so you can test the connection.

advanced.situation: Your company is moving staff to a new VPN application. Many staff are older and not confident with technology, and the old VPN will be shut in two weeks.

options.text: Install the new VPN on staff laptops remotely and shut the old one early.
Hold one large presentation for everyone and share the slides afterwards by email.
Run short hands-on sessions in small groups, give picture guides, and offer follow-up help.
Send a step-by-step guide to all staff and set up a help email address.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to run a command on a staff PC to check its disk for errors after it froze twice.

options.text: Run the disk check and tell the staff member that it looks fine if it finishes.
Run a disk repair that rewrites the drive, since repair tools usually fix freezes.
Run the standard disk check, note the errors, and tell your senior the result.
Run the disk check on the next restart and ask the user to report freezes.

advanced.situation: System logs show the file server's response time slowing a little each week. Nothing has failed yet, but month-end processing is coming.

options.text: Restart the server this weekend and watch whether the response time improves afterwards.
Note the trend in your weekly report and wait to see if it continues.
Compare logs against server load, find the trend's cause, and warn your team before month-end.
Delete old log files on the server to speed up responses before month-end.

basic.situation: You replaced a faulty keyboard and mouse for a user this morning. Your team keeps a record of all remedial actions.

options.text: Log the user, the faulty items, the date, and the replacements in the team record.
Write a brief entry saying the user's keyboard and mouse were replaced today.
Mark the old keyboard and mouse as returned to the supplier in the record.
Mention it in the team chat and leave the record for later.

advanced.situation: Three support staff record repairs differently, so managers cannot see repeat faults. You are asked to define a record-keeping method for the team.

options.text: Move all existing repair records into one new sheet and delete the old files.
Choose the most detailed record style among the three and ask others to copy it.
Write a template of fields and ask everyone to use it from Monday.
Agree standard fields and categories with the team, trial them for a month, and review.

basic.situation: A new employee starts Monday. You follow a checklist to set up her PC with the operating system, cables and standard software.

options.text: Install the software list and connect the cables, then give her the PC.
Follow the checklist, test each application and cable, and tick off every item.
Install the software list but leave the security updates for her first week.
Copy another staff member's whole PC disk image, including their files, onto her PC.

advanced.situation: You must write installation specifications for 30 new laptops across two branches, then train two junior staff to install them following your document.

options.text: Write the steps from the vendor guide and let the juniors start installing.
Install the first five laptops yourself and tell the juniors to copy your methods.
Write step-by-step specifications with checks, test them on one laptop, and coach the juniors.
Have the juniors install all laptops from memory of your demonstration and sign off.

basic.situation: A user's monitor shows lines across the screen. You have tried another cable and port, and the fault remains.

options.text: Swap in a spare monitor for the user and tell your senior it is faulty.
Dispose of the monitor in the office bin and order a replacement from the store.
Open the monitor casing yourself to look for loose parts inside it.
Check the warranty, then refer the monitor to the vendor with your test notes.

advanced.situation: Finance wants a new reporting system, but IT security and the vendor disagree on hosting. You attend a meeting to establish requirements.

options.text: List each side's requirements, spot the conflicts, and propose options for a joint decision.
Side with IT security and ask the other two to revise their needs.
Record the vendor's hosting preference and ask finance to accept it at the meeting.
Tell finance to sign the vendor's contract now to keep their price.

basic.situation: A user asks how to change the default printer in the office software. Several others are waiting for help.

options.text: Change the default printer for the user remotely and close the call.
Show the user the setting on their screen and ask them to try it.
Close the ticket as solved and tell the user to search online.
Email the user the steps from the help guide and move to the next call.

advanced.situation: Staff complain that their old laptops are slow. You have performance data for 80 machines and must prepare an upgrade recommendation for management.

options.text: Recommend buying cheap refurbished laptops from an online seller your friend runs.
Recommend adding memory to all 80 laptops since that is cheap and quick.
Recommend replacing every laptop older than four years with the latest model.
Analyse the data by age and workload, rank machines for replacement, and cost the options.

basic.situation: You are asked to show a new employee how to use the company's video meeting software for the first time.

options.text: Show her the main buttons on your screen while she watches and takes notes.
Send her the vendor's long user manual and ask her to read it.
Let her join a test meeting with you and practise sharing her screen.
Set up her account using your own login so she can start straight away.

advanced.situation: The company is switching to a new ticketing tool. You must develop training materials and procedures for 25 support staff with mixed experience.

options.text: Write a full manual covering every function and share it with all staff.
Tell staff to learn the tool as tickets arrive, since it is easy to use.
Record one long screen video of the tool and send it to everyone.
Check skill levels, build short task guides, and pilot them with a few staff.

basic.situation: A senior architect asks you to draw a simple network diagram for a new 20-person office with one printer and a guest Wi-Fi.

options.text: Reuse the diagram from the last office you worked on and rename the labels.
Put the guest Wi-Fi on the same network as staff to keep the diagram simple.
Draw the staff network and printer, then add the guest Wi-Fi after review.
Ask which devices and rooms exist, draw them with labels, and separate guest Wi-Fi clearly.

advanced.situation: You are using network design software to plan a campus network for 2,000 users. Your model shows one core switch carrying most traffic.

options.text: Keep one core switch and choose the largest model available from the vendor's range.
Split users evenly across two access layers and leave the core as it is.
Reduce the simulated user numbers until the model shows no overloaded switches in the results.
Model a second core path, simulate failures and loads, and document the design rules.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to back up the router configurations before tonight's firmware upgrade.

options.text: Save each router's configuration to the backup server and confirm the files open.
Start the firmware upgrade first, since the backup can be taken from the routers afterwards.
Save the configurations to your laptop and tell your senior they are done.
Copy the main router's configuration, since the other routers are set up very similarly.

advanced.situation: A major expansion adds three new branch offices to the network over six weeks. The team has different views on upgrade order and standards.

options.text: Upgrade all three branches in one weekend to finish ahead of schedule.
Define upgrade standards, stage branches by risk, and set test gates before each go-live.
Let each branch lead choose its own equipment and settings to speed things up.
Upgrade the biggest branch first and use its setup for the other two.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to apply the standard firewall rule set to a new branch router.

options.text: Apply the approved rule set, test traffic allowed and blocked, and save the configuration.
Apply the approved rule set and check that the branch can reach the internet.
Allow all traffic first so staff can work, and add the rules later.
Apply the rule set from the head office router since it is the most tested.

advanced.situation: Management asks for a disaster recovery plan for the network after a flood hit a nearby data centre. Budget is limited and several options are being discussed.

options.text: Rank critical services, set recovery times, and cost each option for management to choose.
Copy a disaster recovery plan from a similar company and adjust names and addresses.
Tell management the data centre insurance covers recovery, so no plan is needed.
Plan to back up all network devices to the cloud and call that the plan.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to check the daily network report and mention anything that looks like an obvious error.

options.text: Read through the report and tell your senior if any figure looks unusual.
Compare today's totals with yesterday's and report any change above ten percent.
Check for gaps, zero values, and sudden spikes, and tell your senior what you find.
Delete any entries that look odd so the report is clean for your senior.

advanced.situation: You must define procedures to track and report network capacity for a growing company. Teams want different reports and a small team will maintain them.

options.text: Pick a few core measures, set thresholds, automate one shared report, and review it quarterly.
Report average utilisation for the month and hide peaks to avoid alarming managers.
Make a separate report for each team's request and update them by hand.
Track every measure the monitoring tool offers and send reports to all teams.

basic.situation: A new user cannot log into the company wireless network. You are asked to check that her account was set up properly.

options.text: Tell her to forget the wireless network on her device and reconnect.
Add her device to the network by turning off the password check for it.
Check her account details, confirm it is enabled, and test a login with her.
Reset her password and ask her to try the wireless network again.

advanced.situation: You must present a proposed network redesign to the company directors, who are not technical, and one director opposes the cost.

options.text: Explain benefits in business terms, show costs against risks, and answer the opposing director's concerns.
Reduce the proposal's scope before the meeting so the cost looks lower.
Present the technical design in detail so the directors see the work behind the cost.
Present the cost as lower by leaving out support fees until after approval.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to estimate the materials needed to wire a new meeting room with six network ports.

options.text: List cables, ports, faceplates and patch leads with a small spare, and show your manager.
Use the materials list from the last room you wired as the estimate.
Count the six ports and estimate the cable length from the room size.
Order the materials at once from the cheapest online seller you can find.

advanced.situation: You must plan and budget for replacing ageing switches across the company over three years. Finance wants flat annual spending, but some switches are failing now.

options.text: Divide the switches into three equal groups and replace one group each year.
Request the full budget in year one so all switches are new together.
Rank switches by risk and age, replace failing ones first, and propose a smoothed budget.
Delay all replacements for a year and keep spare switches on hand for failures.

basic.situation: Your senior asks for a rough cost to upgrade ten office desk phones to a newer model and run them for a year.

options.text: Use last year's cost per phone from an older project and multiply by ten.
Multiply the phone price by ten and add a small amount for installation.
List the unit price, installation, licences and a year of support, then show your senior.
Quote the vendor's introductory price to your senior as the confirmed cost for the year.

advanced.situation: Three departments each request different system modifications, and the budget covers one. You are asked to evaluate the requests and advise.

options.text: Recommend the cheapest request so the budget stays safely within limits for this whole year.
Assess each request's value and cost, rank them, and explain the ranking to the departments.
Recommend the request from the largest department because it has the most users.
Recommend the request from whoever asked first and tell the others afterwards.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to prepare a simple floor plan diagram showing where network points will go in a new meeting room.

options.text: Sketch the points on the architect's floor plan in CAD and send it.
Copy the layout from a similar room in an older drawing and update the title.
Place the points by estimate and mark the plan as checked on site.
Draw the room to scale in CAD, mark each point, and have your senior review.

advanced.situation: Your company's telecom system serves a call centre that must stay running. You are asked to develop a disaster recovery plan for floods and power failures.

options.text: Identify critical services, set recovery targets, define failover steps, and test the plan.
Rely on the building's insurance to cover losses and drop the recovery plan.
Write a plan listing vendor contacts and repair steps and keep it with IT.
Add backup power and a second telecom link for the call centre floor.

basic.situation: Facilities staff are moving a department to another floor. You are asked to relocate its phones and network ports.

options.text: Reuse the old floor's port labels on the new ports to save time.
Ask staff to carry their own phones and plug them in on arrival.
Agree the move date with facilities, label every device, relocate it, and test each port.
Move the phones during the weekend and connect them to the new ports afterwards.

advanced.situation: A backbone switch at a hospital must be replaced. Any outage risks patient systems, and the vendor engineer wants to start at 9 am.

options.text: Let the vendor start at 9 am but with the hospital's IT team present.
Replace the switch at 9 am and tell the wards if a problem happens.
Agree an overnight window with the hospital and trust the vendor to manage the rest.
Agree an overnight window with the hospital, prepare rollback steps, and test after changing.

basic.situation: You helped a user whose desk phone had no dial tone. The cause was a loose patch cable. Your team keeps a support log.

options.text: Note that the phone was fixed and add the user's name and extension.
Copy an earlier entry about a faulty phone and change the date.
Log the problem, the cause, the fix, the date, and that the issue is resolved.
Tell your senior about the loose cable and plan to log it at week end.

advanced.situation: Your team's telecom equipment has no standard specification sheets, and each engineer writes their own. Auditors will review next quarter.

options.text: Write a standard template and ask each engineer to complete theirs before the next audit.
Create a standard template, fill it for each device, and review it with the team.
Fill the sheets for all devices from vendor brochures and mark them as tested.
Collect the existing sheets into one folder and tell auditors they are current.

basic.situation: A department head says her team needs better phones. You are asked to find out what she needs.

options.text: Order a trial set of expensive phones for her team to avoid more discussion.
Suggest the latest model phones to her since newer phones solve most of the problems.
Ask her to list the phone models she prefers and send you the list.
Ask what tasks and problems her team has with the current phones, and note them.

advanced.situation: A company is changing to a new video conferencing system. You must plan training for executives, call centre staff and technicians, who use it differently.

options.text: Assess each group's tasks, tailor short sessions and guides for each, and gather feedback.
Send a link to the vendor's tutorial videos and close the project.
Run one demonstration for everyone and distribute a general quick-start guide afterwards.
Train the technicians in depth and ask them to help other groups.

basic.situation: The store room is down to a few fibre patch cables. Your senior asks you to prepare a purchase requisition for more.

options.text: Count stock, check upcoming jobs, and attach a quote to the requisition for approval.
Prepare the requisition with the same quantity as last time and submit it.
Order the cables directly from a supplier by phone and fill in the paperwork later.
Prepare a requisition for as many cables as the store room can hold.

advanced.situation: Backbone network equipment has long delivery times, and spare parts keep running out. Management asks you to improve inventory levels and vendor arrangements.

options.text: Sign a large three-year contract with one vendor to secure the volume discount.
Double the stock of every spare part to cover the long delivery times.
Analyse failure rates and lead times, set stock levels, and negotiate a bulk supply deal.
Order from the vendor with the shortest delivery time for every part.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to draw a data model for a new library loan system using the team's template.

options.text: Create the tables directly in the live database and draw the model later.
Fill in the template from the paper loan forms and send it to your senior.
Reuse the data model from the bookshop system, since the ideas are similar.
Ask librarians what they track, then fill the template with entities and links.

advanced.situation: You direct two programmers building the physical database for an online ordering system. They disagree about whether to split customer addresses into a separate table.

options.text: Let each programmer build their version and compare the results next month.
Check how addresses are queried and updated, decide with them, and record the decision.
Choose the separate table because it is the textbook approach and tell them.
Keep addresses in the customer table and let the programmers duplicate them where needed.

basic.situation: A developer changed a stored query in the sales database. Your senior asks you to test it on the test copy first.

options.text: Run it on the test copy, compare results with the old version, and report differences.
Read through the query text and tell your senior it looks fine.
Run the query on the test copy and confirm that it finishes and returns rows.
Run the query on the live database during lunch when few people use it.

advanced.situation: The company's database software version will lose vendor support in three months. Finance reports run on it every night, and the upgrade changes some features.

options.text: Keep the old version running another year and accept the lack of vendor support.
Test the upgrade on a copy, plan a rollback, and schedule it after finance close.
Upgrade the live system over a weekend and fix any broken reports on Monday.
Upgrade the live database tonight and remove the old version to save disk space.

basic.situation: A new auditor needs to view the finance tables in the database for two weeks. Your senior gives you the access request form.

options.text: Share an existing finance team login with the auditor for the two weeks.
Create a role that views the finance tables and expires in two weeks.
Give the auditor an administrator account and remind them to be careful.
Give the auditor read access to the whole database to avoid repeat requests.

advanced.situation: Management asks you to write guidelines for protecting customer data in all new database software the company buys.

options.text: Write guidelines that allow default vendor passwords to stay until the first audit.
Write that vendors must provide a security certificate and leave details to them.
Define data classes, encryption and access rules, and review the draft with security staff.
Copy the security guidelines of a large bank and adapt the company name and details.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to change a table's storage setting. The database manual has a procedure for it.

options.text: Apply the same storage setting that worked on another table last year.
Read the manual's steps, try them on a test copy, and ask for review.
Ask the vendor's chat support for commands and run them on the live table.
Read the manual's procedure and apply it to the live table after hours.

advanced.situation: A vendor delivers a new reporting database product on Friday. Management wants it live on Monday, and your team has not tested it.

options.text: Install over the weekend and test the main reports on Sunday before it goes live.
Go live Monday as asked and test in production while users run their reports.
Plan install and test stages, supervise a trial copy, and give management a firm date.
Ask the vendor engineer to install it and test the reports for you.

basic.situation: A colleague from marketing asks how to export a customer list from the database report tool to a spreadsheet.

options.text: Run the export for them and email them the spreadsheet by lunchtime.
Give them your database login so they can export what they need later.
Send them a link to the tool's help page and return to your tasks.
Show them the export option in the report tool and let them try.

advanced.situation: A client calls about a database that slows badly each afternoon. A junior colleague has already tried restarting it twice.

options.text: Review the junior's steps, check activity at slow times, and guide both toward the cause.
Suggest the client buys more memory since slow databases often need it.
Tell the junior to restart the database before the afternoon peak each day.
Run a command to clear the database's log files tonight to free up speed.

basic.situation: Your senior gives you a code list to enter so the database records basic performance figures for the week.

options.text: Enter the codes on the test server first, then confirm the figures are recorded.
Enter the codes on the live server and check the figures after a day.
Enter extra codes from an online forum to record more detail than asked.
Enter the codes you remember from last time since the lists are similar.

advanced.situation: You must create a new production database and set advanced monitoring codes for it. The application team expects it live next week.

options.text: Create the database from the build and set the same codes as the last one.
Create it from the approved build, set monitoring codes, and test alerts before handover.
Create the database now and add monitoring codes when the first problem appears.
Copy the test database into production and switch off monitoring until launch week ends.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to write the logical description of a new table for staff leave records.

options.text: Ask HR what they record, then define columns, keys and types.
Add leave columns to the live payroll table, since staff are stored there already.
Define the table with text columns for everything so any data fits.
Copy the columns from the existing staff table and add a leave date.

advanced.situation: A retailer wants a database architecture that handles seasonal sales spikes ten times normal load. Your team lead asks for your strategy for the modelling, design and implementation stages.

options.text: Design for peak load by choosing the largest database server the budget will allow.
Design for normal load and add servers quickly when the spike arrives.
Estimate peak loads, choose scaling and partitioning per stage, and validate with load tests.
Cache everything in memory and drop the transaction safeguards to handle the peaks.

basic.situation: You use a template to draft a data model for a clinic's appointment system. The clinic staff mention that patients can have several phone numbers.

options.text: Store all numbers in a single text column separated by commas for simplicity.
Keep one phone column and put extra numbers in a notes field.
Create a separate phone table linked to patients and confirm it with the clinic.
Add three phone columns to the patient table and update the model.

advanced.situation: You must create a data model for a warehouse that merges sales, stock and supplier data from five older systems with different customer IDs.

options.text: Use the customer ID from the largest system and match others by name later.
Define a shared customer key, map each source to it, and test with samples.
Model each system's data as its own set of tables and join them in reports.
Use the customer ID from the largest system and delete source records that do not match.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to schedule nightly backups for a new database following the team's standard backup script.

options.text: Schedule the script for nightly runs and check the first result next morning.
Schedule the script, run a test backup and restore, and confirm it works.
Schedule the backups weekly instead of nightly to reduce load on the server.
Schedule the backups to the same disk as the database to save storage.

advanced.situation: Nightly backups of a 24-hour trading database slow queries for users and sometimes time out. Management wants no downtime.

options.text: Move the backup window to the quietest hour and extend the query timeout.
Run backups on a replica using load balancing, then test failover and timing.
Run full backups weekly instead of nightly to reduce the load on users.
Pause the backup job when users complain and restart it when they leave.

basic.situation: A developer asks you to test a new report program on the test database. It runs without error on your first try.

options.text: Run it twice more with the usual data and tell the developer it works.
Tell the developer it works since the first run gave no errors.
Run it on the live database to see how it behaves with real data.
Test with larger data, empty values, and bad inputs, then report to the developer.

advanced.situation: Management asks whether to move the company's databases to a cloud service, as competitors are doing. You must advise using industry trends and costs.

options.text: Advise moving because most competitors are doing it and industry reports favour the cloud.
Compare trends and five-year costs, include risks, and give management a recommendation with options.
Advise moving all databases in one weekend to match the competitors' timing.
Advise staying with the current systems because they still work reliably for the company.

basic.situation: Your team documents database schemas in an accepted notation. You have added a new table and must update the schema document.

options.text: Remove the tables you do not use from the document to keep it short.
Add the table with its columns and keys in the notation, linking related tables.
Add the table name and a short description to the schema document.
Paste a screenshot of the new table into the schema document and save it.

advanced.situation: Developers keep creating tables with inconsistent names and no keys. You are asked to create and enforce development standards.

options.text: Rename the existing tables to the new standard in production and update nothing else.
Publish a naming standard and ask developers to follow it from now.
Write naming and key standards with developers, add automated checks, and review exceptions.
Block developers' permission to create tables so all requests come through you.

basic.situation: A junior colleague asks you why their query for monthly totals is very slow. Their query looks reasonable.

options.text: Suggest they add an index on every column of the table to speed things up.
Tell them to ask the database vendor since their query looks reasonable to you.
Look at the query plan with them, spot the slow step, and explain the fix.
Rewrite the query for them and send it back with a short explanation.

advanced.situation: You are in a project team building a data platform. The product owner keeps adding features, and the database scope is growing past the agreed timeline.

options.text: Raise the growing scope in the next team meeting and wait for guidance.
Add the new features to the design and cut testing time to keep the date.
List the added features with their database effects and agree scope limits with the owner.
Accept the additions and work longer hours to keep the original timeline.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to draw an entity relationship diagram for a sales mart with orders, customers and products.

options.text: Confirm the relationships with the sales team, then draw them with labelled keys.
Draw the links you expect and mark the diagram as validated by the sales team.
Copy the diagram from the finance mart and rename the tables to match sales.
Draw one box per table from the source system's table list and link by name.

advanced.situation: You are designing warehouse tables for claims data that will grow fast over five years. Analysts want fast reports, while loading must finish overnight.

options.text: Prototype star-schema tables with partitions, test load and query times, and tune before committing.
Load the latest year of claims and delete older claims to keep the tables small.
Use fully normalised tables to keep the data clean and consistent for loading.
Build one wide table holding every claims field so analysts can avoid joins.

basic.situation: You follow a script to pull yesterday's billing records from the billing system into the staging area. The script shows a connection warning.

options.text: Stop the run, note the warning, and ask your senior before running it again.
Re-run the script once more and check the row count at the end.
Edit the script's connection settings to point at a different server that responds.
Let the script finish and load the records, then check the row count later.

advanced.situation: A new claims warehouse must load large batches overnight while analysts query it by day. Loading is starting to delay morning reports.

options.text: Move the load start two hours earlier and watch whether morning reports improve.
Limit analysts' queries during the day so the batch loads can run faster.
Turn off data validation steps in the load to finish before morning.
Measure load and query use, adjust batch schedules, and agree priorities with analysts.

basic.situation: After a load, you run a simple script that counts rows in the target table. The count is 3% lower than the source.

options.text: Report the gap with both counts, then compare keys to find missing rows.
Re-run the count after the load settles to see whether the gap remains.
Copy some existing rows in the target table until the two counts match.
Note the 3% gap in your log since small differences are usual.

advanced.situation: A developer's test plan for a new data load covers only normal records. You are reviewing it, and the release is planned for Friday.

options.text: Approve the plan because the developer has delivered reliable loads for years.
Approve the plan and fill the test results sheet yourself before Friday's release.
Add cases for nulls, duplicates and late data, and send the plan back.
Approve the plan and ask the developer to add edge cases later.

basic.situation: A customer asks for a small change: the monthly sales report program should show region names instead of codes.

options.text: Join the region lookup table in a program copy and compare the output.
Hard-code the region names into the report program and send it to the customer.
Add a note beside each code in the report that lists the region name.
Replace the codes with region names directly in the source data table everywhere.

advanced.situation: The business wants a rule that flags orders above RM50,000 from new customers. Several systems use warehouse data, and rules in each would drift apart.

options.text: Implement the rule once as a stored procedure and tell the consuming teams.
Write the rule in the reporting tool where managers see it most often.
Write the rule into the nightly load so that matching orders are removed.
Share the rule wording with each team so they can build it themselves.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to document the simple steps by which sales data flows from the till system into the warehouse.

options.text: List the system names involved, the load times, and who owns the schedule.
Describe the flow from the vendor's marketing brochure and mark it as approved.
Write the steps from the load script's comments and send them to your senior.
Follow one record from the till to the warehouse and write each step down.

advanced.situation: You must design a metadata framework for a warehouse used by four departments, each defining active customer differently.

options.text: Overwrite the other departments' definitions in the metadata with the finance version.
Record the definitions side by side in the metadata and let each department choose.
Use the sales department's definition since it is the largest user of the data.
Gather the definitions, agree one with owners, and record it in the metadata.

basic.situation: A user reports that yesterday's sales figures look too low in a dashboard. You are asked to help troubleshoot.

options.text: Add the expected missing amount to yesterday's total so the dashboard looks right.
Check the load log for errors and tell the user what it shows.
Check the load finished, compare totals with the source, and update the user.
Ask the user to refresh the dashboard and try again in an hour.

advanced.situation: Your team's warehouse documents are out of date, and new staff keep making mistakes. You are asked to set documentation standards.

options.text: Define a template and owners, set review dates, and check documents each quarter.
Write a template and ask each person to update their own documents.
Rewrite all the warehouse documents yourself over the next two months or so.
Delete the outdated documents so new staff are not misled by old versions.

basic.situation: You watch the network dashboard during your shift. One branch link turns amber but users have not complained.

options.text: Reset the branch router remotely to clear the warning while staff are working.
Watch the dashboard for a few minutes and report it if it turns red.
Note the amber link in the shift log for the next person to review.
Check the link's figures and tell your senior about the amber status.

advanced.situation: Network monitoring data over eighteen months shows traffic growing steadily on the finance VLAN. Management plans to double finance staff next year.

options.text: Project traffic with the planned growth and propose capacity changes with dates.
Move other departments' traffic onto the guest network to free capacity for finance.
Wait until utilisation reaches the alarm level, then request more capacity from the vendor.
Add capacity to the finance VLAN now based on the current growth rate.

basic.situation: A sales manager says her team needs faster file sharing. Your senior asks you to gather information on what is needed.

options.text: Ask which files, how large, and with whom, and record the answers.
Buy a trial licence for a popular file sharing service on the company card.
Ask the manager which sharing tool she prefers and write the name down.
Check the network speed test results for her team's floor and report them.

advanced.situation: Server performance records show three ageing servers that fail monthly. A vendor proposes replacing them with one costly cluster, while management prefers repair.

options.text: Recommend the vendor's cluster because it removes the repeated failures in the future.
Recommend continuing repairs and stop keeping failure records to avoid more questions.
Recommend replacing the oldest server first and repairing the other two for now.
Analyse repair costs and downtime, compare options, and recommend a plan with figures.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to run the scheduled backup of the file server and confirm it finished.

options.text: Start the backup and leave, since the system emails you if there is a problem.
Cancel the backup if it runs slowly, to protect the server for daytime users.
Run the job, check the log for errors, and confirm the file count.
Run the backup job and tell your senior when the screen shows complete.

advanced.situation: After a phishing incident, management asks you to implement network security measures. Your budget allows some, not all, of the recommended controls.

options.text: Rank controls by risk reduced, implement the top ones, and report the remaining gaps.
Implement the controls the vendor recommends most strongly in their latest security brochure.
Implement the cheapest controls first to cover as many items as possible.
Implement the controls and mark the remaining ones as completed in the report.

basic.situation: After a switch port was replaced, your senior reminds you to update the maintenance records and network logs.

options.text: Record the date, port, reason, and who replaced it in the maintenance log.
Add a brief entry in the maintenance log saying the switch port was repaired.
Copy last month's entry for another port and change the port number.
Tell your senior in person and write the entry at week's end.

advanced.situation: Users report intermittent printing failures across two floors. Replacing the print server did not help, and the issue seems to appear after software updates.

options.text: Stop all future updates on the network and tell staff not to install any.
Match failures to update dates, test a rollback in a lab, and document findings.
Replace the printers on both floors since the print server has been ruled out.
Roll back the latest update on every computer and see whether printing recovers.

basic.situation: A user complains that the shared drive is slow in the morning. You are asked to talk with her about it.

options.text: Map her computer to an old, retired file server that has less traffic.
Suggest she copies the files to her desktop and works on them there.
Ask when it is slow, then test the drive from her computer.
Tell her the network is busy in the mornings and slowness is expected.

advanced.situation: Your department needs 40 new laptops. Two vendors offer different prices and delivery times, and a staff member suggests a third vendor owned by his relative.

options.text: Order from the relative's vendor to keep the staff member happy and the process short.
Pick the vendor with the shortest delivery time and inform procurement about the choice afterwards.
Request equal quotes from all three, disclose the relationship, and let procurement decide.
Compare the first two vendors on price and delivery and leave the third out.

basic.situation: Your checklist says to shut down the test servers every Friday evening and record that you did.

options.text: Follow the checklist order, confirm each server is off, and sign the record.
Pull the power plugs on the test servers to save time and sign the record.
Shut down the servers and sign the record at the end of your shift.
Shut down the servers you remember using that week and sign the record.

advanced.situation: You take over administration of a branch network whose switches, servers and software versions are inconsistent and undocumented.

options.text: Fix problems as they appear and note the settings you change in a file.
Reset all devices to factory settings during working hours and reconfigure them from memory.
Inventory every device, define a baseline configuration, and migrate systems to it in stages.
Update every server and switch to the latest version available this weekend.

basic.situation: A report program shows total sales as zero for one branch. Your senior says the cause is likely a small coding error.

options.text: Trace the branch's data through the code, fix the error, and rerun.
Remove that branch from the report's list so the zero no longer appears.
Add a rule that replaces a zero total with the previous month's total.
Fix the line that looks suspicious and tell your senior the report works.

advanced.situation: A scheduled job on the company's servers occasionally locks the database for ten minutes. Logs are thin, and several teams use the same job scripts.

options.text: Move the job to the quietest hour and monitor whether the locks continue.
Add logging to the job, find the cause, and agree a fix with users.
Stop the job each time the database locks and delete its working files too.
Add a timeout that cancels the job after five minutes and restart it.

basic.situation: Your manager asks you to write a small program that stores customer phone numbers in a file and finds a number by name.

options.text: Store the numbers in a public shared folder so everyone can search them easily.
Write the save and search functions and test them with a few names.
Write save and search functions and test names that are missing or repeated.
Copy a similar program from an old project and change the file name.

advanced.situation: Management wants the order processing program to handle three times its present volume. It was written years ago and few people understand its code.

options.text: Remove the validation checks to speed up each order and test the result.
Profile the program, plan revisions for the main bottlenecks, and add tests first.
Move the program to a much bigger server and watch whether it copes.
Rewrite the whole program in a newer language over the next year.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to draw a workflow chart for a program that reads an employee file and prints a pay slip.

options.text: List the inputs and outputs, then draw each calculation step in order.
Copy a payroll chart found online, rename the boxes, and submit it as yours.
Draw the steps from the old program's code and send them to your senior.
Draw boxes for reading, calculating and printing, and add the detail later.

advanced.situation: You must turn a complex discount rule (stacked promotions, member tiers and exclusions) into program logic. The rule is described in a long email chain.

options.text: Write the rule as a table of cases, confirm it, then code it.
Code the rule from the latest email and test with a few examples.
Code a simplified rule that gives members the biggest discount in every case.
Code the most common cases now and add the rest when customers complain.

basic.situation: A manager's request says the report should show active staff. You are unsure what active means.

options.text: Check an older report for how active was defined and follow that.
Include all staff in the file as active so nobody is left off.
Ask the manager what counts as active staff and give an example.
Use staff with a current contract as active and mention it to the manager.

advanced.situation: Operators say a nightly program fails every few weeks. An analyst believes the data is at fault, while you suspect your code.

options.text: Re-check your own code against the failed nights and report what you find.
Ask the analyst to clean the data and see whether the failures stop.
Meet both, review the failure logs together, and agree tests to isolate the cause.
Set the job to restart itself automatically each time it fails and close the issue.

basic.situation: You finished a new function that calculates overtime pay. Your team asks for comments in the code so others understand it.

options.text: Describe the function in the team chat and leave the code as it is.
Copy comments from another function into this one so the file looks documented.
Comment the purpose, inputs, rules and an example, and log the change.
Add a comment above the function saying that it calculates overtime pay.

advanced.situation: Your new inventory software is complex, and end users keep phoning with the same questions. You are asked to write a user manual.

options.text: Copy the vendor's technical specification into the manual to save writing time.
Record a long screen video of the software and share it with users.
Write a manual describing every screen and field in the software's menu order.
Collect common questions, write task-based guides with screenshots, and test them with users.

basic.situation: Your manager gives you a list of five coding tasks to finish this week, in a stated order.

options.text: Hand one task to a friend outside the company who is good at it.
Do the tasks in the stated order and mention blockers at the end of the week.
Do the tasks in the stated order and report any blocker to your manager.
Do the tasks in the order you find easiest and report at week end.

advanced.situation: You lead three junior programmers. Their code reviews are inconsistent, and one junior submits code that often breaks the build.

options.text: Agree coding standards and a review checklist, and coach the junior personally.
Ask the junior to test more before submitting and check back next month.
Review all of the junior's code yourself before it is merged each time.
Remove the junior from the team and share the work among the others.

basic.situation: Your team lead asks if the old reporting tool can read the new customer database. The new database is live and serving customers. You have both table lists.

options.text: Run the reporting tool on a database copy and tell the lead if it loads.
Tell the lead it should work, since both systems use the same database software.
Point the reporting tool at the live customer database and see what breaks during working hours.
Compare field names and types in both systems and list the mismatches for the lead.

advanced.situation: Management wants to replace the payroll system. Three vendors submitted proposals, and each reports different performance figures measured on different test data.

options.text: Pick the vendor whose reported speed is highest and plan the installation around its schedule.
Back the vendor your former colleague recommends and schedule the cut-over for month-end payroll week.
Rerun each vendor's tests on one anonymised payroll sample and compare cost and fit.
Compare the three proposals on price and listed features, then recommend the strongest offer.

basic.situation: A new checkout page is being built. The product owner says it must be fast but gives no numbers. You are asked to help define a performance standard.

options.text: Check how long the current page takes, then propose a target time and a user load.
Write fast in the requirements and let the testers decide what that means as they go.
Propose that the page loads in under two seconds, since that is common for web pages.
Promise customers the competitor's page speed in the launch notes and build to match it.

advanced.situation: You are designing a booking system that must handle ten times today's traffic during festival sales. The team wants to start coding next week.

options.text: Add extra servers to the design so it has ten times the capacity and start coding.
Copy the design from a similar booking site and adjust it after the first sale.
Model the peak load from past sales and test the design against it before coding starts.
Keep the current design and fix any slowdowns live while the festival sale is running.

basic.situation: A user reports that the invoice page shows a total that is off by a few cents when a discount applies. You find the line that rounds the total.

options.text: Fix the rounding line, add a discount test, and run the existing tests.
Fix the rounding line and run the existing tests to confirm nothing else broke.
Fix the rounding line and check by trying one discounted invoice by hand.
Edit the live invoice database to adjust the totals that look off and leave the code.

advanced.situation: The team must move a payment module to a new library version. The old library loses support next quarter, and many services call this module.

options.text: Upgrade the module directly on the production servers during the day and watch the error logs.
Map the services using the module, upgrade on a branch, and release in stages with rollback.
Upgrade the module on a branch, run the full test suite, and release it everywhere.
Wait until the final month before support ends, then upgrade the module in one quick release.

basic.situation: Your team lead asks you to write a short weekly status update for the project. The login feature is done, but payments are two days behind.

options.text: Say login is done and payments are two days behind, and offer to explain if asked.
Report both features as done and finish payments quietly before anyone tests the system this week.
Say login is done, payments are two days behind, why, and when you expect them done.
Report that login is done and payments are progressing well, to keep the team calm.

advanced.situation: You are creating a standard weekly report template for five teams. Some teams already use their own formats and say a new one adds paperwork.

options.text: Ask teams what they need, draft one short template, and pilot it with two teams.
Announce the new template as compulsory from Monday and drop reports that use older formats.
Let each team keep its own format and collect the reports in a shared folder.
Write one short template from the existing reports and share it with the five teams.

basic.situation: You are given a checklist to test a new search box on the staff portal. One step fails: a search starting with a space returns no results.

options.text: Mark the whole feature as passed because spaces at the start are rare in real use.
Mark the step failed, note the exact input and result, and tell the developer.
Retype the search with no space, mark the step passed, and note that it works.
Mark the step as failed and move on to finish the rest of the checklist.

advanced.situation: You must set the validation procedure for a new loan calculator. The release date is fixed, and the team proposes testing just common loan amounts.

options.text: Define test cases for common, boundary and invalid amounts and record the expected result of each.
Skip formal tests, since the formula was copied from a spreadsheet that the bank already uses.
Test the common amounts plus the largest and smallest amounts allowed, and record the results.
Test the common amounts and extend the testing after release if users report problems.

basic.situation: A colleague from sales asks how often the company app gets maintenance updates and whether customers will notice. You know the schedule.

options.text: Explain that updates run monthly, usually at night, and tell her where the schedule is posted.
Tell her updates run monthly and that she should ask the support team about timing.
Tell her customers will not notice because updates are small, so she need not worry.
Promise her that there will be no downtime and tell her to say so to customers.

advanced.situation: The CEO asks whether to rebuild the ageing order system or keep patching it. A vendor offers a rebuild, and your team is split.

options.text: Let the team vote on it and send the CEO the result with a short note.
Tell the CEO the rebuild will take two months, since the vendor's sales team said so.
Present both paths with costs, risks and timelines, state your recommendation, and note what is unknown.
Recommend the rebuild because ageing systems cost more over time, and summarise the team's concerns.

basic.situation: Your senior tester asks you to draft test scenarios for a new forgot password feature on a banking app.

options.text: Write scenarios for the normal reset path and one invalid email case for review.
Copy the scenarios from the login feature and change the words to match.
Write scenarios from the finished feature's behaviour and mark them all as passing.
List the normal path and failure cases like expired links and unknown emails.

advanced.situation: Your product launches in two weeks, and managers ask you to define release readiness criteria. Developers say the usual standards are too strict.

options.text: Set criteria using last release's numbers and ask the developers to confirm them.
Set criteria by risk, with agreed limits on open defects, and get sign-off.
Define the criteria after testing so that they match the results you have.
Relax the defect limits for this release to match the developers' timeline.

basic.situation: An automated test script fails after the login page got a new button. Your senior asks you to update the script.

options.text: Update the locator and tell your senior that the script is current now.
Update the button locator in the script, rerun it, and save the change.
Change the script to skip the login steps so the test passes again.
Disable the failing test until the developers confirm the new page design.

advanced.situation: Your team spends two days each release checking the same 200 screens by hand. You are asked to design an automated testing tool to help.

options.text: Find repeated checks, automate the stable screens first, and measure time saved.
Buy a commercial testing tool and ask the team to move all checks into it.
Replace the manual checks with a script that clicks through each screen and reports success.
Write scripts for all 200 screens at once before the next release begins.

basic.situation: Your senior asks you to watch the test server's response time while the team runs a test, and report it.

options.text: Record response times during the run and note any spikes with their timings.
Check the response time at the start and the end of the test run.
Restart the test server when it looks slow and carry on watching it.
Report that the server seemed fine because no errors appeared on the screen.

advanced.situation: A new release meets its feature specification, but its pages load slower than the company's performance standard. The product manager wants to ship.

options.text: Report the deviation with measurements and suggest specific changes before the release date.
Remove the slowest pages from the test set so the results meet the standard.
Ask the product manager to relax the performance standard for this release.
Report the slow pages and let the product manager decide on shipping.

basic.situation: While testing a checkout page you find that the total does not update after removing an item.

options.text: Log the steps, expected result, actual result and a screenshot in the tracker.
Note it in your own file and report it with other defects later.
Fix the page code yourself and merge the change to the test branch.
Report it to the developer in the team chat with a short description.

advanced.situation: Your team has two years of test results. Defects keep recurring in the payment module, and managers ask what to change in the process.

options.text: Remove older closed defects from the database so the module's totals look smaller.
Analyse past defects by cause and module, and propose process changes with data.
Count defects per module and tell managers that payments need more testing time.
Ask the payment developers why the defects recur and report their answers.

basic.situation: Your senior gives you step-by-step instructions to install a mobile app testing tool on a test computer.

options.text: Follow the steps in order, note versions, and run the sample test.
Install the tool on your own laptop using the company licence and test there.
Install the newest version from the tool's website instead of the stated version.
Follow the steps and tell your senior the tool is installed on the computer.

advanced.situation: You need to recreate the live ordering system's environment for testing. The live system holds real customer data and runs on special hardware.

options.text: Build from configuration records, use masked data, and verify it matches live.
Copy the live database into the test environment with the same settings.
Run the tests on the live ordering system during quiet hours to save effort.
Use ordinary servers with similar settings and compare a few results with live.

basic.situation: In a design review for a new booking screen, the designer describes how it should work. You are asked to take notes on the requirements.

options.text: Leave the notes to the designer and rely on the slides sent later.
Write a summary of the main points and send it to the team.
Write down the requirements that seem most relevant to your own test cases.
Write down each requirement, note unclear points, and confirm them after the meeting.

advanced.situation: The team wants a new bug tracking tool. Developers prefer one tool, testers another, and the vendor of a third offers a big discount.

options.text: Recommend the cheapest of the three tools since all of them track bugs.
Recommend the tool most testers prefer since they will use it more.
Define needs with both groups, trial each tool, and recommend one with reasons.
Recommend the discounted tool and sign the vendor's three-year contract for the team.

basic.situation: Your lead asks you to add a contact form to a small clinic's page in Klang. An old project has a form snippet that mostly fits.

options.text: Paste the old snippet, rename its fields for the clinic, and test a submission.
Ask the colleague who wrote the snippet to confirm it works, then use it.
Copy the old snippet into the page as it is, since it already worked once.
Build the form from the clinic's required fields, reusing old snippet lines that clearly fit.

advanced.situation: A Penang shop wants a catalogue site that its two non-technical staff can update daily. You must choose the platform and tools for the build.

options.text: Match a content management system to the staff's daily tasks and the catalogue's likely growth.
Build a small admin page in your familiar framework so staff can edit products.
Hand-code the catalogue as plain pages, so the site stays light and fast.
Pick a popular website builder, since staff can edit pages easily and hosting is included.

basic.situation: You just changed the footer links on a company website. Your checklist says to test the pages before telling the team the update is done.

options.text: Check the home page in one browser, since every page shares the same footer template.
Click each footer link in two browsers and on your phone, then tick the checklist.
Click each footer link in your usual browser, tick the checklist, and tell the team.
Ask a colleague if the footer looks fine on their screen, then report it done.

advanced.situation: Your agency is moving three client sites to a new server whose folders you must set up. The old server kept everything in one folder, but clients' files must stay separate.

options.text: Make clear-named client folders with matching subfolders so the team can find files easily.
Make clear-named client folders with matching subfolders, then restrict each folder to that client's users.
Give the largest client its own folder and keep the other two together for now.
Keep one shared folder and use file name prefixes per client, as before.

basic.situation: You finished testing a new login page and found two display faults on a mobile phone. Your lead wants the results written down for the team.

options.text: Message the developer about the two faults on chat so they can start fixing them.
Record each fault with the phone model, browser, steps to repeat it and a screenshot.
Note each fault with its page name and a short description for your lead.
Write that the login page passed with small issues, since fixing them will take minutes.

advanced.situation: A client's online shop slows down during sales. Your manager asks you to document the technical factors for next week's hosting review.

options.text: Paste the hosting provider's summary report into the document, as it lists the server figures.
Record the monthly average server load and bandwidth, and note the dates customers complained.
Record server load, bandwidth and page timings at sale peaks, with customers' browsers and devices.
Describe the slowdowns in plain words and leave the figures to the hosting team.

basic.situation: A Kuching bakery owner wants an online ordering page and asks for something easy for customers. You must turn this into a short list of technical needs.

options.text: List common ordering features such as menu, cart and payment, and ask her to approve.
Record the need as easy ordering and start designing, so she can react to a draft.
Study how two other bakery sites take orders and copy their features into the list.
Ask how customers order today and how many orders come daily, then list the needs.

advanced.situation: A clinic group wants one appointment system for five branches. Before any coding starts, you must prepare models showing how the data and screens fit together.

options.text: Build a working booking screen for one branch first, then draw the models from it.
Base screens and the data model on how staff book now, then test a prototype.
Draw a data model of patients, doctors and appointments and share it with the developers.
Draw data and screen models from the clinic's booking form and share them with the developers.

basic.situation: Your team lead mentions that an upcoming browser update will change how some page features work. You have one free hour this week to read up on it.

options.text: Skim a headline about the update and tell the team no page checks are needed.
Ask a colleague who has read about the change to explain it at the next meeting.
Read a popular developer blog post on the change and share it with the team.
Read the browser maker's official notes and mark which of your pages the change affects.

advanced.situation: Staff keep editing the company website directly, and last week an outdated price went live. You are asked to set up how future website changes are handled.

options.text: Keep the current arrangement and fix mistakes when reported, since staff know their content.
Email staff a reminder to check prices before saving and to report any slip.
Turn on version history and backups so any earlier page can be restored quickly.
Have changes made on a test copy, checked by a colleague, then published and logged.

basic.situation: A customer emails saying she was charged twice for one order on the company website. Your supervisor gave you a standard reply template for payment questions.

options.text: Forward the email to finance and consider it handled, since payments are their area.
Send the template reply, say finance will follow up, and give finance her order details.
Send the template reply and say finance will follow up on the double charge.
Reply that a refund will arrive within three days, since double charges are usually errors.

advanced.situation: An online shop's pages load slowly every weekend. Your manager asks you to recommend a server improvement within a budget of a few thousand ringgit.

options.text: Use past weekend load and timing records to find the bottleneck, then recommend a fix.
Check the hosting dashboard for resource spikes and recommend moving up to the next plan.
Compress the site's images and report it solved, since images are a common cause.
Get quotes from two hosting providers for a bigger server and recommend the cheaper one.

basic.situation: You collected feedback from five users on a booking page. Three say the confirm button is hard to find. Your lead asks you to document the design requirements.

options.text: List the feedback by theme, note three of five users struggled, and propose a clearer button placement.
Change the button colour on the live site yourself and tell the lead about it afterwards.
Write down that some users find the button hard to see and suggest making it larger.
Record the feedback but leave out the button, since five users is a small sample.
