Compare fault times with billing logs and identify peak interruption conditions.

basic.situation: A customer asks when their statement was mailed. Your account screen shows the dispatch date and the approved response script.

options.text: Confirm the account details first, then share the dispatch date shown on screen clearly.
Read the dispatch date on screen and share it using the approved script.
Tell the customer that mailed statements usually arrive within a few working days.
Use a date from another customer's recent statement as an estimate.

advanced.situation: A customer disputes a protested check and asks you to send supporting account papers to a new address. Your records include a stop-payment notice and mailing details.

options.text: Ask a colleague to explain the notice while you prepare the requested papers.
Send papers to the new address and ask the customer to confirm delivery.
Explain the notice status and refer the address change through the approved account process.
Confirm the account, explain the notice, and route papers through verified address procedures.

basic.situation: You are keying twelve supplier invoices into the accounting software before month-end. One invoice shows a supplier name spelled slightly differently from the vendor list.

options.text: Set that invoice aside, post the other eleven, and ask a colleague about it.
Check the invoice's registration number against the vendor list, then post to that vendor.
Create a new vendor record using the invoice's spelling so it posts today.
Post it under the vendor with the nearest spelling, as it is likely the same.

advanced.situation: A new colleague keeps posting the monthly office rental to general expenses. You have been asked to train her on the accounting software and the chart of accounts.

options.text: Explain how accounts are grouped, then have her classify sample items and review them together.
Reclassify her entries yourself at month-end so the ledger is tidy for the accountant.
Demonstrate the rental posting on screen and give her a list of common account codes.
Send her the software manual link and tell her to read the posting section.

basic.situation: You are matching supplier invoices to purchase orders. One invoice totals RM 4,800, but the purchase order says RM 4,200, and the goods have been received.

options.text: Match it to the delivery order and pass it as billed, since the goods arrived.
Compare the line items to find the RM 600 gap, then query purchasing before posting.
Return the invoice to the supplier and ask for a revised one matching the order.
Post the invoice and add a note saying it differs from the purchase order.

advanced.situation: Two colleagues reconcile supplier statements in different ways, and month-end figures keep arriving late with small unexplained differences. You are asked to help make the checks consistent.

options.text: Park small differences in a suspense account so month-end reports go out on schedule.
Draft a shared checklist with tolerance limits and sign-off steps, then trial it together.
Recheck all their reconciliations yourself before each month-end close so the figures stay dependable.
Review both methods against last month's differences and tell everyone to follow the stronger one.

basic.situation: A caller says he is a customer's brother and asks for the balance on her account. Company policy limits account details to the account holder.

options.text: Give him the balance, since a family member is unlikely to misuse it.
Explain that account details are private and suggest he ask her to contact the office.
Ask him for her account number and name, then share the balance if they match.
Explain the policy and offer to call her on the number in the records.

advanced.situation: A new part-timer emails customer statements to a shared team mailbox for convenience. Policy says statements go to the customer's registered email address, and month-end is tomorrow.

options.text: Pause the practice, list statements already sent there, and report the list to your supervisor.
Remind the part-timer of the policy and ask her to use registered email addresses.
Keep the shared mailbox for this month-end deadline, then raise the policy afterwards.
Copy the shared mailbox on every statement so a record exists if customers query later.

basic.situation: A customer paid RM 2,400 on an RM 2,500 invoice, taking a 4% early-payment discount. The invoice terms allow it within 14 days, and the payment was received on day 16.

options.text: Write off the RM 100 as a small difference so the invoice can be closed today.
Record the RM 2,400 received, show RM 100 still due, since day 16 is late.
Treat the invoice as settled in full, since RM 100 is small and the customer regular.
Record the RM 2,400 received and ask your supervisor whether the discount can still apply.

advanced.situation: A colleague's loan schedule shows monthly interest of RM 540 on a RM 90,000 balance at 6% a year. You are asked to verify the schedule before it goes to the customer.

options.text: Sign it off because the repayment total looks close to the loan offer figure.
Recompute one month by hand, then test her formula against that result on every row.
Tell her the interest looks high and ask her to recheck before sending it.
Recompute the first month by hand, fix that row, and return the schedule to her.

basic.situation: Your supervisor is out. A supplier phones asking whether their invoice has been paid, while you are busy filing. The payment records are on your computer.

options.text: Take the supplier's invoice number and phone number, then call back once the filing is finished.
Say the payment is on its way, since invoices usually get settled within the agreed terms.
Ask for the invoice number, check the payment record on screen, and give the payment status.
Ask the supplier to email your supervisor, who normally handles payment queries, when she returns.

advanced.situation: Two colleagues use different cost-centre codes for the same supplier's documents, so filing and searches are inconsistent. You are asked to guide them on coding.

options.text: Recode the mismatched documents yourself at the end of each week so searches give consistent results.
Pick the code you think is more common and tell both colleagues to follow it.
Make a one-page code list for common suppliers, share it, and spot-check next week's filing.
Ask each colleague to follow the company coding procedure and bring any unclear cases to you.

basic.situation: A customer pays RM 350 in cash at the counter for an overdue invoice. There is a queue behind her, and your supervisor is on a call nearby.

options.text: Count the cash together, issue a numbered receipt, and enter it in the cash book.
Take the cash and tell her a receipt will follow after the day's takings are banked.
Put the RM 350 in the drawer and record it when you balance up at closing.
Take the cash, give a handwritten acknowledgement, and key the payment in after the queue clears.

advanced.situation: While checking the week's cash receipts, you find three receipt numbers missing from the sequence. The cash book total is also RM 120 lower than the bank deposit slip.

options.text: Report the out-of-sequence receipts and the RM 120 difference to your supervisor, and wait for instructions.
Ask the cashier who made the deposit to explain the RM 120 and the receipt gaps.
Treat the RM 120 as a timing difference and move on to the next week's records.
Match receipt copies and the deposit slip to the cash book, then report what you find.

basic.situation: A patron presents gaming chips for exchange during a quiet period. You are learning the cash register process with a cashier nearby.

options.text: Enter the chip value from the table slip and pay the displayed amount.
Count the chips, enter the exchange, and match the register amount before paying.
Use the previous exchange amount and adjust the cash for this patron.
Follow the register prompts and ask the nearby cashier to confirm the amount.

advanced.situation: During a busy shift, a high-value check exchange does not match the expected chip inventory. You are also due to rotate cash between windows.

options.text: Record the difference and finish the scheduled rotation before checking the exchange.
Pause that exchange, recount its items, and reconcile the window before rotating funds.
Ask another cashier to recount the chips while you prepare the cash rotation.
Complete the exchange, then adjust the window inventory to match the expected balance.

basic.situation: You are counting the window funds at closing. The daily transaction summary is ready, and your supervisor can help with the reconciliation.

options.text: Count the cash once and ask your supervisor whether the total seems right.
Count the funds by denomination and compare the total with the daily summary.
Use the supervisor's count and mark the daily summary as balanced.
Compare the drawer total with yesterday's closing figure before signing.

advanced.situation: An exchange summary and authorization forms disagree on a large transaction. You are asked to review the reports and help newer cashiers resolve the error.

options.text: Review the report totals and ask an experienced cashier to explain the difference.
Trace the transaction across forms and summaries, then coach cashiers on documenting the match.
Ask cashiers to check their authorization forms whenever a report differs.
Change the summary to match the authorization form and close the review.

basic.situation: A familiar patron asks what another customer's large exchange was while you are handling transaction slips at the cage window.

options.text: Tell the patron to ask the other customer directly about the exchange.
Say you cannot discuss another patron's exchange and continue serving.
Keep the other patron's transaction private and return to the current exchange.
Mention the amount but leave out the other customer's name.

advanced.situation: You notice transaction slips left exposed at the cage while a visitor without a staff badge is nearby. The visitor is asking where to find the cashier.

options.text: Call a nearby colleague over while keeping the slips in view.
Cover the slips, alert cage security, and direct the visitor to the public counter.
Answer the visitor's question and leave the slips for the next cashier.
Move the slips under the counter and tell a colleague about the visitor.

basic.situation: A department manager requests a supply of chips for a scheduled shift. You can check the request and prepare the transfer from cage inventory.

options.text: Use the last department request as a guide and send the same mix.
Confirm the request details, then supply the chips and record the transfer.
Prepare the requested chips and ask the manager to sign the transfer slip.
Check the cage balance and supply a similar amount from available chips.

advanced.situation: Weekend shifts have repeatedly requested extra small-denomination currency, while unused chips return after each shift. You are asked to forecast window needs and plan inventory orders.

options.text: Compare request and return patterns by shift, then set a practical reserve for windows.
Ask each window to estimate its needs before the next busy weekend.
Order the usual weekly amounts and let windows request any extra currency.
Increase the small-denomination order and reduce the chip stock by a fixed amount.

basic.situation: A patron asks you to process an exchange in a way that differs from the cage procedure you have been shown. Your supervisor is working nearby.

options.text: Pause the exchange and tell the patron you need to check the cage guide.
Ask your supervisor to handle the exchange because it differs from the usual process.
Follow the posted cage procedure and ask your supervisor about the unusual request.
Use the patron's suggested method since it seems faster for both of you.

advanced.situation: Two cage procedures seem to apply differently to a patron's unusual exchange. You are unsure which instruction controls and must keep the transaction within gaming regulations.

options.text: Hold the transaction, compare the relevant procedures, and ask the compliance contact to clarify.
Use the procedure that requires fewer steps and document the patron's details.
Choose the newer procedure and process the exchange using its steps.
Pause the exchange and ask a senior cashier which procedure they usually follow.

basic.situation: A new cashier asks how patrons exchange gaming chips for currency. You have a basic operations script and are helping with their orientation.

options.text: Tell the cashier to watch the next patron and follow their choices.
Walk through the exchange script with a sample transaction and invite questions.
Describe the exchange in your own words and mention the cash register.
Read the exchange script aloud and give the new cashier a copy.

advanced.situation: A new cashier is learning how to explain exchange options to patrons, and questions vary across shifts. You are asked to help improve orientation materials and coach them.

options.text: Write a short guide from common questions and practise responses with the new cashier.
Explain the main exchange options, then listen as the cashier answers one question.
Ask the new cashier to shadow you and note questions patrons ask.
Share your usual answers and let the cashier try them during the next shift.

basic.situation: You are completing this week's time sheets. One employee's clock record is missing a departure time, but the roster shows their scheduled shift.

options.text: Copy yesterday's pattern into today's sheet and submit it before cutoff.
Use the roster times when a clock entry is missing, then note the gap.
Compare the clock record with the supervisor's shift note and flag a mismatch.
Match the roster and clock entries, then enter the confirmed arrival and departure times.

advanced.situation: An employee disputes a leave balance after a transfer between departments. Their record shows a carry-forward and two recent leave entries that do not match their payslips.

options.text: Check the latest payslip and tell the employee to raise any older entries later.
Ask the employee to list their leave dates and update the balance from their reply.
Rebuild the balance from approved leave entries and the transfer record, then explain the difference.
Compare the leave entries with the department record and report any mismatch for review.

basic.situation: A new hire's onboarding form lists a bank account and start date, but the payroll system requires several employee details before the next pay run.

options.text: Copy a similar employee's record and change the new hire's name and account.
Review the form for missing details and enter the complete information into payroll.
Enter the start date and bank account first, then fill remaining fields later.
Enter the supplied details, then check the saved record against the onboarding form.

advanced.situation: You are moving a department's employee records into an updated payroll system. Several staff have similar names, changed bank details, and recent transfers.

options.text: Start with the largest department, using its completed records to guide the rest.
Match employees by name and transfer the remaining fields from the department spreadsheet.
Use the migration template, match staff identifiers, and reconcile transferred records against source totals.
Import the batch, then reconcile record counts and flagged fields against the source file.

basic.situation: You are calculating this week's wages from approved hours and a deduction sheet. One employee has overtime recorded, and the entry differs from the usual pattern.

options.text: Calculate the wages from the hours and deductions, then flag the unusual entry.
Apply the stated wage and deduction rules, then compare the result with approved hours.
Copy the previous wage total and adjust it by the new hours.
Use the usual overtime entry and send the calculation for supervisor review.

advanced.situation: A sales team has a new approved commission plan with tiered rates and returned sales. You are compiling payroll data before the calculation cutoff.

options.text: Calculate commissions with the new tiers and flag returned sales for checking.
Use the prior commission rates and list the returned sales for later review.
Apply the approved tiers to net eligible sales and compare totals with source records.
Enter the new rates for each tier and calculate commissions from reported sales.

basic.situation: You are reviewing a time sheet and wage computation before payroll closes. The hours look plausible, but one shift total does not match the daily entries.

options.text: Compare each daily entry with the shift total, then reconcile the supported figure.
Check the weekly total against the prior week and keep it if they are similar.
Update the shift total using the daily entries and record the change.
Recheck the daily entries and flag the total that differs for follow-up.

advanced.situation: Several payroll clerks are resolving attendance discrepancies differently, and recent adjustments have lacked clear notes. You are asked to improve the review process.

options.text: Let clerks keep their current methods and collect their notes at month-end.
Share a short checklist covering attendance, hours, adjustments, and discrepancy notes.
Ask each clerk to send difficult cases to you for a decision.
Write a shared checklist with evidence fields and coach colleagues through sample discrepancies.

basic.situation: You are preparing a new employee's first pay statement. Their approved hours are in payroll, but the earnings statement has not yet been generated.

options.text: Generate the statement and compare its totals with the approved payroll summary.
Generate the statement from approved payroll data and check the earnings and deductions.
Prepare the statement from payroll and ask the employee to confirm its figures.
Print a statement using the prior pay period's figures as a temporary copy.

advanced.situation: A bulk pay run is ready, but several bank transfers have failed and some employees have retroactive adjustments. You are handling the payment records.

options.text: Separate failed transfers, validate employee details, and record approved adjustments for reissue.
Change the account details from employee messages and resend the failed payments.
Check the failed accounts and prepare approved adjustments for the next payment batch.
Retry every failed transfer using the same batch and record the new status.

basic.situation: You are preparing the period-end payroll report. The issued payroll total differs from the bank statement by a small amount, and you need to reconcile the records.

options.text: Check the largest payments first and ask the bank about the remaining difference.
Compare the payroll and bank totals, then note the amount that differs.
Match each issued payment to the bank entries and record the identified difference.
Adjust the report total to match the bank statement and submit it for filing.

advanced.situation: A payroll guidance update may affect deductions next period. Managers ask whether a planned payroll change is compliant, while the details remain unclear.

options.text: Review the current update and tell managers which deduction questions need confirmation.
Apply the change described in an old payroll email and notify managers afterward.
Ask managers to defer the change until the next scheduled payroll review.
Check current official guidance, identify the affected payroll items, and explain the confirmed change.

basic.situation: A department submits a requisition for printer paper, and you need to check its wording and specifications before processing.

options.text: Ask the department to review the wording before you process it.
Reuse the last paper order and update its requested quantity.
Match the item wording and specification to the department's stated need.
Check the paper size, quantity, and item wording against the request.

advanced.situation: An audit finds inconsistent item descriptions and outdated prices across purchasing files. You are asked to review the records and improve their long-term accuracy.

options.text: Compare descriptions and prices with recent records, then list discrepancies for buyers.
Compare entries with recent quotes and orders, flag stale prices, and set review dates.
Replace outdated prices after checking a current supplier quote and matching order.
Ask buyers to confirm frequently used entries against their recent purchasing records.

basic.situation: Your team needs a replacement label printer, and you are asked to find potential suppliers and collect basic product details.

options.text: Search catalogs for matching models and note their supplier details.
Ask a colleague for a supplier name before starting your search.
Choose the first printer listing with a familiar brand name.
Compare catalog models by key features, then record supplier contacts and details.

advanced.situation: A department needs a specialized label printer that must work with existing stock and fit a tight delivery window. You are asked to find and interview suppliers.

options.text: Contact the usual supplier and ask about model compatibility, available stock, and delivery timing.
Order the familiar model after the department confirms its stock and delivery fit.
Define stock needs and delivery limits, then interview suppliers using matching product questions.
Contact several suppliers about compatibility with existing stock and their delivery estimates.

basic.situation: The storeroom count for packing tape is lower than usual, and a department has submitted its weekly demand forecast.

options.text: Check the count against the forecast and place a routine reorder if needed.
Compare the count and forecast with usual use before deciding whether to reorder.
Order the amount requested by the department for its next delivery.
Use last week's order quantity as this week's reorder amount.

advanced.situation: A high-value materials bill arrives while stock is split between two stores. Your role includes buying duties and routing bills for approval and payment.

options.text: Reconcile store counts with the bill and order, then route it for approval.
Check the purchase order and bill, then send both to the assigned approver.
Forward the bill for payment after checking its quantity against the purchase order.
Ask store staff to confirm the billed quantity before routing the documents for approval.

basic.situation: A routine order includes listed unit prices and delivery charges, and you need to calculate the total before charging the invoice to an account.

options.text: Use the subtotal from the supplier's earlier quotation for this order.
Ask the requesting department to calculate the total before charging it.
Add the listed item costs and delivery charge, then record the total.
Check the order quantities and prices, then total items and delivery charges.

advanced.situation: A supplier asks whether a purchase can be split across budget periods, and the request references internal purchasing rules you maintain for the team.

options.text: Check purchasing guidance, explain the relevant process, and share its source with the requester.
Ask a colleague how the team handled comparable requests during the previous budget cycle.
Review current guidance and summarize the relevant purchasing rule for the requester.
Tell the supplier to follow a similar split used for an earlier purchase.

basic.situation: A department's approved requisition is ready to become a purchase order, and the supplier needs a copy for a routine delivery.

options.text: Match the order details to the approved requisition, then send both copies.
Prepare the order from the approved requisition and send copies to both parties.
Reuse the last order form and change the supplier and requested quantity.
Ask the supplier to confirm the order details before you prepare it.

advanced.situation: Requisitions and contracts are tracked in separate files, so staff cannot see which orders are awaiting action. You are asked to improve status tracking.

options.text: Use the latest order spreadsheet and add each new request with its current status.
Ask departments to email when an order status changes, including its reference number.
Create a shared tracker listing each record's status, owner, dates, and next action.
List open requisitions and contracts in one file with their owners, status, and next steps.

basic.situation: A supplier calls to ask whether a routine order is still due this week. Your order record shows its current status and expected date.

options.text: Use a prior order's timing to estimate this delivery, and explain that the date is unconfirmed.
Tell the supplier you will review the record and call back with its status and date.
Check the record, then tell the supplier its schedule and expected arrival date.
Open the order record, confirm its status and expected date, then explain both to the supplier.

advanced.situation: A supplier reports a shortage that may delay a department's scheduled work. You need to resolve the delivery issue and update the requester.

options.text: Tell the requester the original date remains planned while the supplier checks stock.
Confirm the shortage, agree a partial delivery date, and update the requester with options.
Ask the supplier for a revised date and delivery options, then update the requester promptly.
Tell the requester about the supplier's delay and ask which option suits the work.

basic.situation: A customer presents a cheque for deposit, and the written amount appears different from the numerical amount.

options.text: Pause processing and explain that the amounts need clarification first.
Compare both amounts and ask a colleague to verify the difference before processing.
Enter the numerical amount because it is simpler to process.
Tell the customer the amounts differ and ask them to clarify.

advanced.situation: Your drawer is short after several payments, and one cheque endorsement looks different from the identification presented.

options.text: Reconcile entries and documents, then follow branch steps to report the mismatch.
Record the shortage and ask a colleague to review it before closing.
Review payment entries with a colleague and document any remaining discrepancy.
Change the drawer total to match the closest payment entry.

basic.situation: A customer calls to ask why a bill payment has not appeared in their account yet.

options.text: Suggest the customer call tomorrow if the payment has not appeared.
Say bill payments can take time to appear in the account.
Look up the payment and share its current status with them.
Check the transaction status and explain when the payment should appear.

advanced.situation: A customer disputes a fee after using several services, and a new teller is waiting nearby to learn how you handle complaints.

options.text: Review account history, explain the fee, and guide the teller through the response.
Explain the fee schedule and offer to review the account history together.
Invite the customer to discuss the charge when the branch is quieter.
Waive the fee to settle the complaint and move the queue along.

basic.situation: Your cash drawer is running low before lunch, and you are preparing the day's cash supply request.

options.text: Order the usual amount in the usual denominations.
Check the drawer balance and expected traffic before requesting denominations.
Ask nearby counters which denominations they need before submitting your request.
Request extra large notes to avoid another cash order.

advanced.situation: Two counters need different notes during a busy afternoon, and the remaining cash inventory is lower than forecast.

options.text: Reconcile inventory, prioritize confirmed needs, and request replenishment through branch procedures.
Split remaining notes evenly between both counters after checking their needs.
Send small notes to the busiest counter based on current demand.
Ask both counters to estimate their needs before you allocate remaining notes.

basic.situation: You enter a customer's deposit, but the receipt total differs from the amount on the deposit slip.

options.text: Re-enter the amount shown on the deposit slip and print a replacement receipt.
Ask a colleague to review the entry with you while the customer waits nearby.
Compare the entry and slip, then amend the transaction before printing a receipt.
Give the customer the receipt, then review the entry with a colleague when the queue clears.

advanced.situation: A system error leaves several receipts unconfirmed, and a colleague suggests entering the same transactions again.

options.text: Check transaction status and approved recovery steps before re-entering anything.
Ask the colleague to wait while you check the transaction log.
Print the pending list and retry the entries after the queue falls.
Re-enter each transaction so customers can leave with receipts.

basic.situation: You are counting a mixed bundle of notes and coins before preparing the branch's deposit shipment.

options.text: Run the bundle through the machine and record its displayed total.
Separate denominations, count them, and compare the total with the control sheet.
Estimate the coin value from the labelled bags and finish the notes.
Count the notes first and ask a colleague to check the coins.

advanced.situation: A colleague finds inconsistent denomination bundles across several cash boxes before the branch's scheduled shipment.

options.text: Leave the bundles as they are so shipment stays on schedule.
Rearrange the boxes to match the most common denomination pattern before shipment.
Ask the colleague to recount each box before sealing the shipment.
Recount affected boxes, record variances, and align bundles with branch procedures.

basic.situation: You receive a batch of deposit slips at closing and need to file them with the day's transaction records.

options.text: Stack them in the tray for the next shift to file.
Sort slips by the branch filing sequence and check each batch label.
Group the slips by counter before placing them in the cabinet.
File the slips by date and note the batch on the cover sheet.

advanced.situation: A late night-deposit batch contains mixed transaction slips, and the next shift needs a reliable processing trail.

options.text: Sort by transaction type, log the handoff, and file records by procedure.
Leave the mixed batch on the counter for morning staff to sort.
Sort the slips by transaction type, then place each group in clearly marked trays.
File the whole batch under night deposits for the next shift.

basic.situation: A customer requests a withdrawal, and you need to prepare the order from the account records.

options.text: Fill in the order from the request and check the account number.
Ask a coworker to confirm the account before preparing the order.
Copy the account details from the last order and submit this one.
Match the request to the account, then complete each required order field.

advanced.situation: Several customers are converting securities with different redemption terms, and the team needs a consistent form for recording each transaction.

options.text: Build a template with separate fields for security, conversion terms, and redemption instructions.
Create a template that separates transaction types and prompts checks for required details.
Adapt the usual form and add a notes box for unusual terms.
Use the last conversion form and replace the customer and security details.

basic.situation: A completed customer trade needs its brokerage fee calculated using the rate on your checklist.

options.text: Use the last customer's fee as a guide and enter a similar amount.
Calculate from the trade value and ask a coworker to check it.
Apply the checklist rate to the trade value and record your calculation.
Confirm the fee basis, calculate with the checklist, and compare the result.

advanced.situation: A customer’s account has several trades under different commission arrangements, and your audit finds totals that do not reconcile.

options.text: Recalculate each trade using its recorded arrangement, then compare account totals.
Check the largest trades first and adjust smaller entries to reconcile.
Map each arrangement to its fee basis and document a repeatable reconciliation method.
Apply one familiar commission rate across the account to balance the totals.

basic.situation: Your daily price check shows a pledged stock has fallen, and the account screen flags possible additional collateral.

options.text: Use yesterday’s price as the reference and note a small decline.
Review the price change and account threshold, then record the collateral flag.
Record the lower price and wait for tomorrow’s routine account review.
Check today’s price in the tool and note the flagged account.

advanced.situation: Several pledged stocks move sharply during the day, and staff are manually checking accounts with different collateral thresholds.

options.text: Group accounts by threshold and draft alert levels for review with the team.
Configure alerts around account thresholds and test them against past price movements.
Set alerts for every price move so staff can review each account.
Use one large percentage trigger across pledged stocks and share the alert list.

basic.situation: A dividend instruction names an owner whose details differ slightly from the stock record, and you must verify the entry.

options.text: Ask a coworker whether the name difference looks acceptable before proceeding.
Pause the entry and identify which details need confirmation from the record.
Compare the ownership details and instruction fields against the stock record.
Use the instruction as written and enter its dividend destination.

advanced.situation: A revised government instruction changes what ownership information must be checked, and your team’s verification checklist is now outdated.

options.text: Keep using the familiar checklist until the next scheduled team review.
Replace the old checklist with a short summary of the new instruction.
Map each changed requirement to a verification step and update the checklist draft.
Read the revised instruction and list the fields affected in the checklist.

basic.situation: A customer’s security certificate needs transfer to another department, and you are asked to arrange its delivery.

options.text: Check the destination on the request and reserve the next available dispatch.
Confirm the destination and available handoff time, then schedule delivery.
Copy the destination from an earlier transfer and book the next dispatch.
Use the usual delivery route and put the certificate in today’s batch.

advanced.situation: Several departments request certificate transfers on the same day, with limited dispatch capacity and different customer deadlines.

options.text: Reserve the earliest dispatch for the largest batch to reduce handling.
List destinations and deadlines, then draft a schedule for team review.
Group transfers by destination, then check deadlines before confirming dispatch slots.
Book requests in arrival order and send the remaining items tomorrow.

basic.situation: A caller asks why a recent account transaction differs from their statement, and you have the account file and call script.

options.text: Check the transaction entry and describe the difference using the call script.
Check the transaction entry, explain what the file shows, and note the inquiry.
Tell the caller the transaction probably reflects a routine processing delay.
Read the standard script and offer to send the caller a statement copy.

advanced.situation: A customer disputes several account entries while asking about a market drop, and a new colleague is listening to your call.

options.text: Ask the colleague to record key details while you address the customer's concerns.
Say the entries and market movement appear routine before checking supporting records.
Compare each disputed account entry with available records, then address the market question separately.
Review disputed entries, note findings, and separate verified account details from market context.

basic.situation: A customer writes to confirm that their complaint was received. You need to send an acknowledgment using the standard letter format.

options.text: Reply with a quick note using the complaint subject line as a guide.
Type a brief acknowledgment using the usual wording and send it for review.
Send a form letter for a different complaint type to save time.
Use the standard acknowledgment template and check the customer’s name before sending.

advanced.situation: A customer disputes a damage claim, and the file contains conflicting dates and an unusual request for replacement goods. You are drafting the reply.

options.text: Acknowledge the dispute and ask claims staff to verify dates before sending a reply.
Pick the date shown most often and promise the requested replacement to the customer.
Use standard claim wording and leave the replacement request unanswered for now.
List confirmed facts, note the date conflict, and request details needed to assess replacement.

basic.situation: Your team needs a simple monthly report of incoming service complaints. You are gathering the records for your first report.

options.text: Count the complaint entries for the month and note the reporting period.
Count the files currently in the tray and add that figure to the draft.
Use the previous report’s layout and copy its totals into the new draft.
Gather the complaint files and ask a colleague which ones belong in the report.

advanced.situation: A customer requests a special product, and production asks you to compile the records needed to assess its specifications and cost.

options.text: Gather related orders and correspondence, then label confirmed and missing specifications separately.
Send production the latest order and treat it as the full specification.
Attach the related customer records and ask production to identify any missing details.
Compile the most recent customer details and forward them as the working specification.

basic.situation: A requester sends payment for copies of records. You need to record the collection and secure the money according to office practice.

options.text: Note the amount, date, and requester, then secure the payment as required.
Store it with collections and update the payment record after other tasks.
Use the payment for a small office purchase and record that use later.
Record the payment details and place the money in the office's designated secure location.

advanced.situation: A requester disputes the charge for copied records, and the correspondence includes two different page counts. You are preparing the payment request.

options.text: Recount the copies, compare the charge with the recorded cost, and explain the calculation in your letter.
Hold the payment request and ask the records team which page count is current.
Use the page count on the latest note and send the usual payment letter.
Use the higher page count and request payment before the file leaves your desk.

basic.situation: A letter requests a standard office product, and the order details match the usual form. You are responsible for processing it.

options.text: Verify item and quantity, then record the order details from the letter.
Copy item details onto the form and ask a colleague to review them.
Process the item in the subject line and file the letter afterward.
Use the previous order's quantity and forward the request for processing.

advanced.situation: Several orders arrive together, including a revised request that changes a quantity already entered in the control record. You are updating the files.

options.text: Record the revision date, link it to the earlier order, and update the current quantity.
Replace the old quantity with the revised one and keep no note of the change.
Leave the entered quantity and process the revised order as a separate request.
Update the quantity and keep the revised letter with the existing order papers.

basic.situation: A writer asks why a standard request needs a supporting document. Your script explains the requirement, and you need to respond clearly.

options.text: Use the script to explain the requirement and point out the document requested.
Tell the writer the document is optional so the request can move ahead.
Tell the writer the document is required and repeat the wording from the form.
Say the office usually asks for that document and suggest sending it soon.

advanced.situation: A customer requests an exception to a published requirement, and staff are unsure whether the office can meet it. You are explaining the policy and feasibility.

options.text: Explain the published requirement, summarize the request, and ask the relevant team about feasibility.
Promise the exception based on a similar request accepted last month.
Describe the usual process and invite a written request for an exception.
State that the requirement applies and refer the exception question to the relevant team.

basic.situation: A letter about a billing query arrives at the correspondence desk. Your routing guide lists the department that handles billing inquiries.

options.text: Read the subject and route it to the billing team shown on the guide.
Forward it to the busiest department so someone can pass it along.
Send the letter to the department that handled the writer’s last inquiry.
Check the guide’s billing entry and route the letter to that department.

advanced.situation: A batch of signed records must go by certified mail, and a delivery record will be needed for follow-up. You are preparing the shipment.

options.text: Prepare the certified mail forms and keep the batch list for the file.
Check each address, prepare the certified shipment record, and retain its reference with the file.
Use the addresses on the envelopes and write the shipment date on the batch list.
Bundle the records in regular mail and note the recipient on the office copy.

basic.situation: After a routine municipal meeting, you need to prepare the minutes and distribute them to the listed officials and staff.

options.text: Edit the notes into minutes and check the attendee list before distributing them.
Type the notes into the usual format and send them to the regular team list.
Leave out the discussion points that seem minor and circulate the shortened record.
Send the raw notes to everyone who attended so they can review them.

advanced.situation: A resident asks for an older municipal record, but the archive index has two entries with similar dates. You are researching the request.

options.text: Use the index description and prepare the likely record for release.
Choose the entry with the closest date and send its contents to the resident.
Search both entries and ask the records officer which one should be released.
Compare both entries’ identifying details, document the match, and follow the office’s release process.

basic.situation: An applicant gives you their name and address for a license form, but speaks quietly over the counter. You need to record the details.

options.text: Enter a likely spelling for the name so the application can move forward.
Use the address from the applicant’s earlier form to complete this one.
Enter the details as heard and let the applicant check the form later.
Repeat the name and address back to the applicant before entering them on the form.

advanced.situation: Staff report repeated errors in coded license applications. You are asked to help standardize how applicants’ details are collected and entered.

options.text: Set a field-by-field checklist, include a read-back for key details, and explain the coding guide.
Share the coding guide and remind staff to review each completed application.
Tell staff to copy details from the last application when applicants are waiting.
Ask staff to slow down and check the application before submitting it.

basic.situation: A license application is missing a field that appears on the checklist. You need to check the form before it moves forward.

options.text: Ask a colleague whether the blank field can be left empty before routing it.
Pass the form onward and mention the blank field in a note.
Mark the missing field and return the form to the applicant for completion.
Fill the field using a detail from a similar application on file.

advanced.situation: A court filing includes an unfamiliar document and a procedural detail that does not match the usual checklist. You are reviewing it for completeness.

options.text: List the discrepancy, check the applicable procedure, and route the filing for the required review.
Accept the filing because the main form is complete and easy to read.
Compare the document with a similar filing and mark it ready if it looks consistent.
Flag the unfamiliar document and ask the reviewing officer how to handle it.

basic.situation: A caller asks for a staff member who is away from the desk. You are covering the phone and need to handle the call.

options.text: Take the caller’s name, contact details, and message, then pass it to the staff member.
Take a short message and place it on the staff member’s desk.
Transfer the caller to a random extension that sounds like the right section.
Tell the caller to try again later when the staff member is back.

advanced.situation: Several office requests are overdue, and the tracking system has duplicate entries with different follow-up dates. You are maintaining the tracker.

options.text: Keep both entries and ask the assigned staff to confirm which date applies.
Use the most recent date in the tracker and clear the older reminder.
Compare each duplicate with its correspondence, preserve the history, and mark the verified follow-up date.
Delete the duplicate entries and keep the later follow-up date as current.

basic.situation: A member of the public calls to ask when to attend a court appearance. You have the case information and a standard response script.

options.text: Tell the caller the usual arrival time for appearances at that court.
Confirm the case details and explain the listed appearance time using the script.
Give the listed time and suggest the caller check their notice as well.
Read the time from the first case entry and tell the caller to arrive then.

advanced.situation: A caller asks about an outstanding warrant and a possible court appearance. You need to respond within your role as a clerk.

options.text: Say the warrant may remain active and direct the caller to court staff.
Describe the general inquiry process and refer the caller to the appropriate court office.
Suggest visiting the court counter to ask staff about the caller's inquiry.
Explain how to check case information and provide the listed court contact.

basic.situation: A court order is ready to be typed from an approved template. You need to prepare the document for review.

options.text: Enter approved details, compare them with the source, then send the draft for review.
Fill in the template and print a copy for the case file.
Use the template and copy the case details from a nearby file.
Type each order detail from its source, then ask a colleague to proofread the draft.

advanced.situation: A draft court order has a different outcome from the notes recording the proceeding. You are preparing the document for authorized review.

options.text: Flag the conflict, trace both details to source records, and refer the draft for review.
Change the outcome based on what seems typical for this kind of case.
Pause the draft and ask the responsible officer to confirm which outcome belongs in the order.
Use details from the latest note and prepare the order for authorized review.

basic.situation: You are interviewing an applicant by phone, and the checklist asks for income, debts, and current housing details.

options.text: Ask the checklist questions and record the applicant’s answers as stated.
Fill in a likely income figure so the application can move along.
Write down the answers and leave unclear fields for later review.
Ask each question, then clarify any answer that does not fit the form.

advanced.situation: An applicant has several income sources and irregular monthly debts. You need to capture accurate figures during a short interview.

options.text: Use the applicant’s highest income month as the figure for every month.
List each income source and debt by period, then confirm the figures with the applicant.
Record the applicant’s stated income and debts, then ask how often each amount changes.
Ask which income sources and debts vary, and note their amounts by month.

basic.situation: You are checking an applicant’s stated address against a city directory and a public property record.

options.text: Match the name and address, then note the directory and record checked.
Search the directory and record the address shown for the applicant.
Attach a same-name property record to the applicant’s file as a match.
Use the matching street address as confirmation of the applicant’s residence.

advanced.situation: A public record shows a lien under a similar name, while the applicant’s address history includes two recent moves.

options.text: Search the applicant’s latest address and use that result to assess the lien.
Treat the similar name as a match and note the lien in the report.
Compare available names and addresses, then document why the match remains uncertain.
Record the lien as a possible match and continue reviewing the file.

basic.situation: A merchant sends a credit application by post, and you are responsible for receiving and logging incoming applications.

options.text: Date-stamp the application, log its arrival, and route it for processing.
Set the form aside until the merchant calls to confirm it arrived.
Put the application in the processing tray for the next collection.
Log the applicant’s name and place the form with today’s mail.

advanced.situation: Two credit bureaus request reciprocal information, and their files show different account dates for the same customer.

options.text: Compare the requested fields with approved exchange records and log each response.
Send both bureaus the latest full customer file to settle the difference.
Send the confirmed account date to each bureau and note the responses.
Reply with the date from the most recent file and keep a copy.

basic.situation: A customer’s computerized credit record lists recent payments and one missed instalment. You are compiling the file for review.

options.text: List the missed instalment and recent payments in the file summary.
Mark the customer as risky based on the missed instalment.
Leave out the missed instalment so the file reads more smoothly.
Summarise the payment history and link each point to the record.

advanced.situation: A customer meets the stated credit threshold, but the payment history has a recent pattern the standard does not clearly address.

options.text: Compare the pattern with stated criteria, document the evidence, and flag any gap for review.
Approve the application based on its threshold result, then close the review.
Note the recent pattern in the file and apply the stated threshold.
Decline it based on the recent payment pattern and record your reason.

basic.situation: A customer pays part of an outstanding balance, and you need to update the charge and payment record.

options.text: Enter the payment amount and mark the customer’s balance as reduced.
Post the payment against the matching account and retain the receipt reference.
Post the payment to the account and note the amount received.
Subtract the payment from the nearest open balance on screen.

advanced.situation: A subscriber asks by phone for a customer’s credit report, but the caller’s account details do not match the file.

options.text: Read the report summary aloud because the caller knows the customer’s name.
Check the subscriber details against the file and share the authorised report information.
Record the mismatch and ask the caller to use the documented request channel.
Ask the caller to confirm an account detail, then provide the requested summary.

basic.situation: You are filing sales slips in customer ledgers before the monthly billing run, and one slip has a faint account number.

options.text: Compare the slip with a clear account reference before filing it.
Check the merchant note, then file under the account it identifies.
Use the customer name that seems closest in the ledger while checking later.
Place the slip with unclear items for review before the billing run.

advanced.situation: You are preparing a large batch of charge statements, and several customer files contain recent address updates awaiting confirmation.

options.text: Use the existing address list and sample-check a few updated files.
Print statements for confirmed addresses and hold the pending updates aside.
Print the full batch using the newest address listed in each file.
Separate confirmed addresses from pending updates and reconcile each mailing count.

basic.situation: A customer calls about a delayed repair, and you need to record the inquiry and action taken.

options.text: Note the repair delay and tell the next shift to check back.
Close the interaction as resolved because you passed the message along.
Log the issue, the customer’s preferred contact, and the action you took.
Write that the customer called about a repair delay.

advanced.situation: You are checking a new colleague’s logs and find several complaint entries with no recorded actions or outcomes.

options.text: Compare entries with available notes, verify supported details, and teach the logging format.
Fill the missing actions with what probably happened during each call.
Ask the colleague to complete the entries from memory before the shift ends.
Show the colleague a sample entry and explain which fields need recording.

basic.situation: A customer asks for a service with a deposit, and the rate sheet lists the charge and deposit amount.

options.text: Collect the usual deposit and arrange billing for the remaining amount.
Quote the listed charge, collect the deposit, and record the payment.
Check the rate sheet, explain the charge, and arrange the deposit.
Tell the customer a lower charge to secure the order today.

advanced.situation: A customer disputes several monthly charges and has already paid part of the amount while asking to keep service active.

options.text: Review each billed service period and payment, then explain the itemised balance.
Check the latest bill and offer a payment plan for the balance.
Waive the disputed amount to keep the customer satisfied today.
Compare the bill with the service record and explain the charge difference.

basic.situation: A customer changes their mailing address while signing a standard service contract, and you need to update the records.

options.text: Write the new address on a note for the next shift to enter.
Enter the new address on the form and check it with the customer.
Copy the address from the customer’s message into the system.
Leave the old address on the contract so processing stays quick.

advanced.situation: Several contract forms arrive together, including one with a service change that needs an address update and a discontinuance order.

options.text: Enter the discontinuance order first and leave the address update for later.
Group the forms by type and enter each change into the account.
Process each form in arrival order and check the customer names.
Match each form to the account, enter linked changes, and review the completed record.

basic.situation: A customer asks whether a service includes weekend support, and your product guide lists the available support hours.

options.text: Say weekend support is probably included because the service runs all week.
Offer to take the order and let the service team confirm later.
Read the support hours from the guide to the customer.
Check the guide and explain the listed support hours in plain terms.

advanced.situation: A customer compares two service packages with different limits and asks which one suits a household with frequent evening use.

options.text: Recommend the higher package because frequent use usually costs less overall.
Compare the package limits with the customer’s stated evening needs and explain the trade-offs.
Describe both packages and let the customer decide which sounds suitable.
Explain the evening limits for both packages and mention the listed prices.

basic.situation: A claim review results in a partial adjustment, and you need to notify the customer using the approved template.

options.text: Tell the customer an adjustment was made and offer to send details later.
Tell the customer the claim was accepted and end the call.
Send the template with the result and adjustment amount filled in.
Use the template to state the adjustment and the next billing step.

advanced.situation: Different claim handlers are sending customers varied explanations of approved adjustments, leading to repeated questions about what changed.

options.text: Ask each handler to keep using their own explanation and tone.
Draft shared wording that states the result, adjustment, and next customer step.
Send a template with the claim result and adjustment amount fields.
Share an example message for handlers to adapt to each customer.

basic.situation: A customer reports that a promised account change has not appeared, and your screen shows the case is still open.

options.text: Ask the customer to call again if the change is still missing.
Send the case to its assigned team, record the handoff, and schedule a customer update.
Tell the customer the change should appear soon and close the case.
Check the case, contact its assigned team, and update the customer record.

advanced.situation: A customer’s billing complaint remains open after two referrals, and the account still shows the charge they disputed.

options.text: Send the complaint to billing with notes on both referrals and the action still pending.
Refer it again to the same team and tell the customer to wait.
Tell the customer the issue is being reviewed and check again tomorrow.
Review referral notes, find the pending action, and route it to the designated team.

basic.situation: You are interviewing an applicant for assistance, and the waiting room is filling. The application has blank fields for household members and income.

options.text: Ask about household members and income, then note the answers in the application.
Confirm each answer aloud and record any missing details for follow-up.
Reuse last month's details to finish the form before the queue grows.
Ask standard questions and leave unclear fields blank for later review.

advanced.situation: An applicant reports irregular wages that differ from the employer reference. You are checking the discrepancy before completing the assistance investigation.

options.text: Request a recent payslip and hold the wage entry until it arrives.
Ask the applicant to explain the difference and note their response for review.
Compare the dates and pay periods, then ask both sources to clarify the mismatch.
Use the employer's figure as the applicant's monthly wage and close the inquiry.

basic.situation: An applicant asks which documents to bring for a routine assistance claim, while you are covering the counter during a busy morning.

options.text: Give the standard document list and suggest the applicant check it at home.
List the usual documents from the procedure guide and invite follow-up questions.
Check the claim procedure guide and explain which documents fit this application.
Tell the applicant to bring the same papers their neighbour submitted last week.

advanced.situation: An applicant disputes a payment decision and asks how their rights apply to an unusual change in household circumstances. You are explaining the case information available.

options.text: Summarize payment rules and offer to verify the unusual detail with a specialist.
Explain eligibility details and outline the available review route for the applicant.
Restate the payment explanation and invite the applicant to ask about its meaning.
Distinguish confirmed requirements from uncertain facts, then explain rights and next steps clearly.

basic.situation: You are calculating a routine assistance amount from an approved worksheet. The applicant's household size and income are already recorded.

options.text: Calculate from the worksheet and round the amount to a convenient figure.
Check the recorded inputs against the worksheet, calculate, and enter the amount.
Use the previous household's amount as a quick reference for this case.
Apply the worksheet formula and enter the resulting assistance amount.

advanced.situation: A complex case qualifies for assistance through two program components, and the worksheet flags an unusual combined amount for your authorization.

options.text: Hold authorization and ask a colleague to check the combined amount.
Authorize the combined figure from the worksheet and send the case onward.
Reconcile each component's inputs and interaction, then authorize the supported total.
Approve the usual amount for each component and record both payments.

basic.situation: You are entering an assistance application into the case system. The form includes personal details and monthly income, but one field is hard to read.

options.text: Enter the readable details and leave the unclear field empty for now.
Complete the unclear field using the amount on a nearby case record.
Enter the legible details and mark the unclear field for checking.
Compare each entry with the form and flag the unreadable field for clarification.

advanced.situation: An applicant's reported income and bank records show different monthly patterns. You are evaluating the financial data before determining eligibility status.

options.text: Record both figures and note that the records do not match.
Compare dates and transaction types, then evaluate which figures represent relevant income.
Use the lower figure to complete the eligibility assessment today.
Average the figures and use that amount in the eligibility assessment.

basic.situation: You are updating an assigned case after an applicant submits a missing document. The system asks for a short note and the date received.

options.text: Copy a note from a similar case and change the applicant's name.
Enter the date and save the document in the case folder.
Add the receipt date and document name to the case record.
Record the date, document type, and its link to the pending requirement.

advanced.situation: A complex assigned case has conflicting interview notes, employer information, and payment calculations. You are preparing a report for review.

options.text: Summarize the latest interview and attach the supporting case documents.
Set out the timeline, source differences, calculations, and unresolved points for review.
Use the employer figure and omit the notes that do not match it.
List each source and leave the reviewer to compare the details.

basic.situation: Your review shows that an applicant meets the routine assistance criteria, and the case system is ready for the standard grant procedure.

options.text: Hold the procedure until the applicant calls to confirm the outcome.
Start the grant procedure using the amount from a previous case.
Start the standard grant procedure and record the eligibility basis in the case file.
Confirm the recorded eligibility basis matches this case before starting the grant procedure.

advanced.situation: An applicant needs routine assistance and specialist support for housing stability. You can start the assistance procedure and refer them to another agency.

options.text: Refer the applicant to a familiar agency before starting eligible assistance.
Begin routine assistance and provide current contact details for agencies offering housing stability support.
Start eligible assistance and refer the applicant to an agency for housing support.
Start assistance and tell the applicant the case is fully supported.

basic.situation: You are sorting a morning batch of completed forms using the office's alphabetical filing guide. Two folders have similar names.

options.text: Sort by surname and set aside forms whose names seem similar.
Sort the forms by surname and place unclear ones in a nearby folder.
Use the first name to choose between folders with similar surnames.
Check the guide's name fields and sort each form into its matching folder.

advanced.situation: Staff report that the shared filing structure makes older project records hard to find. You are asked to improve it and brief the team.

options.text: Move older records into a new section and leave staff to adapt.
Add new labels to the existing folders and tell staff about the change.
Map current retrieval needs, design consistent categories, and train staff on the revised guide.
Create a date-based section for older records and circulate a short note.

basic.situation: You are indexing incoming invoices with the office's numbered list. One invoice has a faint supplier name but a clear date.

options.text: Use the date to pick the closest code and stamp the invoice.
Set the invoice aside and ask a colleague to read the supplier name.
Check the index for the supplier and date before stamping its listed code.
Look up the supplier name and stamp the matching number from the list.

advanced.situation: A batch of scanned records covers several projects, and staff have used overlapping codes. You are asked to propose a coding standard and check the current index.

options.text: Set unique code fields, test sample records, and compare the index with that standard.
Retain familiar codes and flag conflicting entries for later staff review.
Add project prefixes to new codes and review older entries for matching patterns.
Use one broad code across projects, then revise the index after staff finish filing.

basic.situation: You are putting classified paper files into storage boxes using the shelf list. A box is nearly full and several files remain.

options.text: Match each file to the box label, then record the shelf and box reference.
Put the remaining files into the nearly full box to save shelf space.
Place the remaining files in the next available box and note its shelf.
Use another box on the same shelf and add the files there.

advanced.situation: A maintenance list identifies old files for review, and some may still be needed for reference. You are handling storage under the office's file guidelines.

options.text: Transfer inactive files to designated archive boxes after confirming their status.
Move listed files to the destruction area after checking their retention dates.
Check each file against the maintenance guide, then archive or destroy as specified.
Keep listed files together pending a review of their storage requirements.

basic.situation: A colleague asks for a specific folder by its exact name and shelf location. You are retrieving it from the records room.

options.text: Use the shelf location and check the folder title before handing it over.
Check the shelf label and folder name, then bring the requested file.
Ask the colleague to confirm the folder title after you retrieve it.
Bring the folder with the closest name from that shelf.

advanced.situation: A colleague requests copies from a sensitive personnel file but gives an unclear project reason. You are handling records requests and access.

options.text: Check requester access and clarify which pages relate to project needs.
Confirm the colleague's access before retrieving any requested personnel file pages.
Ask the colleague to submit a more specific request before searching the file.
Send requested pages to the colleague's team inbox without confirming their access or purpose.

basic.situation: You are answering the office phone while typing a standard appointment letter. A caller asks where to send a completed form.

options.text: Give the address you remember and continue typing the letter.
Pause typing, answer with the guide's mailing details, and note the call.
Check the guide, give the mailing details, and return to the letter.
Ask the caller to check the office website for mailing details.

advanced.situation: You are processing mail containing confidential case papers while another department asks you to type a shared meeting note before day's end.

options.text: Set the papers on the shared desk and type the note first.
Secure the papers, confirm the meeting note's deadline, and plan both tasks.
Put the papers in a drawer and tell the department the note may be late.
Secure the papers and finish the meeting note before processing the mail.

basic.situation: You have filed a stack of labelled folders and must update the computer log with each folder's name and location.

options.text: Compare folder labels with locations and verify each saved log entry.
Copy the last batch's log and change its date for this stack.
Enter each folder name and shelf location in the computer log.
Log the folder names now and add locations after the shelving run.

advanced.situation: Management wants a computerized report on monthly file movement, and the log includes several inconsistent location entries. You are preparing the report.

options.text: Review inconsistent entries, retain their trail, and report qualified movement trends.
Pause the report and ask management to clean the log first.
Remove entries with unclear locations before generating the report.
Generate the monthly totals from the existing log and share them.

basic.situation: A tired guest arrives, but the room assignment screen is unfamiliar. You need to register them and assign an available room.

options.text: Ask a nearby colleague which room seems suitable, then register the guest.
Choose a vacant room from memory and finish the registration to save time.
Check the reservation, then enter the guest details and assign the listed room.
Confirm the guest's reservation and room availability with the desk guide before assigning.

advanced.situation: A tour group arrives early, and its VIP guest needs a room near the lift. You are issuing keys and coordinating bellhop instructions while rooms are still being checked.

options.text: Check the room list, prioritize the VIP request, and brief bellhops on assigned luggage routes.
Hold the group keys until all rooms are checked and bellhops are available.
Hand out keys as rooms appear, then let bellhops sort the luggage route.
Give the group its confirmed keys and tell bellhops the VIP's room preference.

basic.situation: A guest orders tea charged to their room. You are entering the charge, but two room numbers look similar on the ledger.

options.text: Ask a colleague to identify the likely room, then post the charge.
Confirm the guest's room number against the account before posting the tea charge.
Check the room number on the order slip, then enter the tea charge.
Post the tea charge to the first matching room number on screen.

advanced.situation: During checkout, a guest disputes a restaurant charge, and your nightly ledger is out by RM80. You need to review the account and prepare the audit handover.

options.text: Explain the restaurant charge and flag the RM80 difference for the night auditor.
Remove the disputed charge and balance the ledger using a general adjustment.
Compare receipt and ledger entries, explain the charge, and trace RM80 difference before handover.
Review the receipt with the guest, then record the unresolved difference for handover.

basic.situation: A guest asks which nearby places serve breakfast and how to get there. You have the hotel's service guide at the desk.

options.text: Show the guest the guide and let them choose a nearby breakfast place.
Name a café from memory and point toward the main road for directions.
Recommend the nearest café and describe the route from the hotel entrance.
Check the service guide for breakfast options, then explain a clear route.

advanced.situation: A guest says their booked taxi never arrived and they may miss a family event. They are upset in the busy lobby, and you are recording the complaint.

options.text: Apologize for the delay and record the complaint for the duty manager to review.
Tell the guest the taxi delay is outside the hotel's control and continue check-ins.
Record the complaint, acknowledge the missed pickup, and check available transport options with the guest.
Offer the hotel's taxi number and ask the guest to submit a complaint later.

basic.situation: You are restocking lobby tissues and watering plants when you notice several supplies are low. The checklist is at the desk.

options.text: Refill tissues from storage and water every plant on the lobby checklist.
Ask a colleague which supplies are low before starting the restock round.
Check the lobby checklist, refill the listed supplies, and water the marked plants.
Water the plants and take extra tissue packs from a guest room trolley.

advanced.situation: The lobby floor is repeatedly wet after morning coffee service. You are preparing a common-area maintenance schedule and showing a new colleague the upkeep routine.

options.text: Clean the wet floor, note the coffee service timing, and schedule checks around busy periods.
Add the floor to a weekly rota and tell the colleague to follow it.
Ask the colleague to wipe the floor whenever guests mention the wet area.
Show the colleague the cleaning routine and schedule one daily lobby floor check.

basic.situation: A supplier letter and two guest messages arrive together. You are sorting the incoming mail and messages before the next desk handover.

options.text: Date-stamp each item, identify its recipient, and rack it in the matching section.
Date-stamp each item and place the letters and messages in their usual racks.
Put all three items in the outgoing tray for the next shift.
Ask the next shift where these items should go before sorting them.

advanced.situation: Housekeeping reports that several rooms are ready, but the desk still shows guests inside. You are coordinating room-status messages during a busy turnover.

options.text: Request a room list from housekeeping, then pass confirmed vacancies to the next shift.
Ask housekeeping to recheck rooms and call back once the lobby becomes quieter.
Confirm room numbers with housekeeping, update the desk, and relay checked vacancies.
Mark reported rooms vacant and tell housekeeping to begin cleaning after desk checks.

basic.situation: A guest gives you a credit card for the room deposit. The payment screen asks for a verification step you have not handled before.

options.text: Follow the desk guide and check with the manager before completing the prompt.
Enter the card details again and choose the first available payment prompt.
Tell the guest the card needs checking and ask them to wait nearby.
Ask the manager which prompt to use, then finish the card verification.

advanced.situation: A card verification fails for a long-stay guest, but the booking is confirmed and the guest offers another payment card. You are checking how payment will be settled.

options.text: Keep the failed card on file and mark the accommodation as paid.
Ask whether another card is available, then record the guest's answer and agreed follow-up plan.
Contact the manager about the failed check before discussing payment options with the guest.
Explain the failed check, verify the offered card, and record the agreed payment method.

basic.situation: You are interviewing a resident and need their name and address for a survey form. The next question is printed on your script.

options.text: Fill in familiar details from the address label and move to the next question.
Ask the resident to spell their name and repeat the address for your form.
Ask each printed question and confirm the name and address as the resident answers.
Ask the printed question, then record the resident's name and address.

advanced.situation: An interviewee gives two different work start dates, and the survey uses one date for eligibility grouping. You need to clarify the inconsistency without suggesting an answer.

options.text: Repeat both dates and ask which one should go on the survey form.
Record both dates in the notes and continue with the next survey section.
Use the more recent date because it sounds consistent with the interviewee's work history.
Ask what event they use to remember the start date, then clarify the timeline neutrally.

basic.situation: A respondent chooses “sometimes” on a survey item. You are entering the answer on a form that uses numbered response codes.

options.text: Enter “sometimes” in the notes and ask the supervisor about its code later.
Enter the middle code because “sometimes” sounds like a moderate response.
Check the form's response key and enter the code listed for “sometimes.”
Use the code from the last similar survey form you completed.

advanced.situation: Two interviewers have coded “not applicable” differently across a large survey batch. You are documenting a coding standard for the remaining forms.

options.text: Tell each interviewer to keep using their original coding style for consistency.
Choose the code used most often and tell the team to apply it going forward.
Compare the codebook and examples, document one rule, and share it for remaining forms.
Pause the remaining batch and ask the project lead to decide the coding rule.

basic.situation: A completed interview form has one blank field for the respondent's age. You are checking it against the form's completeness checklist before filing.

options.text: Mark the field as missing and file the form with the checklist attached.
Return the form to the interviewer and ask them to review the blank field.
Check the form notes for an age answer, then flag the blank for follow-up.
Estimate the age from the respondent's answers and complete the blank field.

advanced.situation: A batch review finds several interview records with impossible dates, and the next dataset export is due today. You are setting the quality checks for this batch.

options.text: Leave the dates as entered and send the batch before the export deadline.
Ask interviewers to scan their records again before preparing the export.
Review each flagged date and send a list of concerns to the team lead.
Define date-range and sequence checks, flag affected records, and confirm fixes before export.

basic.situation: A visitor is filling out a short survey form and is unsure where to write their contact address. You are helping them complete the questionnaire.

options.text: Read the whole form aloud and ask the visitor which part seems confusing.
Show the address field, explain the requested details, and let the visitor write them.
Point to the address field and explain what details belong there.
Write the visitor's address in the field while they describe it aloud.

advanced.situation: Several clients struggle with the same multi-page application instructions. You are preparing a plain-language guide so they can complete the forms independently.

options.text: Condense application instructions into a handout clients can use to complete forms.
Tell clients to call the office whenever an application instruction is unclear.
Turn each application section into a plain-language step, with examples for common fields.
