Arrange a checklist by application order and test it with one client before sharing.

basic.situation: You find an interview record with no response for a required question. Your supervisor asks you to report problems affecting valid survey data.

options.text: Report the record number, missing question, and effect on the data to your supervisor.
Fill the blank with the most common response from nearby interviews.
Mention the blank response in your next daily update to the supervisor.
Send the supervisor a note saying one interview record has a missing answer.

advanced.situation: Different interviewers describe invalid responses in inconsistent emails, making it hard to track patterns. You are creating a template for reporting data problems.

options.text: Ask staff to keep emailing problems in their preferred format for flexibility.
Share a short template naming the record and issue for future reports.
Create a template with record ID, issue type, evidence, and follow-up status fields.
Collect the emails in one folder and summarize the main concerns weekly.

basic.situation: A colleague is conducting a practice interview using the survey script. You are observing their work and will give brief feedback afterward.

options.text: Praise their clear introduction and suggest reviewing the script before another practice.
Tell the colleague they sounded confident and should keep practicing.
Complete the next practice interview for them so the session stays on schedule.
Note one missed script question and discuss its effect after the practice interview.

advanced.situation: New interviewers are missing follow-up prompts across several survey sessions. You are designing training to improve how the team collects complete responses.

options.text: Demonstrate the prompts in a short session and share a reference sheet afterward.
Tell each interviewer to use personal judgment when a response seems incomplete.
Send staff the script and ask them to read it before their next shift.
Build practice sessions around missed prompts, role-play examples, and feedback on collected responses.

basic.situation: A new patron gives you a form to update their address, but one digit in the postcode is hard to read.

options.text: Check the old record and copy its postcode into the new entry.
Use the postcode directory to choose the most likely final digit.
Ask the patron to confirm the postcode, then update the record with guidance.
Enter the address as written and leave the postcode for later review.

advanced.situation: Your monthly report shows rising requests for beginner language books, while those titles are often unavailable. The next collection review is soon.

options.text: Share the request totals with the librarian who reviews the collection.
Compare request and loan figures by title, then share the trend for collection review.
Order more copies of the most requested titles from the report.
Check last month's figures and flag any titles with higher requests.

basic.situation: A new resident brings the required registration details and asks for a borrower card while the circulation desk is busy.

options.text: Follow the registration checklist and prepare the card for review.
Hand over a blank card and ask the resident to fill it out.
Check each required detail, then prepare the card using the registration steps.
Enter the details and ask a colleague to check the application later.

advanced.situation: A borrowed book is returned late with water damage. The borrower disputes the fine and says the damage was already there.

options.text: Apply the usual late fine and note the borrower's damage dispute.
Record the book's condition, check its loan history, and explain the applicable charges.
Set the book aside and ask the borrower to speak with the librarian.
Waive the charge and return the book to the shelf for the next borrower.

basic.situation: A trolley of returned books is waiting, and a patron asks where one title belongs after you finish sorting it.

options.text: Sort the books by section and ask a colleague where uncertain titles go.
Sort the books by their shelf labels, then return each to its marked place.
Put the trolley beside the nearest shelves for the next shift.
Place familiar titles where you remember seeing them on the shelves.

advanced.situation: A new assistant is shelving a large return trolley before a busy afternoon. Several books have similar titles but different shelf labels.

options.text: Ask the assistant to shelve familiar titles first and finish the rest later.
Sort the trolley into broad sections and tell the assistant to follow suit.
Group returns by shelf location, demonstrate label checks, then observe a short practice round.
Show the assistant how to check each shelf label before placing a book.

basic.situation: A new book arrives with its catalog details, but you are unsure where the library places the spine label.

options.text: Check the processing guide, then apply the spine label in its specified position.
Place the label where it looks clear and send the book to shelving.
Add the catalog details now and leave the spine label for later.
Ask a colleague to confirm the label position before you process the book.

advanced.situation: A well-used reference book has a loose cover and several torn pages. A patron has requested it for a class tomorrow.

options.text: Mend the torn pages and leave the loose cover for the next shift.
Assess the damage, mend what is suitable, and flag binding needs before recirculation.
Set it aside and ask the librarian whether it should go to a bindery.
Tape the cover shut and return the book to the reference shelf.

basic.situation: A patron cannot find a topic in the catalogue and asks you how to search for it on the library computer.

options.text: Demonstrate searching by subject and title, then let the patron try the catalogue.
Suggest related keywords and invite the patron to explore the catalogue results.
Show a subject search and help the patron compare the catalogue results before choosing.
Search the topic, then point the patron to a useful catalogue result.

advanced.situation: A volunteer is helping patrons find reliable sources for a local history project, and several questions are beyond routine catalogue searches.

options.text: Show catalogue searches, discuss reliable local sources, and explain when to refer complex questions.
Give the volunteer a list of history books and let them handle enquiries.
Ask the volunteer to answer each question using the first search result.
Prepare a source guide, explain referrals, and practise enquiry responses with the volunteer.

basic.situation: A patron asks you to scan several pages, but the scanner menu differs from the steps you remember.

options.text: Check the scanner guide, then help the patron preview and save their pages.
Ask a colleague about the menu, then guide the patron through a scan preview.
Choose the first scan setting and save the pages in a shared folder.
Try a familiar setting and check whether the pages appear on screen.

advanced.situation: Near closing, a patron becomes loud after being asked to leave, while another staff member is securing computers nearby.

options.text: Ask a colleague to support the patron while you secure equipment and keep exits clear.
Repeat the closing time firmly and continue securing the nearby computer stations.
Argue the closing rule and block the exit until the patron agrees.
Keep distance, speak calmly, and alert the designated staff contact for support.

basic.situation: An applicant is unsure how to report monthly income on a standard loan form and has brought recent pay details.

options.text: Ask the standard income questions and enter the figures the applicant confirms.
Enter an estimated monthly figure from the pay details for review.
Explain the income fields and ask the applicant to complete them alone.
Use the amount from the first payslip and complete the income section.

advanced.situation: An applicant with several jobs and irregular monthly earnings is applying for a larger loan. Their income documents cover different periods.

options.text: Use the highest recent monthly amount to complete the income section.
Map each job and period with standard questions, then record confirmed figures and gaps.
Average the amounts on hand and note that earnings vary month to month.
Record each job and ask the applicant to clarify the different periods.

basic.situation: A credit report lists an old address that differs from the address on the applicant's form, and your contact instructions are available.

options.text: Ask the applicant to explain the difference and record their response.
Change the form address to match the credit report and continue processing.
Follow the contact instructions to verify the address discrepancy with an approved source.
Use the newer-looking address and flag it for a later check.

advanced.situation: An employer reference confirms the applicant's job but gives a start date that conflicts with the application. The file deadline is today.

options.text: Record both dates and flag the mismatch for the loan officer's review.
Use the application date and add a note about the employer's different date.
Change the application date to match the employer's response and submit it.
Contact the employer through the listed channel, clarify the date, and record the source.

basic.situation: You are typing a standard loan form from a completed application, and one digit in the applicant's identification number is faint.

options.text: Check the source form with the applicant, then enter the confirmed identification number.
Copy the number from an older file and flag it for checking.
Leave the digit blank and mark the field for the reviewer.
Use the clearest-looking digit and finish the form for review.

advanced.situation: Several clerks prepare closing packs, and reviewers keep finding missing insurance forms just before scheduled signings.

options.text: Return incomplete packs with clear notes so clerks can add missing forms before resubmission.
Ask clerks to verify insurance forms while assembling the closing documents for review.
Use a shared checklist to track missing forms before reviewers receive each closing pack.
Give clerks a required forms list before they assemble every closing pack.

basic.situation: A customer asks why the payment on a draft schedule differs slightly from your calculator check of the loan figures.

options.text: Adjust the payment until it matches your calculator result and note the change.
Compare the payment with the draft and ask a colleague to review it.
Tell the customer the schedule is system-generated and continue the file.
Recheck the principal, rate, and period against the approved figures before replying.

advanced.situation: Your review finds several draft schedules with higher payments than your recalculation. A customer is waiting, and collateral values are also due for checking.

options.text: Recheck one schedule and use its difference to estimate the others.
Reconcile inputs and calculation method across files, then flag the pattern with evidence.
Hold the affected schedules and ask the loan officer to review the calculations.
Change each payment to your recalculated amount and release the schedules.

basic.situation: A customer phones to ask whether their loan application has been accepted, but the file status says it is still under review.

options.text: Explain the review status and when the next update is expected.
Read the status message aloud and offer to transfer the call.
Say approval seems likely because the application has already reached the review stage.
Tell the customer to call again tomorrow for a clearer answer.

advanced.situation: A customer questions a repayment schedule after a rate change and is worried the new monthly amount will strain their budget.

options.text: Tell the customer the new amount is final and direct them to pay it.
Read the monthly amounts from the schedule and ask which seems affordable.
Explain the revised payment and offer to send the schedule by email.
Walk through the revised schedule, explain the changed inputs, and check their questions.

basic.situation: A paper loan application arrives with its closing documents, and you are unsure which folder label applies to this file.

options.text: Ask a colleague which folder label applies to this application type before filing.
Consult the filing index, then place the papers in the matching loan folder.
Use a nearby open folder now, then sort these papers during today's filing work.
Hold the papers in your tray until you can confirm the right folder label.

advanced.situation: During a file check, you find a recorded disbursement that does not match the closing documents. Other files may use the same entry method.

options.text: Flag the file and ask the loan officer to verify the disbursement amount.
Edit the disbursement entry to match the closing document and close the review.
Compare source documents and system entries across sampled files, then document the discrepancy.
Add a note to the file and continue with the remaining record checks.

basic.situation: A customer gives you a completed account form, but one address field is hard to read. You are entering the details with guidance nearby.

options.text: Use the account checklist to confirm each required field before saving.
Enter the details from the form, then compare them with your notes.
Copy the form into the account system and file it.
Leave uncertain fields blank and send the form onward for review.

advanced.situation: A file review finds repeated address-entry mismatches across several new accounts. You need to correct the records and help new clerks prevent the same pattern.

options.text: Prioritize affected files, retain originals, document corrections, and coach staff using examples.
Replace source forms with corrected copies so the account files look consistent.
Sample files against the intake standard, then teach staff how to spot each mismatch.
Send the mismatch list to the team lead and wait for direction.

basic.situation: A customer asks at the counter how a savings account differs from a fixed deposit. Your provided script covers both options.

options.text: Give the customer the account leaflet and offer to answer questions.
Read the script's comparison and ask which feature matters most to them.
Explain both options from the script, then check what the customer wants clarified.
Describe the fixed deposit as a better choice for every saver.

advanced.situation: Customers keep mixing up application steps for deposit products, and new colleagues give uneven explanations. You are asked to improve the service guide.

options.text: Ask experienced colleagues to share their preferred wording at the next meeting.
Reuse the existing leaflet and ask colleagues to read it aloud to customers.
Build a plain-language guide around customer questions, then rehearse tricky explanations with colleagues.
Collect common questions and draft a guide with clear steps and product distinctions.

basic.situation: A customer wants advice about financing for a new home, but you handle account intake rather than lending. A banker is available nearby.

options.text: Confirm they need home financing and connect them with the lending desk.
Ask what kind of financing they mean, then introduce the available banker.
Suggest an account product that seems close to their financing need.
Give them the general service number and let them choose a department.

advanced.situation: Several customers report the same deposit posting error, and staff handle corrections differently. You are asked to set a consistent correction approach and coach colleagues.

options.text: Send the reports to operations and pause staff responses until they reply.
Ask each clerk to adjust the balance when a customer reports the error.
Review recent cases, then share a correction checklist at the next briefing.
Set an evidence-based review path, record each correction, and coach staff through sample cases.

basic.situation: A customer hands you cash for a routine deposit while the queue grows. You are learning teller duties with a senior teller supervising.

options.text: Enter the amount the customer stated and print the receipt for them.
Ask the senior teller to complete the deposit while you watch closely.
Count the cash, match the system entry, then issue the receipt under supervision.
Count the cash, enter the deposit, and give the customer a receipt.

advanced.situation: A business customer requests a large wire transfer, but one beneficiary detail differs from the supporting instruction. The processing window is closing.

options.text: Alert the wire team and tell the customer processing may be delayed.
Hold the wire through approved channels, record the mismatch, and resume after confirmation.
Use prior beneficiary details to meet the processing window before cutoff today.
Compare transfer fields with instructions and ask the customer to confirm the difference.

basic.situation: A customer arrives to use a safe-deposit box and presents identification and a key. You are issuing access with a senior colleague nearby.

options.text: Take the customer's word for the box number and show them inside.
Ask the senior colleague to handle the entry while you prepare the register.
Check the customer's details and key, then admit them to the vault.
Match the identification and key to the access record before admitting the customer.

advanced.situation: A review finds that replacement safe-deposit keys are issued with uneven records. You are asked to strengthen the process and coach colleagues on access safety.

options.text: Review recent key issues and remind staff to complete the existing register.
Ask the branch lead to review all key requests before staff make changes.
Set consistent identity, key, and register checks, then coach staff through replacement scenarios.
Give replacement keys to waiting customers first and fill in records later.

basic.situation: A customer deposits cash and pays a service fee at the counter. You are learning the system with a supervisor available to check your work.

options.text: Enter the deposit amount and include the fee in the receipt total.
Ask the supervisor to enter the amounts while you prepare the receipt paper.
Count the cash, record deposit and fee separately, then match the receipt totals.
Enter the deposit and fee, then print a receipt for the customer.

advanced.situation: A cash-handling review finds repeated differences between deposit slips and system entries. You need to audit the records and help staff improve accuracy.

options.text: Trace discrepancies to supporting records, log corrections, and coach staff on reconciliation steps.
Send the review results to the branch lead and wait for a response.
Compare a sample of slips with entries and discuss common errors with staff.
Adjust the system entries to match the deposit slips in each file.

basic.situation: A customer orders office chairs by phone and gives a delivery address that differs from the billing address on file. You are entering the order with guidance.

options.text: Enter both addresses in the notes and let the warehouse choose the destination.
Use the billing address from the customer record and enter the chair quantity.
Record both addresses and ask the customer to confirm which one receives delivery.
Enter the delivery address as spoken and save the order for processing.

advanced.situation: A batch review shows several orders with product codes that do not match their descriptions. You need to audit the entries and help new clerks prevent repeats.

options.text: Refer flagged orders to a senior clerk and pause that batch entry.
Compare flagged codes against order details, then share clear examples with new clerks.
Trace each code to customer specifications, update verified entries, and teach the matching check.
Check each product code against the catalogue before updating the order record.

basic.situation: A completed order form has no requested delivery date, and the checklist asks you to confirm that field before forwarding it.

options.text: Forward the form and let the dispatch team choose a suitable date.
Ask the customer to confirm a date, then add it to the order form.
Check the checklist again and forward the form with the blank date noted.
Mark the missing date and return the form for completion before forwarding.

advanced.situation: A large order includes a custom colour, but the outgoing paperwork lists the standard finish. You are reviewing it before it reaches dispatch.

options.text: Change the outgoing paperwork to the custom colour shown on the order.
Flag the colour mismatch for dispatch and let them decide which finish to use.
Hold the paperwork for clarification and compare it with the customer's specification.
Trace both records to the confirmed specification, update the source entry, and recheck dispatch paperwork.

basic.situation: A customer orders three identical items with a listed unit price and a separate delivery charge. You are calculating the total before confirming the order.

options.text: Use the price list total for one item and add the delivery charge.
Multiply the unit price by three, add delivery, and verify the arithmetic once.
Quote the item price and leave delivery for the invoice to calculate.
Add the three item prices and delivery charge, then tell the customer the total.

advanced.situation: A customer requests several products, different quantities, and separate delivery charges. A price change appears on one line while you prepare the quote.

options.text: Send the price change to a colleague and pause the whole quote for review.
Recalculate each line using the displayed prices and add the listed delivery charges.
Confirm the effective price, calculate each quantity and delivery line, then reconcile the total.
Use the previous quote total and update the item with the new price.

basic.situation: A customer calls to ask when an order will arrive. The system shows a planned shipping date and notes that delivery could be delayed.

options.text: Read the shipping date from the system and end the call politely.
Promise arrival on the planned shipping date to reassure the customer.
Share the planned shipping date and say the delivery date is uncertain.
Explain the planned shipping date, mention the possible delay, and offer an update channel.

advanced.situation: Several customers ask about a shipment delay, but the supplier has not confirmed a new date. You are setting a consistent response for the team.

options.text: Tell customers their usual shipping window remains the current estimate for these orders.
Separate confirmed facts from estimates, and give staff a clear follow-up trigger.
Share a team message explaining the delay and noting that a new date remains pending.
Ask clerks to explain the supplier delay using shared, approved team wording.

basic.situation: A customer says the delivered item differs from the order and sounds frustrated. You are taking the complaint while the order record is available.

options.text: Check the order record and note the customer's concern for the service team.
Listen, record the item and order details, then explain the complaint route.
Apologize for the trouble and offer a replacement before checking the order.
Ask the customer to email the complaint and end the call courteously.

advanced.situation: Complaints about item variant mix-ups have risen this month. You are reviewing the pattern and helping colleagues handle customers with affected orders.

options.text: Group complaints by variant, trace order records, then coach staff with specific case examples.
Review complaint examples and share a practical response during the team briefing.
Offer affected customers a credit after checking each complaint and order record.
Send the complaint list to the manager and request a team briefing on patterns.

basic.situation: A customer requests a particular printer model, and the inventory system shows a low quantity. You need to check availability before discussing the order.

options.text: Recommend a similar model from the catalogue and skip checking the stock count.
Tell the customer the model is available because the system shows stock.
Check the current stock record and explain the quantity shown to the customer.
Share the low quantity and ask the customer whether another model might work.

advanced.situation: Order records show repeated demand for a supply that often runs low. You are asked to improve alerts and coordinate with the supplier before orders deplete stock.

options.text: Ask the supplier to send extra units whenever the department reports a low balance.
Wait until the shelf is empty, then request a replenishment from the supplier.
Notify the department when the system shows low stock and copy the supplier.
Set alerts around stock and order trends, then confirm replenishment timing with the supplier.

basic.situation: A finance company requests an employee's current address, but the signed authorization is filed under a different surname. You have been asked to find the record.

options.text: Use the staff directory to verify the name before retrieving the authorized file.
Check the authorization, search the indexed file, and confirm the address matches.
Send the address from the first matching employee record to meet the deadline.
Ask the requester to clarify the surname, then search again with guidance.

advanced.situation: Two personnel files show different start dates after a transfer, and a colleague needs the verified date for a personnel action today.

options.text: Use the newer date and tell the colleague where that file is stored.
Compare the transfer documents, trace each date to its source, and explain the retrieval protocol.
Send both dates to the colleague and let them choose the more suitable one.
Check the transfer file, then ask the colleague to confirm which date they need.

basic.situation: A department asks for a headcount update, and one team has not sent its latest staff list. Your supervisor asks you to gather the records.

options.text: Send the last available list so the department can meet its reporting deadline.
Gather the available lists and note which team has not replied yet.
Request the missing team's records and label any figures still awaiting confirmation.
Ask the missing team for its list and wait before preparing any figures.

advanced.situation: Different departments submit training figures in different formats, and managers need a monthly personnel report they can compare across teams.

options.text: Combine the figures in a spreadsheet and use each department's existing labels.
Estimate missing training totals from last month's report to complete the comparison.
Create a shared template with clear field definitions and show colleagues how to validate entries.
Copy the largest department's format and ask teams to send their figures again.

basic.situation: A new employee submits an address change form, but the unit number is difficult to read. You are entering the details into the personnel record.

options.text: Check the form against the employee's previous address and enter the matching unit.
Contact the employee to confirm the unit number before saving the address change.
Enter the clearest reading and ask the employee to check it later.
Copy the unclear unit number as it appears and submit the update.

advanced.situation: A file audit finds inconsistent dates and missing signatures across recruitment and training documents. Colleagues ask how to prevent repeat errors.

options.text: Ask each colleague to check their own files before sending them for filing.
Fill missing dates from nearby documents so the audit can be closed today.
Return every incomplete file to its owner and ask for a fresh copy.
Set a document checklist with date and signature fields, then review a sample with colleagues.

basic.situation: An employee asks how to submit a leave request, and you have the company's approved guide beside you at the reception desk.

options.text: Read the guide's submission steps and point out where the request goes.
Explain the steps from memory and suggest the employee submit the form soon.
Tell the employee to ask their manager what the leave process involves.
Promise the employee that the request will be approved if they file today.

advanced.situation: A job applicant asks whether prior experience makes them eligible for a salary step, but the guide does not clearly cover their situation.

options.text: Tell the applicant salary steps are usually decided after they are hired.
Explain the published criteria, flag the unclear point, and refer it to the HR contact.
Use a similar applicant's outcome to estimate the salary step they might receive.
Share published criteria and note that HR must confirm the final salary step.

basic.situation: A new employee starts tomorrow, and you have been asked to set out the orientation pack using the department's checklist.

options.text: Arrange the pack by checklist and verify each listed item before setup.
Arrange available materials in the checklist order and note any missing items.
Reuse suitable packs left from the previous orientation for tomorrow's new starter where available.
Print the checklist and gather materials as the employee arrives for orientation.

advanced.situation: Several new starters arrive across two departments on Monday, and room availability and equipment differ. A colleague asks you to coordinate setup.

options.text: Put all new starters in the first available room and reuse its equipment.
Map each session's room, equipment, and pack needs, then share setup plans.
Use the usual room and equipment list for every session to keep setup simple.
Ask the colleague to set up one room while you prepare all the packs.

basic.situation: An employee is completing a benefit enrollment form but is unsure which section records a dependent. You are assisting with the paperwork.

options.text: Fill in the dependent section using details from the employee's previous form.
Show the dependent section and check matching supporting details with the employee.
Give the employee a blank form and ask them to read its instructions.
Show the employee the section and ask them to complete the remaining fields.

advanced.situation: An employee reports an injury at work and asks which benefit documents are needed, while the incident details are still being confirmed.

options.text: Provide the claim form and ask the employee to submit it once details are ready.
Tell the employee the claim should qualify based on the incident they described.
Explain the claim process, record confirmed details, and flag gaps for benefits staff.
Ask the employee to wait until the incident report is complete before discussing forms.

basic.situation: A courier arrives with two envelopes for departments on different floors, and one label is partly smudged. You are sorting the morning deliveries.

options.text: Deliver both envelopes to the department named on the clearer label.
Set aside the unclear envelope and deliver the clearly labelled one first.
Check the readable label details and confirm the unclear department with the sender.
Put both envelopes in the largest department's incoming tray for collection.

advanced.situation: A new receptionist sorts courier items differently from the shared mail trays, and a time-sensitive document was delayed yesterday. You are asked to guide them.

options.text: Review yesterday's delayed item and agree on one step to prevent another delay.
Ask which shared trays they find clear, then review delivery timing at day's end.
Create a sorting checklist with destination cues, then practice routing one sample delivery together.
Place urgent envelopes in labeled trays and confirm their destination before sorting.

basic.situation: A caller asks to speak with a staff member who is away from their desk and leaves a number for a return call.

options.text: Transfer the caller to the staff member's extension and let voicemail take over.
Give the caller a colleague's direct number so they can try someone else.
Write down the caller's number and pass it along when the staff member returns.
Take the caller's name, number, and message, then route it to the staff member.

advanced.situation: Two callers request the same meeting room at overlapping times, and a new colleague asks how to prevent duplicate bookings in the calendar.

options.text: Set a shared booking rule that checks room and time conflicts before confirming appointments.
Ask the callers to choose whichever available time suits them better.
Check the calendar before confirming either caller and note the existing booking.
Enter both appointments and ask the room users to settle the overlap.

basic.situation: A visitor asks where the training room is while the reception magazines have become scattered across the waiting table.

options.text: Tell the visitor the room is upstairs even though you are unsure.
Give clear directions to the training room, then straighten the magazines when free.
Ask the visitor to wait while you finish arranging the magazines.
Point toward the corridor and leave the magazines for the next shift.

advanced.situation: Visitors repeatedly ask where departments are, and magazines are often left scattered after busy mornings. You are asked to help colleagues maintain reception.

options.text: Assign a colleague to straighten magazines and keep the current directory within reach.
Ask each shift to tidy magazines and check that the department directory remains current.
Create lobby checks on a schedule and share the verified department directory.
Post a dated department list after confirming it matches the current office directory.

basic.situation: A visitor arrives for an appointment but is unsure which office to visit. You are covering reception while the usual host is in a meeting.

options.text: Welcome them and call the listed host to confirm where they should go.
Ask the visitor's name and appointment details, then direct them to the listed office.
Point them toward the offices and suggest they ask someone along the way.
Send them to the first office with an open door so they can ask there.

advanced.situation: A visitor says they have waited past their appointment time and complains that no one has updated them. The host is still unavailable.

options.text: Say the host should arrive soon to reassure the visitor.
Tell the visitor the host is busy and ask them to wait briefly.
Apologize for the wait and check whether another staff member can help.
Acknowledge the delay, check appointment status, and explain when you can update them.

basic.situation: A customer asks you to email a copy of a service document, and the filed record has two similar versions with different dates.

options.text: Send the newest looking version because it is likely the one requested.
Tell the customer that you will locate the document and reply later.
Check both file dates and ask which service document the customer wants you to email.
Match the requested service and date with the file before emailing its copy.

advanced.situation: A colleague regularly files signed forms in personal folders, making them hard to retrieve when customers request copies. You are asked to improve the process.

options.text: Move every signed form into the shared folder under its received date.
Email each signed form to the team so colleagues can search for it later.
Set shared filing labels and a transmission log, then demonstrate their use.
Ask colleagues to keep personal folders organized and search them when requests arrive.

basic.situation: A customer pays for a service at the counter, but the receipt printer jams after the payment is accepted.

options.text: Write the amount on a note and give it to the customer as temporary proof.
Record the payment details and tell the customer you will print the receipt later.
Log the payment and explain how the customer can collect a printed receipt later.
Keep the cash aside and wait for the printer to work before recording it.

advanced.situation: The daily receipt log total differs from the cash counted at closing, and a colleague asks how to make the records easier to check.

options.text: Compare receipt entries with counted cash and note any difference for review.
Adjust the log to match the cash count and close the register for the day.
Recount the cash and ask a colleague to review that day's receipts with you.
Review larger receipt entries first and compare them with the day's cash count.

basic.situation: A customer requests a hotel room for Friday, but your system shows limited availability. You need to confirm the reservation with guidance.

options.text: Reserve a room for Friday and tell the customer the hotel will confirm later.
Offer the first available room and let the customer decide at check-in.
Check the room type and dates, then confirm the available room with the customer.
Ask the supervisor to review the dates before you send a reservation request.

advanced.situation: A family's connecting flights show separate seats and a short transfer. One leg has just changed, and a junior colleague asks you to resolve the booking.

options.text: Move the family onto the next available flight and update their itinerary.
Recheck both legs, protect the connection, and explain workable choices before changing seats.
Ask a senior agent which leg to change, then revise the booking accordingly.
Keep the original itinerary and ask the junior colleague to monitor seat changes.

basic.situation: A customer asks for the fare on a simple return route. Your rate book lists a base fare and a separate service fee.

options.text: Ask a colleague to confirm the service fee before you share the fare.
Use yesterday's total from a similar booking and offer that amount today.
Quote the base fare now and mention that other charges may apply later.
Check both rates, add the service fee, and explain the total to the customer.

advanced.situation: You are preparing an itinerary for a group with different return dates. A fare change affects several tickets before the documents are issued.

options.text: Apply the lowest group fare to everyone and adjust tickets if queries arise.
Calculate the changed fares for each date and flag uncertain cases for review.
Issue the original group itinerary and explain the fare change at collection.
Separate travellers by return date, recalculate each fare, and issue matching itineraries.

basic.situation: A traveller asks whether the 10 a.m. coach connects with the listed train. Your desk guide includes the published schedules.

options.text: Say the connection should work because the coach usually arrives early.
Tell the traveller the train leaves at ten and end the enquiry.
Compare both times in the guide and explain the listed connection clearly.
Read the coach time from the guide and ask a colleague about the train.

advanced.situation: A family asks about visa and connection requirements for a multi-stop trip. Your reference sheet is dated before a recent policy update.

options.text: Check current official travel guidance for each stop, then explain verified requirements and limits.
Use the old sheet to outline requirements and suggest they check before departure.
Explain the known connection details and refer uncertain visa points to current guidance.
Summarise the first destination's rules and apply them to the whole journey.

basic.situation: A passenger presents a passport and asks for a boarding pass. The name on the booking appears different from the passport.

options.text: Compare the booking and passport details, then seek guidance before assigning the pass.
Ask the passenger to check the booking details while you serve others.
Show the mismatch to a colleague and wait for their direction.
Use the booking name and issue the pass to keep the queue moving.

advanced.situation: A passenger's travel document shows a name variant, and the booking is for a connecting trip. You are checking documents at the counter.

options.text: Ask the passenger to confirm the spelling and update the booking from their answer.
Check the main destination details and ask a colleague whether the variant is acceptable.
Assign the boarding pass using the first segment and let the next desk review it.
Compare document details with each booking segment and follow the check-in verification process.

basic.situation: A customer asks whether a flight still has seats, and your inventory screen shows a recent reservation pending update.

options.text: Promise the last seat to the customer before the reservation appears.
Ask a colleague to check the pending reservation before you answer.
Read the available count now and tell the customer to book quickly.
Refresh the inventory, check reserved and available seats, then share the current status.

advanced.situation: A traveller reports delayed baggage after a transfer, and two similar bag records appear in the tracing system. They need an update before leaving the airport.

options.text: Review both records and ask the handling desk which bag they received.
Select the closest record and tell the traveller the bag should arrive tonight.
Match the tags and route history, open the trace, and give a clear update time.
Tell the traveller to return later while the system refreshes its bag list.

basic.situation: A passenger using a walking aid asks for help reaching a departure gate. A colleague is nearby, and boarding has begun.

options.text: Confirm the passenger's assistance needs and coordinate a safe route to the gate.
Point out the gate number and let the passenger choose how to get there.
Tell the passenger to board with the crowd before the queue grows.
Ask the nearby colleague to guide the passenger while you stay at the desk.

advanced.situation: A passenger with limited mobility needs help boarding, while a companion asks for an update on a gate change over the public address system.

options.text: Repeat the gate change announcement and ask the passenger to follow nearby travellers.
Arrange a colleague to assist boarding and ask another staff member about the announcement.
Escort the passenger toward the old gate while the new announcement is prepared.
Confirm boarding support needs, coordinate the assistance, and announce the verified gate update.

basic.situation: A customer gives you a tracking number and asks whether a parcel has reached the local depot. You have access to the shipment system.

options.text: Mark the parcel as delivered so the customer can collect it today.
Tell the customer the parcel is probably at the depot based on its route.
Ask a colleague to check the local depot after you find the number.
Search the tracking number, check the latest scan, and explain the recorded status.

advanced.situation: A shipment has no scan after a transfer, and two pallets share similar references. The client needs a trace update before a delivery slot.

options.text: Review both references and ask the carrier to check its transfer bay.
Compare pallet references and transfer records, open a trace, and give a timed update.
Tell the client to move the delivery slot while scans catch up.
Choose the closest pallet record and confirm that delivery remains on schedule.

basic.situation: You are filling a bill of lading template for a routine parcel. The customer has supplied the destination, weight, and contents.

options.text: Match supplied details to template fields, then review the completed bill of lading.
Enter the supplied address and weight, then confirm contents against customer information.
Start a fresh bill of lading and enter all supplied shipment details.
Enter customer details, then ask a colleague to review the finished template.

advanced.situation: A shipment's invoice weight differs from the scale reading, changing the estimated freight charge. The documents are due for carrier handover.

options.text: Use the invoice weight and let the carrier reconcile any difference later.
Record both weights and ask a colleague which figure to use for billing.
Use the higher weight for the estimate and send the current paperwork onward.
Verify the measured weight, recalculate the estimate, and align the documents before handover.

basic.situation: You scan a parcel barcode, but the screen displays an address that differs from the label. The shipment record is not yet saved.

options.text: Compare the barcode record with the label and update the entry before saving.
Ask a colleague to check the address after you save the scanned entry.
Pause the entry and ask a colleague to compare the label with the screen.
Save the scanned address and let the next depot update any mismatch.

advanced.situation: During an audit, you find that several received cartons were scanned twice, while a few stored cartons have no matching record.

options.text: Keep the current records and note the mismatch for the next audit.
Reconcile scan logs against the physical count, remove duplicate entries, and document missing records.
Remove duplicate entries and assume the unrecorded cartons were already shipped.
List the duplicate and missing entries for a senior clerk to review.

basic.situation: A shipment arrives at the local depot, and the customer record includes a phone number and a standard arrival message.

options.text: Confirm the shipment reference, then send the arrival notice with collection details.
Send the standard arrival message to the number on the nearest record.
Send the message now and ask the customer to confirm the shipment reference.
Ask a colleague to confirm the number before you send the arrival message.

advanced.situation: A consignee says the arrival notice listed a different depot, and their delivery slot is today. Your system shows two similar shipment references.

options.text: Send the consignee to the nearer depot and ask them to resolve the discrepancy there.
Check both references and tell the consignee the depot is being investigated.
Repeat the original notice and suggest the consignee reschedule for another day.
Match the reference and depot record, update the notice, and offer confirmed delivery choices.

basic.situation: A customer needs a small shipment sent this week. You are helping compare transport quotes from two freight companies.

options.text: Compare the quotes' timing and charges, then confirm the customer's service needs.
Ask a colleague which company usually handles shipments of this size.
Choose the lower quote and reserve space before the offer expires.
Accept the quote and add a delivery date the carrier has not confirmed.

advanced.situation: Two carriers quote different rates and transfer times for fragile goods. The customer needs a firm plan, but neither quote covers handling clearly.

options.text: Accept the cheaper quote and assume standard handling covers the fragile goods.
Clarify handling terms with both carriers, then compare offers with the customer.
Ask both carriers for written handling details before recommending an offer.
Choose the faster route and ask the customer to accept its higher rate.

basic.situation: A customer asks whether a small parcel can travel by road or air. Your reference guide lists the available methods and payment options.

options.text: Recommend air because it is usually faster and move to the next customer.
Tell the customer road transport is unavailable without checking the guide.
Compare the guide's timing and payment details, then explain suitable choices.
Read the road option from the guide and ask a colleague about air.

advanced.situation: A client asks how to move mixed-size goods across two transport legs and divide payment among recipients. Your guide covers standard single-leg shipments.

options.text: Clarify cargo, route, and payer needs, then compare feasible methods and payment arrangements.
Suggest the standard road service and let recipients settle costs among themselves.
Recommend air for the mixed goods and invoice the main client for everything.
Outline the standard service and ask a senior colleague about the second leg.

basic.situation: A client needs a pallet delivered by Friday and asks you to compare the transit times on two available routes.

options.text: Use the usual road route and confirm its estimated arrival with dispatch.
Compare transit times and cargo needs, then recommend the suitable route.
Choose the cheapest carrier shown and accept its standard transit estimate.
Ask the client to choose between air and road service.

advanced.situation: A clinic needs temperature-sensitive supplies across several states. You are asked to propose a lower-emission route with road and rail options.

options.text: Keep the full journey by road to avoid extra handling at transfers.
Ask the clinic which mode it prefers before reviewing available connections.
Compare road and rail legs, checking transfer times against the cargo temperature limits.
Use the rail service with the lowest quoted price for the full journey.

basic.situation: A first-time exporter sends carton details for a shipment, and you need to prepare its packing list for review.

options.text: Copy the carton quantities and descriptions into the packing list.
Ask the exporter to complete the packing list before you review it.
Use the previous shipment's packing list as a template and update the destination.
Prepare the list from the supplied details and flag missing weights for confirmation.

advanced.situation: Customs queries a declared product description that differs from the invoice. The truck booking is due today, and the exporter is asking you to clear it.

options.text: Compare the invoice and declaration, then ask the exporter for supporting product details.
Send customs both documents with a note that the exporter is checking.
Hold the filing and tell the exporter customs needs more time to review.
Amend the declaration to match the invoice and submit it before cutoff.

basic.situation: A new food shipment arrives with labels in two languages. Your checklist asks you to verify the package markings before dispatch.

options.text: Check each label against the shipment checklist and flag unclear markings.
Ask the packing team whether they used the usual label format.
Look over the outer cartons and accept labels that appear familiar.
Review a sample carton and record the label details for dispatch.

advanced.situation: A team audit finds repeated differences between customs forms and shipment records. You are asked to propose a compliance check for future files.

options.text: Ask staff to compare forms with records whenever they have spare time.
Sample completed files weekly and share recurring errors at team meetings.
Set a file checklist linking required documents to shipment records and review exceptions.
Use last month's files as a model and remind staff to copy them.

basic.situation: A shipper provides carton dimensions and weights for a quotation. You need to calculate the shipment's chargeable details.

options.text: Calculate the total weight and ask the shipper to confirm the dimensions.
Enter each carton’s dimensions and weight, then check the totals before quoting.
Add the listed weights and send the total to the quotation desk.
Reuse the last quotation’s shipment weight because the carton count matches.

advanced.situation: Two customers have separate pallets going to the same destination this week. You are asked whether combining them could reduce each customer's freight cost.

options.text: Check the truck capacity and share a preliminary saving estimate with both customers.
Compare combined and separate load costs, checking delivery timing for both customers.
Ask both customers whether they would accept sharing the same truck.
Combine the pallets and divide the usual truck charge by their shipment weights.

basic.situation: A small importer asks whether a road or sea shipment is more likely to arrive before a stock delivery date next month.

options.text: Recommend the cheaper option based on the last shipment you handled.
Give the road and sea estimates and let the importer compare them.
Share the usual sea transit time and ask whether that sounds acceptable.
Explain the available timelines and transfers, then suggest a route fitting the date.

advanced.situation: A regular exporter challenges a proposed carrier rate for a large seasonal shipment and wants a lower price while keeping the agreed sailing window.

options.text: Review shipment volume and sailing needs, then negotiate a rate tied to that commitment.
Accept the quoted rate and tell the exporter the sailing window is secured.
Ask the carrier for a lower rate because the exporter ships regularly.
Request a discount and share the carrier’s revised offer with the exporter.

basic.situation: A client confirms a pallet shipment for tomorrow, and dispatch asks you to reserve space on a truck serving that destination.

options.text: Check tomorrow’s truck list and ask dispatch which one they prefer.
Reserve space on the matching truck and confirm the pallet count with dispatch.
Reserve a full truck to make sure the pallet has room.
Book the first truck with room and update dispatch after confirmation.

advanced.situation: A container arrives damaged after a road transfer, and the insurer requests details while the next leg is due to leave by rail this evening.

options.text: Proceed with the rail transfer and report the damage after delivery.
Photograph the damage and ask the client whether to continue by rail.
Record the damage, notify the insurer, and coordinate rail release after checking cargo condition.
Send the insurer the arrival update and keep the rail booking in place.

basic.situation: You have a bag of office parcels and a route sheet, but one address is unfamiliar and the delivery window is tight.

options.text: Arrange parcels by neighbourhood and follow the route sheet as closely as possible.
Ask a nearby driver which address they would visit first.
Put the largest parcels near the door and deliver them first.
Sort the parcels by listed stops and check the unfamiliar address before leaving.

advanced.situation: Three riders share a busy town route with timed document pickups. You are asked to reorder stops to reduce backtracking and fuel use.

options.text: Map timed pickups first, then group nearby stops into workable rider loops.
Split the town into equal areas and let riders choose their sequence.
Assign the shortest route to the fastest rider and keep the rest unchanged.
Group the stops by neighbourhood and compare each rider’s distance estimate.

basic.situation: Before your morning delivery round, the van’s fuel gauge is low and the route sheet shows several distant stops.

options.text: Refuel the van before leaving and tell the supervisor about the low gauge.
Check the fuel level, refuel, and note it before starting the round.
Start the first nearby deliveries and refuel when the warning light appears.
Ask the supervisor whether the van has enough fuel for today’s route.

advanced.situation: During a delivery round, a tyre-pressure warning appears and the van feels different on turns. A trainee asks whether to continue to the next stop.

options.text: Ask the trainee to check the tyre while you continue toward the next stop.
Pull over and inspect the tyre before deciding whether the van can move.
Stop at a safe place, check the tyre, and arrange help before driving further.
Reduce speed and continue to a nearby workshop after finishing this delivery.

basic.situation: You and a colleague are loading boxes onto a van. One marked fragile box is listed for the first stop.

options.text: Stack the fragile box under the light parcels to keep the load compact.
Secure the fragile box near the door and ask your colleague to watch it.
Place the fragile box securely where it can be unloaded at the first stop.
Put the fragile box on top of the other boxes near the rear door.

advanced.situation: A collection includes glass samples and a sealed container marked for careful handling. The van is nearly full, and you need to load both safely.

options.text: Place the glass samples in a padded area and fit the container beside them.
Ask the sender whether the container can wait for the next vehicle.
Load both items near the rear door so they remain easy to reach.
Check the handling markings, secure the samples, and make space for the sealed container.

basic.situation: You reach an office reception with a document envelope addressed to a named department and clear delivery instructions.

options.text: Hand the envelope to the first staff member who offers to take it.
Confirm the department at reception and hand over the envelope as instructed.
Leave the envelope at reception and note the building on your route sheet.
Ask reception to pass the envelope to the department when convenient.

advanced.situation: A hospital ward says a labelled specimen container is missing from its expected delivery, while your manifest shows it on the current round.

options.text: Return the container to dispatch and note that the ward reported it missing.
Tell the ward the manifest lists the container and ask them to check again.
Check the manifest and handover details, then contact the ward to reconcile the specimen.
Leave the container at the hospital reception and mark the delivery complete.

basic.situation: A shop owner gives you a parcel and an address verbally, but the street number is difficult to hear over the counter noise.

options.text: Take the parcel and call the owner if the address causes trouble.
Write the number you heard and ask the office to verify it later.
Repeat the street number and recipient details back before accepting the delivery instructions.
Ask the shop owner to write the street number on the parcel.

advanced.situation: A recipient disputes a cash-on-delivery amount and says the sender quoted a lower figure. Your route is behind, and the recipient is waiting.

options.text: Call the office and ask what to tell the recipient about the amount.
Check the collection amount against your instructions and explain the difference calmly.
Accept the lower amount to clear the stop and report the difference later.
Collect the amount shown and tell the recipient to contact the sender later.

basic.situation: You complete a parcel delivery, but the recipient says the package count differs from what they expected.

options.text: Record the delivered count and note the recipient’s comment on your route sheet.
Record the full expected count because that is what the manifest lists.
Write down the count you handed over and tell dispatch about the comment.
Mark the parcel delivered and leave a note for the office to check later.

advanced.situation: A weekly review finds several delivery logs with missing recipient responses. You are asked to suggest a change to make the records easier to audit.

options.text: Remind drivers to write more detail in the notes section after each round.
Add a recipient-response field and review completed logs for blank entries each week.
Ask drivers to send missing responses to dispatch at the end of each day.
Copy last week’s delivery notes into blank responses to complete the report.

basic.situation: You answer a call about smoke near a shop. The caller sounds rushed and gives a street name but no building number.

options.text: Transfer the caller to the relevant desk after noting the request.
Answer, confirm the incident type, and capture the caller's location.
Ask the caller to call back when they have more details.
Keep the line open while using the intake prompts and logging details.

advanced.situation: A caller reports a chemical smell near a school, while another agency asks you to transfer the line. Your local protocol for this combination is unclear.

options.text: Tell the caller to contact the school office while you check the protocol.
Keep the caller connected, gather key facts, and follow the escalation protocol.
Ask a nearby dispatcher to handle the caller while you contact the agency.
Transfer the caller and send the agencies the address already given.

basic.situation: A caller says someone fell outside a flat but cannot name the block. You need to work out where help should go.

options.text: Ask for the nearest entrance, landmark, and a callback number.
Send a unit toward the main road near the flats.
Use the caller's first street name as the final location.
Record the neighbourhood and ask the caller to check a sign.

advanced.situation: Two callers report a crash on different sides of a bridge; one mentions smoke and a trapped passenger. Units are limited and the exact lane is unclear.

options.text: Wait for matching locations before assigning response units, despite the reported smoke and trapped passenger.
Prioritise the trapped passenger and smoke, then clarify the safest approach lane.
Dispatch separate units to both sides, then confirm incident details over the radio.
Send the closest unit toward the bridge and ask both callers for nearby landmarks.

basic.situation: A caller says a colleague cut a hand at work and is bleeding. Your approved first-aid script is available on screen.

options.text: Read the approved steps calmly and check the caller can follow them.
Tell the caller to press a clean cloth on the wound.
Give a brief instruction from memory, then return to the script.
Ask the caller to search online for first-aid advice nearby.

advanced.situation: A caller says a person is unconscious and breathing irregularly. A trainee beside you is unsure which emergency instructions apply.

options.text: Ask the trainee to read the script while you dispatch the call.
Tell the caller to wait for responders before touching the person.
Use the critical-call script, assess the response, and guide each next step.
Give the trainee the standard first-aid script to read aloud.

basic.situation: You check the unit status chart for a reported road hazard. One crew's status is unclear, and the caller is waiting for an update.

options.text: Ask another dispatcher which crew they think is free.
Use the last chart entry and note that status may have changed.
Choose a listed available crew and alert the field channel.
Check the chart, contact the crew, and confirm its availability.

advanced.situation: Two field teams request the same available unit for separate incidents. Radio traffic also reports a blocked access road near one scene.

options.text: Hold the unit until both teams agree on who needs it more.
Compare incident priorities, confirm the route, and relay one clear assignment.
Check the status board and ask a team to take another route.
Assign the unit to the first request and update the other team.

basic.situation: An alarm register shows a call near your service boundary. The map label is small, and you have been asked to check coverage.

options.text: Read the map reference and compare it with the service boundary.
Check the nearest named road and report its likely service area.
Ask a colleague to inspect the map while you update the register.
Mark the call outside the area based on the small map label.

advanced.situation: During a busy shift, two alarm terminals show different locations for one incident. A routine system test is also due, and the map feed appears delayed.

options.text: Use the clearer terminal and record that the other display differs.
Flag the location mismatch, verify using another source, and report the delayed feed.
Restart the map feed and advise units that the display is uncertain.
Run the routine test first, then revisit the incident location.

basic.situation: After a routine call, you need to enter the caller's location, time, and dispatch message into the call record before the shift changes.

options.text: Enter the time, location, and message, then review the saved record.
Copy the last call's details and change the street name.
Enter the caller's location and message, then add the time later.
Write the details on a shift note and enter them later.

advanced.situation: You notice a sensitive call record was left visible on a shared screen during a handover. The next dispatcher needs access to current calls.

options.text: Close the record and tell the next dispatcher to reopen it as needed.
Move to another screen and mention the record during handover.
Secure the record, check access, and document the handover concern.
Leave the screen open so the next dispatcher can continue quickly.

basic.situation: A customer requests a pickup from a shop. You have one available driver and a work order showing the delivery address.

options.text: Put the pickup at the end of today's run schedule.
Send the driver to the shop listed on yesterday's schedule.
Confirm the address and assign the available driver to the pickup.
Call the driver and ask them to confirm the destination first.

advanced.situation: Three urgent jobs need two crews before closing. One crew is near a job but needs equipment from the depot; the other has the equipment and a longer drive.

options.text: Send each crew to a job and leave the third for later.
Compare job deadlines, equipment needs, and travel before setting crew runs.
Assign all jobs to the crew with equipment and ask them to prioritize.
Give the nearer crew the closest job and revise the run later.

basic.situation: A customer asks when a service vehicle will arrive. The tracking map shows its last location several streets away.

options.text: Check the latest vehicle position and share a cautious arrival update.
Ask the driver for a location update before replying to the customer.
Read out the last map location as the vehicle's current position.
Estimate arrival from the distance shown and give that time.

advanced.situation: Service requests rise sharply during rain, while several vehicles show low use on the tracker. Work orders vary in urgency and equipment needs.

options.text: Keep the current allocation until the rain and backlog have passed.
Compare request urgency, vehicle positions, and equipment needs before reallocating.
Move the least-used vehicles toward the busiest area for coverage.
Send every available vehicle to the busiest area for faster coverage.

basic.situation: A new work order arrives for a repair visit. The customer provided an address and preferred time, but the job description is brief.

options.text: Enter the address and schedule a visit using the usual repair slot.
Copy a similar work order and replace its customer address.
Enter the request, address, and preferred time, then flag the unclear job details.
Save the request and ask the customer about the repair details later.

advanced.situation: A monthly review finds several completed jobs with mismatched charges and service notes. Your team uses those records for customer reports.

options.text: Hold the affected reports while checking a sample of completed jobs.
Change charges to align with service notes, then issue revised customer reports today.
Compare source work orders with service notes and flag each mismatch for review.
List the mismatches and tell the team reports may need revision.

basic.situation: A crew phones to ask whether a work order has changed. The supervisor has sent a short update to your dispatch desk.

options.text: Ask the crew to call the supervisor directly for clarification.
Forward the supervisor's message to the crew by phone.
Tell the crew to continue with the original order until later.
Read the update back and confirm the crew received the changed instruction.

advanced.situation: Several crews call during a road closure, and a field inspector reports a safer route. One crew is about to enter the blocked section.

options.text: Broadcast the closure and route, then confirm the approaching crew received it.
Keep the radio clear until all crews finish their current messages.
Tell the nearest crew about the route and let them alert others.
Send the route details to crews through separate phone calls.

basic.situation: A customer calls to ask whether a scheduled collection is still planned for today. The work system shows the order as open.

options.text: Say the collection should happen today and end the call promptly.
Check the open order and explain what its current status confirms.
Tell the customer the collection is on track because the order remains open.
Ask the customer to call again after the collection window ends.

advanced.situation: A customer is upset that a missed collection affected their shop opening. The service log says the crew reported an access problem, and the customer wants a new time.

options.text: Refer the complaint to the service team and ask the customer to wait.
Offer the next usual collection window and explain the access note.
Acknowledge the impact, check the log, and coordinate a revised service time.
Promise a return visit today so the customer can reopen on time.

basic.situation: A service vehicle will not start before its next scheduled job. The driver reports the issue by phone and asks what to do.

options.text: Notify the supervisor and mark the vehicle unavailable until a mechanic assesses it.
Ask the driver to stop testing the vehicle and report any safety concerns.
Arrange a repair contact and revise the schedule to cover the unavailable vehicle.
Keep the vehicle off its schedule and ask dispatch to assign another crew.

advanced.situation: A depot power fault has stopped several service vehicles charging. Jobs are already scheduled for the morning, and the repair team gives no completion estimate.

options.text: Ask drivers to share charged vehicles and notify customers of delays.
Confirm repair status, identify affected jobs, and prepare workable vehicle substitutions.
Delay all morning jobs until the repair team gives a firm estimate.
Wait for the repair update before changing any vehicle assignments.

basic.situation: You reach a water meter on your route, but glare makes one dial digit hard to read. Your route book is due at the end of the round.

options.text: I would read each dial from its marked scale and enter the figure.
I would compare the reading with the last entry before submitting it.
I would copy the previous reading to finish the route book before closing.
I would record the dial carefully, then flag an unclear digit for checking.

advanced.situation: After your meter round, the handheld upload shows a sync error and several readings are missing from the office system before billing closes.

options.text: I would retry the upload once and report any remaining gaps to the office.
I would check the sync status and match missing entries to the route records.
I would resend the whole file and replace any office entries that differ.
I would note the error and ask the office to check the upload later.

basic.situation: A road closure blocks part of your established route, and two nearby meters are still waiting to be read before your shift ends.

options.text: I would take the nearer meter first, then rejoin the printed route.
I would follow the route as printed and return after finishing it.
I would use the approved detour to reach both meters and resume the route.
I would skip both meters and mark the route complete before returning.

advanced.situation: Your established route doubles back across a busy area, and a new group of meter locations could be visited in a different order.

options.text: I would reorder every stop by distance and finish the route sooner.
I would map the accessible stops into a shorter loop and retain every assigned meter.
I would remove the distant stops from the route to shorten the drive.
I would keep the current route and mention the extra travel at handover.

basic.situation: A customer confirms payment, and your work order lists a service reconnection at the property while your supervisor is nearby.

options.text: I would reconnect the service at the nearest matching meter and update the work order.
I would check the listed meter number, then reconnect and record the result.
I would confirm the address and work order details before reconnecting the service.
I would reconnect the service and note completion on the work order.

advanced.situation: A reconnection order covers a shared service cabinet, but its labels are faded and two nearby meters appear to serve different units.

options.text: I would compare the order with meter labels and confirm the unit before connecting.
I would pause and ask the service team to confirm which unit each meter serves.
I would verify the meter labels and cabinet number before reconnecting the listed unit.
I would hold both meters and report the unclear labels for confirmation before reconnecting.

basic.situation: During a routine visit, you notice a meter cover with a small crack and a seal that appears loose.

options.text: I would press the loose seal back into place and continue the route.
I would report the loose seal and mention the cracked cover at handover.
I would photograph the meter and report the visible damage to the service department.
I would note the crack in my route book and finish the nearby readings.

advanced.situation: A meter’s seal looks intact, but a new cable enters the service box beside it and the reading pattern seems unusual.

options.text: I would inspect the cable path and document the seal and meter condition.
I would recheck the meter face and proceed if the seal still looks intact.
I would log the unusual reading and ask the service team to inspect the connection.
I would report a broken seal and request a replacement without checking the cable.

basic.situation: A customer asks why the meter reader needs access to a water meter behind a locked gate, and you have the service script with you.

options.text: I would tell the customer the visit is required and move to the next address.
I would ask the customer to leave the gate open for the next visit.
I would give the customer the service number and suggest calling about access.
I would explain the reading visit and offer the customer service contact details.

advanced.situation: A customer disputes a high bill after a meter visit, says the meter is behind a locked gate, and asks you to change the reading.

options.text: I would repeat the recorded reading and ask the customer to arrange gate access next visit.
I would check visit notes and arrange gate access through the approved customer service channel.
I would explain the reading cannot be changed and direct the customer to billing support.
I would change the reading to match the customer's estimate and revise the bill.

basic.situation: You verify an unusually high water reading against the dial, and a nearby leak is visible by the meter box.

options.text: I would record the high reading and note the wet ground beside the meter box.
I would record the reading and report the nearby leak to the service team.
I would enter the reading and mention the leak during shift handover.
I would lower the reading to match the customer’s usual monthly use.

advanced.situation: Several meters on your route show sharp consumption jumps after recent visits, and the office asks you to review the readings and site notes.

options.text: I would average the disputed readings and recommend using that figure for billing.
I would compare readings with notes and report recurring patterns and likely causes.
I would check the latest readings and report the largest increase to the office.
I would send the office the unusual readings and ask them to investigate further.

basic.situation: A recipient collects a registered letter at the counter while the queue grows, and the delivery screen requests a signature.

options.text: I would hand over the letter after the recipient signs the delivery screen.
I would check the name on the screen before collecting the recipient’s signature.
I would match the recipient details, obtain the signature, and record the handover.
I would ask the recipient to sign the screen and pass over the letter.

advanced.situation: A new counter colleague asks how to obtain signatures for registered mail when the recipient’s identification differs slightly from the delivery name.

options.text: I would ask the recipient to sign under the delivery name and release the item.
I would show the colleague how to compare the details and follow the counter procedure.
I would explain the name check and ask the colleague to consult the reference guide.
I would hold the item and tell the colleague to call a supervisor for each mismatch.

basic.situation: A customer brings a parcel for another Malaysian address, and the scale reading falls near a weight break shown on your rate guide.

options.text: I would use the displayed weight and check the domestic parcel rate guide.
I would ask the customer to choose a service before weighing the parcel.
I would apply the lower weight band and affix its postage to save time.
I would weigh the parcel again, confirm its service type, and use the matching rate.

advanced.situation: A customer questions a parcel charge because the destination and service choice differ from the example on your local pricing guide.

options.text: I would restate the charge and offer a smaller parcel service option.
I would compare destination and weight with the guide, then show the listed charge.
I would use a familiar example rate and explain that parcel prices can vary.
I would check the current rate table for destination, weight, and service, then explain.

basic.situation: A bundle of letters arrives with mixed destinations, and the printed sorting guide is open beside your station.

options.text: I would sort the letters by destination using the guide and verify each tray label.
I would sort by the first address line and set unclear letters aside.
I would follow the guide for local letters and leave the rest for later.
I would put unfamiliar destinations into the nearest full tray to keep the line moving.

advanced.situation: The sorting device begins sending several letters to unintended destination trays, and outgoing dispatch is due soon.

options.text: I would clear the device queue and restart the current sorting run.
I would keep the device running and move misrouted letters at dispatch.
I would pause the feed, verify destination settings, and sort affected letters by hand.
I would alert the next station and continue sorting the current bundle by hand.

basic.situation: A customer presents a padded envelope with postage attached, but one corner is split and the contents shift when handled.

options.text: I would weigh the envelope and tell the customer the postage appears sufficient.
I would check the postage and ask the customer to secure the split before mailing.
I would check the stamp and suggest stronger packaging for the contents.
I would accept the envelope and add tape at the counter for the customer.

advanced.situation: During a busy shift, you inspect parcels for mailing and notice a heavy box with a loose seam and postage near the required amount.

options.text: I would weigh the box and estimate whether its current postage will cover it.
I would ask the customer to reinforce the seam and check the postage afterward.
I would check the postage and inspect the seam before accepting the parcel.
I would accept the box and let the sorting station reinforce the loose seam.

basic.situation: A full mail bag must move from the sorting station to the dispatch station, and a smaller bag is waiting beside it.

options.text: I would leave both bags until dispatch staff can help move them.
I would move one bag securely, then return for the smaller bag.
