advanced.situation: After body repairs, a vehicle's wheels and headlights need adjustment before it can return to the customer.

options.text: Set the headlights by eye and return the vehicle after a short road check.
Check wheel alignment and headlight aim against the service specifications, then adjust both.
Adjust the headlights and check the wheels for visible alignment concerns.
Adjust the wheels, then ask a colleague to check the headlight aim.

basic.situation: A supervisor gives you a repair list and time estimate, asking you to restore the listed parts in the planned order.

options.text: Start with the first listed part and ask the supervisor if priorities change.
Restore the easiest parts first so the vehicle can move through the bay sooner.
Review the listed parts and sequence, then follow the assigned restoration plan.
Follow the part list and keep track of time as the work progresses.

advanced.situation: A repaired vehicle is ready for final inspection, but the damage report mentions a measurement near the repaired frame section.

options.text: Return the vehicle after a short drive because it feels normal on the road.
Road-test the vehicle and ask the supervisor to review the repair dimensions.
Inspect the paint and panel gaps, then arrange a road test with a colleague.
Check the repair dimensions, inspect finish and function, then road-test the vehicle.

basic.situation: You remove a cracked side window and find loose glass and dust around the frame before fitting its replacement.

options.text: Vacuum the frame and ask a colleague to check for remaining fragments.
Fit the replacement after sweeping the largest shards aside.
Remove loose glass and dirt, then keep the frame clean for fitting.
Brush out the loose pieces, then check the frame before fitting glass.

advanced.situation: A windscreen has concealed clips beneath its trim, and rain has dampened one edge while you prepare to remove it.

options.text: Pry the trim free and continue once the visible edge looks dry.
Use a trim tool and place removed clips in a labelled tray.
Map the clips first, then let the edge air dry before removal.
Lift the trim carefully, note each fastener, and shield the damp edge before bonding.

basic.situation: After removing a windscreen, you spot a small scratch on the pinchweld before the replacement is ready.

options.text: Apply primer to the scratch, then prepare the replacement glass.
Ask the senior fitter whether this scratch needs primer first.
Prime the scratch and give the coating time to dry before bonding.
Wipe the scratch and apply urethane over the bare area.

advanced.situation: You have installed a windscreen late on a humid day, and the customer hopes to collect the car before closing.

options.text: Tell the customer the collection time may move after a curing check.
Check the product guidance against the workshop conditions before estimating collection time.
Release the car at closing if the urethane feels firm at the edges.
Allow extra curing time because humidity may affect the installation.

basic.situation: You and a fitter are positioning a replacement windscreen, and the prepared pinchweld is ready for urethane.

options.text: Help align the glass, then check its seating before the fitter secures it.
Follow the fitter's marks and lower the glass evenly onto the bead.
Set the glass onto the bead as soon as one edge lines up.
Hold the glass steady while the fitter checks the first edge.

advanced.situation: A large replacement windscreen has a narrow pinchweld, and you need a consistent seal around its curved perimeter.

options.text: Add more urethane at each corner, then press the windscreen into place.
Ask another fitter to watch the bead as you place the glass.
Apply a continuous bead, then inspect the full perimeter for visible gaps.
Lay a steady urethane bead and maintain even height around the pinchweld.

basic.situation: A customer’s car needs a windscreen, and two similar models are listed on the stock shelf.

options.text: Compare the stock labels with the work order before selecting the glass.
Choose the windscreen with the closest shape and prepare it for fitting.
Ask a colleague which of the two windscreens looks more suitable.
Match the vehicle details to stock records, then inspect the selected windscreen.

advanced.situation: Before a complex windscreen job, you find faint waviness in one stock panel and must choose tools for the installation.

options.text: Set out standard tools and ask a fitter to review the panel.
Inspect the waviness under workshop lights and compare it with another panel.
Inspect the panel surface, confirm vehicle fitment, and select suitable installation tools.
Use the panel because its edge profile matches the vehicle opening well.

basic.situation: After replacing a side window, you have several removed clips and the matching door molding beside the vehicle.

options.text: Replace the clips in their original positions and seat the molding evenly.
Ask the fitter to identify the clips before you refit the molding.
Press the molding back on and leave loose clips for later.
Sort the clips by shape, then replace the molding along the edge.

advanced.situation: A power window binds after glass replacement, and the door panel is still open for adjustment.

options.text: Run the window through its travel and note where resistance occurs.
Cycle the mechanism, locate the bind, and adjust the regulator.
Close the panel and tell the customer the window may settle in.
Ask a senior fitter to inspect the regulator while you hold the glass.

basic.situation: A replacement side window has been stored in a cool room, while the vehicle is waiting in a warm service bay.

options.text: Move the cold glass into the bay and fit it while work is ready.
Let the glass adjust gradually to bay temperature before handling it for fitting.
Check the glass temperature and ask when it is ready for fitting.
Keep the glass shaded while you prepare the installation area for fitting.

advanced.situation: A windscreen arrives cold on a hot afternoon, and the vehicle is parked in direct sun before installation.

options.text: Move the vehicle to shade and let the windscreen warm gradually.
Fit the cold windscreen in the sunny bay while the opening is ready.
Ask a colleague to check the panel before you bring it inside.
Keep the windscreen shaded and allow it time to warm before fitting.

basic.situation: A car returns with a rough idle, and the work order notes a warning light but no recent diagnostic results.

options.text: Scan for fault codes and compare the results with the reported idle symptoms.
Read the fault codes and record them for the repair discussion.
Clear the warning light and return the car for another drive.
Check the spark plugs first and ask a senior mechanic about the light.

advanced.situation: A van has an intermittent stalling fault, but earlier checks found no stored codes and several electrical symptoms occur together.

options.text: Replace the sensor linked to the last warning before the fault returns.
Ask a junior mechanic to check each connector while you review the manual.
Plan a repeatable test sequence, capture live readings, and compare related circuit behaviour.
Repeat the road test while monitoring the main electronic readings.

basic.situation: A customer says the car pulls left, but the work order lists only a tyre check and no road-test findings.

options.text: Inspect the tyres, then raise the pulling concern during handover.
Explain that a tyre inspection may not address the pulling concern.
Review the work order, note symptoms, and clarify the check with your supervisor.
Check the work order and ask your supervisor whether to add the concern.

advanced.situation: A customer requests a repair estimate after inspection reveals two possible causes, with different parts and labour needs.

options.text: Ask the parts counter for both prices before speaking with the customer.
Explain both findings, price the supported repair paths, and state what remains uncertain.
Estimate the more likely repair and note that inspection may change it.
Quote the cheaper repair so the customer can decide quickly.

basic.situation: After a tune-up, the engine still idles unevenly, and your senior mechanic asks you to check its adjustment.

options.text: Ask the senior mechanic to make the adjustment while you observe.
Adjust the engine using the service procedure and report the result.
Turn the idle setting until the engine sounds smoother to you.
Use the service information to tune the engine, then recheck how it runs.

advanced.situation: A powered seat moves unevenly after repair, and its hydraulic lift mechanism has several adjustment points.

options.text: Adjust the mechanism gradually and test the seat through its travel.
Check the service specifications, adjust the lift points in sequence, and verify smooth travel.
Raise the seat until it looks level and return the vehicle.
Ask a colleague to hold the seat while you turn each adjuster.

basic.situation: You are dismantling a small starter assembly and notice grease and removed fasteners spreading across the bench.

options.text: Pause dismantling and ask a senior mechanic to help clear the bench.
Keep the fasteners together and continue working on the greasy bench.
Use a tray for grouped fasteners and wipe the bench during dismantling.
Group the fasteners in a tray, clear grease from the bench, then continue dismantling.

advanced.situation: You dismantle a steering linkage and need to compare several worn parts before deciding which should be replaced.

options.text: Replace the part with the most visible wear and rebuild the linkage.
Measure each suspect part with suitable gauges and record its condition for comparison.
Ask a senior mechanic which parts look too worn to reuse.
Use calipers on the worn parts and compare the readings with each other.

basic.situation: A sedan is on the alignment rack, and you are asked to help position it before the readings begin.

options.text: Ask the alignment technician to position the car while you fetch tools.
Drive onto the rack and start readings once the car is parked.
Centre the vehicle on the rack and check each wheel's position.
Position the car on the rack and check that it sits level before readings.

advanced.situation: A vehicle still pulls after an alignment, though the readings were within range and the steering wheel remains off-centre.

options.text: Ask another mechanic to road-test the vehicle and assess steering position before adjustments.
Review the readings, road-test the vehicle, and inspect steering centring and alignment angles.
Compare alignment readings, then road-test with another technician before changing any settings.
Recheck toe settings and road-test the vehicle to assess steering wheel position.

basic.situation: During an oil service, you find the filter is due and the customer is waiting for the car before lunch.

options.text: Top up the oil and return the car promptly to keep the queue moving.
Drain oil, replace the filter, refill to specification, and check for leaks.
Change the oil and filter, then check the level before handover.
Ask the supervisor whether the filter can wait until the next service.

advanced.situation: A vehicle's engine has low compression across several cylinders, and the workshop has approved an internal repair assessment.

options.text: Ask a senior mechanic to decide which internal parts should be replaced.
Replace the engine assembly based on low readings and return the vehicle to service.
Disassemble the engine and inspect components for damage before planning the rebuild.
Record compression readings, inspect the assembly, and plan repairs from measured wear.

basic.situation: You are helping dismantle a diesel engine and find worn bearings mixed with usable parts. What do you do next?

options.text: Put questionable parts in a shared tray and continue dismantling the engine.
Label each piston and bearing as it comes off, then follow the rebuild notes.
Reuse the old bearings after wiping them clean to save workshop time.
Separate measured parts by condition and ask the senior mechanic before removing uncertain items.

advanced.situation: A rebuilt diesel engine has uneven compression, and a replacement piston set is costly. You are leading the rebuild; what do you do?

options.text: Compare cylinder measurements and clearances with specifications before approving replacement parts.
Ask a colleague to review the measurements, then use the usual rebuild process.
Replace the full piston set to keep the rebuild moving on schedule.
Select an old piston that appears sound and finish assembly for a monitored test.

basic.situation: A bus engine warning light comes on during a service check. Your senior mechanic asks you to attach a test instrument. What do you do?

options.text: Clear the warning light and report that the bus passed the check.
Connect the analyzer as shown and record the readings for your senior mechanic.
Check the connection, note the gauge readings and engine conditions, then share them.
Read the warning code and ask a nearby mechanic what it usually means.

advanced.situation: A truck's analyzer shows intermittent readings after a long uphill run, but the fault disappears at idle. How do you investigate?

options.text: Record the code and ask the driver whether the warning has appeared before.
Replace the sensor that most often causes this warning in similar trucks.
Clear the code and return the truck since it runs smoothly at idle.
Repeat the test under similar load and compare readings with the engine conditions.

basic.situation: A coach tyre is ready for mounting, and the driver asks you to adjust a loose seat nearby. What do you do first?

options.text: Ask another mechanic to handle the seat while you prepare the tyre tools.
Check the tyre size and condition, mount it safely, then assess the seat adjustment.
Mount the tyre using the workshop sequence, then inspect the loose seat afterward.
Inflate the tyre quickly and send the coach out before the queue grows.

advanced.situation: Several bus tyres show uneven wear before a scheduled route, and one door window sticks. You are coordinating repairs; what do you do?

options.text: Replace the visibly worn tyres and adjust the window during the same workshop slot.
Inspect tyre wear and door movement, then arrange the repairs in route order.
Record each tyre's wear, prioritize safe replacements, and check the window mechanism separately.
Change the worst tyre and tell the driver to monitor the others during the route.

basic.situation: You are assisting with a bus headlamp repair and have hand tools ready. A wire connector looks loose. What do you do?

options.text: Check the connector against the diagram, secure it, and test the lamp before refitting.
Tighten the connector, refit the panel, and tell the senior mechanic it is ready.
Use the wiring diagram to identify the connector, then help secure it properly.
Ask a colleague to hold the panel while you tighten the visible connector.

advanced.situation: A truck pulls right after suspension work, and its steering angle reading is inconsistent. What do you do before returning it?

options.text: Recheck alignment readings and inspect the sensor setup before making further adjustments.
Adjust the front alignment toward the last stable reading and retest the truck.
Center the steering wheel and return the truck if it feels better nearby.
Ask the senior mechanic to review the steering angle reading and alignment sheet.

basic.situation: You are reassembling a bus brake area and notice a loose protective guard near the wheel. What do you do?

options.text: Leave the guard in place and finish the brake work before the next job.
Check the guard mounting and specified safety devices, then secure them before reassembly.
Tell the senior mechanic about the guard and continue with the brake assembly.
Tighten the guard and check nearby bolts before finishing the brake assembly.

advanced.situation: An emissions warning returns after a computer controlled exhaust device repair, while a safety device check is due. What do you do?

options.text: Retest the exhaust device and note whether the warning returns during operation.
Replace the exhaust sensor and ask the senior mechanic to review the safety check.
Clear the warning and complete the safety checklist using the previous readings.
Repeat the emissions check and confirm the safety device readings against the service criteria.

basic.situation: You are assigned a bus service with an oil change and battery check. The workshop is busy. What do you do?

options.text: Top up the oil and mark the battery as checked to keep the queue moving.
Change the oil and check the battery using the service notes as your guide.
Confirm the oil grade, change it, then record the battery condition and service result.
Ask a colleague to confirm the battery reading while you finish the oil change.

advanced.situation: A hybrid bus returns after a battery warning, and the next shift needs it for service. You are assigned maintenance and testing. What do you do?

options.text: Follow the hybrid service procedure, record the warning, and test the bus under suitable conditions.
Clear the warning and take the bus around the depot to confirm it moves.
Ask the next shift to monitor the warning while you complete routine checks.
Record the warning and ask a hybrid technician whether the bus can be released.

basic.situation: A tractor loses power in the field, and the operator says it began after refuelling. You are checking it. What do you do?

options.text: Check the fuel filter and ask whether refuelling may have introduced debris.
Listen to the engine, review notes, and ask when the power loss began.
Ask the operator what fuel was added and when the power loss started.
Review the last service report and explain which fault it may suggest.

advanced.situation: A harvester loses power only when its hybrid drive is hot, though the inspection report looks normal. How do you investigate?

options.text: Review the report, listen during a hot run, and compare symptoms with the operator's account.
Discuss the report with a senior technician and arrange a hot-system inspection.
Replace the hybrid part commonly linked to power loss when the drive heats up.
Ask the operator to pause work and record when power loss returns.

basic.situation: A tractor's work light flickers, and your supervisor asks you to test its wiring with a multimeter. What do you do?

options.text: Ask another mechanic to check the multimeter reading after your test.
Bridge the wires to keep the light on for the rest of the shift.
Check the meter leads, test the wiring as shown, and record the readings.
Swap the bulb with a spare and return the tractor if it lights up.

advanced.situation: A farm sprayer has added work lamps and a replacement controller, but its wiring overheats under load. What do you do?

options.text: Connect the lamps to a nearby supply so the sprayer can finish today's work.
Replace the overheated section with rated wire, then retest the sprayer under load.
Ask the supervisor how the last modified sprayer's wiring route was selected.
Trace the modified circuit, check wire capacity against its load, and document the layout.

basic.situation: You are dismantling a small tractor engine and find metal flakes in the oil pan. How do you proceed?

options.text: Wipe away the flakes and reuse bearings that appear smooth after cleaning.
Set oily parts aside together and continue dismantling the engine for now.
Separate flakes, label removed parts, and request review before deciding what can be reused.
Keep parts in order, clean them, and show the flakes to the senior mechanic.

advanced.situation: A tractor engine rebuild must finish before planting, but compression remains uneven after tuning. You are guiding the overhaul. What do you do?

options.text: Set aside the rebuild and replace every piston to meet the deadline.
Compare compression by cylinder with part clearances, then set replacement criteria for the team.
Reuse the old pistons and adjust the engine until it runs smoothly.
Review the rebuild notes with the team and repeat the tuning sequence.

basic.situation: A cracked guard needs a simple replacement plate, and you are asked to drill its mounting holes. What do you do?

options.text: Measure the plate and make a paper template before setting up the drill press.
Mark hole positions from the old plate, then drill the replacement sheet.
Clamp and measure the plate, mark mounting holes, and request a fit check.
Drill holes by eye and file them wider until the bolts fit.

advanced.situation: A harvester's bent sheet metal panel must be replaced, but the original part is unavailable before harvest. How do you approach fabrication?

options.text: Cut a thicker plate to cover the opening and weld it onto the frame.
Ask the parts desk for a similar panel and adapt it with shop tools.
Copy the damaged panel's outline and form a replacement from similar sheet metal.
Measure the mounting points, check the panel's clearance, and fabricate a verified replacement.

basic.situation: You are driving tools to a field repair where an irrigation pump has stopped. The crew asks you to clean and lubricate its parts. What do you do?

options.text: Apply grease to every moving part so the pump can restart sooner.
Check service notes, clean specified parts, and apply suitable lubricant before reassembly.
Ask the crew which parts need grease and prepare those parts for cleaning.
Unload the tools, identify parts for cleaning, and check the pump lubrication notes first.

advanced.situation: Several tractors are due for field repairs during a wet week, and one service truck has limited tools. How do you organize the work?

options.text: Group repairs by urgency and location, then load tools matched to each machine.
Take the full tool stock to the largest site and leave other machines running.
Load common tools and drive to the largest repair site before the rain starts.
Send the truck to the nearest tractor first and bring tools as needed.

basic.situation: You have finished replacing a worn belt on a farm machine, and the supervisor asks you to record the repair. What do you note?

options.text: Tell the supervisor the belt was changed and ask them to update the record.
Write that the belt was changed and put the record in the tray.
Record the repair date and belt used, then leave the machine for the next job.
Note the belt part, repair details, and operating check result in the service record.

advanced.situation: A repaired harvester returns with a loose panel, and the record does not show which replacement part was fitted. What do you do?

options.text: Add the part details from memory and reassemble the loose panel for testing.
Ask the mechanic who did the repair and update the record after testing.
Verify the fitted part, document the repair, then reassemble and test the panel.
Tighten the panel and close the record since the harvester is running.

basic.situation: You are checking a machine manual for a replacement component's size, but two similar models are listed.

options.text: Note both sizes and check the identification plate with a coworker.
Use the first listed size and prepare the replacement for fitting.
Compare the listed sizes and ask a mechanic which one looks familiar.
Check the machine identification and match it to the manual specification.

advanced.situation: A technical drawing for a specialized machine shows a different hose route from the one found during dismantling, and the repair team is waiting.

options.text: Show the mismatch to the lead mechanic before the team fits the hose.
Compare drawing views and callouts, then brief the team on the specified route.
Route the replacement hose along the path that clears nearby parts.
Follow the old hose path and mark the drawing for later review.

basic.situation: You are inspecting a mobile machine with a checklist and notice a cracked guard near a moving part.

options.text: Photograph the guard and ask the lead mechanic whether testing can continue.
Record the crack and keep testing the machine under normal operation.
Mark the crack, report it, and keep the machine out of your test route.
Check nearby guards and add the crack to the inspection checklist.

advanced.situation: A repaired crawler machine passes its basic movement check, but a measured gear clearance is close to the manufacturer's limit.

options.text: Run the machine longer and listen for changes before signing the checklist.
Record the clearance and ask the lead mechanic to review the result.
Repeat the measurement with the specified gauge and compare the stated limit.
Accept the repair because the machine moved smoothly during testing.

basic.situation: A loader moves slowly in one direction, and your basic diagnostic tool shows a different reading from the other direction.

options.text: Compare readings in both directions and trace the affected circuit.
Replace the component with the most familiar matching part.
Repeat the test and record the readings for the repair notes.
Write down the readings and ask a mechanic which part often fails.

advanced.situation: Computerized tests show intermittent faults across two machine systems after a repair, while the machine works normally during a brief run.

options.text: Record the codes and ask the lead mechanic which system to check first.
Review fault data and test conditions, then reproduce the symptoms before narrowing causes.
Clear the codes and release the machine after the brief run.
Replace the sensor named by the most frequent code and run another test.

basic.situation: You are helping dismantle a heavy equipment panel, and several similar bolts must be removed before the panel is lifted.

options.text: Place the bolts in separate trays and ask a coworker to note their locations.
Set each bolt in order on a clean bench beside the panel.
Label the bolt locations as you remove them and keep each group together.
Remove the bolts together and sort them by length after the lift.

advanced.situation: After rewiring a mobile machine, a control responds inconsistently and the wiring diagram shows two similar connectors nearby.

options.text: Swap the connectors and run the control to see which response improves.
Inspect the pins for damage and reseat both connectors before a short test.
Check the connector labels and ask the lead mechanic to confirm the circuit.
Trace each connector against the diagram, then verify the wiring before testing.

basic.situation: You are replacing a worn seal on a mobile machine, and the new seal looks slightly different from the removed one.

options.text: Compare part markings and dimensions with the removed seal before fitting the replacement.
Check package label and part number against the service record before installation.
Fit the seal and tighten the assembly until it sits flush against the housing.
Ask a coworker to compare both seals and review the machine parts guide.

advanced.situation: During a transmission overhaul, a bearing feels rough after fitting and the machine is scheduled for a field return that afternoon.

options.text: Run the machine briefly and return it if the noise stays low.
Record the rough feel and ask the lead mechanic to approve the return.
Check the bearing fit and alignment, then test operation against the service requirements.
Add lubricant and repeat the hand rotation before closing the housing.

basic.situation: You are cleaning and lubricating a machine during routine service, and dust has collected around a grease point.

options.text: Clean around the fitting, lubricate it, and record the service performed.
Lubricate the point and ask the next shift to inspect the fitting.
Wipe the fitting and lubricate it before moving to the next service item.
Apply grease over the dusty fitting and record the service task.

advanced.situation: Several machines are due for service, but a key replacement part is low in stock and deliveries to the site can take several days.

options.text: Schedule the services in arrival order and let each team request parts as needed.
Reserve the remaining part for the first machine booked into the workshop.
Check service dates and stock, then order the shortage and sequence jobs by need.
Tell the teams about low stock and ask them to update their service records.

basic.situation: You inspect an incoming wagon and notice a wheel bearing seal is damp, though the car is scheduled for loading soon.

options.text: Wipe the seal, note the dampness, and let the loading team proceed.
Compare both bearing seals and record the visible leak for repair planning.
Tell the yard lead and mark the bearing for inspection before release.
Ask a colleague to look, then report whichever finding seems more urgent.

advanced.situation: An inspection reveals a roof seam has lifted near a stained interior panel, but the visible damage may extend beneath the coating.

options.text: Map the lifted seam and interior stain, then check adjacent roof sections for spread.
Paint over the seam and record the interior stain for the next inspection.
Patch the lifted seam with roofing cement and tell the crew about the stain.
Mark the stained panel and ask the repair crew to inspect the roof area.

basic.situation: A repair order calls for removing a small mechanical unit with a hand jack before the car returns to service.

options.text: Raise the unit from the nearest edge and finish before the next car arrives.
Review the removal instructions and ask a teammate to steady the unit.
Use the hand jack at the marked point and pause if the unit shifts.
Check the unit's attachment points, position the jack, and remove it steadily.

advanced.situation: A heavy mechanical unit must come off a rail car, and one mounting point is partly hidden behind a plate slated for torch cutting.

options.text: Expose and verify the mounts, then coordinate the hoist and cutting sequence around the supported unit.
Attach the hoist to the visible points and cut the plate to free the unit.
Ask the crew to hold the hoist while you inspect the plate and mounts.
Set the hoist under tension, then check whether the plate hides another mount.

basic.situation: You find a worn seal during a routine bearing repair, and the replacement part matches the work order.

options.text: Fit the new seal and return the bearing to the repair bench.
Confirm the seal size, replace it, and tighten the assembly to its work instructions.
Replace the seal and ask a teammate to review the bearing afterward.
Use the matching seal and tighten the assembly by feel before moving on.

advanced.situation: A gearbox returns after repair with uneven gear wear and a bearing that runs hot during its first test.

options.text: Measure gear wear and bearing fit, then document repair limits before rebuilding the gearbox.
Inspect the gears closely and order a new bearing for the next rebuild.
Replace the hot bearing and run the gearbox again at its usual speed.
Record the wear and heat, then ask the senior fitter how to proceed.

basic.situation: You must install a pre-made steel fitting, and the shop sketch shows its position on the car interior frame.

options.text: Hold the fitting against the frame and use the manual's fastener guidance.
Place the fitting from the sketch and ask a teammate to check it before fastening.
Match the fitting to the sketch, check its position, and secure it with specified fasteners.
Fasten the fitting at the nearest open holes and finish the interior panel.

advanced.situation: A bent interior bracket must be remade from a blueprint, but its dimensions meet an uneven frame that has changed during repairs.

options.text: Measure the frame and prepare a shop sketch for the fabricator to follow.
Cut a bracket to blueprint dimensions, then adjust its edges during a careful fitting.
Ask the fabricator to shape a bracket using the old part as a reference.
Compare the blueprint with the frame, sketch the fit, then check the bracket before installation.

basic.situation: You are assigned a small accessible patch on a car interior after a repair, and the surrounding paint is intact.

options.text: Prepare the patch, match its finish, and apply an even coat.
Clean the patch and apply paint listed on the work order.
Apply a light coat first, then check its colour after drying.
Brush paint across the patch, then move the car carefully to the next bay.

advanced.situation: Several repaired exterior panels need repainting before a fleet inspection, and their exposed edges face frequent rain and handling.

options.text: Ask the paint crew to add coats around exposed edges before panels enter service.
Prepare each panel, inspect its finish, and confirm repaired areas before moving the car onward.
Coordinate panel preparation and coating, then inspect edges and repaired areas as they dry.
Paint each panel in sequence, then touch up visible marks and inspect edges before release.

basic.situation: After a scheduled cleaning, you are assigned to test a repaired unit before the car returns to the yard.

options.text: Clean the unit, run its operating check, and record the result before release.
Record the cleaning and return the car to the yard for its next shift.
Run the unit and tell the shift lead whether it seems to operate normally.
Clean around the unit, then listen for unusual sounds during a short run.

advanced.situation: A repaired unit passes its initial run, but the maintenance record shows repeated adjustments and a scheduled service is due before the next busy period.

options.text: Log the successful run and defer scheduled service until after the busy period has passed.
Complete scheduled service and record the unit as operational after its initial run.
Ask the next shift to monitor the unit and record any further changes.
Review adjustments, check operation under relevant conditions, and update the maintenance record and schedule.

basic.situation: You start a motor after service and hear uneven running, while the boat is booked for a short water test.

options.text: Note the uneven running, check for smoke and vibration, and report before the water test.
Ask another mechanic to listen while you prepare the boat for testing.
Watch the motor for smoke and vibration, then share what you observe.
Let the motor idle briefly, then tell the senior technician it sounded rough.

advanced.situation: A motor overheats during testing, and its temperature rises again after a brief cool-down despite steady running.

options.text: Restart the motor and keep it running until the temperature stabilizes.
Check the thermometer reading again and schedule another test after lunch.
Compare temperature behavior with cooling-system flow and document the repeat rise before further testing.
Record the temperature rise and ask the senior technician to review the cooling system.

basic.situation: A motor in a water-filled test tank idles unevenly after a carburetor adjustment, and the senior technician is nearby.

options.text: Follow the mixture procedure, make a small adjustment, and observe the idle response.
Ask the senior technician to confirm the setting before making another adjustment.
Turn the mixture screw until the idle sounds smoother and finish the check.
Check the tank setup and let the motor idle longer before deciding what to change.

advanced.situation: A motor runs smoothly in the test tank but loses power at higher speeds during a waterway test after its timing was adjusted.

options.text: Record the speed loss and ask the senior technician to review the timing.
Run the boat again at higher speed and note whether the power drops.
Restore the previous timing mark and send the boat back for another run.
Compare the speed loss with the timing change, record conditions, and refine settings through controlled checks.

basic.situation: You are assigned to align a boat's steering control, and the gauge shows the linkage sits slightly off its mark.

options.text: Ask a teammate to hold the wheel while you adjust the linkage by sight.
Move the linkage until the wheel looks centered and return the tools.
Align the linkage to the gauge mark and tell the senior technician what changed.
Use the gauge to align the linkage, then check steering movement through its range.

advanced.situation: A boat's throttle sticks near full travel, and the steering linkage also feels stiff after a recent shaft repair.

options.text: Inspect the steering linkage and adjust its position for smoother movement.
Trace both control paths, check linkage travel and shaft alignment, then document findings.
Check throttle travel and ask the senior technician to assess the stiff steering linkage.
Lubricate the throttle linkage, then arrange another run with the senior technician.

basic.situation: A service checklist calls for replacing a fouled spark plug, and the specified replacement is available at the bench.

options.text: Replace the plug and ask a teammate to check the reassembly afterward.
Fit the replacement plug from the bench and close the engine cover.
Confirm the plug type, replace it, and reassemble the engine using the checklist.
Compare the old plug with the new one and continue with the checklist.

advanced.situation: A worn gear must be reworked on the mill, and a junior mechanic has prepared a part that is close to the drawing dimensions.

options.text: Measure the gear against the drawing and ask the junior mechanic to revise it.
Measure the machined gear against the drawing, explain any corrections, and verify fit before assembly.
Install the gear and see whether it turns smoothly during the run.
Have the junior mechanic compare the gear with the old part before assembly.

basic.situation: You are changing engine oil and filters during a scheduled service, using the workshop checklist with a senior technician nearby.

options.text: Change the oil and filter, then move the boat to the collection area.
Replace the filter and top up the oil before the next booking.
Use the checklist, fit the specified filter, and record the oil service.
Change the oil and filter using the checklist, then tell the senior technician.

advanced.situation: Several boats are due for oil and filter service before a busy weekend, and parts deliveries have been delayed for some models.

options.text: Review each boat's service needs and parts availability, then sequence work around due dates.
List the delayed models and ask the senior technician which boats should go first.
Service the boats with parts on hand and postpone the others until after the weekend.
Set aside the boats with missing parts and continue servicing the remaining fleet.

basic.situation: You finish an inspection and test on a motor, and the provided form has fields for results, repairs, and follow-up work.

options.text: Write the repair performed and leave the result field for the next shift.
Record the test result and tell the senior technician what repair was completed.
Record test results, completed work, and any follow-up on the form.
Mark the inspection complete and hand the form to the senior technician.

advanced.situation: Repeated inspection forms omit test conditions, making it hard to compare results across similar motors during a quality review.

options.text: Add fields for test conditions and results, then check forms for omissions.
Tell the team to add test conditions in the comments field when useful.
Draft a test-conditions section and ask the senior technician to review it.
Copy the latest form and ask mechanics to fill it out as usual.

basic.situation: After a routine service, you find a cracked fuel hose while replacing a customer's carburetor.

options.text: You install a similar hose from stock and note the substitution on the job card.
You compare the hose route with the service diagram before fitting the specified replacement.
You fit the matching hose, then ask your supervisor to check the routing.
You reuse the old hose after trimming its cracked end to save time.

advanced.situation: A generator's output remains unstable after you dismantle its magneto, and the customer needs the machine for work tomorrow.

options.text: You fit a used magneto from another unit to meet tomorrow's deadline.
You replace the visibly worn parts and return the generator after a brief run.
You ask a senior mechanic to review your magneto findings before ordering parts.
You inspect the magneto parts against the service limits, then test output after assembly.

basic.situation: You remove a mower's cylinder head and find carbon deposits around the valves during a guided service.

options.text: You clean the head, then ask your supervisor to inspect the valve faces.
You clean the deposits carefully, keeping debris away from the open cylinder.
You scrape the carbon quickly and leave loose flakes for the next service.
You use a wire brush on the head and wipe away visible residue.

advanced.situation: A customer's engine has uneven compression, and you find worn valves and a scored cylinder during inspection.

options.text: You measure the affected parts against service limits before recommending valve and piston work.
You grind the valves and reuse the scored cylinder to keep costs down.
You replace the valves and piston together because both show visible wear.
You ask a senior mechanic which parts to replace after showing the scoring.

basic.situation: A customer's headlight stops working, and you find a loose connector while replacing the lamp with guidance.

options.text: You fit the lamp and return the motorcycle after seeing it light once.
You tape the loose connector in place and leave the old lamp installed.
You replace the lamp, then ask your supervisor to confirm the connector is secure.
You secure the connector, fit the lamp, and test both beam settings.

advanced.situation: A motorcycle's starter works intermittently after a repair, and the customer reports it failed again on the way home.

options.text: You trace the starter connections and reproduce the fault before replacing a confirmed defective part.
You replace the starter motor because intermittent starting often points to that part.
You ask a senior mechanic to inspect your starter checks before returning the bike.
You clean the battery terminals and tell the customer to monitor the starter.

basic.situation: You have finished repairing a carburetor subassembly and need to refit it before the motorcycle's scheduled collection.

options.text: You finish the assembly, then ask your supervisor to check the fit.
You reassemble the unit in sequence and check its movement before refitting.
You tighten the fasteners by feel and move on to the next job.
You refit the unit and test it during a short engine run.

advanced.situation: After an engine repair, you reinstall the engine and accessories, but a test ride reveals vibration near the frame mounts.

options.text: You remove the accessories and return the motorcycle with the vibration noted.
You tighten the mounts again and ask the rider to report any further vibration.
You inspect mount alignment and accessory clearances, then retest before releasing the motorcycle.
You ask a senior mechanic to review the reassembly before another road test.

basic.situation: A customer says their motorcycle loses power uphill, and you are asked to listen to the engine and inspect the frame.

options.text: You listen under different engine speeds and record when the power loss appears.
You inspect the frame and suggest a tune-up based on the mileage.
You tell the customer the engine sounds normal after listening at idle.
You listen at idle, then ask your supervisor what to inspect next.

advanced.situation: Your test panel shows inconsistent generator output, while the engine runs smoothly and the customer disputes a previous diagnosis.

options.text: You report the generator as faulty and begin replacement to resolve the dispute.
You show the readings to a senior mechanic before discussing another repair estimate.
You repeat the output test at specified engine speeds and compare readings with service limits.
You replace the generator because one reading falls below the expected range.

basic.situation: During a routine check, you find one motorcycle tyre below its recommended pressure and notice uneven tread wear.

options.text: You add air until the tyre looks firm and continue the inspection.
You check the pressure and recommend the customer monitor the tread at home.
You check the tyre condition, adjust pressure to specification, and record the wear.
You inflate the tyre with a gauge, then ask your supervisor about the wear.

advanced.situation: After adjusting a motorcycle's brakes, you find inconsistent lever travel during the final check before a customer collection.

options.text: You ask a senior mechanic to check your adjustment before the customer arrives.
You make a small adjustment and return the motorcycle when the lever feels firmer.
You inspect brake movement against specifications, address the cause, and retest lever travel.
You release the motorcycle and tell the customer the lever may settle during use.

basic.situation: A customer says their lawn mower stalls after starting, and you are asked to inspect it with diagnostic instruments.

options.text: You replace the spark plug because it is a common cause of stalling.
You test the engine and record the readings before checking likely causes.
You tell the customer the mower needs a tune-up and prepare an estimate.
You repeat the engine test and compare the readings with service guidance.

advanced.situation: A generator still surges after a repair, and your apprentice's instrument readings vary between test runs.

options.text: You demonstrate a consistent test setup, then have the apprentice repeat and interpret readings.
You replace the carburetor based on the highest reading and finish the repair.
You use the first reading and tell the apprentice to note that the generator runs.
You review the readings together and ask a senior mechanic to confirm the diagnosis.

basic.situation: During a scheduled mower service, you find dust and dry residue on the engine parts you were assigned to clean and oil.

options.text: You wipe the visible dust and leave the engine oiling for another visit.
You clean the parts and ask your supervisor which surfaces need oil.
You clean the parts, apply suitable oil, and record the maintenance performed.
You spray oil across the engine parts and wipe away the excess.

advanced.situation: Several mowers return with rough idling after ignition tuning, and you are asked to guide an apprentice during maintenance.

options.text: You raise the idle setting on each mower to reduce the rough running.
You review the service guidance with the apprentice before tuning the returned mowers.
You tune each mower by ear and let the apprentice copy your adjustments.
You set a repeatable tuning sequence and have the apprentice verify idle after each adjustment.

basic.situation: You remove a small engine from a lawn mower and need to secure it on a repair stand with help.

options.text: You bolt the engine down where it rests and begin dismantling parts.
You support the engine while aligning its mounting points before bolting it down.
You tighten the stand bolts firmly and check that the engine does not rock.
You position the engine, then ask your coworker to check the bolts.

advanced.situation: After internal repairs, you reassemble a generator engine, but two components feel tight as the crankshaft turns.

options.text: You ask a senior mechanic to review the tight components before closing the engine.
You add lubricant and turn the crankshaft until the resistance eases.
You pause assembly, inspect component alignment, and measure clearances against specifications.
You tighten the remaining fasteners and run the engine to see if it frees.

basic.situation: You are asked to set a mower's spark plug gap, and the supervisor shows you the feeler gauge.

options.text: You bend the electrode until the gap looks close to the sample.
You adjust the gap, then ask your supervisor to verify the gauge reading.
You use the nearest gauge size and record that choice on the job card.
You select the specified gauge, adjust the gap, and recheck its fit.

advanced.situation: A repaired engine still loses power, and measurements suggest the cylinder bore may be outside its specified clearance.

options.text: You calibrate the micrometer, take repeated bore measurements, and compare them with specifications.
You ask a senior mechanic to confirm your micrometer readings before machining.
You hone the bore lightly and return the engine after a short run.
You ream the bore until the piston moves freely by hand.

basic.situation: A mower arrives with a cracked spark plug lead, and you are assigned to replace the defective part with guidance.

options.text: You replace the lead, then ask your supervisor to inspect the connection.
You fit a similar lead from stock and note the change for the customer.
You splice the cracked lead and return the mower after it starts once.
You match the replacement lead, fit it securely, and verify the engine starts.

advanced.situation: A generator's replacement water pump fails again within a week, and an apprentice is ready to install another unit.

options.text: You inspect the pump drive and mating parts, then confirm the replacement matches specifications.
You review the previous repair with the apprentice before choosing another pump.
You fit a used pump from another generator to get the unit back today.
You install another pump from the same box and run the generator briefly.

basic.situation: A customer collecting a chainsaw asks how to clean and oil its chain after routine servicing.

options.text: You show the customer the manual and offer to answer questions afterward.
You tell the customer to ask another shop if the chain looks dry.
You describe the steps quickly while handing over the chainsaw and receipt.
You demonstrate the maintenance steps on the equipment and invite the customer to practise.

advanced.situation: Several customers ask which replacement mower blades fit their equipment, and you are asked to help explain available parts.

options.text: You compare the blade labels with customers' mower details before discussing options.
You recommend the fastest-selling blade and mention that it fits most mowers.
You show customers two similar blades and let them choose by size.
You check each model's parts information and explain compatible choices and fitting needs.

basic.situation: A customer's rear gears skip after a cable change, and the bike is due back before lunch. You have the indexing checklist beside the stand.

options.text: Check cable seating and limit stops, then index each gear through the cassette.
Turn the barrel adjuster until shifting feels smoother, then return the bike.
Tighten the cable further and send it out if one gear catches.
Follow the indexing steps and test several gears before handing it back.

advanced.situation: A bike still skips under load after routine tuning. An apprentice is watching, and the customer needs it for a long weekend ride.

options.text: Replace the stretched cable and tune shifting, then ask the apprentice to repeat it.
Adjust the barrel until the noisy gears quiet down, then resume work.
Trace wear and alignment in sequence, then coach the apprentice through measured indexing.
Compare the symptom with the service manual, then verify each drivetrain adjustment.

basic.situation: A commuter's front wheel wobbles after a new tube was fitted. The customer is waiting, and you have a wheel stand and alignment guide.

options.text: Tighten the loose-looking spokes and return the wheel to the customer.
Use the alignment guide and recheck the wheel after small spoke adjustments.
Spin the wheel by eye, then adjust spokes near the widest wobble.
Secure the wheel in the stand, check runout, and adjust spokes gradually.

advanced.situation: A touring customer needs a replacement rear wheel built today. The rim and hub are available, but the spoke pattern and tension need your judgment.

options.text: Use the spoke calculator, lace the wheel, and check tension across spokes.
Confirm hub and rim measurements, lace to the pattern, then balance tension and alignment.
Match the old wheel's spoke lengths and tension by feel, then fit it.
Follow a familiar lacing pattern and true the wheel before fitting it.

basic.situation: A new bicycle is nearly ready for collection, but its front light and kickstand are still boxed. You have the assembly checklist and fitting tools.

options.text: Attach the light and stand where they seem convenient, then call the customer.
Install the stand first, then ask a colleague to check the light later.
Check the fitting points, mount both accessories securely, and test the light.
Fit the light and stand using the checklist, then check their security.

advanced.situation: Several new bicycles are due for collection, and two staff members are fitting lights and stands inconsistently. You have the assembly guide and can coordinate their work.

options.text: Demonstrate a shared fitting sequence, then check mounting and function on each bicycle.
Assign the faster fitter to accessories and review any customer complaints afterward.
Have staff follow the guide and inspect one finished bicycle from each batch.
Let each staff member choose a familiar fitting method to keep work moving.

basic.situation: A rear axle feels rough during a service, and the parts diagram is available at your bench. You have hand tools and guidance from a senior mechanic.

options.text: Follow the diagram while disassembling, then ask for a check before reassembly.
Open the axle carefully, lay out parts, and compare them with the diagram.
Loosen the axle, remove the rough parts, and put them in a tray.
Replace the axle assembly and keep the old parts for later inspection.

advanced.situation: A replacement spacer is slightly too wide, and the bike is booked for collection today. You can shape parts at the bench grinder and have a senior mechanic nearby.

options.text: Grind the spacer in short passes, then compare it with the original part.
Ask the senior mechanic to show a safe setup before you shape the spacer.
Mark the needed width, secure the spacer, and grind gradually with fit checks.
Hold the spacer firmly and remove enough material to match the old one.

basic.situation: A customer's bike is due for pickup after a wet commute. The chain and cassette are dirty, and your maintenance checklist is ready at the wash area.

options.text: Brush the visible grime off and lubricate the chain for a quieter ride.
Clean the chain and cassette, then lubricate them using the checklist.
Wipe the chain quickly and add lubricant before returning the bike.
Clean the drivetrain, dry it, apply suitable lubricant, and wipe excess away.

advanced.situation: After several bikes return with noisy chains, you are asked to coach two new staff on cleaning and lubrication during a busy service week.

options.text: Share the checklist and review one cleaned drivetrain from each staff member.
Demonstrate cleaning, drying, measured lubrication, and excess removal, then observe each worker.
Tell staff to add lubricant whenever a chain looks dry during service.
Ask staff to use their usual method and compare customer feedback next week.

basic.situation: A customer wants a bicycle for daily commuting and weekend park rides, but is unsure about frame size. You can help with fitting and have the size guide.

options.text: Use the size guide to suggest a frame, then let the customer decide.
Ask about routes and budget, then show bicycles near the customer's height.
Check the customer's fit on suitable frames and compare models for both uses.
Recommend the popular model and arrange the order before the customer leaves.

advanced.situation: A popular helmet is nearly out of stock, and a customer asks for a bicycle suitable for a school commute. You are helping with fitting and parts orders during a busy shift.

options.text: Discuss commute needs and fit, then note the low helmet stock for reordering.
Show the fastest-selling model and reserve a helmet before checking bicycle fit.
Check the customer's fit and route needs, then explain suitable bicycle and accessory options.
Recommend a bicycle by height and offer the helmet that remains in stock.

basic.situation: A customer reports that an RV's brakes feel soft after a recent service. You have the work order, inspection bay, and a technician's checklist.

options.text: Review the work order, inspect the brake system, and record what you find.
Check the fluid level and suggest a brake adjustment for the customer.
Top up the brake fluid and return the RV if the pedal feels firmer.
Use the checklist to inspect the brakes, then report any visible concerns.

advanced.situation: An RV returns with intermittent braking complaints, and the earlier repair notes list several possible parts. You need to plan further checks before giving the customer an estimate.

options.text: Review earlier notes and prepare a parts estimate for the likely brake repair.
Replace the parts named in earlier notes, then update the estimate afterward.
Ask the customer to clarify symptoms, then revise the parts list as needed.
Recheck symptoms and brake components, then use the manual to plan evidence-based checks.

basic.situation: A repaired RV window sticks near the end of its track. The customer is waiting, and you have a fitting tool and the final inspection checklist.

options.text: Use the checklist to test the window and tell the lead it still sticks.
Cycle the window, locate the contact point, and make a measured fit adjustment.
Trim the edge slightly and return the RV if the window moves once.
Open and close the window several times, then note where it binds.

advanced.situation: Several RVs are ready for final checks, and one air conditioner has a history of intermittent operation. You are helping set inspection standards for the shift.

options.text: Run each air conditioner once and clear the bay for incoming work.
Set a repeatable operating check for the known fault and record each result.
Have staff repeat the standard test when a unit sounds unusual.
Test each appliance from the checklist and note any intermittent operation.

basic.situation: A cabinet door has scratches after an RV repair, and its latch no longer sits flush. You have finishing tools and can consult the job notes.

options.text: Sand the scratched area, refinish it, and check the latch alignment.
Apply varnish over the scratches and adjust the latch by eye.
Prepare and refinish the surface, reset the latch, then explain its operation.
Reset the latch first, then ask a senior technician about the finish.

advanced.situation: A cabinet refinish is part of a larger interior repair due tomorrow. A junior technician is helping, and the customer will need to use the repaired latch.

options.text: Show the junior surface preparation and latch resetting, then review the finish and demonstrate operation.
Assign the sanding and latch work, then inspect the cabinet before handover.
Refinish the door yourself and have the junior reset the latch for review.
Let the junior use their usual method and touch up visible marks later.

basic.situation: After a sink replacement, the water hose is connected but the customer is due to collect the RV. You have access to the supply and can run a basic check.

options.text: Turn on the water, run the sink, and check beneath the fittings for leaks.
Ask a coworker to check the hose while you finish the paperwork.
Use the checklist to run water and note any visible drips.
Run the sink briefly and tell the service desk it works.

advanced.situation: An RV's outside power connection works, but its lights flicker when an appliance starts. You are checking utility connections and can consult the wiring diagram.

options.text: Compare the wiring diagram with the connection, then test the lights under load.
Check the outlet and note when the flicker occurs during appliance use.
Replace the outside connection and retest the lights after the appliance starts.
Reseat the plug and test the lights while the appliance starts.

basic.situation: A small leak appears beneath an RV sink where a pipe meets a fitting. You have caulking compound, a wrench, and the repair guide.

options.text: Dry the joint, apply caulk, and check for drips after running water.
Wipe the leak, add caulk around the joint, and close the panel.
Use suitable material on the joint, then retest for leaks.
Tighten the fitting, dry it, then run water and inspect for seepage.

advanced.situation: A custom RV build has limited space for a replacement water pipe, and a previous joint seeped during testing. You are preparing a repair approach within the work order.

options.text: Copy the old pipe route and seal the replacement joints with caulk.
Use the shortest pipe route and ask the lead to review the joints.
Follow the build notes and test the replacement pipe for visible leaks.
Measure the route, choose compatible pipe, and plan accessible joints for leak checks.

basic.situation: An RV light flickers, and you notice a frayed wire near a broken connector. The repair bay has a wiring diagram and basic electrical tools.

options.text: Trace the circuit, repair the connection, and retest the light.
Tape the frayed section and test the light before returning the RV.
Inspect the wire and connector, then report the fault for repair planning.
Replace the connector and check the light using the standard inspection steps.

advanced.situation: An RV has a damaged exterior panel and a bent frame member nearby. You are assigned to support the structural repair and check related wiring before the panel is replaced.

options.text: Replace the panel first, then inspect the frame from inside the RV.
Document panel and frame damage, check nearby wiring, and coordinate the repair sequence.
Inspect the frame and nearby wiring, then report measurements to the lead technician.
Remove the panel and replace the bent member, then close the area for wiring review.

basic.situation: A customer reports a slow leak, and you find no obvious nail in the tread. You need to check the casing for a puncture.

options.text: Inflate it and check the tread by eye before returning it.
Look over the casing, then ask a senior fitter to confirm.
Pull the tire aside and fit a new one from stock.
Use a water bath, then mark the bubble point for repair.

advanced.situation: A trainee cannot find a leak that appears only when the tire flexes. You need to coach them through checking the casing and leak pattern.

options.text: Suggest they replace the tire when another visual check looks unclear.
Ask them to repeat a visual check, then take over the inspection.
Have them mark the first bubbles, then patch that spot together.
Show how to inspect the casing and compare bubbles as the tire turns.

basic.situation: After a tire change, you are asked to find the counterweight needed for a customer's wheel using the shop balancing machine.

options.text: Mount the wheel as shown, then run the machine and note its reading.
Fit a familiar weight from a similar wheel and check the result.
Place the wheel on the machine and use its first displayed value.
Ask a fitter to mount it while you watch the machine display.

advanced.situation: An apprentice gets different readings on a wide alloy wheel. You need to guide the setup and choose where to place the required counterweights.

options.text: Show how to seat the wheel, select its setup, and interpret both readings.
Ask them to try another setup, then compare the displayed readings together.
Set a familiar machine setup and have them repeat the displayed reading.
Use the larger reading and fit the nearest available counterweight.

basic.situation: A car is on the lift for a tire change. You need to remove one wheel with a lug wrench under a fitter's guidance.

options.text: Ask the fitter to loosen the lugs while you steady the wheel.
Loosen the lugs in sequence, support the wheel, and lift it clear.
Use the power wrench on every lug, then pull the wheel free.
Loosen two lugs, then lift the wheel off the hub.

advanced.situation: You are mentoring a new fitter on a car with mismatched tires after a repair. You need to rotate the wheels to the positions specified on the work order.

options.text: Use the usual rotation pattern and compare it with the work order afterward.
Have the trainee move one wheel, then review the full layout together.
Rotate the front wheels first and sort out the remaining positions later.
Move the wheels by the listed positions and confirm each tire's placement.

basic.situation: You find a small nail in a tubeless tire during inspection. With guidance, you need to remove it and seal the puncture.

options.text: Push adhesive material into the hole and inflate the tire for a check.
Remove the nail, inspect the opening, then insert the plug with hand tools.
Remove the nail, then ask a fitter which repair method suits it.
Pull the nail and fit a valve stem from the parts tray.

advanced.situation: A tire has a puncture near a damaged casing area, and a junior fitter is unsure whether to patch it. You need to assess the repair options.

options.text: Patch the visible opening and return the tire after inflation.
Compare the rupture and casing condition, then explain whether a patch can hold.
Buff the damaged area and patch it if the surface looks smooth.
Ask another fitter to inspect the casing before deciding on a patch.

basic.situation: The bay is cluttered after several tire jobs, and you are asked to clean and tidy the shop before the next vehicle arrives.

options.text: Push loose tools onto a bench and sweep the open floor space.
Put away the tools you used and leave other items for later.
Clear the bay, return tools to their places, and sweep the floor.
Ask a coworker to handle the floor while you sort the tools.

advanced.situation: Several vehicles need lifting during a busy shift, and the bay floor is cluttered. You need to guide the team in keeping the shop orderly around the hydraulic jacks.

options.text: Keep jacks together and sweep the bay after the final vehicle leaves the shop.
Ask the team to clear clutter between vehicles and return each jack after every job.
Move clutter away before positioning each vehicle over a hydraulic jack in the bay.
Clear the lifting area, then return each jack to its storage place after work.

basic.situation: A customer needs a replacement tire, and the sidewall markings are hard to read. You need to identify its size and ply using the shop chart.

options.text: Use the chart to interpret sidewall markings and confirm the tire size and ply.
Compare the old tire width with nearby chart sizes before choosing a replacement.
Select a listed size that matches the vehicle model and its specified tire fitment.
Ask a fitter to read the markings while you locate the matching chart entry.

advanced.situation: Two tires are low in stock, and a vehicle needs a matching replacement set. You need to identify the size and ply and prepare an order for the fitter.

options.text: Use the existing invoice to order the same tires again.
Review the stock list and ask the fitter which tires to order.
Check the sidewalls and chart, then order the specified sizes and quantities.
Order the common size for that vehicle and adjust the count later.

basic.situation: A shop door closes too quickly after a repair. You need to adjust its opening or closing effort with guidance.

options.text: Turn the adjustment screw several times and see how the door feels.
Test the door, make a small adjustment, and check its movement again.
Ask the fitter to adjust it while you observe the door's movement.
Tighten the closer slightly and return the door for use.

advanced.situation: A hydraulic closer behaves differently at each stage of travel on a heavy door. You need to calibrate it and guide an apprentice through the adjustment.

options.text: Use the previous door's settings and check the closing speed once.
Turn the main control until the door feels acceptable at mid-swing.
Ask the apprentice to adjust one control while you watch a full cycle.
Map the movement stages, adjust each control, then retest the full cycle.

basic.situation: The track is installed, and you are helping set a sectional door into the opening. You need to position its hardware under supervision.

options.text: Stack the sections quickly, then fasten the hardware at the end.
Hold the next section while the fitter positions and fastens it.
Position the sections by eye and adjust the track after assembly.
Set each section into the opening and check that it follows the track.

advanced.situation: You are fitting an electronic-eye mechanism on a busy loading bay. You need to install it and check that its parts sit in the planned positions.

options.text: Fit the eyes at the marked points and ask the fitter to test them.
Follow the cable route, then mount the eyes at matching heights.
Mount the eyes to the plan and check their alignment across the opening.
Place each eye where its cable reaches and test the door once.

basic.situation: A door opening needs a short angle iron stop cut to fit. You need to measure and prepare the piece with help.

options.text: Hold the angle iron to the opening and mark it by eye.
Measure the opening, mark the angle iron, and cut to the measured length.
Cut a standard length and trim it if the stop sits proud.
Ask the fitter for the length, then cut the angle iron.

advanced.situation: A worn door part has no replacement in the van, and the opening must be secured today. You need to fabricate a replacement from the available stock.

options.text: Measure the worn part, select matching stock, and shape a replacement to fit.
Copy the part's outline onto scrap and drill the visible holes.
Measure the part and ask a fitter to confirm your stock choice.
Use a similar part as a template and file the edges to fit.

basic.situation: Before installing a replacement door, you need to inspect the opening's headroom and side room with guidance.

options.text: Look upward and choose the door that seems to fit the opening.
Measure the side room and use the previous job's headroom figure.
Check the headroom and ask the fitter to measure the side room.
Measure headroom and side room, then note any obstructions at the opening.

advanced.situation: A repair drawing shows an automatic opener beside a low beam and an uneven wall. You need to interpret the schematic and assess the installation method.

options.text: Check the beam clearance and ask the fitter to interpret the rest.
Use the usual opener layout and compare it with the drawing afterward.
Trace the opener layout against site clearances and flag conflicts before planning work.
Follow the drawing as shown and adjust the opener during installation.

basic.situation: A track is ready for installation, and you are asked to fasten its angle iron back-hangers to the ceiling under supervision.

options.text: Fasten the hangers where the ceiling looks strongest and adjust later.
Attach the hangers to the track first, then lift the assembly into place.
Hold the hanger in place while the fitter checks its position.
Align each hanger with the track, then fasten it at the marked points.

advanced.situation: A new opener layout needs low voltage wiring run across the ceiling near the track. You need to route and secure it as part of the assembly.

options.text: Ask the fitter to mark a path, then staple the wiring in place.
Follow the ceiling edge and secure the wiring at convenient points.
Route the wiring along the planned path and secure it with insulated staples.
Take the shortest route and staple the wiring near the track.

basic.situation: You finished replacing a worn closer part, and the customer is ready to leave. You need to complete the work order for the service performed.

options.text: Write that the closer was repaired and hand the order to the fitter.
List the replaced part and work performed, then check the order before filing.
Record the customer name and mark the job as completed.
Note the repair and ask the fitter to review the work order.

advanced.situation: A heavy curtain door has a defective part, and the repair took longer than expected. You need to coordinate its movement with a lift and record the completed work.

options.text: Plan the lift movement, replace the part, and record the work and time taken.
Replace the part and use the last job's lift arrangement for the door.
Move the curtain door with the lift, then note the repair briefly.
Record the part replacement and ask a fitter to review the lift plan.

basic.situation: You are assigned to restore a customer's gas service. The meter is off, and the work order is on your tablet.

options.text: Ask a nearby colleague to confirm the order before opening the meter.
Open the meter and mark service active from the customer's request.
Check the address on the order, then open the meter and note its reading.
Check the service order details, open the meter, and record the reading.

advanced.situation: A regulator's outlet pressure drifts during calibration, and two gauges disagree. The system serves several workshops waiting to reopen.

options.text: Use the recently calibrated gauge and repeat the pressure check.
Average both gauge readings and set the regulator to that figure.
Check gauge condition and test setup, then calibrate against the specified pressure standard.
Adjust the regulator until the outlet reading matches the older service note.

basic.situation: During a scheduled valve service, you open the unit and find grime around its moving parts, with no visible damage.

options.text: Clean the parts with a rag and compound, then note the service.
Brush away the heaviest grime and reassemble the valve for testing.
Clean the moving parts with suitable compound, then inspect their movement.
Wipe the exposed surfaces and close the valve for the next job.

advanced.situation: A regulator dismantled for repair has a worn seat and a damaged inspection port. Replacement parts are delayed, but the body appears salvageable.

options.text: Measure the body, cut a matching seat, and tap the port to spec.
Cut a new seat and tap the port to salvage the usable body.
Fit the nearest available seat and seal the damaged port with compound.
Use a matching spare body and return this unit for full replacement.

basic.situation: You finish a meter visit where the reading differs from the previous card. The customer is waiting while you complete the work order.

options.text: Enter the new reading and ask the customer whether it seems plausible.
Copy the previous card's reading to keep the service record consistent.
Record the reading, note the difference, and check the meter identifier.
Enter the observed reading and installation details on the work order.

advanced.situation: You audit work orders before monthly close and find several repairs recorded without test results or material usage, making follow-up difficult.

options.text: Fill the gaps with typical test results and standard material amounts.
Compare orders with field notes, resolve gaps, and propose required record fields.
Mark the gaps for the close report and leave the orders unchanged.
Return the incomplete orders to technicians and request missing details.

basic.situation: You are mounting a replacement electric meter at a shop. The mounting points are clear, and the approved work order lists the equipment.

options.text: Use a spare meter that fits the bracket and update the work order later.
Mount the meter where the old unit sat and finish the visit.
Mount the meter securely and check its position against the work order.
Fit the meter using the listed equipment and record its location.

advanced.situation: A customer asks where to place a regulator for a new workshop extension. The proposed spot is near a busy loading area.

options.text: Ask the customer to review the layout and share a preferred regulator location.
Suggest a wall location away from loading traffic, then let the customer choose.
Recommend the spot nearest the customer's preferred route for the workshop equipment.
Explain the loading-area concern and discuss a safer location with the customer.

basic.situation: You inspect a returned valve before testing and notice a dent near one attachment. Your supervisor is finishing another inspection nearby.

options.text: Tell your supervisor about the dent and leave the unit on the bench.
Mark the dent and identify the part for review before testing.
Test the valve at its usual settings and see if the gauge moves.
Mark the dent and continue with the standard inspection steps.

advanced.situation: A site inspection finds an unexplained branch on a service line beside a meter. The customer says it has been there since moving in.

options.text: Ask the customer who installed the branch and note their answer.
Remove the branch and restore the line before the customer returns.
Trace the branch, document what you find, and follow site procedures.
Photograph the branch and report a likely illegal tapping incident.

basic.situation: You connect a meter to an air prover for a routine seam check. The outlet is plugged, and the pressure gauge is ready.

options.text: Connect the hose, plug the outlet, and record the starting pressure only.
Attach the hose, plug the outlet, and watch the gauge for pressure loss.
Attach the hose and use a quick hand check for escaping air.
Raise the prover pressure and disconnect the hose when the gauge steadies.

advanced.situation: After a meter cable splice, the switchboard reading fluctuates when equipment starts. Production is waiting, and the connection box is accessible.

options.text: Stop the equipment and request an electrician to inspect the connection.
Isolate the circuit, inspect the splice, and retest the connection safely.
Check the splice visually and ask production to restart the equipment.
Retighten the splice while the equipment runs to find the fault.

basic.situation: You are connecting a replacement heater to the site's water supply. The approved work order lists the unit and connection point.

options.text: Ask the site contact which nearby water line is easiest to reach.
Connect the heater to the nearest pipe and run it for a while.
Connect the heater at the listed point and check the fittings for leaks.
Follow the work order and connect the heater to the listed water line.

advanced.situation: A client wants a ground source heat pump for a new building, but the proposed loop route crosses a crowded service area.

options.text: Suggest a route around the service area based on the existing site plan.
Use the shortest loop route and adjust the pipe length during installation.
Show the client the route options and ask which one they prefer.
Review the site layout and equipment requirements, then propose a workable loop route.

basic.situation: You are checking a replacement fan circuit before startup. The meter is ready, and the wiring diagram is beside the unit.

options.text: Ask a colleague to hold the probes while you watch the meter.
Isolate the circuit and test continuity across the fan terminals.
Touch the probes to the terminals and watch for a continuity tone.
Check the diagram, isolate the circuit, and test continuity at the terminals.
