basic.situation: You are checking a wellhead control panel with an experienced pumper when the flow reading shifts from its usual range.

options.text: You compare the panel with a flow line check and report the reading before changing settings.
You record the reading and keep the pump running at its current setting.
You alter the panel setting until the flow number returns to its usual value.
You tell the experienced pumper and ask whether the reading needs a check.

advanced.situation: The panel pressure is steady, but a flow line reading is falling and your gas check shows a new leak indication.

options.text: You lower the rate and report both readings for team review.
You follow leak response training, secure the operation, and report both readings.
You check the panel connection and log the falling flow for handover.
You hold the setting and wait for the next scheduled gauge check.

basic.situation: Your supervisor asks you to attach a pump and hose to a wellhead, and the setup sheet lists the connection order.

options.text: You match each connection to the setup sheet, secure the joints, and report the completed setup.
You assemble the listed parts and tell the crew that the pump is ready.
You connect the hose to the nearest fitting so the crew can start sooner.
You attach the hose in the listed order and ask your supervisor to check the joints.

advanced.situation: A well service needs a different pump arrangement than the last job, and the available truck has several hose lengths and fittings.

options.text: You select the pump listed on the service sheet and prepare the standard hose set.
You check the service requirements and truck inventory, then prepare the specified pump and fittings for review.
You use the last job's arrangement and ask the crew to adapt the hoses on site.
You load the largest pump and connect the available hoses to save setup time.

basic.situation: You are assigned to mix a dry cement batch, and the job sheet gives the required proportions and mixing order.

options.text: You measure each ingredient against the job sheet and mix in the listed order.
You measure the listed ingredients and ask a coworker to confirm the batch.
You prepare the batch using the listed order and estimate one small measure.
You use the usual proportions and tell the supervisor when the batch is ready.

advanced.situation: A job sheet calls for a custom chemical mixture, but one ingredient label is hard to read and the mixing window is approaching.

options.text: You verify the ingredient against the job sheet and container before measuring.
You pause mixing and ask a coworker to read the unclear label.
You set the ingredient aside and ask the supervisor to confirm its label.
You use the prior recipe and ask the crew to check during pumping.

basic.situation: The production schedule calls for switching oil flow to a storage tank, and your supervisor asks you to operate the listed valve.

options.text: You verify the valve label and schedule, then report the flow change.
You open the nearest valve and tell the supervisor that flow has changed.
You open the listed valve and watch the tank level as flow changes.
You wait for the next operator to confirm which tank should receive the oil.

advanced.situation: A scheduled gas recovery cycle is due, but the storage tank level is near its operating limit and the compressor is ready.

options.text: You ask the next shift to check tank level before running the cycle.
You hold the cycle and report the tank level before starting it.
You start the compressor and monitor the tank during the scheduled recovery cycle.
You check tank capacity and follow the approved recovery sequence.

basic.situation: You are assembling a pump line with a coworker, and the parts list shows two similar fittings for different positions.

options.text: You check the parts list and ask your coworker to confirm both fittings.
You ask your coworker which fitting they used on the previous assembly.
You compare both fittings with the parts list before assembling the line.
You fit a matching fitting and ask your coworker to check it later.

advanced.situation: After a water filter change, the pressure reading differs from the usual range, and the assembly is due for handover.

options.text: You check the filter seating and connections against the assembly instructions, then report the reading.
You report the changed reading and ask the supervisor whether to recheck the filter.
You record the reading and hand over the assembly for the next crew to monitor.
You adjust the gauge to its usual reading and mark the filter change complete.

basic.situation: You are checking a service vehicle before a well job and notice a loose fitting on the pump equipment it carries.

options.text: You tighten the fitting and note the repair on the vehicle check sheet.
You list the fitting as serviceable and send the vehicle to the job site.
You secure the vehicle, inspect the fitting as trained, and record its condition before release.
You tell the next driver about the fitting and leave the vehicle check sheet unchanged.

advanced.situation: A meter has needed repeated adjustment, and you are coordinating two pumpers who will use it on the next shift.

options.text: You withdraw the meter, log the fault, and arrange a trained repair check.
You reset the meter and close the maintenance entry before shift handover.
You document each adjustment and ask both pumpers to compare readings during their shift.
You adjust the meter again and tell both pumpers to watch readings.

basic.situation: You are following a marked collection route with your supervisor when a parked van narrows a residential turn. The truck may fit, but clearance is tight.

options.text: Ask your supervisor to drive this section while you guide from the cab.
Take the usual turn at normal pace to keep the collection on schedule.
Pause before the turn, check clearance, then take the wider approved street.
Drive the marked route slowly and use the agreed turn with your supervisor nearby.

advanced.situation: Heavy rain floods part of your industrial collection route, and a loaded truck is waiting behind you. The marked lane still looks passable, but water is rising.

options.text: Turn back to the last junction and let the following truck pass first.
Use the site's raised service road after checking clearance and confirming it reconnects safely.
Keep the route time by crossing the flooded lane at a steady crawl.
Stop before the water, report the blockage, and wait for route guidance.

basic.situation: At a collection point, you are helping operate the bin hoist when a wheelie bin sits slightly off-centre beneath the lifting arms.

options.text: Lift the bin gently and watch its position as it rises.
Lower the arms, centre the bin, then raise it from the marked position.
Ask your partner to guide the bin while you raise it slowly.
Check the bin sits within the guides before operating the hoist together.

advanced.situation: During a busy collection, the compactor stops partway through a cycle and the warning light stays on. Several full bins are waiting beside the truck.

options.text: Pause loading, keep people clear, and report the warning to dispatch.
Handle nearby bins manually and leave the compactor for the next shift.
Secure the controls, record the warning and cycle state, then request maintenance support.
Try restarting the compactor once, then resume collection if the warning clears.

basic.situation: At the disposal site, you are directed to unload recyclable material, but the marked bay is occupied by another truck.

options.text: Keep the load secured, follow the site queue, and use the next assigned bay.
Circle the site once and return when the bay appears clear.
Unload beside the occupied bay so your truck can clear the queue.
Wait near the entrance and ask the site attendant where to queue.

advanced.situation: Your truck carries a high volume of mixed refuse, and the usual disposal area is closed. Dispatch asks you to clear the load before the shift ends.

options.text: Keep the load secured and ask dispatch which approved site can receive it.
Drive to the usual site and wait nearby for it to reopen.
Unload at the nearest open area to avoid holding up collection.
Verify an approved site's capacity, then coordinate the revised drop with dispatch.

basic.situation: Before starting your route, your checklist shows a low engine fluid level and one rear light that does not come on.

options.text: Record both defects and park the truck for a maintenance check before departure.
Top up the fluid and begin the route, noting the light later.
Tell the supervisor about both items and wait for the next instruction.
Check the fluid against the guide, record the failed light, and report both before leaving.

advanced.situation: During your pre-route check, you notice a new grinding sound when the truck brakes and a small fluid mark beneath the rear axle.

options.text: Report the grinding sound and fluid mark, then arrange a maintenance inspection before departure.
Check the brake fluid level and tell the next driver about the sound.
Keep the truck parked, note the leak location, and request a brake inspection.
Drive a short loop around the depot to see whether the sound fades.

basic.situation: A weather report warns of a storm near two neighbourhoods on your collection route. Your crew is about to leave the depot.

options.text: Leave on schedule and monitor conditions as you approach the first neighbourhood.
Review affected streets and report which sections may need route adjustments.
Tell dispatch about the warning and ask whether the route needs changes.
Wait at the depot and confirm storm timing with dispatch before departure.

advanced.situation: A fallen tree blocks the main road during a large collection run. Several side streets remain open, but the truck's route and timing are now disrupted.

options.text: Report the blockage and ask dispatch to assign a safe route around it.
Backtrack along the route and revisit missed streets after the blockage clears.
Check access on open streets, map a safe loop, and update dispatch.
Use a nearby side street, then rejoin the route once access permits.

basic.situation: After collection, you find a cracked side mirror on the truck and need to complete the equipment report before handover.

options.text: Mention the cracked mirror to the next driver during the handover.
Add the mirror to tomorrow's checklist for the next crew to review.
Record the damage on the defect form and notify the supervisor before handover.
Record the mirror damage, location, and route impact for maintenance review.

advanced.situation: The same bin-hoist fault has delayed your crew twice this week. You are completing today's defect report as the truck returns to the depot.

options.text: Reset the hoist controls before parking so the next crew can start faster.
Log the fault time, load conditions, warning signs, and prior reports for maintenance review.
Write that the hoist failed again and submit the report with the truck number.
Tell dispatch the hoist is unreliable and ask to avoid that truck tomorrow.
